title: [Pass Bug] AutoTileMatmulL0 skips Mem.Vec-fed matmul (fused-attention PV), blocking L0B reuse
body:
### Pass Name

AutoTileMatmulL0 (`auto_tile_matmul_l0`)

### Description

`AutoTileMatmulL0` only L0-tiles matmuls whose **left (A) operand is a `Mem.Mat`-loaded tile**. In a fused flash-attention root (QK → softmax → PV in one mixed cube+vec function), the **PV matmul** (`score·V`) has its left operand in **`Mem.Vec`** — it is the softmax/`exp` output at the cube↔vector (C2V) boundary. The pass tiles the QK matmul but **silently skips PV**.

Consequence: the un-tiled PV matmul keeps its right operand `V` as a full `[SEQ_TILE, 128]` L0B tile. Because it is not tiled into the same `Mem.Right` sub-tile shape as QK, `LegalizePtoBufferReuse` / `MemoryReuse` **cannot alias V's L0B buffer onto the (now-dead) QK matmul's `Mem.Right` buffer**, even though QK fully completes before PV starts. L0B usage therefore doubles:

| `SEQ_TILE` | QK Right (L0B, tiled, double-buffered) | PV Right (L0B, un-tiled) | total | 910B L0B = 64 KB |
| --: | --: | --: | --: | :--: |
| 128 | 32 KB | 32 KB | 64 KB | fits |
| 256 | 64 KB | 64 KB | **128 KB** | **fails** |

This caps the fused-attention KV block (`SEQ_TILE`) at 128 on Ascend 910B and blocks coarser block-level work decomposition. The fix belongs in the **compiler pass** (so every fused-attention kernel benefits automatically), not in per-kernel DSL hand-tiling.

### Git Commit ID

567eb669dba0d16e7a04dea8b25afe452b6d5f9e

### Before IR (Input)

From `passes_dump/16_after_FlattenTileNdTo2D.py` (`fa_fused`, `SEQ_TILE=256`) — **both** matmuls are single untiled `pl.tile.matmul`. Note PV's left operand is `Mem.Vec`, QK's is `Mem.Mat`:

```python
# QK — left operand q_padded is Mem.Mat
k_tile__tile:   pl.Tile[[128, 256], pl.BF16, pl.Mem.Mat] = pl.tile.load(k_cache, ..., transpose=True)
raw_scores__tile: pl.Tile[[16, 256], pl.FP32, pl.Mem.Acc] = pl.tile.matmul(q_padded__tile, k_tile__tile)
# ... scale / row_max / exp / cast  (vector) ...
exp_scores_bf16__tile: pl.Tile[[16, 256], pl.BF16, pl.Mem.Vec] = pl.tile.cast(exp_scores__tile, target_type=pl.BF16)
# PV — left operand exp_scores_bf16 is Mem.Vec
v_tile__tile:   pl.Tile[[256, 128], pl.BF16, pl.Mem.Mat] = pl.tile.load(v_cache, ..., [256, 128])
oi_tmp__tile:   pl.Tile[[16, 128], pl.FP32, pl.Mem.Acc] = pl.tile.matmul(exp_scores_bf16__tile, v_tile__tile)
```

### Expected IR (After Transformation)

Both matmuls L0-tiled **symmetrically** — PV should get the same contraction K-loop + `Mem.Left`/`Mem.Right` sub-tile extraction as QK, so V's right buffer is a reusable sub-tile that `MemoryReuse` aliases onto QK's freed L0B (peak L0B = `max(QK, PV)`, not the sum):

```python
# PV tiled like QK (contraction = SEQ_TILE, stepped to fit L0):
for oi_tmp__l0_ko in pl.pipeline(0, 256, 64, stage=2):
    oi_a = pl.tile.extract(exp_scores_bf16__tile, 0, oi_tmp__l0_ko, [16, 64], target_memory=pl.Mem.Left)
    oi_b = pl.tile.extract(v_tile__tile, oi_tmp__l0_ko, 0, [64, 128], target_memory=pl.Mem.Right)  # 64x128x2 = 16 KB
    oi_tmp = pl.tile.matmul / matmul_acc(oi_a, oi_b)
# => PV Right buffer is a reusable sub-tile aliasable onto QK's freed Mem.Right L0B.
```

### Actual IR or Error

From `passes_dump/17_after_AutoTileMatmulL0.py` — QK is tiled, PV is **not**:

```python
# QK: TILED — contraction K-loop, [64,256] Mem.Right sub-tile (double-buffered => 64 KB)
for raw_scores__tile_l0_ko, (...) in pl.pipeline(0, 128, 64, stage=2, ...):
    raw_scores__tile_l0_a: pl.Tile[[16, 64],  pl.BF16, pl.Mem.Left]  = pl.tile.extract(q_padded__tile, ...)
    raw_scores__tile_l0_b: pl.Tile[[64, 256], pl.BF16, pl.Mem.Right] = pl.tile.extract(k_tile__tile, ...)
    ... pl.tile.matmul / matmul_acc ...

# PV: NOT TILED — full V tile -> L0B as [256,128] = 64 KB, un-reusable
v_tile__tile: pl.Tile[[256, 128], pl.BF16, pl.Mem.Mat] = pl.tile.load(v_cache, ..., [256, 128])
oi_tmp__tile: pl.Tile[[16, 128], pl.FP32, pl.Mem.Acc] = pl.tile.matmul(exp_scores_bf16__tile, v_tile__tile)
```

Downstream failure at `AllocateMemoryAddr`:

```
[1] ERROR - AllocatedMemoryAddr
  Message: Function 'fa_fused_aic': Right buffer usage (131072 bytes) exceeds platform limit (65536 bytes)
  Error Code: 1
Status: FAILED
```

`131072 = 128 KB = QK Right (64 KB) + PV Right (64 KB)`. With `SEQ_TILE=128` the two are 32 KB each (sum 64 KB) and it compiles — masking the bug until the block size grows.

### NPU Kind (if relevant)

Ascend 910B

### Host Platform (if relevant)

Linux (aarch64)

### Additional Context

Repro: qwen3-14b single-layer fused decode (`fa_fused` mixed cube+vec root, QK + tail-masked softmax + PV) at `SEQ_TILE=256`.

Proposed compiler fix: make `AutoTileMatmulL0` recognize and tile matmuls whose **left operand is `Mem.Vec`-resident** (the PV / `score·V` pattern), emitting the same contraction K-loop with `Mem.Left`/`Mem.Right` L0 sub-tiles it already produces for `Mem.Mat`-fed matmuls. This makes the right buffer reuse-compatible so `MemoryReuse` can alias PV's L0B onto QK's freed buffer. (A reuse-pass enhancement to alias an un-tiled right operand onto a freed tiled right buffer would also resolve it, but tiling PV symmetrically is the cleaner root fix.)

Related (same subsystem, different root cause): #1310 (AutoTileMatmulL0 / MemoryReuse acc->acc `tmov`), #1475 / #1547 (MemoryReuse allocation).

title: [Feature] Fine-grained guard for OutWindowExternalizer (Pattern 5) — relax "any later full-parent read disqualifies"
body:
### Summary

The conservative guard added to `OptimizeOrchTensors` Pattern 5 (`OutWindowExternalizer`) in #1468 disables window externalization whenever any later callee reads the rewritten Out's buffer root as a *full parent* tensor. This rule is correct but too coarse — it disqualifies safe and high-value externalization cases where the producer and consumer are already ordered via the same iter-arg chain, so no race is actually possible. We request a more fine-grained safety check (or per-Out / structure-aware decision) so that externalization can resume for these cases.

### Motivation / Use Case

**Observed regression on qwen3-14b decode (pypto-lib `models/qwen3/14b/`):**

Scope-1 `q_proj` / `k_proj` / `v_proj` in `decode_layer.py` use the standard `pl.parallel(0, N, CHUNK)` + `pl.assemble(buf, acc, [b0, q0])` idiom. Before #1468, Pattern 5 (`OutWindowExternalizer`) externalized the windowed write into `slice → windowed callee → assemble`, breaking the loop-carried buffer chain and letting the parallel loop actually fan out across cores. After #1468, the externalization is skipped because the downstream `qk_norm` reads the *full* `q_proj` / `k_proj` tensors:

```python
# passes_dump/14_after_OptimizeOrchTensors.py (qwen3-14b decode_fwd, num_layers=2)
self.qk_norm(..., q_proj_inline102__rv_v2, ..., k_proj_inline78__rv_v2, ...)
#            ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^      ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
#            full-tensor In arg (triggers HasLaterFullParentReadOfRewrittenOutput)
```

**L2 swimlane evidence (real-device a2a3, 2-layer decode_fwd):** all 20 q_proj tile-tasks land on a *single core* (layer-0: AIC_2), strictly back-to-back (~47 µs each, zero overlap) — i.e., ~940 µs fully serial per layer per projection. k_proj/v_proj show the same pattern (each a 4-tile serial chain). Parallelism only exists *between* q/k/v because they have distinct buffers (three chains on three cores), not *within* each projection.

The qk_norm read is **not** racy: it is sequenced after the producing parallel loop via the same iter-arg chain in the orchestration. The guard's conservative "any later full-parent read disqualifies" rule errs on the safe side at the cost of substantial perf on a very common shape (windowed-writer followed by a callee that takes the producer as a whole-tensor In).

### Proposed API / Behavior

Several non-exclusive options, roughly increasing in scope:

1. **Order-aware guard.** Treat a later full-parent read as *safe* (and allow externalization) when it is statically provable that the read is sequenced after the producing loop has fully completed — e.g., the read sits in a subsequent sibling statement that consumes the loop's `return_var`, so runtime ordering is already implied by SSA. The current guard (`HasLaterFullParentReadOfRewrittenOutput`, `src/ir/transforms/optimize_orch_tensors_pass.cpp:2411`) returns true purely on root-set membership without checking this.
2. **Per-Out granularity.** Today the policy is all-or-nothing across a callee's Outs ("Multi-Out policy is all-or-nothing"). Allow externalizing the safe Outs and leaving the unsafe ones on the parent tensor when the callee shape permits.
3. **Producer/consumer-aware rewrite.** When the only later "full read" is in fact a tile-sliced consumption inside a callee that itself loads windowed sub-ranges (e.g., per-head slices of q_proj inside `qk_norm`), prefer externalizing *both* sides (producer writes windows + consumer reads windows) so the buffer-root identity is preserved while parallelism is recovered.
4. **Opt-in escape hatch.** As a stop-gap, a Function/Call-site attribute (e.g., `pl.attr(allow_window_externalization=True)`) to override the guard when the user knows the producer/consumer ordering is safe.

### Alternatives Considered

- **Rewriting the consumer to take windowed slices** (e.g., make `qk_norm` read per-head slices of `q_proj` / `k_proj` instead of the full tensor). This works around the guard in pypto-lib but requires non-trivial source rewrites in every affected kernel and is fragile to future passes.
- **Promoting scope-1 to `pl.spmd`** (as scope-3 / scope-2 already do in pypto-lib commit `2d6f086`). This bypasses Pattern 5 entirely but changes the loop construct and is a larger refactor than the guard issue warrants.

Neither alternative addresses the root cause — the guard's conservatism — and both leave perf on the table for other models that match the same shape.

### Additional Context

- Guard added in: f8731b22 (#1468 "fix(pass): guard unsafe window externalization", Fixes #1444, 2026-05-22).
- Pass source: `src/ir/transforms/optimize_orch_tensors_pass.cpp` (Pattern 5 = `OutWindowExternalizer`, guard at line 2411, `AddFullRootReadsFromCall` at line 2345).
- Affected pypto-lib path: `models/qwen3/14b/decode_layer.py` (scope-1 q/k/v projection, ~L201-237) → `decode_fwd.py` (multi-layer driver).
- Reproduction: `python decode_fwd.py -p a2a3 -d 0 --num-layers 2 --enable-l2-swimlane` (run from `models/qwen3/14b/`). Inspect `build_output/<jit_dir>/passes_dump/14_after_OptimizeOrchTensors.py`: the q_proj `tensor.create` remains hoisted outside the parallel loop and is threaded as iter-arg (no externalization). Swimlane shows 20 q_proj tiles on one core per layer.
- The #1444 fix targeted DSv4's `score_flat.view(...)` windowed-writer / full-parent-reader pattern; the conservative rule catches qwen3-14b q/k/v→qk_norm as collateral.
- Related: hw-native-sys/pypto#1468, hw-native-sys/pypto#1444.

**Host Platform:** Linux (aarch64)

title: outlining captures dead phi from if/else branches as scalar return, breaks C++ codegen
body:
## Summary

When two SPMD loops live in the two branches of an `if/else` and they both rebind the same Python-scope scalar (`t1 = ob * TILE`), pypto's SPMD outlining captures that dead phi as a `Scalar[INDEX]` return on both outlined functions. The orchestration C++ codegen then fails (or emits ill-typed code) because it can't materialize a meaningful caller-side value from an async `rt_submit_aiv_task` call.

## Repro

Minimal pattern (full repro: pypto-lib `models/deepseek/v4/gate.py` sort path; trips automatically when `EP_ROUTING_GLOBAL=True` is exercised, or with `python gate.py -p a2a3sim --layer-id 3`):

```python
for ob_g in pl.spmd(T // TILE, name_hint="prep"):
    t1 = ob_g * TILE          # def #1  (gets DCE'd by the rebinds below)
    # ... uses t1 ...

if layer_id < N_HASH_LAYERS:
    for ob_h in pl.spmd(T // TILE, name_hint="route_hash"):
        t1 = ob_h * TILE      # def #2
        # ... uses t1 inside spmd only ...
else:
    for ob_s in pl.spmd(T // TILE, name_hint="route_sort"):
        t1 = ob_s * TILE      # def #3
        # ... uses t1 inside spmd only ...

# t1 has NO consumer after this point.
```

## What happens

Final IR (`39_after_MaterializeRuntimeScopes.py`) gives the two branch-spmd outlines an unwanted Scalar return:

```python
def route_hash(...) -> pl.Scalar[pl.INDEX]:     # ← spurious return
    ...
def route_sort(...) -> pl.Scalar[pl.INDEX]:     # ← spurious return
    ...

# chip_orch call sites:
t1_inline155__ssa_v1: pl.Scalar[pl.INDEX] = self.route_hash_spmd(...)
t1_inline155__ssa_v2: pl.Scalar[pl.INDEX] = self.route_sort_spmd(...)
```

The same outlining run on the `ob_g` spmd correctly DCE's `t1`: `gate_spmd` returns only the InOut tensors (`route_scores_buf`, `biased_scores_buf`) that have real downstream consumers — t1's def #1 dies because def #2 / #3 overwrite it in both branches.

Generated `chip_orch.cpp` from `orchestration_codegen.cpp` then fails to build:

```cpp
int64_t t1_inline155;
if (static_cast<int64_t>(layer_id) < 0) {
    // ... rt_submit_aiv_task(10, params_t8) — task is fire-and-forget ...
    const Tensor& t1_inline155__ssa_v1 = indices;   // GenerateSingleReturnAlias fallback to out_indices[0]
    t1_inline155 = t1_inline155__ssa_v1;            // const Tensor → int64_t : type error
} else {
    // ... rt_submit_aiv_task(11, params_t9) ...
    const Tensor& t1_inline155__ssa_v2 = indices;
    t1_inline155 = t1_inline155__ssa_v2;
}
// t1_inline155 is NEVER used after this point.
```

Compiler error:

```
chip_orch.cpp:295:32: error: cannot convert 'const Tensor' to 'int64_t' in assignment
chip_orch.cpp:309:32: error: cannot convert 'const Tensor' to 'int64_t' in assignment
```

## Why is this asymmetric (ob_g vs ob_h/ob_s)

- The `ob_g` spmd's t1 (def #1) is killed by def #2 / #3 in both arms of the if/else → SSA pass DCE's it → outlining sees no live-out → no return.
- The `ob_h` / `ob_s` spmds' t1 (def #2 / #3) reach the function exit (if/else has no successor). The SSA pass keeps the phi node, even though the phi has no consumer. Outlining treats every phi predecessor as needing to be returnable, so both branch-spmd outlines pick up `-> Scalar[INDEX]`.

`GenerateSingleReturnAlias` in `src/codegen/orchestration/orchestration_codegen.cpp:2156` then falls back to `out_indices[0]` (the first Out param) when it can't trace the return back to a Param, emitting `const Tensor& <ret> = <first_out_param>;` — type-incorrect when the LHS was declared as `int64_t` from the Scalar return.

## Expected

Either:
1. The SSA/outlining pipeline DCEs phi nodes whose result has no users (preferred — it would also shrink the outlined function ABI), OR
2. The codegen of `GenerateSingleReturnAlias` declines to alias when the call's return type is not `TensorType` (defensive; doesn't help the dead-return-type "leaks into outlined ABI" issue, but prevents the type-mismatch crash).

## Possible fixes

- **A (root cause)**: in the SSA pass or outlining pass, drop phi nodes that have no consumers before computing the outlined-function return signature. The `ob_g` path already gets this right; the same DCE should handle the if/else exit phi.
- **B (defensive band-aid)**: in `GenerateSingleReturnAlias` (orchestration_codegen.cpp:2156), early-return when `call->GetType()` is not a `TensorType`. This stops the bad `const Tensor& = indices` alias from being emitted but the leftover `t1_inline155 = <undeclared ssa>;` line is still broken — so A is really what's needed.

## Environment

- pypto HEAD: `6abbf46c`
- Platform: `a2a3sim`
- Repro program: pypto-lib `models/deepseek/v4/gate.py` sort path (exercised via `python gate.py -p a2a3sim --layer-id 3` or any layer where `layer_id >= num_hash_layers`)

title: [Feature] Software-pipeline pl.pipeline across the fused cube/vector C2V/V2C (tpush/tpop) boundary
body:
### Summary

`pl.pipeline` over a loop whose body is a **fused cube+vector root** (cube matmul → vector op → cube matmul, with the C2V/V2C moves lowered to `tile.tpush_to_aiv` / `tile.tpop_from_aiv` through the GM pipe) does **not** software-pipeline across the `tpush`/`tpop` boundary. The pass keeps every iteration strictly serial, so the cube (AIC) stalls at each `tpop` waiting for the vector (AIV), and the two engines never overlap across iterations.

A user can recover the overlap **only** by hand-writing a manual unroll that reorders the body engine-grouped (all cube ops of N iterations, then all vector ops, then the next cube ops). The request is for `pl.pipeline` (via `LowerPipelineLoops` / the pipeline scheduler) to perform that cross-iteration reordering automatically — i.e. hoist iteration `i+1`'s cube matmul ahead of iteration `i`'s vector-dependent `tpop`/second matmul — so the declarative form matches the hand-unrolled performance.

### Motivation / Use Case

Fused flash-attention is the concrete case. The per-head loop body is:

```
QK matmul (AIC/cube) → softmax (AIV/vector) → SV matmul (AIC/cube)
```

with C2V (`tpush_to_aiv`) moving QK scores to the vector core and V2C (`tpop_from_aiv`) moving the softmax result back to the cube. On A2/A3 this round-trips through GM, so the cube sits idle during the vector's softmax and vice-versa.

Measured on a single-layer Qwen3-14B decode (BATCH=16, SEQ_TILE=256, GP_SIZE=8 heads per work item), `fa_fused` kernel `Exec` time:

| Form | AIC Exec | AIV Exec |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Serial `pl.range(GP_SIZE)` (baseline) | 111.3 µs | 109.8 µs |
| **`pl.pipeline(GP_SIZE, stage=2)`** | 108.1 µs (−3%) | 106.8 µs (−3%) |
| **Manual 2-way unroll** (engine-grouped) | **98.1 µs (−12%)** | **96.7 µs (−12%)** |

The manual unroll's ~12% comes from overlapping the cube's `QK(gp_{i+1})` with the vector's `softmax(gp_i)`. `pl.pipeline` only achieves ~3% (incidental load double-buffering) because it does not reorder across `tpush`/`tpop`.

The user-facing problem: the *declarative* `pl.pipeline` is the natural way to ask for software pipelining, but today it forces users to hand-write the unrolled, engine-grouped program to actually get the cube/vector overlap. Closing this gap makes the cube/vector software pipeline a one-line `pl.pipeline` instead of a manual unroll.

### Proposed API / Behavior

No new API — make the existing `pl.pipeline` deliver the overlap:

```python
# Today the user must hand-unroll + reorder engine-grouped to get the overlap:
for gp_pair in pl.range(GP_SIZE // 2):
    rs0 = pl.matmul(q0, k0, b_trans=True)      # AIC: QK gp0
    rs1 = pl.matmul(q1, k1, b_trans=True)      # AIC: QK gp1   (issued before softmax0)
    e0, m0, l0 = softmax(rs0)                   # AIV
    e1, m1, l1 = softmax(rs1)                   # AIV
    oi0 = pl.matmul(e0, v0)                     # AIC: SV gp0
    oi1 = pl.matmul(e1, v1)                     # AIC: SV gp1
    ...stores...

# Desired: the declarative form should produce the SAME overlapped schedule.
for gp in pl.pipeline(GP_SIZE, stage=2):
    rs  = pl.matmul(q, k, b_trans=True)         # AIC: QK
    e, m, l = softmax(rs)                        # AIV (C2V/V2C tpush/tpop)
    oi  = pl.matmul(e, v)                        # AIC: SV
    ...stores...
```

Concretely, when scheduling a `pl.pipeline` loop whose body crosses an AIC→AIV→AIC boundary via `tpush`/`tpop`, the AIC instruction stream should become:

```
QK_i, tpush_i, QK_{i+1}, tpush_{i+1}, tpop_i, SV_i, tpop_{i+1}, SV_{i+1}, ...
```

i.e. iteration `i+1`'s cube `QK` is hoisted ahead of iteration `i`'s `tpop`/`SV`, so the cube stays busy while the vector consumes iteration `i`'s scores. Today `LowerPipelineLoops` instead emits the strictly-serial `QK_i, tpush_i, tpop_i, SV_i, QK_{i+1}, ...` (verified in the generated ptoas AIC stream).

### Alternatives Considered

- **Manual unroll** (`for gp_pair in pl.range(GP_SIZE // 2): ...` with the body reordered engine-grouped): works and yields the full ~12%, but requires the user to hand-write the unrolled program — exactly what `pl.pipeline` is supposed to abstract away. It also doesn't compose well with other axes (e.g. adding K-dim double-buffering on top busts the L0B budget).
- **`pl.pipeline(stage=3)`**: deeper staging does not help — the scheduler still doesn't cross the `tpush`/`tpop` boundary, so the per-iteration serialization remains.

### Additional Context

- Evidence: generated ptoas AIC stream for the `pl.pipeline(stage=2)` form shows `QK_i, tpush_to_aiv_i, tpop_from_aiv_i, SV_i, QK_{i+1}, ...` — no reordering across the fused boundary.
- Pass to enhance: `LowerPipelineLoops` (`src/ir/transforms/lower_pipeline_loops_pass.cpp`) / the pipeline scheduler, which currently treats `tile.tpush_to_aiv` / `tile.tpop_from_aiv` as a per-iteration barrier.
- Related (cube/vector pipeline stalls, but different root cause — MemoryReuse buffer-reuse policy rather than pipeline reordering): #1475, #1352.
- Repro branch/commit: `issue-1595-autotile-vec-fed-matmul` @ `e2866596`.

title: [Feature] @pl.jit diagnostics: report real source provenance instead of "<string>"
body:
### Summary

When a `@pl.jit` kernel fails to parse or compile, the diagnostic header and code snippet reference a synthesized `<string>` source rather than the user's real kernel file. `@pl.jit` re-derives the kernel into a fresh `@pl.program` **source string** (via `ast.unparse`, `specializer.py:1418`) and parses that string with no filename (`decorator.py:1288` → `pl.parse(source)`), so `text_parser.parse` falls back to `filename="<string>"` (`text_parser.py:144`). Improve the error provenance so a JIT compile error can be mapped back toward the original source the user wrote.

### Motivation / Use Case

- For `@pl.jit` kernels, parse/compile errors print `--> <string>:N:C` plus a snippet of the **generated (specialized)** program — not the user's file. A reader hunts for the error at a file/line that doesn't correspond to what they wrote. This is exactly what made #1558 confusing to triage.
- Plain `@pl.function` / `@pl.program` parsed from a real file already report the real path + line numbers (`decorator.py:676-798`); only the JIT path loses provenance.
- Even a minimal improvement (naming the failing kernel in the header) makes the error far more navigable.

Note: #1611 already fixed the caret to be correct **within** the printed `<string>` snippet, so JIT errors are actionable today. This issue is specifically about source *provenance / navigability*, not correctness of the caret.

### Proposed API / Behavior

Two tiers, smallest first.

**Tier 1 — cheap, no semantic risk (recommended starting point).**
Pass a descriptive `filename` into the JIT parse call (`decorator.py:1288`):

```python
# before
parsed = pl.parse(source)
# after
parsed = pl.parse(source, filename=f"<jit:{self.__name__}>")
```

The header then reads e.g. `--> <jit:matmul>:15:86` instead of an anonymous `<string>`, so the user immediately knows which kernel failed. Line numbers still index the generated source, which the diagnostic already prints in full.

**Tier 2 — larger, design discussion (optional source map).**
Build a `generated_line -> (original_file, original_line)` map in the specializer and translate spans before rendering (consumed in `SpanTracker.get_span` or at render time), so the `-->` can point into the user's actual `.py`.

### Alternatives Considered

- **Feed the transformed AST directly to `ASTParser`** (skip the `unparse -> reparse` round-trip) so original `lineno`/`col_offset` survive. Moderate refactor of `ASTParser.__init__` + `SpanTracker`; still hits the transformed-text caveat below.
- **Do nothing.** #1611 makes the caret correct within the printed snippet, so errors are already actionable — this is purely a provenance/UX enhancement.

### Additional Context

**Why a clean real-file remap is hard.** The generated string is a *transformed* program, so there is no 1:1 line/column mapping back to the user's source, and original AST positions are lost across `unparse -> reparse`. The transformations that break the mapping:

- `ast.unparse` collapses multi-line statements onto a single line (this is why #1558's `with pl.at(...)` shows as one line).
- Variables are alpha-renamed (`_rename_map`, `x -> x_v1`).
- Tensor shapes are baked in, scalars folded, dynamic dims rewritten to `pl.tensor.dim(...)`.
- Statements are added / removed / reordered (e.g. `M, N = a.shape` expanded; `bind_dynamic` stripped; loop bridge assignments synthesized).

Consequence: pointing at the original file can show text that does not match the (transformed) error context. Errors about the user's **literal syntax** (e.g. the `deps=` shape in #1558) map cleanly; errors about **synthesized content** do not. `_rewrite_jit_error` (`decorator.py:84-110`) already un-renames variables in the error **message text** but intentionally does not remap `span` / `file` / `source_lines`.

**Pointers:** `decorator.py:1288` (parse call), `specializer.py:1418` (`ast.unparse`), `text_parser.py:144` (default filename), `decorator.py:84-110` (`_rewrite_jit_error`), `span_tracker.py:37-55` (`get_span` adds `line_offset`).

Related: #1558 (caret bug found while diagnosing this; fixed in #1611), #1305 (source mapping for verifier output).

title: [Pass Bug] 8 passes skip the Submit IR kind (exact-kind Call dispatch) inside pl.manual_scope
body:
### Pass Name

Umbrella tracking issue across **8 passes** (shared root cause). Per-pass checklist below: `normalize_return_order`, `inject_gm_pipe_buffer`, `inline_functions`, `flatten_call_expr`, `convert_tensor_to_tile_ops`, `optimize_orch_tensors`, `materialize_tensor_strides`, `fuse_create_assemble_to_slice`.

### Description

Each of these passes walks call-like IR nodes via **exact-kind** `As<Call>` / `VisitExpr_(CallPtr)` / the `GetCallFromStmt` helper (`include/pypto/ir/transforms/utils/transform_utils.h:84`, which is `As<Call>`-only). `Submit` is a **sibling `ObjectKind`** (emitted by `pl.submit` inside `pl.manual_scope`), **not** a `Call` subclass, so these passes silently skip it — the exact failure mode documented in `.claude/rules/pass-submit-awareness.md`.

All 8 run **before** `DeriveCallDirections` (pass 34, the point where `Submit` is lowered to `Call`), so they genuinely see live `Submit` nodes. `DeriveCallDirections` itself was already made submit-aware in #1552 and is the reference implementation.

Each item below has a committed `xfail(strict=False)` regression test (branch `test/pass-before-after-coverage`) that encodes correct behavior and **fails today**; it flips to passing once its pass is fixed.

- [x] **normalize_return_order** — `normalize_return_order_pass.cpp:241` (`TupleIndexPermutationMutator`): `Submit` result `TupleGetItem` indices not remapped after Out-param reorder → unpacked names bind the wrong output buffers. Repro: `test_normalize_return_order.py::TestNormalizeReturnOrderSubmit::test_submit_swapped_returns_remapped`
- [x] **inject_gm_pipe_buffer** — uses `GetCallFromStmt`: a Group launched via `pl.submit` on Ascend910B is invisible → no `tensor.create` placeholder, `__gm_pipe_buffer` not forwarded. Repro: `test_inject_gm_pipe_buffer.py::test_gm_pipe_injection_handles_submit_launched_group`
- [x] **inline_functions** — `CalledInlineCollector`/`InlineCallsMutator`: `pl.submit` of an Inline fn is not inlined; the fn is dropped but the dangling `Submit` survives and `InlineFunctionsEliminated` misses it. Repro: `test_inline_functions.py::TestInlineFunctionsSubmitCallSite::test_submit_of_inline_eliminates_reference`
- [x] **flatten_call_expr** — no `VisitExpr_(SubmitPtr)`: a nested `Call` arg of a `Submit` is not hoisted → three-address invariant violated. Repro: `test_flatten_call_expr_pass.py::TestFlattenPreservesAttrs::test_nested_call_arg_in_submit_is_flattened`
- [x] **convert_tensor_to_tile_ops** — `CallSiteUpdateMutator`: a `pl.submit` call site to a transformed InCore gets no `tensor.create` and the appended Out arg is not forwarded. Repro: `test_convert_tensor_to_tile_ops.py::TestSubmitCallSiteUpdate::test_submit_call_site_gets_tensor_create`
- [x] **optimize_orch_tensors** — `OrchRewriter::TryRewriteCall`: the `IsSubmitCall` branch is dead for real `Submit` nodes → a windowable kernel launched via `pl.submit` stays baseline. Repro: `test_optimize_orch_tensors.py::TestOutWindowSubmitCall::test_submit_windowable_kernel_is_externalized`
- [x] **materialize_tensor_strides** — no `VisitExpr_(SubmitPtr)`: a `Submit` node's own return type keeps an empty stride while every other reachable `TensorType` is materialized. Repro: `test_materialize_tensor_strides_pass.py::test_submit_return_type_materialized`
- [x] **fuse_create_assemble_to_slice** — `BufferRootCollector` (`As<Call>`): a `pl.submit` callee never propagates its Out-param buffer root → create+assemble around a submit is left unfused. Repro: `test_fuse_create_assemble_to_slice.py::test_submit_create_assemble_fused_to_slice`

Related (context, different root cause): #1368.

### Git Commit ID

35731d4833cdef3c49d8da254bba1d9a145be92f

### Before IR (Input)

Representative case — `normalize_return_order`. The InCore `kernel` returns `(out_b, out_a)` (reversed vs Out-param order); the orchestrator launches it via `pl.submit` and unpacks `(a, b)`:

```python
@pl.program
class Before:
    @pl.function(type=pl.FunctionType.InCore)
    def kernel(self, x: pl.Tensor[[16], pl.FP32],
               out_a: pl.Out[pl.Tensor[[16], pl.FP32]],
               out_b: pl.Out[pl.Tensor[[16], pl.FP32]]) -> tuple[pl.Tensor[[16], pl.FP32], pl.Tensor[[16], pl.FP32]]:
        x_tile = pl.load(x, [0], [16])
        a_tile = pl.tile.add(x_tile, x_tile)
        b_tile = pl.tile.mul(x_tile, x_tile)
        out_b_store = pl.store(b_tile, [0], out_b)
        out_a_store = pl.store(a_tile, [0], out_a)
        return (out_b_store, out_a_store)   # reversed vs (out_a, out_b)

    @pl.function(type=pl.FunctionType.Orchestration)
    def main(self, x, out_a: pl.Out[...], out_b: pl.Out[...]) -> tuple[...]:
        with pl.manual_scope():
            (a, b), tid = pl.submit(self.kernel, x, out_a, out_b)
        return (a, b)
```

### Expected IR (After Transformation)

Step A reorders the kernel's returns to match Out-param order `(out_a, out_b)`; Step B must then **remap the caller's projections** so `a`/`b` still bind the same logical buffers (encoded as the swapped `(b, a)` unpack):

```python
class Expected:
    def kernel(...) -> tuple[...]:
        ...
        return (out_a_store, out_b_store)   # normalized order

    def main(...) -> tuple[...]:
        with pl.manual_scope():
            (b, a), tid = pl.submit(self.kernel, x, out_a, out_b)  # _submit_tmp indices remapped
        return (a, b)
```

### Actual IR or Error

Step A reorders the kernel returns, but `TupleIndexPermutationMutator` matches `As<Call>` only and never tracks the `Submit` result, so the caller's `TupleGetItem` indices are left unchanged:

```python
    def main(...) -> tuple[...]:
        with pl.manual_scope():
            (a, b), tid = pl.submit(self.kernel, x, out_a, out_b)  # NOT remapped — stale indices
        return (a, b)
```

`ir.assert_structural_equal(After, Expected)` fails on `['main'].body` (the manual_scope projection order differs). Net effect: after the kernel's outputs are reordered, `a` and `b` silently bind the wrong output tensors.

### NPU Kind (if relevant)

N/A (not hardware-specific)

### Host Platform (if relevant)

N/A (not hardware-specific)

### Additional Context

**Common fix shape** (same for all 8): make each call-walk Submit-aware — use `AsCallLike` / a `SubmitToCallView` adapter, preserve Submit-ness through rewrites, relax the args-vs-params size guard to the **prefix invariant** (`args_.size() <= params_.size()`, not `==`), and account for the trailing `Scalar[TASK_ID]` in the return tuple. See `.claude/rules/pass-submit-awareness.md` and the reference fix in #1552 (`DeriveCallDirections`).

The 8 `xfail(strict=False)` regression tests are committed on branch `test/pass-before-after-coverage`; each will flip to passing (xpass) once its pass is fixed, so they double as ready-made acceptance checks.

---

**Status: implemented** on branch `test/pass-before-after-coverage` (commit `b24d7409`). All 8 passes are now Submit-aware; the 8 committed before/after regression tests (previously `xfail`) pass as normal tests, and the full `tests/ut/ir` transforms suite is green. `DeriveCallDirections` reference fix: #1552.

title: [Bug] tensor.gather on local TileType input can overwrite source row during lowering
body:
### Component

IR / `ConvertTensorToTileOps` / `tensor.gather` lowering for `TileType` inputs

### Description

`tensor.gather` can mutate or alias its local TileType input when the input is a local tensor lowered to a tile.

The repro below creates a local `[16, 256]` FP32 tensor `local_scores`, reads it with a scalar loop, then calls:

```python
gathered_tile = pl.gather(local_scores, dim=-1, index=idx)
```

The gather output itself is correct. However, reading the same `local_scores` again with the same scalar loop after `pl.gather` returns wrong values: row 0 behaves as if it has been overwritten by row 15.

This violates the expected read-only semantics of `gather`: neither the source input nor the index input should be modified by the operation.

This was observed on PyPTO main after #1609, where `tensor.gather` now accepts `TileType` input/index and no longer fails at compile time.

### Minimal Reproducer

Save this as `repro_tensor_gather_local_alias.py` and run it with the normal PyPTO runtime environment configured.

```python
import argparse

import pypto.language as pl
import torch
from pypto.runtime.runner import RunConfig


ROWS = 16
COLS = 256
TOPK = 8


@pl.jit
def repro_kernel(
    scores: pl.Tensor[[ROWS, COLS], pl.FP32],
    idx: pl.Tensor[[ROWS, TOPK], pl.INT32],
    before: pl.Out[pl.Tensor[[ROWS, TOPK], pl.FP32]],
    gathered: pl.Out[pl.Tensor[[ROWS, TOPK], pl.FP32]],
    after: pl.Out[pl.Tensor[[ROWS, TOPK], pl.FP32]],
):
    for _ in pl.spmd(1, name_hint="gather_alias_repro"):
        local_scores = pl.create_tensor([ROWS, COLS], dtype=pl.FP32)
        local_scores[:, :] = scores[:, :]

        local_idx = pl.create_tensor([ROWS, TOPK], dtype=pl.INT32)
        local_idx[:, :] = idx[:, :]

        before_tile = pl.full([ROWS, TOPK], dtype=pl.FP32, value=0.0)
        for r in pl.range(ROWS):
            for k in pl.range(TOPK):
                col_i32 = pl.read(local_idx, [r, k])
                col = pl.cast(col_i32, pl.INDEX)
                val = pl.read(local_scores, [r, col])
                pl.write(before_tile, [r, k], val)
        before[:, :] = before_tile

        gathered_tile = pl.gather(local_scores, dim=-1, index=idx)
        gathered[:, :] = gathered_tile

        after_tile = pl.full([ROWS, TOPK], dtype=pl.FP32, value=0.0)
        for r in pl.range(ROWS):
            for k in pl.range(TOPK):
                col_i32 = pl.read(local_idx, [r, k])
                col = pl.cast(col_i32, pl.INDEX)
                val = pl.read(local_scores, [r, col])
                pl.write(after_tile, [r, k], val)
        after[:, :] = after_tile


def make_scores() -> torch.Tensor:
    row = torch.arange(ROWS, dtype=torch.float32).reshape(ROWS, 1) * 1000.0
    col = torch.arange(COLS, dtype=torch.float32).reshape(1, COLS)
    return row + col


def make_idx() -> torch.Tensor:
    base = torch.tensor([7, 9, 3, 128, 255, 0, 64, 11], dtype=torch.int32)
    return torch.stack([(base + r * 13) % COLS for r in range(ROWS)])


def first_mismatch(actual: torch.Tensor, expected: torch.Tensor) -> str:
    neq = actual != expected
    if not bool(neq.any()):
        return ""
    flat_idx = int(torch.nonzero(neq.reshape(-1), as_tuple=False)[0].item())
    idx = torch.unravel_index(torch.tensor(flat_idx), actual.shape)
    idx_tuple = tuple(int(x) for x in idx)
    return f"{idx_tuple}: actual={actual[idx_tuple].item()} expected={expected[idx_tuple].item()}"


def main() -> None:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    parser.add_argument("-p", "--platform", default="a2a3sim", choices=["a2a3", "a2a3sim", "a5", "a5sim"])
    parser.add_argument("-d", "--device", type=int, default=0)
    args = parser.parse_args()

    scores = make_scores()
    idx = make_idx()
    expected = torch.gather(scores, dim=-1, index=idx.long())
    before = torch.zeros_like(expected)
    gathered = torch.zeros_like(expected)
    after = torch.zeros_like(expected)

    repro_kernel(
        scores,
        idx,
        before,
        gathered,
        after,
        config=RunConfig(platform=args.platform, device_id=args.device, dump_passes=True),
    )

    for name, actual in {"before": before, "gathered": gathered, "after": after}.items():
        ok = torch.equal(actual, expected)
        print(f"{name}: {'PASS' if ok else 'FAIL'}")
        if not ok:
            print(f"  first mismatch: {first_mismatch(actual, expected)}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
```

Run:

```bash
python repro_tensor_gather_local_alias.py -p a2a3sim
```

### Expected Behavior

All three outputs should match `torch.gather(scores, dim=-1, index=idx)`:

```text
before: PASS
gathered: PASS
after: PASS
```

`before` and `after` use the same scalar-read loop:

```python
val = pl.read(local_scores, [r, col])
pl.write(out_tile, [r, k], val)
```

The only operation between them is `pl.gather(local_scores, dim=-1, index=idx)`, which should not mutate `local_scores`.

### Actual Behavior

Observed result:

```text
before: PASS
gathered: PASS
after: FAIL
  first mismatch: (0, 0): actual=15007.0 expected=7.0
```

The input is constructed as:

```python
scores[row, col] = row * 1000 + col
```

Therefore `15007.0` means the `after` scalar-read path read row 15, col 7 where row 0, col 7 was expected. The scalar-read loop itself is not the cause, because the same loop passes before `pl.gather`.

### Preliminary Analysis

The generated PTO shows that the TileType-input `tensor.gather` path materializes each source row into a scratch tile before calling `pto.tgather`. The scratch tile for the sliced `[1, 256]` row aliases the same base address as the full `local_scores` tile:

```mlir
%local_scores__tile = pto.alloc_tile addr = %c96_i64 ... rows=16, cols=256
...
%0 = pto.alloc_tile addr = %c96_i64 ... rows=16, cols=256
...
%gather_inp_row = pto.alloc_tile addr = %c96_i64 ... rows=1, cols=256
%slice_view = pto.subview %0[%gather_lv, %c0_index] sizes [1, 256] ...
pto.tmov ins(%slice_view) outs(%gather_inp_row)
pto.tgather ins(%gather_inp_row, %gather_idx_row, %gather_row_tmp) outs(%gather_row)
```

Since `%gather_inp_row` starts at the same address as `local_scores`, every row materialization writes the current source row into `local_scores` row 0. The gather result is still correct in the same iteration because `pto.tgather` immediately consumes that scratch row. After the loop finishes, row 0 has been overwritten by the last materialized row, row 15. This explains the `after` mismatch:

```text
after[0, 0] reads local_scores[0, 7]
actual = 15007.0  # row 15, col 7
expected = 7.0    # row 0, col 7
```

This suggests that the TileType-input `tensor.gather` lowering needs to ensure its row materialization scratch does not alias the source input tile, or otherwise avoid materializing by writing into the source tile's address range.

### Environment

Observed with:

```text
PyPTO: b5341e805fae2c4ee0b3ec1615b59755fa1015f9
ptoas: 0.42
platform: a2a3sim
```

### Related

- #1609 fixed the compile-time `TileType` acceptance path for `tensor.gather`.
- This issue tracks a separate runtime correctness problem after the code can compile and execute.

title: [Feature] pl.col_expand_add 需要补一下
body:
### Summary

"""Minimal PyPTO repro: `pl.col_expand_add` is missing.

Run:
    PTO_PLATFORM=a2a3sim python inductor_pto/docs/repro/repro_col_expand_add.py

Background
----------
PyPTO's unified ops provide column-broadcast `sub`, `mul`, `div` and the row
counterpart `row_expand_add`, but there is **no `col_expand_add`**. Column
broadcast add is `[1, N] + [M, N]` — a 1-D weight/bias added to every row of a
2-D tile (e.g. `a[N] + b[M, N]`). Without `col_expand_add` this pattern has no
correct primitive: plain `pl.add([1, N], [M, N])` does not expand along rows and
produces wrong numbers.

What this script shows
----------------------
1. Symbol table: `col_expand_{sub,mul,div}` and `row_expand_add` exist;
   `col_expand_add` does not.
2. A real `@pl.program` that column-broadcasts with `col_expand_mul` builds
   fine — proving the shapes / tiling are valid PyPTO.
3. The identical program written for **add** cannot be expressed: there is no
   `pl.col_expand_add` to call.

Desired fix
-----------
Add `col_expand_add` to `pypto/python/pypto/language/op/unified_ops.py` (plus
the matching `ir/op/tensor_ops.py` + tile lowering), aligned with the existing
`col_expand_{sub,mul,div}` and `row_expand_add`.
"""
import pypto.language as pl


def report_symbol_table():
    present = [n for n in ("col_expand", "col_expand_sub", "col_expand_mul",
                           "col_expand_div", "row_expand_add")
               if hasattr(pl, n)]
    missing = [n for n in ("col_expand_add",) if not hasattr(pl, n)]
    print("present :", present)
    print("missing :", missing)
    assert hasattr(pl, "col_expand_mul"), "expected col_expand_mul to exist"
    assert hasattr(pl, "row_expand_add"), "expected row_expand_add to exist"
    assert not hasattr(pl, "col_expand_add"), \
        "col_expand_add now exists — gap is fixed, update inductor_pto _PTO_COL_EXPAND_OPS"


# A column-broadcast MUL program — builds today (proves the pattern is legal).
@pl.program
class ColBroadcastMul:
    @pl.function(type=pl.FunctionType.Opaque)
    def compute(self,
                a: pl.Tensor[[256], pl.FP32],            # 1-D weight
                b: pl.Tensor[[128, 256], pl.FP32],
                out0: pl.Out[pl.Tensor[[128, 256], pl.FP32]]
                ) -> pl.Tensor[[128, 256], pl.FP32]:
        with pl.at(level=pl.Level.CORE_GROUP, optimization=pl.chunked_loop_optimizer):
            for r in pl.parallel(0, 128, 32, chunk=1):
                col_vec = pl.reshape(pl.slice(a, [256], [0]), [1, 256])  # [1, 256]
                tile = pl.slice(b, [32, 256], [r, 0])                    # [32, 256]
                res = pl.col_expand_mul(tile, col_vec)                   # broadcasts col_vec across rows
                out0 = pl.assemble(out0, res, [r, 0])
        return out0


def show_add_has_no_primitive():
    # The same column broadcast for ADD has no callable: the only way to write
    # `a[N] + b[M, N]` correctly would be pl.col_expand_add, which is absent.
    fn = getattr(pl, "col_expand_add", None)
    print("pl.col_expand_add =", fn)
    if fn is None:
        print("=> CONFIRMED GAP: cannot express column-broadcast add "
              "([1, N] + [M, N]) without pl.col_expand_add.")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    report_symbol_table()
    print("ColBroadcastMul program object:", ColBroadcastMul)  # builds OK
    show_add_has_no_primitive()
    print("OK: gap demonstrated (col_expand_mul works; col_expand_add missing).")

title: [Feature] Support Gather Directly to L1 — Eliminate GM Round-Trip
body:
### Summary

We need the pypto framework to support gathering data directly into L1, so that the subsequent Cube compute can read from L1 without going through GM.

Specifically:
1. **L1 buffer allocation**: A way to allocate buffers in L1 (currently `pl.create_tensor()` only creates GM tensors)
2. **Gather into L1**: The gather operation should be able to write its output directly to L1 instead of GM
3. **Cube reads from L1**: matmul and other Cube operations should be able to consume L1 buffers as input, skipping GM loads
4. **Synchronization**: When gather and compute are fused in one task, the compute side must wait until the gather side finishes writing to L1


### Motivation / Use Case

In sparse attention decode, the KV gather stage (`gather_kv`) gathers scattered KV rows from two paged KV pools (sliding-window + compressed cache) and writes the result to GM (`sparse_kv`). The subsequent QK/PV compute stage (`qk_pv`) must then reload that same data from GM into L1→L0. This GM write+read round-trip costs ~90 us per token, dominating the critical path.

Current data flow:
```
gather_kv: GM(ori_kv/cmp_kv) → GM(sparse_kv)    ## gather writes to GM
qk_pv:    GM(sparse_kv) → L1 → L0               ## compute reads back from GM
```

Desired data flow:
```
fused gather+compute: GM(ori_kv/cmp_kv) → L1 → L0  ## gather directly into L1, compute reads from L1
```

title: Consider integrating pre-runtime pass IR validation into the compile flow
body:
## Background

`pypto.debug.torch_codegen.validate_pass_ir_codegen_results` (python/pypto/debug/torch_codegen.py) can re-run each dumped pass IR via `torch_codegen` and numerically compare against golden outputs, giving us per-pass correctness checking before ever touching the device.

Today this is a standalone debug utility that is **not** wired into the compile flow:

- `pypto.ir.compile` (python/pypto/ir/compile.py) only emits the per-pass IR into `output_dir/passes_dump/` when `dump_passes=True`. It never calls the validator.
- Each consumer has to discover `passes_dump/`, prepare golden inputs/outputs, and call `validate_pass_ir_codegen_results` themselves.

## Where this is currently being wired up

The integration is presently being done downstream, at the test-harness level, in pypto-lib:

- hw-native-sys/pypto-lib#162 — adds `RunConfig.validate_ir` / `validate_ir_only` to the golden runner and calls `validate_pass_ir_codegen_results` between input generation and runtime.

## Question / proposal

Should pypto expose this as a first-class, optional step so consumers don't each re-implement the wiring? For example:

- an optional `validate_ir` path on `pypto.ir.compile` (or a thin helper next to it) that, given golden inputs/expected outputs + tolerances, runs the per-pass validation right after `passes_dump` is produced; or
- a documented, supported entry point that makes the `passes_dump` → `validate_pass_ir_codegen_results` contract official.

Looking for guidance on whether this belongs in pypto's compile flow, or should remain a debug-only utility that downstreams (like pypto-lib) integrate as needed.

Filed per discussion; closing pypto-lib#162 in favor of this issue.

title: [Feature] Support pld.DistributedTensor parameters in @pl.jit / @pl.jit.inline
body:
### Summary

The JIT specialization path does not recognize `pld.DistributedTensor` as a parameter kind. `@pl.jit` / `@pl.jit.inline` functions can only declare `pl.Tensor` params, so any kernel taking HCCL window tensors (`DistributedTensor`) or doing cross-rank communication cannot be authored as a jit function — it must be a `@pl.function(InCore)` inside a `@pl.program` class.

### Motivation / Use Case

Single-card compute kernels (hc_pre / gate / expert / …) are clean `@pl.jit.inline` functions composed by a top-level `@pl.jit` (`models/deepseek/v4/moe.py`). The cross-rank dispatch/combine stages take `DistributedTensor` window params and use `pld.system.notify` / `pld.system.wait` / `pld.tile.remote_store`. To keep the EP MoE (`moe_ep.py`) consistent with that jit composition style, we want dispatch/combine as `jit.inline` in their own files — impossible today, forcing two divergent authoring styles (jit for single-card, `@pl.program`/`@pl.function` for EP) for conceptually identical kernel composition.

### Proposed API / Behavior

```python
@pl.jit.inline
def dispatch_ep(
    indices: pl.Tensor[[T, TOPK], pl.INT32],
    recv_x: pld.DistributedTensor[[N_LOCAL * RECV_MAX, D], pl.INT8],
    ...
):
    pld.tile.remote_store(x_tile, target=recv_x, peer=dst, offsets=[row, 0])
```

The specializer's annotation classifier (`_is_tensor_annotation`, `pypto/python/pypto/jit/specializer.py:1176`) should recognize the subscripted `pld.DistributedTensor[[...], dtype]` form and route it to the right param kind — the way the `@pl.function` parser already does for InCore methods.

### Alternatives Considered

Author the cross-rank kernels as standalone `@pl.function(type=pl.FunctionType.InCore)` functions in separate files, called as bare cross-function calls from a `@pl.program` orchestration method. This works (verified — compiles end-to-end) but the EP kernels can't share the `jit.inline` style and can't be unit-tested via `run_jit` like single-card `dispatch.py`/`combine.py`.

### Additional Context

- Root cause: `_is_tensor_annotation` only matches `Tensor` (bare/subscripted), not `DistributedTensor`; zero references to `DistributedTensor` under `pypto/python/pypto/jit/`.
- The `@pl.function` parser path already resolves `pld.DistributedTensor` annotations for InCore methods.
- Concrete case: pypto-lib `models/deepseek/v4/{dispatch_ep.py, combine_ep.py, moe_ep.py}`.
- Related: #1127, #1320.
- pypto commit: `e851ba54` (main).

title: [Feature] Host-orchestrator JIT signature to author distributed programs without @pl.program
body:
### Summary

Add a JIT decorator/signature variant for **HOST-level orchestration** so distributed programs can be authored entirely with `@pl.jit` functions instead of a `@pl.program` class. Today the host orchestrator — the function that allocates HCCL windows (`pld.alloc_window_buffer` / `pld.window`), loops `for r in pl.range(pld.world_size())`, and dispatches each rank via `chip_orch(..., device=r)` — can only be a `@pl.function(level=pl.Level.HOST, role=pl.Role.Orchestrator)` method inside a `@pl.program` class. There is no jit equivalent.

### Motivation / Use Case

We're aligning the 2-rank EP MoE (`models/deepseek/v4/moe_ep.py`) with the clean single-card jit composition style (`moe.py`: `@pl.jit.inline` kernels composed by a top-level `@pl.jit`). With #1635 (DistributedTensor params in jit), the **chip-level orchestration** (`chip_orch`) can be expressed as a jit function. But the **host layer** still forces `@pl.program`, so the program can't fully drop the class form. A host-orchestrator jit variant would let the entire distributed program — host loop + chip orchestration + InCore kernels — be authored as jit functions, giving one consistent authoring style for single-card and EP.

### Proposed API / Behavior

A distinct decorator (not the default `@pl.jit` / `@pl.jit.inline`) that carries HOST + Orchestrator semantics and permits window allocation + the `world_size` rank loop + per-rank `device=` dispatch, e.g.:

```python
@pl.jit.host          # or @pl.jit(level=pl.Level.HOST, role=pl.Role.Orchestrator)
def host_orch(... per-rank inputs/outputs ..., layer_id):
    pub_counts_buf = pld.alloc_window_buffer(N_RANKS * N_RANKS * N_LOCAL * 4)
    ...
    for r in pl.range(pld.world_size()):
        pub_counts = pld.window(pub_counts_buf, [...], dtype=pl.INT32)
        ...
        chip_orch(..., pub_counts, ..., layer_id, r, device=r)   # chip_orch is a @pl.jit orchestration fn
```

Key requirements the new signature must support that default jit does not: (1) `pld.alloc_window_buffer` / `pld.window`; (2) `pld.world_size()` and the per-rank loop; (3) the `device=` dispatch kwarg targeting a jit chip-orchestration function.

### Alternatives Considered

Keep `host_orch` (and the enclosing `@pl.program` class) as the only non-jit shell while everything below it is jit — i.e. a thin `@pl.program` that just hosts `host_orch` + bare-calls jit `chip_orch`. This is the current fallback and works, but it means the program can never be fully `@pl.program`-free, so two authoring paradigms persist.

### Additional Context

- Depends on / pairs with **#1635** (DistributedTensor params in jit) — that unblocks `chip_orch`; this unblocks `host_orch`.
- Builds on **#1127** (L3 Distributed Programming Interface RFC).
- Current reference shape: `host_orch` in `models/deepseek/v4/moe_ep.py` (`@pl.function(level=pl.Level.HOST, role=pl.Role.Orchestrator)`).
- pypto commit: `e851ba54` (main).

title: [Bug] tile.slice → col_expand lazy pto.textract materialization can overwrite source tile (dynamic offset)
body:
### Component

Codegen / `tile.slice` lazy subview materialization (`pto.textract`) for `pto.tcolexpandmul` / `pto.tcolexpandadd` consumers

### Summary

When a `tile.slice` view of a **local tile** is consumed by `pl.col_expand_mul` / `pl.col_expand_add`, codegen lazily materializes the subview via `pto.textract ins(source, off) outs(result_target)`. For a **dynamic-offset** slice, `result_target` is the slice's own result buffer, which — because `tile.slice` is `set_output_memory_inherit_input` — falls back to the **source allocation base** (`AllocateMemoryAddr` cannot encode a dynamic offset as a `ConstInt` address, so it uses the bare base). The `pto.textract` therefore writes the extracted row back into **row 0 of the source tile**, corrupting it. This is the same corruption class as #1622, but reached through the lazy `pto.textract` path instead of the eager `pto.tmov` path.

This is **pre-existing**: the `materialize_target_ssa = result_target` registration and the `pto.textract` materialization were introduced in #1217 ("Rewrite tile.slice lowering"). It is independent of #1636 (which removes the *eager* materialization path; the lazy path is unchanged by that PR).

### Why it is not hit today

No model currently chains "**dynamic-offset slice of a local tile** → `col_expand_mul/add` → re-read of the source tile". Real RoPE / MoE call sites slice **GM tensor parameters**, which lower to `tile.load` (a fresh Vec-memory load), not `tile.slice` (subview) — so they never enter the lazy `pto.textract` path. The hazard is latent but one kernel away.

### Minimal trigger (constructed)

```python
import pypto.language as pl

ROWS, COLS = 16, 256

@pl.program
class Trigger:
    @pl.function(type=pl.FunctionType.InCore)
    def kernel(
        self,
        scores: pl.Tensor[[ROWS, COLS], pl.FP32],
        gamma: pl.Tensor[[1, COLS], pl.FP32],
        out_scaled: pl.Out[pl.Tensor[[ROWS, COLS], pl.FP32]],
        out_echo: pl.Out[pl.Tensor[[ROWS, COLS], pl.FP32]],
    ) -> pl.Tensor[[ROWS, COLS], pl.FP32]:
        local: pl.Tile[[ROWS, COLS], pl.FP32] = pl.load(scores, [0, 0], [ROWS, COLS])   # local tile
        gamma_t: pl.Tile[[1, COLS], pl.FP32] = pl.load(gamma, [0, 0], [1, COLS])
        acc: pl.Tile[[ROWS, COLS], pl.FP32] = pl.tile.create(
            [ROWS, COLS], dtype=pl.FP32, target_memory=pl.MemorySpace.Vec
        )
        for r in pl.range(ROWS):
            row: pl.Tile[[1, COLS], pl.FP32] = pl.tile.slice(local, [1, COLS], [r, 0])   # dynamic-offset slice
            scaled: pl.Tile[[1, COLS], pl.FP32] = pl.col_expand_mul(row, gamma_t)         # lazy textract
            acc = pl.tile.assemble(acc, scaled, [r, 0])
        out_scaled = pl.store(acc, [0, 0], out_scaled)
        out_echo = pl.store(local, [0, 0], out_echo)   # re-read local: exposes corruption
        return out_echo
```

### Generated PTO (the bug)

```mlir
%local__ssa_v0 = pto.alloc_tile addr = %c0_i64 ...                 // local @ addr 0
scf.for %r__idx_v0 = 0 to 16 {
  %row__ssa_v0   = pto.alloc_tile addr = %c0_i64 ...               // slice result @ addr 0 == local base (inherited + dynamic offset)
  %slice_view    = pto.subview %local__ssa_v0[%r__idx_v0, 0] sizes [1,256] -> ...
  pto.textract ins(%local__ssa_v0, %r__idx_v0, 0) outs(%row__ssa_v0)   // writes local[r,:] into addr 0 = local row 0
  pto.tcolexpandmul ins(%row__ssa_v0, %gamma_t) outs(%scaled__ssa_v0)
  ...
}
pto.tstore ins(%local__ssa_v0) outs(out_echo)                      // re-reads local; row 0 now = row 15
```

`%row__ssa_v0` shares `addr = %c0_i64` with `%local__ssa_v0`, so each iteration's `pto.textract` overwrites the source's row 0. After the loop, `out_echo` row 0 reads row 15's data.

### Expected Behavior

`col_expand_mul/add` consuming a `tile.slice` must not mutate the slice's source tile. The lazy `pto.textract` materialization must write into a buffer that does **not** inherit / alias the source allocation.

### Proposed fix direction

Materialize the subview operand into a **fresh non-inherited scratch tile** rather than the slice's `result_target` (which inherits source memory). Options:
- give the materialization a dedicated scratch buffer (codegen needs a non-aliased address source, currently absent post-`AllocateMemoryAddr`), or
- at the IR level, ensure a `tile.slice` feeding a materializing consumer (`col_expand_mul/add`) does not inherit source memory for its result buffer.

### Location

- `src/backend/common/pto_ops_common.cpp` — `MaterializeSubviewOperandIfNeeded` (`outs(mat->materialize_target_ssa)`), and the `tile.slice` codegen registering `mat_info.materialize_target_ssa = result_target`.
- Origin: #1217.

### Severity

Medium (latent — no live trigger today; silent data corruption if a kernel writes the trigger pattern).

title: [Bug] PTO codegen elides tile view ops to disconnected same-address alloc_tile, dropping PTOAS PIPE_S→PIPE_V handshake (scatter race)
body:
### Component

Codegen

### Description

PyPTO's PTO kernel emission lowers metadata-only tile **view** ops (`tile.reshape`, `tile.as_layout`, col-major reinterpret) into **separate `pto.alloc_tile` ops that share the same UB address but carry no dataflow edge** back to the producer, instead of threading the producer SSA through a `pto.treshape` view. This severs the SSA def-use chain that PTOAS's dependency analyzer relies on, so a required cross-pipe **`set_flag/wait_flag(PIPE_S, PIPE_V)`** handshake is never emitted. The result is a non-deterministic data race in the generated AICore kernel.

This is the PyPTO-side root cause of the a2a3 column-scatter corruption tracked downstream in simpler issue `hw-native-sys/simpler#967` (investigated in `simpler#969`). simpler PR #878 only shifted binary layout/timing enough to surface a latent race; the missing handshake is emitted (or rather, *not* emitted) here.

**Mechanism, confirmed end-to-end:**

1. The scatter row-offset iota chain is lowered correctly at the IR level — `tile.ci → tile.reshape → tile.muls → tile.row_expand_add`, all threaded through SSA Vars (`src/ir/transforms/op_conversion_registry.cpp:1581-1587`).

2. At PTO emission, `tile.reshape` is **elided to nothing** whenever the per-var alloc model already pre-declared the result var's `alloc_tile` — `src/backend/common/pto_ops_common.cpp:3629-3632`:
   ```cpp
   auto existing_type = codegen.GetSSATileBufType(result_target);
   if (!existing_type.empty() && existing_type == result_type) {
     return std::string("");   // emits no pto.treshape, drops ins(src)
   }
   ```
   `existing_type` and `result_type` both derive from the **result** var's TileType, so they are ~always equal → the `pto.treshape` fallback is effectively dead, and the reshape result becomes a bare same-address `alloc_tile`.

3. The emitted `.pto` therefore has the producer (`pto.tci outs(%scatter_ci_rows)`) and the consumer (`pto.tmuls ins(%scatter_row_base__rm_a0_tmp_v0)`) reading **two distinct `pto.alloc_tile` ops both at `addr = 5152`**, with no view op linking them.

4. PTOAS's `MemoryDependentAnalyzer::MemAlias` for local/UB memory keys on **SSA root-buffer identity** (`GetRealRoot` peels `ViewLikeOpInterface`/cast ops but stops at `alloc_tile`). Two distinct allocs at the same address resolve to different roots → `realRootA != realRootB` → **no dependency** → no sync. The address-range-overlap check exists but is gated behind root identity and is never reached here.

Net effect: TCI (PIPE_S) and TMULS (PIPE_V) touch the same UB bytes with no handshake; TMULS can read stale high lanes of the iota, zeroing the per-row offset for rows 14/15 and collapsing them onto row 0.

### Steps to Reproduce

```bash
# Build, then run the column-scatter ST on a2a3 silicon and save kernels:
pytest tests/st/runtime/ops/test_scatter.py::TestScatterIndexForm::test_scatter_fp16[a2a3] \
  --save-kernels --kernels-dir /tmp/scatter_repro
```

1. Inspect the saved `ptoas/main_incore_0.pto`: the row-offset iota chain emits multiple `pto.alloc_tile addr = %c5152_i64` for `scatter_ci_rows` / `scatter_row_arange` / `scatter_row_base__rm_a0_tmp_v0` / `scatter_row_base`, with **no `pto.treshape`** linking them.
2. Inspect the PTOAS-emitted `ptoas/main_incore_0.cpp`: between `TCI(...)` (PIPE_S) and `TMULS(...)` (PIPE_V) over the shared buffer there is only a no-op `pipe_barrier(PIPE_V)` — no `set_flag/wait_flag(PIPE_S, PIPE_V)` pair.
3. On a2a3 the test corrupts intermittently (`val[14,*]`/`val[15,*]` land at row 0); manually inserting `set_flag(PIPE_S,PIPE_V)/wait_flag` after the `TCI` makes it pass deterministically (verified in simpler#969).

### Expected Behavior

The view chain should preserve the SSA dataflow edge so PTOAS sees the cross-pipe RAW and emits the `set_flag/wait_flag(PIPE_S, PIPE_V)` handshake. Concretely, `tile.reshape` / `tile.as_layout` should emit a `pto.treshape %src` (`ViewLikeOpInterface`, `getViewSource()=src`) that PTOAS's `GetRealRoot` can peel back to the producer's `alloc_tile`, restoring root identity — rather than a disconnected same-address `alloc_tile`.

### Actual Behavior

`tile.reshape` (and the col-major reinterpret) are elided to bare same-address `pto.alloc_tile` ops with no `ins(src)`. PTOAS finds distinct SSA roots, infers no dependency, and omits the handshake. The generated kernel races, corrupting the high rows of the scatter output non-deterministically.

### Git Commit ID

a09f425138b10e29c314a1b71df4468260401ee1

### NPU Kind

Ascend 910B

### Host Platform

Linux (aarch64)

### Additional Context

**Suggested fix (PyPTO side, primary):** stop eliding view ops to disconnected allocs — always emit `pto.treshape %src` for `tile.reshape` (guard/remove the early-return at `pto_ops_common.cpp:3629-3632`, route through the existing treshape fallback) and add view-result vars to the alloc skip set (`src/codegen/pto/pto_codegen.cpp:1324-1326`, mirroring tpop/scatter-alias) to avoid orphan allocs. The whole chain must be threaded: the `.pto` has ~4 view break points (reshape, the row-major reinterpret before `tmuls`, the col-major reinterpret `scatter_row_base` before `row_expand_add`), each from a metadata view that is currently elided — all must emit `treshape`/view ops or any remaining break re-severs the root.

**Alternative (PTOAS side, defense-in-depth):** make `MemAlias` for local memory fall back to address-range overlap when SSA roots differ but both accesses have concrete overlapping `baseAddresses`. Needs careful evaluation against intentional address reuse (disjoint-lifetime allocs sharing an address).

Related: #1475 (MemoryReuse same-address cross-pipe WAR hazards), #1640 (tile view materialization writing to the wrong address). Downstream: simpler#967, simpler#969.

title: [RFC] Unify pl.spmd with pl.parallel + pl.at to avoid re-indentation when switching dispatch
body:
### Summary

`pl.parallel` + `pl.at` and `pl.spmd` express the same intent — dispatch independent work blocks across cores, each block running an InCore region — but with different *nesting depth*. `pl.parallel` + `pl.at` is two indentation levels (the `with pl.at` wraps the body); `pl.spmd` is one (the body is implicitly InCore and an explicit `pl.at` is currently disallowed). Because of this, every time we convert a `pl.parallel`+`pl.at` block to `pl.spmd` (or back), we must re-indent the entire loop body. This proposes letting the two forms share the same structure so switching the dispatch model is a one-line change to the `for`/`with` header, not a whole-body re-indent.

### Motivation

Switching a region between `pl.parallel`+`pl.at` and `pl.spmd` is a routine operation during kernel development (e.g. when a per-core parallel region needs SPMD dispatch for block-index addressing, or when profiling pushes us one way or the other). Today the two forms differ in nesting depth:

**Before — `pl.parallel` + `pl.at` (two levels):**
```python
for b0 in pl.parallel(0, batch_padded, BATCH_TILE):
    with pl.at(level=pl.Level.CORE_GROUP, name_hint="rmsnorm"):
        x = pl.slice(inp, [b0, 0], [BATCH_TILE, HIDDEN])
        y = pl.rmsnorm(x, gamma)
        pl.assemble(out, y, [b0, 0])
```

**After — `pl.spmd` (one level; whole body re-indented):**
```python
for b0 in pl.spmd(BATCH_BLOCKS, name_hint="rmsnorm"):
    x = pl.slice(inp, [b0, 0], [BATCH_TILE, HIDDEN])
    y = pl.rmsnorm(x, gamma)
    pl.assemble(out, y, [b0, 0])
```

The compute body is byte-for-byte identical, yet the diff touches every line because the `with pl.at` wrapper disappeared. This produces noisy diffs, error-prone manual re-indentation, and merge friction — for a change that is semantically just "use SPMD dispatch for this region."

### Design

Two candidate designs, presented as open options for discussion. Both reduce a dispatch switch to a header-only diff; neither moves the compute body or its indentation.

**Option A: allow an explicit `pl.at` inside a `pl.spmd` body.**

Today the rule is "No surrounding `pl.at` is needed or allowed" inside `pl.spmd`. Relax it so a single `with pl.at(level=pl.Level.CORE_GROUP, ...)` directly inside the `pl.spmd` loop body is *permitted* and simply marks the InCore region that `pl.spmd` already creates implicitly (the `pl.at` becomes the explicit handle for that region rather than a second, nested one). The structure then matches `pl.parallel`+`pl.at` exactly:

```python
# parallel form
for b0 in pl.parallel(0, batch_padded, BATCH_TILE):
    with pl.at(level=pl.Level.CORE_GROUP, name_hint="rmsnorm"):
        body            # unchanged

# spmd form — identical body & indentation, only the `for` header changed
for b0 in pl.spmd(BATCH_BLOCKS, name_hint="rmsnorm"):
    with pl.at(level=pl.Level.CORE_GROUP, name_hint="rmsnorm"):
        body            # unchanged
```

Converting between the two becomes a one-line edit of the `for` header; the body and its indentation never move. The bare (no-`pl.at`) `pl.spmd` form stays valid for brevity. This adds the least new surface — it only relaxes an existing restriction and reuses `pl.at`'s existing `name_hint`/`level` arguments — and keeps `pl.spmd` as the construct that owns SPMD semantics (block-index binding, `sync_start`, outlining).

**Option B: a `dispatch=` kwarg on `pl.at`.**

Keep `pl.parallel` as the outer loop and select the InCore dispatch model on the `pl.at`:

```python
for b0 in pl.parallel(0, batch_padded, BATCH_TILE):
    with pl.at(level=pl.Level.CORE_GROUP, dispatch=pl.Dispatch.SPMD, name_hint="rmsnorm"):
        body
```

`dispatch=pl.Dispatch.PARALLEL` (default) lowers as today; `dispatch=pl.Dispatch.SPMD` lowers the region to an SPMD-outlined function with the loop variable bound to the block index. Switching is a single kwarg; the two-level structure is preserved for both modes. This keeps a single outer-loop spelling but overloads `pl.parallel`'s loop-variable semantics depending on the `dispatch` mode.

### Alternatives Considered

- **Status quo + editor auto-indent.** Doesn't address noisy diffs or the conceptual asymmetry, and still requires manual fix-ups when the body has nested blocks.
- **A separate sugar macro** that expands to either form. Adds a third spelling for the same concept; worsens rather than reduces cognitive load. The existing `pl.parallel(..., chunk=N)` sugar shows the project already favors collapsing these patterns, but it goes the opposite direction (hides `pl.at`); this RFC instead makes the explicit forms structurally interchangeable.

### Open Questions

- Under Option A, when both `pl.spmd(name_hint=...)` and the inner `pl.at(name_hint=...)` carry a `name_hint`, which wins for the outlined-function label? (One possibility: `pl.at`'s if present, else `pl.spmd`'s.)
- Should an explicit `pl.at` inside `pl.spmd` be allowed only as the *sole* top-level statement of the body (mirroring the context-manager form), or anywhere?
- For Option B, does binding the `pl.parallel` loop variable to a block index under `dispatch=SPMD` conflict with `pl.parallel`'s documented "iterations may be split/reordered" contract?

title: [Bug] vec-produced GM tensor used as matmul RIGHT operand in a later scope is not dependency-ordered (intermittent reads of zero-init data)
body:
### Component

Codegen — IR dependency tracking / task scheduler (missing producer → matmul-RHS edge)

### Description

A GM tensor produced by a **vector** scope and then consumed as the **right operand (B / weight matrix)** of a `pl.matmul` in a **later scope** is not reliably dependency-ordered. The matmul intermittently executes before the producing scope's store completes, reading the still **zero-initialized** tensor, which yields non-deterministic wrong results.

Passing the *same* tensor as a kernel input (i.e. no in-kernel producer) always passes. This isolates the missing dependency edge to the **vec-producer → matmul-RHS** path. It reproduces with a single-task `CORE_GROUP` matmul consumer (not SPMD), so it is not about many concurrent readers. Likely shares a root cause with #1503 (dependency-edge gap) but is more general: any vec-produced tensor used as a matmul right operand.

### Steps to Reproduce

Self-contained kernel, run on `-p a2a3` (real device) ~3 times:

```python
import pypto.language as pl

M, K, N = 128, 64, 64

@pl.jit
def rhs_race_test(
    a: pl.Tensor[[M, K], pl.BF16],
    w_param: pl.Tensor[[K, N], pl.BF16],
    out_inkernel: pl.Out[pl.Tensor[[M, N], pl.FP32]],
    out_param: pl.Out[pl.Tensor[[M, N], pl.FP32]],
):
    # Build identity W in-kernel via vector ops (arange + cmp + cast)
    w_build = pl.create_tensor([K, N], dtype=pl.BF16)
    with pl.at(level=pl.Level.CORE_GROUP, name_hint="build_w"):
        ones = pl.full([K, N], dtype=pl.FP32, value=1.0)
        col = pl.col_expand_mul(ones, pl.cast(pl.arange(0, [1, N], dtype=pl.INT32), target_type=pl.FP32))
        row = pl.cast(pl.reshape(pl.arange(0, [1, K], dtype=pl.INT32), [K, 1]), target_type=pl.FP32)
        w_build[:, :] = pl.cast(pl.cmp(col, pl.row_expand_mul(ones, row), cmp_type=0), target_type=pl.BF16)
    # Consume W as matmul RIGHT operand in a SEPARATE scope -> intermittently wrong
    with pl.at(level=pl.Level.CORE_GROUP, name_hint="mm_inkernel"):
        out_inkernel[:, :] = pl.matmul(a[:, :], w_build[:, :], out_dtype=pl.FP32)
    # Control: same matmul, but W is a kernel input (no producer) -> always correct
    with pl.at(level=pl.Level.CORE_GROUP, name_hint="mm_param"):
        out_param[:, :] = pl.matmul(a[:, :], w_param[:, :], out_dtype=pl.FP32)
    return out_inkernel, out_param
```

Driver: `a` = random BF16 `[128, 64]`; `w_param` = identity `[64, 64]`. Since `W = I`, both outputs must equal `a`. Run 3 times.

### Expected Behavior

`out_inkernel == out_param == a` on every run. The `build_w` → `mm_inkernel` dependency should force the vector store of `w_build` to complete before the matmul reads it.

### Actual Behavior

`out_param` PASSes on every run; `out_inkernel` is **non-deterministic** (observed PASS / FAIL / PASS over 3 consecutive runs). On a failing run the mismatches are `actual=0.0, expected=<nonzero>` (e.g. `[55] actual=0.0 expected=0.126953125`), ~127/8192 elements — i.e. the matmul read `w_build` before it was written (zero-initialized memory).

The same pattern caused an in-kernel-select matmul RoPE in pypto-lib (`decode_qkv_proj_rope.py`) to fail ~1–2% of elements standalone and ~79% end-to-end (attention amplifies the q/kv error), with the error ratio varying run-to-run.

### Environment

| Component | Version |
|---|---|
| pypto | `f9ad3fa0` (branch `main`) |
| pypto runtime (submodule) | `324df3d6` |
| pto-isa | `8bd3ac8f` |
| ptoas | `0.43` |
| pypto-lib (repro driver) | `a64563c` |
| CANN | not detected |

### Host Platform

Linux (aarch64). NPU: a2a3 (real device, `--device auto`).

### Additional Context

Related: #1503 (dependency-edge gap, narrower MoE fan-in case). Full driver lives in pypto-lib at `models/deepseek/v4/_tmp_rhs_race.py`.

title: [Bug] ptoas rejects pto.tmov (non-mat, mismatched src/dst shapes) when slicing sub-columns of a matmul output's vec epilogue
body:
### Diagnosis

**pypto** (PTO codegen / subview materialization). ptoas correctly rejects a malformed `pto.tmov` that pypto emits: when a sub-column slice of a cube (matmul) output — after a vec epilogue lands it in Vec ND — is materialized, pypto allocates the destination tile with **unset** `valid_shape` (`v_row=?, v_col=?`) while the source subview carries `v_row=16, v_col=8`. A non-mat `tmov` requires matching src/dst shapes, so ptoas (correctly) fails.

This is the same family as #1507 (cube→vec bridge drops `valid_shape`) / #1535 (subview valid_shape inference) / #1505 (broadcast op valid_shape propagation): those fix the subview's *own* valid_shape, but the **spill/materialization copy still mismatches** on this path.

### Description

Slicing sub-columns of a matmul result that has been brought into Vec ND by a vector epilogue fails ptoas codegen. Minimal repro (a2a3 real device):

```python
import pypto.language as pl

M, K, N, SUB = 16, 128, 32, 8

@pl.jit
def repro(
    x: pl.Tensor[[M, K], pl.BF16],
    w: pl.Tensor[[N, K], pl.FP32],
    out: pl.Out[pl.Tensor[[M, SUB], pl.FP32]],
):
    for ob in pl.spmd(1, name_hint="cube_slice"):
        x_f   = pl.cast(x[0:M, 0:K], target_type=pl.FP32)
        w_s   = pl.slice(w, [N, K], [0, 0], valid_shape=[24, K])
        acc   = pl.matmul(x_f, w_s, b_trans=True, out_dtype=pl.FP32)  # [M,N] cube/L0C
        acc_nd = pl.mul(acc, 1.0)                # vec epilogue: land cube output in Vec ND
        sub    = pl.mul(acc_nd[0:M, 0:SUB], 2.0) # <-- in-place sub-column slice -> fails
        out[0:M, 0:SUB] = sub
    return out
```

**Result:**
```
ptoas compilation failed: error: 'pto.tmov' op expects A2/A3 non-mat tmov to use matching src/dst shapes
```

**Generated `.pto` (the offending tmov):**
```
%342 = pto.subview %115[0,0] sizes [16,8] : tile<...rows=16,cols=32...> -> tile<...rows=16,cols=8, v_row=16, v_col=8...>
pto.tmov ins(%342 : ...v_row=16, v_col=8) outs(%116 : ...v_row=?, v_col=?)   # <-- dst valid_shape unset -> mismatch
```

The subview `%342` correctly carries `v_row=16, v_col=8` (so #1535 is working), but the destination `alloc_tile %116` that the materialization copies into has `v_row=?, v_col=?`, and ptoas rejects the shape mismatch. The fix should either propagate the subview's `valid_shape` onto the materialization target, or avoid emitting the materializing `tmov` (let the consumer read the subview directly).

Origin: trying to fuse `models/deepseek/v4/hc_pre.py` into one spmd — slicing the `mixes` (matmul → `row_expand_mul`) result in place for the pre/post/comb split. The workaround is the existing GM bridge (spill `mixes` to GM, reload sub-ranges with `pl.load`).

Notes for minimizing (two *unrelated* errors mask this one if not avoided):
- A `[M,1]` FP32 tile (4B row) trips `alloc_tile` 32B-row-alignment first → use a scalar `pl.mul(acc, 1.0)` as the epilogue, not a `[M,1]` operand.
- Slicing the **boxed/L0C** matmul output directly trips `boxed tile cols must be multiple of innerCols(16)` → the vec epilogue (to Vec ND) + slice width ≥ 8 (32B) is required to expose the `tmov` bug cleanly.

### Environment

| Component | Version |
|---|---|
| pypto-lib | `a64563c` (branch: `perf/dsv4-decode-attention-csa`) |
| pypto | `f9ad3fa0` (branch: `main`) |
| pypto runtime (submodule) | `324df3d6` |
| pto-isa | `8bd3ac8f` |
| ptoas | `0.43` |
| CANN | `9.0.0` |

### Host Platform

Linux (aarch64)

### Additional Context

Related: #1507, #1535, #1505. Full standalone repro: `models/deepseek/v4/repro_hc_pre_blocker1_cube_slice_tmov.py` (pypto-lib) — attaching to this issue.

title: [Bug] AICPU scheduler deadlock (507018) when one fanned-out spmd scope both writes and reads the same GM scratch (intra-scope self-RAW)
body:
### Diagnosis

**pypto runtime / simpler scheduler** (intra-scope dependency scheduling). A single fanned-out `pl.spmd` scope that **both writes and reads the same GM scratch tensor** compiles to a legal, acyclic orchestrator program but **deadlocks at runtime** with `507018`. The emitted orch DAG is acyclic and GM dependencies are tracked at **whole-tensor** granularity, so the read-side fan-out units depend on *all* write-side units; under limited core co-residency the units wait on each other and the AICPU scheduler deadlocks. pypto is only an enabler (it permits such a scope); the failure is a runtime scheduling deadlock, not a codegen error, not ptoas/pto-isa, not hardware.

### Description

Within one `pl.spmd` scope, storing to a GM scratch and later reading it back (here via tensor-subscript + `pl.transpose`) deadlocks:

```
aclrtSynchronizeStreamWithTimeout (AICPU) failed: 507018
PTO2 runtime failed: orch_error_code=0 sched_error_code=100 runtime_status=-100
RuntimeError: run_prepared failed with code 507018
```

The deadlocking kernel is `models/deepseek/v4/hc_pre.py` fused into 3 spmd scopes; the offending **scope 2** does (per 16-row tile):

```python
mixes_gm   = pl.create_tensor([T, MIX_PAD], pl.FP32)   # written by scope 1 (matmul)
pre_val_gm = pl.create_tensor([T, HC_PAD],  pl.FP32)   # scratch

for ob in pl.spmd(T // TILE, name_hint="hc_post"):     # scope 2
    t0 = ob * TILE
    # pre: read mixes_gm, compute, WRITE pre_val_gm
    pre_in = pl.load(mixes_gm, [t0, 0], [TILE, HC_PAD], target_memory=pl.MemorySpace.Vec)
    ...
    pl.store(pl.add(pre_sig, HC_EPS), [t0, 0], pre_val_gm)   # write scratch
    # post: read mixes_gm, write `post`
    ...
    # mix_x: READ the just-written pre_val_gm (same task), transpose, write x_mixed
    pre_tile   = pre_val_gm[t0:t0 + TILE, 0:HC_PAD]          # <-- self read-after-write
    pre_tile_t = pl.transpose(pre_tile, axis1=0, axis2=1)
    ... pl.row_expand_mul(x, pre_k) -> x_mixed_view[...] ...
```

**Splitting `mix_x` into its own 4th spmd scope (so no scope reads a scratch it wrote) runs the identical data flow and passes precision** — i.e. the GM round-trip is valid; only the intra-scope self-RAW is fatal.

### Evidence (which layer)

- **Orchestrator DAG is acyclic.** With `--enable-dep-gen` on the *working* 4-spmd variant, `deps.json` has 1 task per spmd scope and only forward edges (`pred < succ`). The deadlocking 3-spmd compiles (static IR `MaterializeRuntimeScopes`) to a legal sequential program: `mixes_gm = hc_pre_spmd(); x_mixed = hc_post_spmd(); hc_comb_spmd()`. So this is **not** a pypto graph-construction cycle.
- **GM deps are whole-tensor granularity.** Every GM arg in `deps.json` has `start_offset=0` + full shape (even the per-tile-accessed `mixes_gm[128,32]` / `pre_val_gm[128,8]`); per-tile sub-ranges are internal to the kernel and invisible to the scheduler. So a scope that is `INOUT` on `pre_val_gm` forces every read-unit to wait on every write-unit across the whole tensor.
- `deps.json` is **not** flushed when the run deadlocks (killed before dump), so it can only be captured on the working variant.

### Isolation

- A standalone single-task store-then-`pl.load` of a GM scratch (same rows): **passes** (no deadlock).
- Standalone store-then-(tensor-subscript + `pl.transpose`) read of a GM scratch: **passes**.
- The deadlock needs the fuller scope: cross-scope `mixes_gm` read + self-written `pre_val_gm` + the `post` store + the `mix_x` transpose, all in one fanned-out spmd task. (So a *truly minimal* self-RAW does not reproduce — the full repro kernel is required.)

### Asks

1. Handle an intra-scope self-RAW on a GM tensor correctly (disambiguate by `start_offset`/`shape` so a fan-out unit only depends on its own write, or serialize without deadlock) — rather than deadlocking.
2. Failing that, emit a compile-time diagnostic instead of compiling clean and deadlocking at runtime.

### Environment

| Component | Version |
|---|---|
