| pypto-lib | `a64563c` (branch: `perf/dsv4-decode-attention-csa`) |
| pypto | `f9ad3fa0` (branch: `main`) |
| pypto runtime (submodule) | `324df3d6` |
| pto-isa | `8bd3ac8f` |
| ptoas | `0.43` |
| CANN | `9.0.0` |

### Host Platform

Linux (aarch64)

### Additional Context

Related: #1592 — same `507018` symptom, but a **different trigger** (that was a cube+vec `CORE_GROUP` mix with a **dynamic-address** GM scatter, now closed/resolved). This one is a **pure-vec `pl.spmd`** scope with **static-offset** self-RAW, and reproduces on current `main` (`f9ad3fa0`). Full repro: `models/deepseek/v4/repro_hc_pre_blocker2_selfraw_507018.py` (3-spmd deadlocks; the 4-spmd `hc_pre_fused_draft.py` passes) — attaching to this issue.

title: [Bug] FlattenTileNdTo2D: standalone N-D tile.transpose fails — auto tmp flattened to 2D while transpose input stays N-D (tmp rank != input rank)
body:
### Component

Codegen — IR pass `FlattenTileNdTo2D` (`src/ir/transforms/flatten_tile_nd_to_2d_pass.cpp`)

### Description

A **standalone** N-D `tile.transpose` (transpose of the last two axes of a 3D+ tile, with leading batch dims) fails to compile. This is exactly the primitive needed to de-interleave columns for an interleaved RoPE the way the pypto2.0 frontend does it (`reshape [T, d] -> [T, d/2, 2] -> transpose(1,2) -> [T, 2, d/2] -> [T, d]`), so without it the only way to express de-/re-interleave on this stack is the much slower `pl.gather`/`pl.tensor.scatter` mask path.

**Root cause (traced):**
- The frontend auto-allocates the transpose scratch tile correctly at **input rank** — `python/pypto/ir/op/tile_ops.py:2223`: `tmp = create(list(input_type.shape), ...)` → a 3D input gets a 3D tmp.
- In `FlattenTileNdTo2D`, the `tile.create`/`tile.full` handler (`flatten_tile_nd_to_2d_pass.cpp:1718`) flattens that 3D tmp down to **2D**.
- But there is **no handler for a standalone `tile.transpose`** — the pass only special-cases transpose when it is a `tile.batch_matmul` operand (`flatten_tile_nd_to_2d_pass.cpp:1799`). A plain transpose falls through to the generic "substitute args + re-create" path, which leaves its **input 3D**.
- The re-created `tile.transpose` is then re-verified with **input rank 3 but tmp rank 2**, tripping the CHECK in `DeduceTileTransposeType` (`src/ir/op/tile_ops/transform.cpp:335`).

### Steps to Reproduce

Self-contained kernel (`-p a2a3`), fails at compile (in `run_passes`):

```python
import pypto.language as pl

T, RD = 128, 64
RH = RD // 2

@pl.jit
def nd_transpose_test(
    x: pl.Tensor[[T, RD], pl.FP32],
    even_out: pl.Out[pl.Tensor[[T, RH], pl.FP32]],
    odd_out: pl.Out[pl.Tensor[[T, RH], pl.FP32]],
):
    with pl.at(level=pl.Level.CORE_GROUP, name_hint="deint"):
        x3d = pl.reshape(x, [T, RH, 2])
        x3d_t = pl.transpose(x3d, axis1=1, axis2=2)   # 3D transpose of last two axes
        x_deint = pl.reshape(x3d_t, [T, RD])
        even_out[:, :] = x_deint[:, :RH]
        odd_out[:, :] = x_deint[:, RH:RD]
    return even_out, odd_out
```

Driver: `x = arange(T*RD).reshape(T, RD)`; expect `even_out = x[:, 0::2]`, `odd_out = x[:, 1::2]`.

### Expected Behavior

The N-D transpose compiles: `FlattenTileNdTo2D` lowers `[T, RH, 2] transpose(1,2)` to a batched 2D `pto.ttrans` (`[RH,2] -> [2,RH]` with `T` merged into the partition/outer), allocating a matching **2D** tmp so input and tmp ranks stay consistent. Result de-interleaves the columns.

### Actual Behavior

Compile aborts in `FlattenTileNdTo2D`:

```
ValueError: tile.transpose: tmp rank must match input rank, got input rank=3 tmp rank=2
Check failed: input_type->shape_.size() == tmp_type->shape_.size()
  at src/ir/op/tile_ops/transform.cpp:335
C++ Traceback:
  ... src/ir/transforms/flatten_tile_nd_to_2d_pass.cpp:1870
  ... src/ir/transforms/flatten_tile_nd_to_2d_pass.cpp:1833
```

(Reproduces both when the reshape/transpose are written at tile level and at tensor level — tensor-level `pl.transpose` also lowers to `tile.transpose` and hits the same pass.)

### Suggested Fix

Add a dedicated `tile.transpose` handler in `FlattenTileNdTo2D` (next to the `tile.load`/`tile.store`/`tile.sum`/`tile.batch_matmul` handlers around `:1799`) for the common "last-two-axes transpose with leading batch dims" case:
- merge leading batch dims into the partition/outer dim (mirror the `tile.batch_matmul` handler at `:1778`),
- emit a batched 2D `pto.ttrans` of the inner `[A,B] -> [B,A]`,
- flatten the tmp to the matching **2D** `[A,B]` so input/tmp ranks agree.

`MakeTileTransposeCodegenPTO` (`src/backend/common/pto_ops_common.cpp:480`) already emits a 2D `pto.ttrans`; it likely needs the batch-loop emission mirrored from batch_matmul codegen. Transposes that involve a batch axis (e.g. `transpose(0,1)` on 3D) can be rejected with a clear error for now.

### Environment

| Component | Version |
|---|---|
| pypto | `f9ad3fa0` (branch `main`) |
| pypto runtime (submodule) | `324df3d6` |
| pto-isa | `8bd3ac8f` |
| ptoas | `0.43` |
| pypto-lib (repro driver) | `a64563c` |
| CANN | not detected |

### Host Platform

Linux (aarch64). Fails at compile time (IR pass) — not hardware-specific.

### Additional Context

Related: #1578, #1349 (both touch `FlattenTileNdTo2D` / N-D handling, but for dynamic dims and rank-reducing slices respectively — not the standalone-transpose tmp-rank gap). Unblocking this enables a scatter-free, matmul-free interleaved RoPE on the `pl` frontend (the pypto2.0 `models/deepseek_v4` rope approach). Full driver in pypto-lib at `models/deepseek/v4/_tmp_nd_transpose.py`.

title: [Feature] Dispatch @pl.jit.host distributed kernels end-to-end via the JIT runtime
body:
### Summary

A `@pl.jit.host` host-orchestrator kernel — per-rank dispatch of a `@pl.jit` chip
orchestrator over `pld.window` buffers — can be **specialized and compiled** today
(thanks to #1638 DistributedTensor params + #1645 `@pl.jit.host`), but it cannot be
**run end-to-end through the JIT runtime**:

1. There is no way for a JIT caller to supply a `distributed_config`. `JITFunction.__call__` / `_resolve_compiled` derive `ir.compile()` kwargs only from a `RunConfig` (`_run_config_compile_kwargs`), and `RunConfig` has no `distributed_config` field. (`JITFunction._compile` *does* forward `**ir_compile_kwargs` verbatim to `ir.compile()`, so the plumbing only needs a caller-facing entry point.)
2. The post-compile path does not recognize or dispatch a `DistributedCompiledProgram`. An L3 HOST orchestrator has no top-level `kernel_config.py`, so the normal `execute_compiled` / runner path cannot drive it — it must be invoked as a per-rank callable with a `pypto.runtime.RunConfig`.

This is exactly the runtime follow-up that #1645 deferred:

> Runtime distributed dispatch (plumbing `distributed_config` through `JITFunction._compile` so a host-orchestrator jit kernel can be executed end-to-end) is **out of scope** here and tracked as follow-up. The parser, IR pipeline, and `ir.compile()` already accept the generated source; the JIT runtime side just needs a way for the user to specify `distributed_config` (likely through `RunConfig`).

### Motivation / Use Case

We refactored `pypto-lib`'s `models/deepseek/v4/moe_ep.py` (2-rank EP MoE) from the
`@pl.program` class form to the `@pl.jit` family: a `@pl.jit` chip orchestrator
`moe_ep`, a `@pl.jit.host` driver `host_orch`, plus `@pl.jit.incore` dispatch/combine
and `@pl.jit.inline` compute deps. Specialization + `ir.compile(distributed_config=...)`
succeed and the kernel validates on 2 NPUs — but only via a **private-API workaround**,
because there is no supported way to run a host-orchestrator JIT kernel.

Current workaround (in `moe_ep.py`'s test harness):

```python
# run_jit() can't dispatch an L3 host orchestrator (uses _execute_via_runner,
# which needs a top-level kernel_config.py). So we stop at the specialized
# ir.Program and hand it to the @pl.program-style run() path instead.
program = host_orch._compile_to_program(   # test-only private API
    tensor_meta, scalar_values, scalar_dtypes, dynamic_dims, pl,
)
run(program=program, compile_cfg=dict(distributed_config=DistributedConfig(...)))
```

`host_orch._compile_to_program(...)` is documented "intended for testing only", and the
caller must hand-replay the `_bind_args` prelude. Closing this gap removes the workaround
and makes `@pl.jit.host` a first-class, runnable authoring form (the stated goal of #1645).

### Proposed API / Behavior

Let the JIT caller specify a `distributed_config` (per #1645's own suggestion, likely a
new `RunConfig.distributed_config` field forwarded through `_run_config_compile_kwargs`
→ `ir.compile()`), and have the post-compile path recognize a `DistributedCompiledProgram`
and route it through the L3 per-rank dispatch instead of `execute_compiled`:

```python
from pypto.runtime import RunConfig

# host_orch is a @pl.jit.host kernel; today this cannot run end-to-end.
host_orch(
    *args,
    config=RunConfig(platform="a2a3", distributed_config=DistributedConfig(device_ids=[0, 1])),
)
# JITFunction.__call__ detects the DistributedCompiledProgram and dispatches per-rank,
# the same way golden run()'s _try_l3_dispatch already does for @pl.program L3 programs.
```

### Alternatives Considered

- **Bridge through `run(program=...)`** (current workaround): call the test-only
  `host_orch._compile_to_program(...)` to get a parsed `ir.Program`, then feed the
  existing `@pl.program` `run()` path (whose `_try_l3_dispatch` already handles
  `DistributedCompiledProgram`). Works, but depends on private API and a hand-rolled
  `_bind_args` prelude — not a supported user-facing flow.
- **Keep `@pl.program` for distributed kernels** — defeats the purpose of #1638/#1645,
  which exist to let distributed programs be authored entirely with `@pl.jit`.

### Additional Context

- Precursors (both merged): #1638 (recognize `pld.DistributedTensor` params in `@pl.jit` / `@pl.jit.inline`), #1645 (add `@pl.jit.host`).
- A companion PR fixes three **specializer** correctness gaps surfaced by the same refactor (per-rank subscript-arg metadata `chip_orch(x[r], ...)`, `pld.window(...)` local metadata, and body-level annotation constant inlining). Those are independent of this runtime-dispatch request and are filed separately as a PR.
- Reference end-to-end consumer: `pypto-lib` `models/deepseek/v4/moe_ep.py`.

title: [Pass Bug] DeriveCallDirections marks a pld.tile.remote_store target as input, so a window write->read across kernels isn't ordered
body:
### Pass Name

DeriveCallDirections

### Description

A kernel that fills a distributed window via `pld.tile.remote_store(..., peer=dst)` (plus a cross-rank barrier) is **not** scheduled before a later kernel that reads that same window.

`DeriveCallDirections` classifies the `remote_store` **target** as `pl.adir.input`: the write lands on a *peer's* copy of the window, so from local dataflow the param looks read-only. The producing kernel is therefore never seen as a producer of the window. A downstream reader (also `input`) gets no producer→consumer (RAW) edge, the two tasks run concurrently, and the reader races on an unfilled window → silent, non-deterministic wrong results.

### Git Commit ID

`89698531`

### Before IR (Input)

```python
# Minimal @pl.program shape. Real trigger: dsv4 models/deepseek/v4/moe_ep.py
# EP-MoE, where the cross-rank `combine` is split into a push+barrier InCore
# kernel and a separate local-reduce kernel that reads the routed_y_buf window.
import pypto.language as pl
import pypto.language.distributed as pld

@pl.program
class Repro:
    @pl.function(type=pl.FunctionType.InCore)          # writer: cross-rank push + barrier
    def push_step(self, src: pl.Tensor[[N, D], pl.BF16],
                  win: pld.DistributedTensor[[N, D], pl.BF16],
                  done: pld.DistributedTensor[[R, 1], pl.INT32],
                  my_rank: pl.Scalar[pl.INT32]):
        # ... pld.tile.remote_store(tile, win, peer=dst, offsets=[r, 0]) ...
        # ... pld.system.notify / pld.system.wait  (cross-rank barrier) ...
        ...

    @pl.function(type=pl.FunctionType.Inline)           # reader: local read of the filled window
    def read_step(self, win: pld.DistributedTensor[[N, D], pl.BF16],
                  out: pl.Tensor[[N, D], pl.BF16]):
        # ... pl.load(win, [r, 0], [1, D]) -> out ...
        ...

    @pl.function(type=pl.FunctionType.Orchestration)
    def chip(self, src, win, done, out, my_rank):
        self.push_step(src, win, done, my_rank)
        self.read_step(win, out)        # must run AFTER push_step's barrier fills `win`
```

### Expected IR (After Transformation)

```python
# push_step's `win` (the remote_store target) should be classified output/inout,
# so the orchestration emits a producer->consumer edge and read_step is ordered
# AFTER push_step:
self.push_step(src, win, done, my_rank,
    attrs={"arg_directions": [pl.adir.input, pl.adir.output, pl.adir.inout, pl.adir.scalar]})
#                                            ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^ win produced here
self.read_step(win, out,
    attrs={"arg_directions": [pl.adir.input, pl.adir.inout]})
#                            ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^ RAW on win -> read_step ordered after push_step
```

### Actual IR or Error

Real excerpt from `passes_dump/35_after_DeriveCallDirections.py` (dsv4 moe_ep
compile, `python models/deepseek/v4/moe_ep.py -p a2a3 -d 0,1 --compile-only`):

```
# inside combine_ep, the window `routed_y_buf` is ONLY ever a remote_store target:
pld.tile.remote_store(y_tile__ssa_v0, routed_y_buf__ssa_v0, dst__idx_v0, [r_route__tile, 0])

# orchestration (moe_ep) — both calls mark routed_y_buf as `input`, so no edge:
self.combine_ep(
    recv_y, recv_r_route_out, pub_counts, routed_y_buf, combine_done, my_rank,
    attrs={"arg_directions": [input, input, input, input, input, scalar]},
)                          # routed_y_buf (4th) = input  <-- should be output/inout
self.comb_reduce_spmd(sh, routed_y_buf, ffn_out_flat,
    attrs={"arg_directions": [input, input, inout]})   # routed_y_buf = input (read)

# Both `input` -> no producer -> reduce is not ordered after the push -> race.
```

### NPU Kind (if relevant)

N/A (not hardware-specific) — the wrong `arg_directions` is visible at `--compile-only`; the resulting race manifests on Ascend 910B.

### Host Platform (if relevant)

N/A (not hardware-specific)

### Additional Context

On 2x Ascend 910B the split EP-MoE combine produces `x_next` ~97.9% wrong (`ratio_reldiff`), with values varying run-to-run and `actual ≈ sh` (the routed contributions are missing) — consistent with the reduce reading an unfilled window.

**Workaround:** keep the window write (push + barrier) and the window read in the **same** InCore function — sequential statements in one InCore body are ordered, so the bug only appears once they are split into separate kernels (which is required to parallelize the reduce with `pl.spmd`, since `pl.spmd`/`pl.parallel` aren't valid inside an InCore body).

A host-backed "sync" token (output of the writer, input of the reader) did **not** help when the reader was `@pl.jit.inline` (it is spliced, not a separate task, so the dep wasn't carried); and fundamentally the writer is not recognized as a producer of the window at all.

**Suggested fix:** treat a `pld.tile.remote_store` target (a cross-rank-written, barrier-synchronized window) as producing that window for scheduling — e.g. classify the `remote_store` target as `output`/`inout` in `DeriveCallDirections`, or provide a way to express a window producer→consumer ordering edge across kernels.

Related: #1648, #1503, #1368.

title: [RFC] Replace Program::comm_groups_ with CommDomainScopeStmt IR op
body:
### Summary

Replace the program-level `Program::comm_groups_` metadata vector (and its companion `CommGroup` IRNode) with a new `CommDomainScopeStmt` scope statement that wraps the host-orchestration body. The `CollectCommGroups` pass is repurposed (renamed `MaterializeCommDomainScopes`) to emit the scope chain instead of populating program metadata; distributed codegen lowers each scope to its `with orch.allocate_domain(...)` block. The user DSL (`pld.alloc_window_buffer` / `pld.window` / `device=` dispatches) is unchanged, and the generated `host_orch.py` is byte-identical to today (strict-equivalence nesting). Tracked branch base commit: `b8e0c6f678825cca28e764a104aec38906fe7674`.

Related: #565 (distributed IR foundation), #1127 (L3 distributed programming interface), #1189 (orchestration-level collective communication).

### Motivation

The flat-metadata-on-program shape is a vestige of the old runtime that required communication domains to be constructed statically before worker initialization. The current `simpler` runtime supports per-`orch_fn` `orch.allocate_domain(...)`, so a domain is just another scoped resource inside the host orchestrator body — exactly the shape `RuntimeScopeStmt` already models for `PTO2_SCOPE` (`include/pypto/ir/stmt.h:950-972`, `src/codegen/orchestration/orchestration_codegen.cpp:792-821`).

Problems with the status quo:

- Codegen reads program-level metadata to decide nesting structure (`src/codegen/distributed/distributed_codegen.cpp:270-339`). Nesting is implicit in declaration order + indentation tracking, not in the IR.
- Several passes thread `comm_groups_` through Program reconstruction even though the data is purely orchestration-body concern (`simplify_pass.cpp`, `expand_manual_phase_fence_pass.cpp`, `optimize_orch_tensors_pass.cpp`, `passes.cpp`).
- A `WindowBuffer → group_idx` map is rebuilt at codegen entry (`distributed_codegen.cpp:79-84`) instead of being resolvable from the IR ancestor chain.
- Existing scope ops (`RuntimeScopeStmt`, `InCoreScopeStmt`, `ClusterScopeStmt`, `HierarchyScopeStmt`, `SpmdScopeStmt`) all express "wrap a body in a named runtime scope". Communication-domain construction is the obvious next sibling and currently the odd one out.

### Design

#### 1. New IR node: `CommDomainScopeStmt`

Clone `RuntimeScopeStmt`'s shape (`include/pypto/ir/stmt.h:950-972`). Inherits `ScopeStmt` (`body_`, `name_hint_`, `attrs_`, `leading_comments_`) and adds the two fields `CommGroup` carries today:

```cpp
class CommDomainScopeStmt : public ScopeStmt {
 public:
  std::vector<int64_t> devices_;        // empty = all devices (= *range(world_size))
  std::vector<WindowBufferPtr> slots_;  // alloc-order slots

  CommDomainScopeStmt(std::vector<int64_t> devices, std::vector<WindowBufferPtr> slots,
                      std::string name_hint, StmtPtr body, Span span, ...);

  ObjectKind GetKind() const override { return ObjectKind::CommDomainScopeStmt; }
  ScopeKind  GetScopeKind() const override { return ScopeKind::CommDomain; }
  std::string TypeName() const override { return "CommDomainScopeStmt"; }

  static constexpr auto GetFieldDescriptors() {
    return std::tuple_cat(ScopeStmt::GetFieldDescriptors(),
        std::make_tuple(reflection::UsualField(&CommDomainScopeStmt::devices_, "devices"),
                        reflection::UsualField(&CommDomainScopeStmt::slots_, "slots")));
  }
};
```

`name_hint_` is the handle base — codegen derives `__comm_d<n>`. `WindowBufferPtr` identity is preserved end-to-end: the same `shared_ptr<const WindowBuffer>` stays threaded through `DistributedTensorType::window_buffer_` (`include/pypto/ir/program.h:79`), so existing routing logic keeps working without an explicit map.

#### 2. Repurpose `CollectCommGroups` → `MaterializeCommDomainScopes`

The analysis (clustering by merged device descriptor, source-ordering) is unchanged. Only the **output** shape changes:

- **Before** (`src/ir/transforms/collect_comm_groups_pass.cpp:426`): rebuild `Program` with `comm_groups_` populated.
- **After**: rewrite each host-orchestrator function body as

  ```
  CommDomainScopeStmt(group 0)
    └── body: CommDomainScopeStmt(group 1)
                └── body: ... CommDomainScopeStmt(group N-1)
                              └── body: original function body
  ```

  Same outer-to-inner declaration order today's codegen emits, so generated `host_orch.py` is byte-identical.

Pipeline position stays (slot 36, before final `Simplify`). `IRProperty::CommGroupsCollected` → `IRProperty::CommDomainScopesMaterialized`.

#### 3. Distributed codegen migration

`src/codegen/distributed/distributed_codegen.cpp`:

- **Remove** `EmitCommDomainAllocations()` (lines 270-339) and the `with_blocks` indent-balancing in `EmitFunction` (lines 248-264).
- **Remove** the program-init `window_to_group_idx_` map (lines 79-84).
- **Add** `VisitStmt_(const CommDomainScopeStmtPtr&)` that emits the same text `EmitCommDomainAllocations` emits today — workers list, window-size sum, `CommBufferSpec(...)` per slot — then `IncreaseIndent()`, visit `op->body_`, `DecreaseIndent()`. Mirrors `RuntimeScopeStmt`'s handler in the orchestration codegen.
- **Replace** `GroupIdxForWindowBuffer()` (lines 131-138) with an in-codegen open-scope stack: push on entry, pop on exit; look up a `WindowBufferPtr` by scanning the stack inner-to-outer (nesting depth is small and bounded).
- Per-dispatch routing emit sites (lines 667-685, 719-727) switch from `HandleVarForGroup(GroupIdxForWindowBuffer(wb))` to a stack query (same `__comm_d<n>` output).

#### 4. Program cleanup

`include/pypto/ir/program.h`:

- Delete `class CommGroup` and `using CommGroupPtr` (lines 81-112).
- Delete `Program::comm_groups_` field (line 207), the two CommGroup-aware constructors (lines 141-146, 168-169), and the `comm_groups` descriptor in `GetFieldDescriptors` (line 201).
- Remove `ObjectKind::CommGroup` from `include/pypto/ir/kind_traits.h`; add `ObjectKind::CommDomainScopeStmt`.

Passes that thread `comm_groups_` through Program reconstruction (grep `comm_groups_` in `src/ir/transforms/`): drop those lines — `simplify_pass.cpp`, `expand_manual_phase_fence_pass.cpp`, `optimize_orch_tensors_pass.cpp`, `passes.cpp`.

#### 5. Python bindings, type stubs, printer, structural-equal

- `python/bindings/modules/ir.cpp`: drop `program.comm_groups` getter and `CommGroup` class binding; add `CommDomainScopeStmt` binding.
- `python/pypto/pypto_core/ir.pyi`: same surface deltas.
- `python/bindings/modules/passes.cpp` + `python/pypto/pypto_core/passes.pyi`: rename `collect_comm_groups` factory → `materialize_comm_domain_scopes`.
- `python/pypto/ir/pass_manager.py:172-181`: rename the pass entry.
- `src/ir/transforms/structural_equal.cpp`: add `EQUAL_DISPATCH(CommDomainScopeStmt)`; remove the `CommGroup` dispatch.
- `src/ir/transforms/python_printer.cpp`: add `VisitStmt_(const CommDomainScopeStmtPtr&)` that emits a **single leading comment** then descends into `op->body_` at the same indent (no `with` wrapper — it would have no parser surface). Comment format:

  ```
  # pld.comm_domain: devices=[0, 1], slots=[scratch, signal]
  ```

  (`devices=all` when the scope covers every rank.) Reparse produces pre-pass IR (the comment is dropped by the parser); pipeline re-run reconstructs the scope. Round-trip table:

  | Round-trip kind | Path | Works? |
  | --------------- | ---- | ------ |
  | `assert_structural_equal(post-pass A, post-pass B)` | in-memory reflection over stmt subtree, including `devices_` and `slots_` | yes — same as `RuntimeScopeStmt` |
  | Python source: post-pass IR → printer → file → parser → pipeline | printer emits the comment + body (no wrapper); parser drops the comment and produces pre-pass IR; pipeline re-runs `MaterializeCommDomainScopes` and rebuilds the same scope chain | yes — same contract today's `comm_groups_` uses |

- The IR msgpack `ir.serialize` / `ir.deserialize` API has no real consumer in this repo (grep guard) and remains a dead API; we do not need to teach it about `CommDomainScopeStmt` to land this refactor.

#### 6. Documentation

Rename `docs/en/dev/passes/36-collect_comm_groups.md` → `36-materialize_comm_domain_scopes.md` (and the `docs/zh-cn/` mirror). Rewrite to describe the new pass output and update the table in `.claude/rules/pass-doc-ordering.md`.

### Affected Files

**Add**

- `include/pypto/ir/stmt.h` — declare `CommDomainScopeStmt`
- `src/ir/transforms/materialize_comm_domain_scopes_pass.cpp` — replaces `collect_comm_groups_pass.cpp` (rename + rewrite output side)
- `docs/en/dev/passes/36-materialize_comm_domain_scopes.md` and `docs/zh-cn/` mirror

**Modify**

- `include/pypto/ir/program.h` — delete `CommGroup`, `comm_groups_`, the two CommGroup-aware ctors
- `include/pypto/ir/kind_traits.h` — swap `CommGroup` for `CommDomainScopeStmt`
- `include/pypto/ir/transforms/pass_properties.h` — rename `IRProperty::CommGroupsCollected`
- `src/codegen/distributed/distributed_codegen.cpp` / `.h` — remove metadata reader, add scope-stmt handler + open-scope stack
- `src/ir/transforms/python_printer.cpp` — handler for the new stmt
- `src/ir/transforms/structural_equal.cpp` — dispatch updates
- `src/ir/transforms/{simplify,expand_manual_phase_fence,optimize_orch_tensors}_pass.cpp`, `src/ir/transforms/passes.cpp` — drop `comm_groups_` threading
- `python/bindings/modules/{ir,passes}.cpp` — bindings
- `python/pypto/pypto_core/{ir,passes}.pyi` — stubs
- `python/pypto/ir/pass_manager.py` — entry name
- IR msgpack serializer/deserializer — drop optional `comm_groups`

### Testing Plan

1. **Pass-level unit tests** — `tests/ut/ir/transforms/test_collect_comm_groups.py`: re-target assertions from `program.comm_groups` to the function-body scope chain (`func.body` is a `CommDomainScopeStmt` whose `body_` is either the next scope or the original body).
2. **Codegen golden** — `tests/ut/codegen/distributed/test_host_orch_distributed.py`: assertions should pass byte-identically (strict-equivalence nesting).
3. **End-to-end on hardware** — `tests/st/distributed/test_l3_multi_group.py`, `tests/st/distributed/test_l3_put.py`: should pass unchanged.
4. **Round-trip** — `tests/ut/ir/parser/`: confirm `assert_structural_equal` works across the new stmt.
5. **Grep guard** — after the migration, `git grep -n 'comm_groups_'` should return zero matches outside the rename history; `git grep -n 'CommGroup\b'` should be empty.

### Alternatives Considered

- **Explicit user-facing DSL surface** (e.g. `with pld.comm_domain(devices=..., buffers=[...]):` that users write directly). Rejected for the initial refactor — it expands the surface area significantly (parser + builder + DSL class) and is not required to remove the program-level metadata. The implicit / pass-synthesized path keeps user code unchanged while still achieving the IR cleanup. The explicit DSL can be added later as a separate enhancement.
- **Tighter "actual lifetime" nesting** (sibling scopes when lifetimes don't overlap, instead of strict declaration-order nesting). Rejected for this refactor — within a single `Worker.run` the runtime defers `comm_release_domain_windows` to drain regardless of explicit `release()` timing, so tighter scoping yields no current runtime benefit. Strict equivalence keeps `host_orch.py` byte-identical. Tighter scoping becomes meaningful only if combined with a future "early drain" optimization, which is orthogonal.
- **Two ops (alloc op + release op) rather than one body-wrapping scope op**. Rejected — the `with`-semantics of the runtime API is naturally body-wrapping, and PyPTO already has the `ScopeStmt` family precedent (`RuntimeScopeStmt`, `SpmdScopeStmt`, etc.) for exactly this shape.

### Rollout / Migration

Phased delivery, one PR per phase, each independently buildable:

1. **Phase A ** — Add `CommDomainScopeStmt` IR node end-to-end (header, kind_traits, structural-equal, reflection, visitor/mutator base, transparent-with-comment printer, Python binding, type stub). Pure addition; no producer or consumer yet. Build green.
2. **Phase B** — Repurpose the pass to ALSO wrap host_orch body in scope stmts (dual-write with `comm_groups_` for safety).
3. **Phase C** — `DistributedCodegen` visitor + open-scope stack consumes scope stmts; remove `EmitCommDomainAllocations`.
4. **Phase D** — Remove `Program::comm_groups_`, `CommGroup`, `ObjectKind::CommGroup`, and the threading in other passes.
5. **Phase E** — Clean CommGroup binding/stub, update IR msgpack serializer/deserializer.
6. **Phase F** — Port unit tests, rename docs (en + zh-cn), update `.claude/rules/pass-doc-ordering.md`.
7. **Phase G** — Run unit + st tests; grep guard for residual `comm_groups` references.

User DSL is unchanged throughout. Generated `host_orch.py` is byte-identical after Phase C (strict-equivalence nesting). No downstream consumer of the IR msgpack format exists, so dropping its `comm_groups` field is not user-visible.

### Open Questions

- Should the open-scope stack lookup live on the visitor base (reusable by future scope kinds) or be local to `DistributedCodegen`? Leaning local for now since no other consumer exists; revisit if a second scope-aware codegen path appears.
- Should the `name_hint_` for synthesized scopes follow a convention (e.g. `comm_d0`, `comm_d1`) so dumps are stable across runs, or be left empty (codegen derives `__comm_d<n>` from visit order)? Leaning convention-based for dump stability.
- Should we keep `CollectCommGroups` as the public pass name (Python factory) and only rename internally? Leaning rename to `materialize_comm_domain_scopes` for symmetry with `materialize_runtime_scopes` (slot 37), but flagging as a public-API rename.

title: [Feature] Support tensor-level ops (slice / assemble / slice-assign) on local access of a pld.DistributedTensor window
body:
### Summary

Tensor-level ops reject a `pld.DistributedTensor` (window) operand, so the only way to access window data is the tile-level `pl.load` / `pl.store`. Concretely:

- `pl.slice(win, ...)` / `win[i:i+1, :]` → `tensor.slice requires first argument to be a TensorType, but got DistributedTensorType`
- `pl.assemble(win_view, src, off)` likewise needs a `TensorType`
- so a window can only be read/written through `pl.tile.load` / `pl.tile.store`

A `pld.DistributedTensor` is backed by local GM on each rank; a *local* (own-rank) read/write of it is just a GM access. It would be useful to let the tensor-level slice / assemble / slice-assign ops accept a `DistributedTensor` for local access (treating it as its local GM tensor), the same way they accept a plain `pl.Tensor`.

### Motivation / Use Case

In dsv4 EP-MoE (`models/deepseek/v4/moe_ep.py`), the cross-rank dispatch/combine kernels stage data through HCCL window scratch. The single-card `dispatch` / `combine` express their scatter/gather with tensor-level idioms — `recv_x_flat = pl.assemble(recv_x_flat, pl.slice(x_norm_i8, [1, D], [t, 0]), [dst, 0])` and `routed_y_buf_flat[dst:dst+1, :] = recv_y_flat[i:i+1, :]`. The EP variants can't reuse those idioms on the window: every window access has to go through `pl.tile.load` / `pl.tile.store` instead.

This matters in two situations:

1. **Pure staging / copies through a window.** A window→host copy (or a reshape-and-row-store of a window) is forced through tile load+store even when no compute is involved. Combined with `ConvertTensorToTileOps`, a `pl.tile.store` to a *reshaped* output view inside a `pl.at(CORE_GROUP)` scope tile-loads the whole output into Vec (separate problem), whereas a tensor-level `assemble`/slice-assign would not.

2. **Trying to express these kernels with tensor-level ops.** When attempting to author the EP combine reduce (read `routed_y_buf` window + `sh` → `ffn_out`) or the EP dispatch stage-out with slice/assemble, the window read immediately fails with the `DistributedTensorType` rejection, so the whole tensor-level path is unavailable and one must fall back to `pl.load` + a `pl.cast` tile + `pl.store`.

### Proposed API / Behavior

Allow `tensor.slice`, `tensor.assemble`, and slice-assign (`dst[...] = src`) to accept a `pld.DistributedTensor` operand for **local** (own-rank) access, lowering it to an op on the window's local GM tensor — i.e. `win[i:i+1, :]` reads the local copy, `win_flat[i:i+1, :] = src_tensor` writes the local copy. Cross-rank access stays via the existing `pld.tile.remote_store` / `pld.tensor.put` / `pld.tensor.get` APIs.

### Additional Context

pypto `89698531`. Surfaced while exploring whether the dsv4 EP dispatch/combine InCore kernels can be authored as `@pl.jit.inline` (they can't, for separate reasons). Related: #1670 (window write→read ordering across kernels).

title: [Bug] @pl.jit.host L3 dispatch breaks when the host orchestrator is renamed: CommBufferSpec.__init__() got an unexpected keyword argument 'tensors'
body:
### Component

Runtime — JIT `@pl.jit.host` distributed dispatch (`distributed_runner.py` entry-function resolution)

### Description

Renaming the `@pl.jit.host` orchestrator function **deterministically** breaks end-to-end L3 dispatch (the path added by #1660). The same program runs fine when the host function is named `host_orch`, but fails at dispatch when it is renamed to `moe_ep_l3` (also `l3_moe_ep`, `moe_l3`) with:

```
TypeError: CommBufferSpec.__init__() got an unexpected keyword argument 'tensors'
```

The generated orchestration code is **byte-identical** between the two names (only the function symbol differs), so this is a runtime entry-resolution issue, not codegen. `distributed_runner.py` calls the entry as `entry_fn(orch, _args, config, tensors=tensors, callables=chip_cids, ...)`; with certain host names `entry_fn` ends up bound to the wrong callable, so the `tensors=` kwarg lands on `CommBufferSpec.__init__`.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. A `@pl.jit.host` host orchestrator `host_orch` that allocates HCCL windows and dispatches a `@pl.jit` chip orchestration **named `moe_ep`** per rank (`device=r`), run via `run_jit(fn=host_orch, compile_cfg=dict(distributed_config=DistributedConfig(device_ids=[0,1])))`. (Concrete case: dsv4 `models/deepseek/v4/moe_ep.py` in pypto-lib.)
2. Run on 2 NPUs → **PASS**.
3. Rename only the host function `host_orch` → `moe_ep_l3` (nothing else) → re-run → **FAIL** with the error above.

Names tested in a single env window (same pypto, same hardware): `host_orch` → PASS, immediately followed by `moe_ep_l3` → FAIL. Also `l3_moe_ep` and `moe_l3` → FAIL (same error).

### Expected Behavior

L3 dispatch succeeds regardless of the host orchestrator's Python function name — the generated code is identical, so the name must not affect runtime entry resolution.

### Actual Behavior

```
File ".../pypto/runtime/distributed_runner.py", line 347, in execute_distributed
    _dispatch(w, entry_fn, tensors, chip_cids, sub_ids, _make_call_config(dc), len(dc.device_ids))
File ".../pypto/runtime/distributed_runner.py", line 291, in _dispatch
    w.run(orch_fn)
File ".../pypto/runtime/distributed_runner.py", line 280, in orch_fn
    entry_fn(
TypeError: CommBufferSpec.__init__() got an unexpected keyword argument 'tensors'
```

### Git Commit ID

`71b557f7`

### NPU Kind

Ascend 910B

### Host Platform

Linux (aarch64)

### Additional Context

- The generated `orchestration/host_orch.py` for the passing (`host_orch`) and failing (`moe_ep_l3`) builds is byte-identical after normalizing the function name (`diff` is empty).
- The generated host entry is `def <name>(orch, _args, config, *, tensors, callables, sub_ids, _keep, world_size)` — it **does** accept `tensors` — and it constructs `CommBufferSpec(name=..., dtype="opaque", count=..., nbytes=...)`, which matches the installed `simpler.task_interface.CommBufferSpec.__init__(name, dtype, count, nbytes, load_from_host, store_to_host)`. No generated code passes `tensors=` to `CommBufferSpec`.
- So the `tensors=` reaching `CommBufferSpec` comes from `distributed_runner.py:280` calling `entry_fn(..., tensors=tensors, ...)` against the wrong resolved callable. The likely trigger is a name collision/ordering with the chip orchestration named `moe_ep` (the host dispatches it via `callables["moe_ep"]`); host names that pass (`host_orch`) vs fail (`moe_ep_l3` / `l3_moe_ep` / `moe_l3`) differ in how they relate to `moe_ep`.
- Surfaced while authoring the dsv4 EP MoE end-to-end as a `@pl.jit.host` kernel (hw-native-sys/pypto-lib#452). Workaround: name the host orchestrator `host_orch`.

title: [Feature] Surface per-run RunTiming (device/host wall) through execute_on_device / execute_compiled
body:
### Summary

The runtime worker already measures per-run wall-clock timing and returns it as a `RunTiming` object (`host_wall_ns` / `device_wall_ns`, exposed in Python as `host_wall_us` / `device_wall_us`). However, this data is silently discarded by the upper dispatch layers, so callers (e.g. the pypto-lib golden harness) have no way to obtain the device/host timing breakdown of a run. Please plumb `RunTiming` up through `execute_on_device()` and `execute_compiled()` so callers can read it.

### Motivation / Use Case

`RunTiming` is the only source of on-NPU orchestrator wall time (`device_wall_ns`, computed from `orch_summary.end_time - start_time` and populated on the default `PTO2_PROFILING` build). It is genuinely useful for lightweight performance reporting — e.g. the pypto-lib harness currently only records a Python wall-clock (`RunResult.execution_time`) around the whole `run()`/`run_jit()`, which includes compile + golden + validate overhead and cannot isolate device time. Today there is no public API path to retrieve the device/host split even though the runtime computes it on every L2 run.

The data flows correctly all the way up to `Worker.run()` and is then thrown away:

- `ChipWorker.run()` (`runtime/python/simpler/task_interface.py:387-406`) returns `RunTiming`.
- `Worker.run()` (`runtime/python/simpler/worker.py:1950-2016`) returns `RunTiming` (L2: real device + host wall; L3+: host wall only, device_wall = 0).
- `execute_on_device()` (`python/pypto/runtime/device_runner.py:494-627`) calls `worker.run(cid, orch_args, cfg)` at **line 626 but ignores the return value**, and returns `None`.
- `execute_compiled()` (`python/pypto/runtime/runner.py:790-883`) returns `None`.

So the last surviving reference to the timing is dropped at `device_runner.py:626`.

### Proposed API / Behavior

Thread the existing `RunTiming` through the two dispatch functions (no new measurement needed):

```python
# device_runner.py: execute_on_device(...) -> RunTiming
cid = worker.register(chip_callable)
timing = worker.run(cid, orch_args, cfg)   # currently the result is discarded
worker.close()
return timing

# runner.py: execute_compiled(...) -> RunTiming | None
timing = execute_on_device(...)            # capture instead of dropping
if dfx_dir is not None:
    _collect_dfx_artifacts(...)
return timing
```

Callers can then read `timing.device_wall_us` / `timing.host_wall_us`. Returning the object (rather than logging) keeps it opt-in and backward compatible for callers that ignore the return value.

### Additional Context

- `RunTiming` C++ definition: `runtime/src/common/hierarchical/types.h:220-231`
- Python binding (ns->us properties): `runtime/python/bindings/task_interface.cpp:673-722`
- C API doc on field semantics: `runtime/src/common/worker/pto_runtime_c_api.h:51-74`
- Note: for L3+ DAG runs, `device_wall_us` is currently 0 (per-task device cycles are not aggregated in the ring scheduler — see `worker.py:2012-2016`); only L2 single-task runs carry a real device wall.

Repo HEAD at filing: `71b557f7c12ae1a8f916c5946240d09767338a26`

title: [RFC] SuperscalarNPU backend: DDR + TREG register-file architecture
body:
### Summary

Add a new compiler backend, **SuperscalarNPU**, whose only memory spaces are **DDR** (off-chip) and **TREG** — a register file of **256 fixed 4 KB blocks (1 MB total)** addressed by block index. Unlike the Ascend backends, SuperscalarNPU has no cube/vector cores and no L1/L0 buffer hierarchy: on-chip data lives in TREG and is allocated by **register renaming** (liveness-based coalescing + block-index assignment with a register-pressure limit). This RFC tracks the end-to-end development of the backend, from IR generation through (eventually) code generation.

This issue is the umbrella tracker. Phase 1 + 2 (IR generation) are implemented in #1680.

### Motivation

PyPTO's pass pipeline and memory model are currently Ascend-centric: memory-space inference targets `Vec/Mat/Left/Right/Acc`, `AllocateMemoryAddr` assigns byte addresses, and the default pass strategy runs cube/vector/cross-core passes (`AutoTileMatmulL0`, `ExpandMixedKernel`, `InjectGMPipeBuffer`, `SplitVectorKernel`, ...). None of this fits a register-file NPU.

SuperscalarNPU is the first non-Ascend backend and a forcing function to validate that the `BackendHandler` + `MemoryAllocatorPolicy` abstractions actually decouple backend behaviour from shared passes. It also introduces a genuinely different allocation model (register renaming over a fixed-size register file) that the existing byte-addressed allocator did not support.

### Design

**Memory model**
- New `MemorySpace::TREG`. SoC = single compute core carrying a 1 MB TREG (256 × 4 KB, 4 KB-aligned) + DDR; memory graph `DDR ↔ TREG`.

**Register-renaming allocation**
- Extend `MemoryAllocatorPolicy` with `AddressUnitBytes(space)` (default 1) and `MaxAddressUnits(space)` (default unbounded).
- `AllocateMemoryAddr` stores **block indices** for register-file spaces (unit > 1), reserves consecutive blocks for tiles larger than one block, and raises a user-facing error when more blocks are simultaneously live than exist (register pressure). The `AllocatedMemoryAddr` verifier scales stored addresses by the unit so the byte-based capacity check stays unit-agnostic.
- `SuperscalarNPURegisterAllocatorPolicy`: 4 KB blocks, 256-block limit. Liveness-based coalescing remains the shared `MemoryReuse` pass — i.e. MemoryReuse = renaming/coalescing, the policy = block assignment.

**Backend decoupling (no `BackendType` branching in passes)**
- `BackendHandler::GetDefaultOnChipMemorySpace()` → `Vec` on Ascend, `TREG` here. `InferTileMemorySpace` reads it instead of hardcoding `Vec`; a generic `Vec` op input-constraint is realized as this default so no spurious `tile.move` is inserted. Ascend behaviour is unchanged (default is `Vec`, so all new paths are no-ops).
- `Backend::CreateMemoryAllocatorPolicy()` returns the TREG policy.

**Pass pipeline**
- `OptimizationStrategy.SuperscalarNPU`: tensor prefix + outline + `ConvertTensorToTileOps` + `InferTileMemorySpace` + `InitMemRef` + `MemoryReuse` + `AllocateMemoryAddr`, omitting all Ascend cube/vector/cross-core passes. Stops after allocation (IR-only).

### Affected Files

See #1680 for the full diff. Key additions:
- `include/pypto/backend/superscalar/` — **New** — backend, handler, register allocator policy
- `src/backend/superscalar/` — **New** — backend + handler impl
- `include/pypto/ir/memory_space.h`, `src/ir/memref.cpp` — **Modify** — `MemorySpace::TREG`
- `include/pypto/ir/memory_allocator_policy.h`, `src/ir/transforms/allocate_memory_addr_pass.cpp` — **Modify** — block-index addressing + pressure check
- `include/pypto/backend/common/backend_handler.h`, `src/ir/transforms/infer_tile_memory_space_pass.cpp` — **Modify** — `GetDefaultOnChipMemorySpace`
- `python/pypto/ir/pass_manager.py` — **Modify** — `OptimizationStrategy.SuperscalarNPU`

### Testing Plan

- Backend construction / SoC / handler unit tests.
- End-to-end TREG strategy test: TREG assignment, block-index addressing, register renaming (coalescing), register-pressure error.
- Regression: `tests/ut/ir/transforms/` and `tests/ut/codegen/` must stay green (Ascend unaffected). Verified in #1680.
- Future: codegen golden tests once codegen lands.

### Rollout / Migration

Additive and backward-compatible. The new `BackendHandler` / `MemoryAllocatorPolicy` methods have defaults equal to existing Ascend behaviour, so Ascend910B/950 are unchanged. SuperscalarNPU is opt-in via `BackendType.SuperscalarNPU` + `OptimizationStrategy.SuperscalarNPU`.

### Roadmap / Tracking

- [x] Phase 1 — Memory space + register-renaming allocator (TREG enum, `AddressUnitBytes`/`MaxAddressUnits`, `SuperscalarNPURegisterAllocatorPolicy`, pressure CHECK) — #1680
- [x] Phase 2 — Backend registration + TREG pass strategy + handler-driven memory inference — #1680
- [x] Tests + docs (en/zh-cn) for the above — #1680
- [ ] Phase 3 — Code generation for SuperscalarNPU (currently IR-only)
- [ ] Phase 4 — Runtime / simulator integration and `compile()` wiring (currently the flow runs passes via `run_passes`; `compile()` would fail at codegen)
- [ ] Phase 5 — Op coverage validation on TREG (matmul / reductions / control flow) and a dedicated `CoreType` value (single core currently reuses `VECTOR`)

### Open Questions

1. **Sub-block views**: TREG addresses are block indices; non-4 KB-aligned view offsets currently truncate on division. Do we need sub-block addressing, or constrain views to block granularity?
2. **`CoreType`**: should we add a dedicated SuperscalarNPU core type instead of reusing `VECTOR`?
3. **Spilling**: on register pressure we currently error. Should the allocator spill to DDR instead?
4. **Tiles > 4 KB**: currently span consecutive blocks. Is there a hardware cap on a single value's block span?

### Reference

Implementation PR: #1680
Git commit: `c5525d70b2e800a7ac1d791d0238cff06f1e8994`

title: [Feature] Replay an already-compiled L3 distributed program from its build_output dir (runtime_dir workflow for DistributedCompiledProgram)
body:
### Summary

L3 distributed programs (`@pl.jit.host` → `DistributedCompiledProgram`) cannot use the **`runtime_dir` replay workflow** that single-chip (L2) programs rely on: pointing the harness at an already-compiled `build_output/` directory, hand-editing the generated `.cpp`/`.pto` files, and re-executing on device **without** re-running the pypto pass/compile chain.

There is currently no runtime entry point to *load and execute a distributed program from its on-disk build directory alone*. Replay only works while the in-memory `DistributedCompiledProgram` object is still alive; once you want to skip compilation and reuse a prior `build_output/`, there is no supported path.

### Motivation / Use Case

The `runtime_dir` workflow is the primary fast-iteration loop for kernel debugging: compile once, then repeatedly tweak the emitted PTO/cpp and re-run on device, skipping the (slow) pypto compile. It is fully supported for single-chip kernels but silently breaks for distributed (EP) kernels.

Concretely, `models/deepseek/v4/moe_ep.py` (2-rank EP MoE, an L3 host orchestrator) exposes `--runtime-dir`, but passing it routes through the single-chip runner and fails, because:

1. The harness has **no live `compiled` object** in the `runtime_dir` branch (compilation was skipped), so the L3 dispatch path (`compiled(*args, config=...)`) is unreachable — it falls through to `execute_compiled(work_dir, ...)`, which only understands single-chip builds.
2. `execute_compiled` expects a **top-level `kernel_config.py`**, which an L3 build does not have (per-rank configs live under `next_levels/{chip_task_name}/`).
3. Even the pto→cpp rebuild + binary-cache-invalidation helpers assume a flat `kernels/` + `orchestration/` layout and don't recurse into the nested `next_levels/` per-rank directories.

Without this, EP/distributed kernel authors lose the entire edit-pto-and-rerun fast loop and must pay a full recompile on every change.

### Proposed API / Behavior

A way to reconstruct and dispatch a distributed program from just its `output_dir`, analogous to `execute_compiled` for single-chip. For example either:

```python
# Option A: a reload-from-dir factory on the distributed program
prog = DistributedCompiledProgram.from_dir(output_dir)   # rebuilds metadata from artifacts
prog(*args, config=RunConfig(...))

# Option B: a distributed counterpart to execute_compiled
from pypto.runtime import execute_distributed_compiled
execute_distributed_compiled(output_dir, args, config=RunConfig(...))
```

This implies persisting (or re-deriving) the metadata that `DistributedCompiledProgram.__call__` currently reads from the **post-pass IR** (`self._program`): per-rank param infos / post-SSA names and the Orchestration functions iterated during chip-callable assembly — without re-running the pass chain.

It should also make the `runtime_dir` rebuild helpers L3-aware (walk `next_levels/{rank}/kernels` and `.../orchestration`).

### Alternatives Considered

- **Re-compile every iteration** — defeats the purpose of `runtime_dir`; the pypto compile is exactly what we want to skip.
- **Serialize the post-pass `Program` IR** alongside the build artifacts and reload it (lighter than a from-scratch reconstruction, if the IR is serializable).

### Additional Context

Evidence (commit `3f421313`, pypto):

- Harness routing — the `runtime_dir` branch leaves `compiled is None`, so `_try_l3_dispatch` is skipped and it falls to `execute_compiled`: `golden/runner.py` (pypto-lib) `_setup_runtime_dir` / `_execute_via_runner` / `_try_l3_dispatch`. The L3 dispatch docstring notes "L3 (HOST Orchestrator) programs cannot use `execute_compiled` (no top-level `kernel_config.py`); the compiled object is callable directly."
- `execute_compiled` requires a top-level `kernel_config.py`: `python/pypto/runtime/device_runner.py:408-410` (`compile_and_assemble`).
- L3 output layout puts `kernel_config.py` per-rank under `next_levels/{chip_task_name}/`: `python/pypto/backend/pto_backend.py:533-554`.
- `DistributedCompiledProgram` needs the live post-pass `Program` IR and has no `from_dir`/reload path: `python/pypto/ir/distributed_compiled_program.py:116-119`.
- Rebuild helpers assume a flat layout: `python/pypto/runtime/debug/pto_rebuild.py:123-129` (`_find_kernel_cpp` only searches `work_dir/kernels/{aic,aiv}`) and `python/pypto/runtime/debug/replay.py:82-89` (`invalidate_binary_cache` only walks `work_dir/{kernels,orchestration}`).

Reproduction:

```bash
# 1) Compile + run once (produces build_output/ for the L3 program)
python models/deepseek/v4/moe_ep.py -p a2a3 -d 0,1

# 2) Try to replay from the build dir (edit pto/cpp, skip compile) -> fails:
#    falls into execute_compiled, which can't find a top-level kernel_config.py
python models/deepseek/v4/moe_ep.py -p a2a3 -d 0,1 --runtime-dir <build_output_dir>
```

title: [Bug] L3 distributed BF16 publish remote_store fails with AICPU 507057 at two token tiles
body:
### Component

Runtime / L3 distributed execution (`pld.tile.remote_store` + `pld.system.notify/wait`)

### Description

A minimal L3 distributed program that publishes BF16 tiles from every rank to every other rank via `pld.tile.remote_store`, then synchronizes with `pld.system.notify` / `pld.system.wait`, fails on Ascend NPU once the token dimension reaches two `token_tile=16` blocks.

This was extracted from the DeepSeek-V4 `lm_head` DP/EP-owner-to-TP handoff debugging, but the repro has no model dependency, no matmul, and no lm_head weight. The failure is in the L3 distributed runtime/device path.

Observed behavior:

- `tokens=16`: PASS
- `tokens=32`: FAIL with `aclrtSynchronizeStreamWithTimeout (AICPU) failed: 507057`
- `tokens=32 --route-only`: PASS
- `tokens=32 --publish-only`: also reproduces `507057` in this minimal program

The `tokens=16 -> tokens=32` change does not change the remote-store tile shape. It doubles the number of token blocks:

- tile shape: `[16, 512]` BF16 = 16 KiB per hidden remote_store
- per-rank publish stores at `tokens=16`: `(4 - 1) * (16 / 16) * (4096 / 512) = 24`
- per-rank publish stores at `tokens=32`: `(4 - 1) * (32 / 16) * (4096 / 512) = 48`

The notify/wait count is unchanged: each rank still notifies and waits on the other 3 ranks.

Related but not duplicate:

- Related: #1650. Same broad AICPU scheduler failure family, but that issue is an intra-scope GM self-RAW deadlock with `507018`; this repro is L3 distributed window traffic and notify/wait with `507057`, and contains no GM self-RAW pattern.
- Related: #1678. That issue is a host entry-resolution bug (`CommBufferSpec.__init__(tensors=...)`). This repro uses a host entry named `host_orch`, so it does not depend on that failure mode or its workaround.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Save the following script as `tmp_l3_two_phase_comm_repro.py` in a repo that can import `pypto` and the local `golden` runner.
2. Run the passing control:

```bash
task-submit --device 8,9,10,11 --timeout 600 --run \
"python tmp_l3_two_phase_comm_repro.py -p a2a3 -d 8,9,10,11 --tokens 16"
```

3. Run the failing case:

```bash
task-submit --device 8,9,10,11 --timeout 600 --run \
"python tmp_l3_two_phase_comm_repro.py -p a2a3 -d 8,9,10,11 --tokens 32"
```

4. Optional controls:

```bash
# Route-only control passes at tokens=32.
task-submit --device 8,9,10,11 --timeout 600 --run \
"python tmp_l3_two_phase_comm_repro.py -p a2a3 -d 8,9,10,11 --tokens 32 --route-only"

# Publish-only is an even smaller failing signal in this minimal program.
task-submit --device 8,9,10,11 --timeout 600 --run \
"python tmp_l3_two_phase_comm_repro.py -p a2a3 -d 8,9,10,11 --tokens 32 --publish-only"
```

<details>
<summary>Minimal repro script</summary>

```python
import argparse

import pypto.language as pl
import pypto.language.distributed as pld
from pypto.ir.distributed_compiled_program import DistributedConfig


def build_program(
    *,
    world_size: int,
    tokens: int,
    hidden_size: int,
    route_cols_per_rank: int,
    token_tile: int,
    hidden_chunk: int,
    route_chunk: int,
    publish_first: bool,
    route_second: bool,
):
    route_cols = world_size * route_cols_per_rank
    assert tokens % token_tile == 0
    assert hidden_size % hidden_chunk == 0
    assert route_cols_per_rank % route_chunk == 0

    hidden_blocks = hidden_size // hidden_chunk
    route_blocks = route_cols_per_rank // route_chunk
    full_route_blocks = route_cols // route_chunk

    @pl.program
    class L3TwoPhaseCommRepro:
        @pl.function(type=pl.FunctionType.InCore)
        def zero_route_shard(
            self,
            route_shard: pl.Out[pl.Tensor[[tokens, route_cols_per_rank], pl.FP32]],
        ) -> pl.Tensor[[tokens, route_cols_per_rank], pl.FP32]:
            for t0 in pl.range(0, tokens, token_tile):
                for rb in pl.range(route_blocks):
                    c0 = rb * route_chunk
                    tile = pl.tile.full([token_tile, route_chunk], dtype=pl.FP32, value=0.0)
                    pl.store(tile, [t0, c0], route_shard)
            return route_shard

        @pl.function(type=pl.FunctionType.InCore)
        def zero_out(
            self,
            out: pl.Out[pl.Tensor[[tokens, route_cols], pl.FP32]],
        ) -> pl.Tensor[[tokens, route_cols], pl.FP32]:
            for t0 in pl.range(0, tokens, token_tile):
                for rb in pl.range(full_route_blocks):
                    c0 = rb * route_chunk
                    tile = pl.tile.full([token_tile, route_chunk], dtype=pl.FP32, value=0.0)
                    pl.store(tile, [t0, c0], out)
            return out

        @pl.function(type=pl.FunctionType.InCore)
        def publish_hidden_phase(
            self,
            hidden: pl.Tensor[[tokens, hidden_size], pl.BF16],
            hidden_window: pld.DistributedTensor[[world_size * tokens, hidden_size], pl.BF16],
            hidden_done: pld.DistributedTensor[[world_size, 1], pl.INT32],
            my_rank: pl.Scalar[pl.INT32],
        ):
            for peer in pl.range(world_size):
                if peer != my_rank:
                    row_base = my_rank * tokens
                    for t0 in pl.range(0, tokens, token_tile):
                        for hb in pl.range(hidden_blocks):
                            h0 = hb * hidden_chunk
                            tile = pl.load(hidden, [t0, h0], [token_tile, hidden_chunk])
                            pld.tile.remote_store(
                                tile,
                                target=hidden_window,
                                peer=peer,
                                offsets=[row_base + t0, h0],
                            )

            for peer in pl.range(world_size):
                if peer != my_rank:
                    pld.system.notify(
                        target=hidden_done,
                        peer=peer,
                        offsets=[my_rank, 0],
                        value=1,
                        op=pld.NotifyOp.Set,
                    )

            for src in pl.range(world_size):
                if src != my_rank:
                    pld.system.wait(
                        signal=hidden_done,
                        offsets=[src, 0],
                        expected=1,
                        cmp=pld.WaitCmp.Ge,
                    )

        @pl.function(type=pl.FunctionType.InCore)
        def route_logits_phase(
            self,
            route_shard: pl.Tensor[[tokens, route_cols_per_rank], pl.FP32],
            out: pl.Out[pl.Tensor[[tokens, route_cols], pl.FP32]],
            route_window: pld.DistributedTensor[[tokens, route_cols], pl.FP32],
            route_done: pld.DistributedTensor[[world_size, 1], pl.INT32],
            my_rank: pl.Scalar[pl.INT32],
        ) -> pl.Tensor[[tokens, route_cols], pl.FP32]:
            col_base = my_rank * route_cols_per_rank
            for owner_rank in pl.range(world_size):
                for t0 in pl.range(0, tokens, token_tile):
                    for rb in pl.range(route_blocks):
                        c0 = rb * route_chunk
                        tile = pl.load(route_shard, [t0, c0], [token_tile, route_chunk])
                        if owner_rank == my_rank:
                            pl.store(tile, [t0, col_base + c0], out)
                        else:
                            pld.tile.remote_store(
                                tile,
                                target=route_window,
                                peer=owner_rank,
                                offsets=[t0, col_base + c0],
                            )

            for peer in pl.range(world_size):
                if peer != my_rank:
                    pld.system.notify(
                        target=route_done,
                        peer=peer,
                        offsets=[my_rank, 0],
                        value=1,
                        op=pld.NotifyOp.Set,
                    )

            for src in pl.range(world_size):
                if src != my_rank:
                    pld.system.wait(
                        signal=route_done,
                        offsets=[src, 0],
                        expected=1,
                        cmp=pld.WaitCmp.Ge,
                    )

            for src in pl.range(world_size):
                if src != my_rank:
                    src_base = src * route_cols_per_rank
                    for t0 in pl.range(0, tokens, token_tile):
                        for rb in pl.range(route_blocks):
                            c0 = rb * route_chunk
                            tile = pl.load(route_window, [t0, src_base + c0], [token_tile, route_chunk])
                            pl.store(tile, [t0, src_base + c0], out)
            return out

        @pl.function(type=pl.FunctionType.Orchestration)
        def chip_orch(
            self,
            hidden: pl.Tensor[[tokens, hidden_size], pl.BF16],
            out: pl.Out[pl.Tensor[[tokens, route_cols], pl.FP32]],
            status: pl.Out[pl.Tensor[[1], pl.INT32]],
            hidden_window: pld.DistributedTensor[[world_size * tokens, hidden_size], pl.BF16],
            hidden_done: pld.DistributedTensor[[world_size, 1], pl.INT32],
            route_window: pld.DistributedTensor[[tokens, route_cols], pl.FP32],
            route_done: pld.DistributedTensor[[world_size, 1], pl.INT32],
            my_rank: pl.Scalar[pl.INT32],
        ) -> tuple[pl.Tensor[[tokens, route_cols], pl.FP32], pl.Tensor[[1], pl.INT32]]:
            if publish_first:
                self.publish_hidden_phase(hidden, hidden_window, hidden_done, my_rank)

            if route_second:
                route_shard = pl.create_tensor([tokens, route_cols_per_rank], dtype=pl.FP32)
                route_shard = self.zero_route_shard(route_shard)
                out = self.route_logits_phase(route_shard, out, route_window, route_done, my_rank)
            else:
                out = self.zero_out(out)

            pl.write(status, [0], pl.cast(1, pl.INT32))
            return out, status

        @pl.function(level=pl.Level.HOST, role=pl.Role.Orchestrator)
        def host_orch(
            self,
            hidden: pl.Tensor[[world_size, tokens, hidden_size], pl.BF16],
            out: pl.Out[pl.Tensor[[world_size, tokens, route_cols], pl.FP32]],
            status: pl.Out[pl.Tensor[[world_size, 1], pl.INT32]],
        ):
            hidden_window_buf = pld.alloc_window_buffer(world_size * tokens * hidden_size * 2)
            hidden_done_buf = pld.alloc_window_buffer(world_size * 4)
            route_window_buf = pld.alloc_window_buffer(tokens * route_cols * 4)
            route_done_buf = pld.alloc_window_buffer(world_size * 4)

            for r in pl.range(pld.world_size()):
                hidden_window = pld.window(hidden_window_buf, [world_size * tokens, hidden_size], dtype=pl.BF16)
                hidden_done = pld.window(hidden_done_buf, [world_size, 1], dtype=pl.INT32)
                route_window = pld.window(route_window_buf, [tokens, route_cols], dtype=pl.FP32)
                route_done = pld.window(route_done_buf, [world_size, 1], dtype=pl.INT32)
                self.chip_orch(
                    hidden[r],
                    out[r],
                    status[r],
                    hidden_window,
                    hidden_done,
                    route_window,
                    route_done,
                    r,
                    device=r,
                )

    return L3TwoPhaseCommRepro


def build_specs(world_size: int, tokens: int, hidden_size: int, route_cols: int):
    import torch
    from golden import TensorSpec

    return [
        TensorSpec(
            "hidden",
            [world_size, tokens, hidden_size],
            torch.bfloat16,
            init_value=lambda: (torch.randn(world_size, tokens, hidden_size) * 0.1).to(torch.bfloat16),
        ),
        TensorSpec("out", [world_size, tokens, route_cols], torch.float32, is_output=True),
        TensorSpec("status", [world_size, 1], torch.int32, is_output=True),
    ]


def golden(tensors):
    tensors["out"].zero_()
    tensors["status"][:] = 1


def main():
    from golden import run

    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    parser.add_argument("-p", "--platform", default="a2a3", choices=["a2a3", "a2a3sim", "a5", "a5sim"])
    parser.add_argument("-d", "--device", default="0,1,2,3")
    parser.add_argument("--world-size", type=int, default=4)
    parser.add_argument("--tokens", type=int, default=32)
    parser.add_argument("--hidden-size", type=int, default=4096)
    parser.add_argument("--route-cols-per-rank", type=int, default=32320)
    parser.add_argument("--token-tile", type=int, default=16)
    parser.add_argument("--hidden-chunk", type=int, default=512)
    parser.add_argument("--route-chunk", type=int, default=320)
    parser.add_argument("--route-only", action="store_true")
    parser.add_argument("--publish-only", action="store_true")
    parser.add_argument("--compile-only", action="store_true")
    args = parser.parse_args()

    if args.route_only and args.publish_only:
        raise SystemExit("--route-only and --publish-only are mutually exclusive")

    publish_first = not args.route_only
    route_second = not args.publish_only
    route_cols = args.world_size * args.route_cols_per_rank
    device_ids = [int(d) for d in args.device.split(",")]
    assert len(device_ids) >= args.world_size

    program = build_program(
        world_size=args.world_size,
        tokens=args.tokens,
        hidden_size=args.hidden_size,
        route_cols_per_rank=args.route_cols_per_rank,
        token_tile=args.token_tile,
        hidden_chunk=args.hidden_chunk,
        route_chunk=args.route_chunk,
        publish_first=publish_first,
        route_second=route_second,
    )
    result = run(
        program=program,
        specs=build_specs(args.world_size, args.tokens, args.hidden_size, route_cols),
        golden_fn=golden,
        compile_only=args.compile_only,
        compile_cfg=dict(
            distributed_config=DistributedConfig(device_ids=device_ids[: args.world_size], num_sub_workers=0),
        ),
        runtime_cfg=dict(platform=args.platform),
        rtol=0,
        atol=0,
    )
    if not result.passed:
        if result.error:
            print(result.error)
        raise SystemExit(1)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
```

</details>

### Expected Behavior

The L3 distributed program should complete successfully at both `tokens=16` and `tokens=32`. Increasing the number of token tiles from 1 to 2 should not cause AICPU stream synchronization failure.

### Actual Behavior

`tokens=16` passes:

```text
[RUN]   'out' PASS  shape=(4, 16, 129280) dtype=torch.float32
[RUN]   'status' PASS  shape=(4, 1) dtype=torch.int32
[RUN] PASS
```

`tokens=32` fails:

```text
[ERROR] sync_run_streams: [device_runner_base.cpp:877] aclrtSynchronizeStreamWithTimeout (AICPU) failed: 507057
[ERROR] destroy_comm_stream: [device_runner.cpp:173] aclrtSynchronizeStream during stream teardown failed: 507057
RuntimeError: WorkerThread::dispatch_process: child failed (code=1): chip_process dev=11: RuntimeError: run_prepared failed with code 507057
```

`tokens=32 --route-only` passes, so the FP32 route-window path alone does not reproduce the failure.

`tokens=32 --publish-only` also fails in this repro. After the 507057 messages, teardown can hang; the reproduced task may need to be killed to release devices.

### Diagnosis

**pypto runtime / L3 distributed execution**. The failure occurs during on-device L3 distributed execution with `pld.tile.remote_store` and `pld.system.notify/wait`. It is not a parser/codegen/ptoas/pto-isa issue: the program compiles, `tokens=16` runs, and the route-only control at `tokens=32` runs.

### Git Commit ID

`3f421313f02777267cdd48ba1e134e51ecf03b9e`

### Environment

| Component | Version |
|---|---|
| pypto-lib | `49f8d7c` (branch: `temp`, dirty: local repro script plus unrelated lm_head debug edits) |
| pypto | `3f421313` (branch: `main`, dirty: unrelated local loader fallback patch in `distributed_runner.py`; this repro uses `host_orch` and does not depend on it) |
| pypto runtime (submodule) | `48980572` |
| pto-isa | `8bd3ac8f` (branch: `main`) |
| ptoas | `0.43` |
| CANN | `9.0.0` (`Ascend-cann-toolkit`, path `/usr/local/Ascend/cann-9.0.0`) |
| Python | `3.10.20` |
| Torch | `2.11.0+cpu` |

### NPU Kind

Ascend 910B

### Host Platform

Linux (aarch64)

### Additional Context

The issue surfaced while validating DeepSeek-V4 `lm_head` DP/EP-owner hidden handoff to TP logits route. The original full path failed at `TP=4, tokens=32`; this minimal repro removes model math and isolates the distributed runtime traffic pattern.
