title: [Bug] Orchestration cross-assigns __ssa_v aliases for multiple in-place outputs of an inlined InCore scope
body:
### Component
Codegen

### Description
When an `@pl.jit.inline` kernel is inlined into a `@pl.jit` caller and writes
several output tensors **in place inside one `pl.at(level=pl.Level.CORE_GROUP)`
(= ScopeStmt InCore) scope via tile `pl.store`**, those tensors are classified
`add_inout`, and the orchestration codegen emits post-write SSA aliases
(`<name>__ssa_v1`) that are **cross-assigned to the wrong source tensors**.
Downstream consumers then read a completely unrelated tensor — a silent
miscompile producing NaN/Inf and a runtime 507018 (AICPU chip fault).

This is the same cross-assignment class as the (closed) #1573, but a distinct
trigger: #1573 is about 3+ outer-loop **carries** (`__phi` nodes) in a
`pl.parallel`/`pl.range` loop; here there is no loop carry — they are plain
in-place outputs of an inlined kernel, and the scrambled aliases are `__ssa_v1`,
not `__phi`. It still reproduces on current `main` (0ac36c0f, which includes
#1573's closure).

### Steps to Reproduce
In pypto-lib, convert `dispatch_ep` in `models/deepseek/v4/dispatch.py` from
`@pl.jit.incore` to `@pl.jit.inline`, writing the recv_*_out outputs in place
inside one `pl.at(CORE_GROUP)` scope, with `recv_scale_out` / `recv_w_out`
written via tile `pl.store` (TROWSUM form). Then:

    python models/deepseek/v4/moe_ep.py -d 0,1   # 2-rank EP, 2 NPUs

`recv_scale_out` and `recv_w_out` are `[N_LOCAL, RECV_MAX]` FP32; both written
via tile `pl.store` of full rows -> classified `add_inout`.

### Expected Behavior
Each in-place output's post-write alias references itself, e.g.:

    recv_scale_out__ssa_v1 = recv_scale_out;
    recv_w_out__ssa_v1     = recv_w_out;

### Actual Behavior
Generated `next_levels/moe_ep/orchestration/moe_ep.cpp`:

    // Task 12: dispatch_ep  (params add_inout recv_scale_out, recv_w_out, ...)
    ...
    const Tensor& recv_w_out__ssa_v1   = recv_count_out;   // WRONG (int32 count)
    const Tensor& recv_scale_out__ssa_v1 = ext_recv_x;     // WRONG (FP16 recv_x window)
    ...
    params_t13.add_input(recv_scale_out__ssa_v1);   // exp_gate_up dequant reads recv_x window
    params_t15.add_input(recv_w_out__ssa_v1);       // exp_w2 reads recv_count_out

-> expert_routed dequant reads garbage -> x_next NaN=246680 Inf=1126612, or
RuntimeError 507018. The kernel<->call arg order is otherwise consistent
(verified e.g. v2 = pub_counts). Outputs written write-only via scalar
`pl.write` are classified `add_output`, get no `__ssa_v1`, and are read
correctly via the original handle — that is the current workaround
(recv_count_out / recv_r_route_out always did this).

### Git Commit ID
0ac36c0f

### NPU Kind
Ascend 910B

### Host Platform
Linux (aarch64)

### Additional Context
Related: #1573 (loop-carry __phi scramble, closed), #1463 / #1390 (out-window
multi-output alias collisions), #1580 (phi naming swap). Surfaced converting
dsv4 EP dispatch_ep/combine_ep to `@pl.jit.inline` (enabled by #1670 + #1685).
Environment: pypto 0ac36c0f, runtime 48980572, ptoas 0.43, pto-isa 8bd3ac8f.

title: [Pass Bug] ConvertTensorToTileOps rejects a DistributedTensor (window) slice inside an InCore scope
body:
### Pass Name
ConvertTensorToTileOps

### Description
#1685/#1672 made `tensor.slice` / `assemble` / slice-assign accept a
`pld.DistributedTensor` (window) for local access at the tensor/type level. But
ConvertTensorToTileOps still rejects a window slice when it appears **inside an
InCore scope** (`pl.at(CORE_GROUP)`), so the assemble idiom can't be used for
window staging copies inside an InCore kernel — one must fall back to
`pl.load`/`pl.store` (tiles) or scalar `pl.read`/`pl.write`.

### Git Commit ID
0ac36c0f

### Before IR (Input)
A slice-assign copying column 0 of a padded window into an output column,
authored inside an InCore scope:

    # recv_scale: pld.DistributedTensor[[N_LOCAL*RECV_MAX, W_PAD], pl.FP32] (window)
    # recv_scale_out_flat: pl.Tensor[[N_LOCAL*RECV_MAX, 1], pl.FP32]
    with pl.at(level=pl.Level.CORE_GROUP, name_hint="dispatch_ep"):
        ...
        recv_scale_out_flat[:, :] = recv_scale[:, 0:1]   # window slice (local read)

### Expected IR (After Transformation)
The local window slice lowers like a plain `Tensor` slice (the window is local
GM on this rank), producing a valid tile/GM copy — the same way the op is
accepted at the tensor/type level after #1685.

### Actual IR or Error

    pypto.InternalError: tensor.slice conversion: unexpected input type: DistributedTensorType
      at models/deepseek/v4/dispatch.py:291:8
    Check failed: unreachable at src/ir/transforms/op_conversion_registry.cpp:307
      File "src/ir/transforms/convert_tensor_to_tile_ops_pass.cpp", line 1777
      File "src/ir/transforms/convert_tensor_to_tile_ops_pass.cpp", line 1321

Moving the same slice-assign OUTSIDE the InCore scope (to orchestration level)
compiles, but then produces wrong values at runtime (the orchestration lowers it
to `ext_recv_scale.view([M,1],[0,0])` + copy; appears to mishandle the strided
column view / ordering) — likely a separate, related gap worth noting.

### NPU Kind (if relevant)
Ascend 910B

### Host Platform (if relevant)
Linux (aarch64)

### Additional Context
Related: #1672 / #1685 (closed; enabled window local tensor ops at the type
level), #1670 (window write->read ordering), #1693 (the multi-output SSA
scramble found in the same conversion). Surfaced converting dsv4 dispatch_ep to
`@pl.jit.inline`. Environment: pypto 0ac36c0f, ptoas 0.43, pto-isa 8bd3ac8f.

title: [Bug] Orchestration codegen does not hoist a manual_scope-internal tensor's SSA alias, breaking after-scope readers ("was not declared in this scope")
body:
### Component

Codegen

### Description

The orchestration C++ codegen emits a tensor's SSA-versioned `const Tensor&` alias at the **current indentation** — i.e. inside the deep `PTO2_SCOPE(MANUAL) { ... }` block when the producing write is inside a `pl.manual_scope` — with **no live-out / hoisting analysis**. When a task placed **after** the `manual_scope` reads that tensor, the generated `add_input(<name>__ssa_v<N>)` is emitted at the outer indent and references the now-out-of-scope alias, so the orchestration `.cpp` fails to C++-compile:

```
error: '<name>__ssa_v<N>' was not declared in this scope
```

This blocks any optimization that moves a consumer of a `manual_scope` `pl.assemble` output to after the scope (e.g. fusing an MLP-tail residual-add / `down_cast_residual`-style writer into an after-scope auto-dep writer).

Atomic/inout tensors are unaffected: their producer-call alias is bound in the outer function body (atomic-add does not mint a deep downstream SSA version), so the after-scope reader resolves to an outer alias. A plain (non-atomic) `pl.assemble` inside the scope mints a new SSA version aliased at deep indent, which dies when the block closes.

**Why it is easy to miss:** `compile_for_test` / `--smoke` generate the orchestration `.cpp` but do **not** C++-compile it, so they pass. The error only surfaces when the `.cpp` is C++-compiled — i.e. a real device dispatch / orchestration C++ build.

Related: #1693 (orchestration codegen `__ssa_v` alias cross-assignment).

### Steps to Reproduce

Self-contained minimal repro (`repro_manual_scope_hoist.py`): a tensor created **before** `pl.manual_scope`, written **inside** it, read by a `pl.at` task **after** it.

```python
import torch
import pypto.language as pl
from pypto.backend import BackendType, set_backend_type
from pypto.runtime import RunConfig

M, N = 16, 256

@pl.jit
def repro(x: pl.Tensor, out: pl.Out[pl.Tensor]):
    acc = pl.create_tensor([M, N], dtype=pl.FP32)  # atomic-written  (works)
    buf = pl.create_tensor([M, N], dtype=pl.FP32)  # plain-assemble-written (breaks)
    tids = pl.array.create(1, pl.TASK_ID)           # hoisted outside manual_scope (correct usage)

    with pl.at(level=pl.Level.CORE_GROUP, name_hint="seed") as seed_tid:
        acc = pl.assemble(acc, pl.full([M, N], dtype=pl.FP32, value=0.0), [0, 0])

    with pl.manual_scope():
        with pl.at(level=pl.Level.CORE_GROUP, name_hint="producer", deps=[seed_tid]) as ptid:
            acc = pl.assemble(acc, pl.full([M, N], dtype=pl.FP32, value=1.0), [0, 0], atomic=pl.AtomicType.Add)
            buf = pl.assemble(buf, pl.slice(x, [M, N], [0, 0]), [0, 0])
        tids[0] = ptid

    # AFTER manual_scope: read both acc (atomic, OK) and buf (assemble, bug)
    with pl.at(level=pl.Level.CORE_GROUP, name_hint="consumer", deps=[tids[0]]):
        out = pl.assemble(out, pl.add(pl.slice(acc, [M, N], [0, 0]), pl.slice(buf, [M, N], [0, 0])), [0, 0])
    return out

if __name__ == "__main__":
    set_backend_type(BackendType.Ascend910B)
    x = torch.randn(M, N, dtype=torch.float32); out = torch.zeros(M, N, dtype=torch.float32)
    repro.compile_for_test(x, out)   # PASSES — generates .cpp but does NOT C++-compile it
    cfg = RunConfig(platform="a2a3", device_id=0, backend_type=BackendType.Ascend910B)
    repro(x, out, config=cfg)        # FAILS at the orchestration C++ compile (host-side, before device use)
```

Run: `PYTHONPATH=python python repro_manual_scope_hoist.py`

The generated `repro.cpp` declares `acc__ssa_v2` / `buf__ssa_v1` **inside** the `PTO2_SCOPE(MANUAL) {` block, while the `consumer` task reads them at the outer indent after the block closes.

### Expected Behavior

The orchestration `.cpp` should C++-compile. A tensor created before a `manual_scope`, written inside it, and read by a task after the scope must have its `const Tensor&` alias visible (hoisted) at the after-scope reader — the same way atomic/inout tensors already are.

### Actual Behavior

```
RuntimeError: Orchestration compilation failed with exit code 1:
repro.cpp:68:29: error: 'acc__ssa_v2' was not declared in this scope
         params_t2.add_input(acc__ssa_v2);
repro.cpp:69:29: error: 'buf__ssa_v1' was not declared in this scope
         params_t2.add_input(buf__ssa_v1);
```

(In the real decode_layer fusion the failure was `'post_norm_partial_inline289__rv_v14' was not declared in this scope`; `down_acc_all` — atomic — compiled fine.)

### Git Commit ID

3f421313f02777267cdd48ba1e134e51ecf03b9e

### NPU Kind

N/A (not hardware-specific)

### Host Platform

Linux (aarch64)

### Additional Context

**Root cause** (`src/codegen/orchestration/orchestration_codegen.cpp`):
- `EmitTensorAlias` (line 2417) emits `const Tensor& <name>__ssa_v<N> = ...;` at **line 2424** using the current `Indent()` — the deep manual_scope block — with no hoisting.
- `VisitStmt_(RuntimeScopeStmtPtr)` (lines 792-821) is the C++ `{ }` scope boundary the alias cannot escape.
- The after-scope reader's `add_input(...)` (`GenerateFunctionCallCode`, ~line 2201) names the out-of-scope alias.
- Same duplicate emit at line 2670 (`GenerateSubmitReturnAliases`).

**Suggested fix:** in `EmitTensorAlias` (and line 2670), when `mutable_tensor_name_scopes_.size() > 1` (inside a nested scope), buffer the `const Tensor& <alias> = <out_name>;` and flush it at function-body scope (after `SetInitialIndent`, ~line 3036) instead of at the deep indent — with a hoisted pointer-holder fallback when `out_name` is not itself body-scope-valid. Alias names are already globally unique (`ReserveUniqueName`). Read-only views, so no semantic change; needs golden `.cpp`/`.pto` updates + an orchestration-codegen test re-run to confirm the atomic path is unchanged.

title: Support multi-program dispatch for DistributedCompiledProgram
body:
## Feature request

`DistributedCompiledProgram` should support a multi-program runtime/worker flow so several compiled HOST programs can be prepared on one L3 worker and dispatched independently while sharing the same child process and device-resident memory.

Reference implementation PR: https://github.com/hw-native-sys/pypto/pull/1699

## Motivation

Serving-style generation needs to dispatch Qwen3 prefill and decode JIT HOST programs through the same L3 worker. Prefill writes the KV cache and decode consumes/updates the same KV cache, so the runtime needs one shared worker lifecycle and one worker-resident `DeviceTensor` KV cache across multiple compiled programs.

Without first-class multi-program support, callers must either create a worker per compiled program, which loses shared device-resident state, or fall back to host-backed KV buffers, which adds expensive host/device traffic and degrades decode throughput.

## Desired behavior

- Allow multiple `DistributedCompiledProgram` objects with compatible distributed configs to be prepared on the same L3 worker.
- Register each program's chip callables, sub-worker functions, orchestration entry, base tensors, and parameter metadata independently.
- Provide an API like `worker.run(compiled_program, *args)` that dispatches a selected program on the shared worker.
- Preserve existing single-program behavior and `worker(*args)` compatibility for the primary program.
- Keep worker-resident `DeviceTensor` inputs valid across dispatches from different programs.

## Constraints / validation

Compatible programs should use the same platform, runtime, and device ids. The reference PR implements this by validating compatibility, keeping per-program dispatch state, and preserving single-program compatibility.

title: [Bug] Orchestration codegen aliases a multi-output spmd scope's return value to the wrong output tensor (out_indices[0] fallback) -> numel-mismatched reshape -> 507018
body:
### Component

Codegen

### Description

When a fanned-out `pl.spmd` scope writes **multiple** GM output tensors and the
function's return value is one of the **non-first** outputs, the orchestration
codegen aliases the scope's returned SSA value to the **wrong** output tensor.
Downstream the wrong tensor is reshaped to the return shape; because the two
tensors have different element counts, the AICPU runtime hits
`debug_assert(valid_reshape(...))` (`runtime/.../runtime/tensor.h:435`,
`valid_reshape() = numel()==product(new_shapes)`). The asserting executor thread
aborts that subtask, it never writes FIN, the producer task never reaches
COMPLETED, its consumers' fan-in never closes, the scheduler latches the
GLOBAL_STUCK timeout (`sched_error_code=100`), and the host surfaces it as
`aclrtSynchronizeStreamWithTimeout (AICPU) failed: 507018`. A kernel-side shape
bug thus masquerades as a scheduler deadlock.

**Root cause (pinned):** `GenerateSingleReturnAlias`
(`src/codegen/orchestration/orchestration_codegen.cpp:2446`):

```cpp
auto returned_idx = FindReturnedParamIndex(callee, program_);
size_t param_idx = returned_idx.value_or(out_indices[0]);  // <-- falls back to FIRST output
EmitTensorAlias(var_name, call, param_idx);
```

For a multi-output `pl.spmd` scope, `FindReturnedParamIndex` returns `nullopt`
(a Spmd wrapper has no traceable top-level `ReturnStmt`), so `param_idx` falls
back to `out_indices[0]` = the **first** Out/InOut arg — but the actually
returned value is a **later** output. The returned SSA value should instead be
aliased to the output arg that shares its SSA base / buffer root.

This is the same **class** as #1573 (closed) and #1693, but a distinct trigger
and code path: #1573 is `__phi` loop carries; #1693 is `__ssa_v1` in-place
outputs of an inlined `pl.at(CORE_GROUP)` InCore scope; **this** is the
`__rv_v` *return-value* alias of a `pl.spmd` scope via the
`GenerateSingleReturnAlias` `out_indices[0]` fallback.

Related: #1693, #1573, #1650, #631

### Steps to Reproduce

In pypto-lib, take the DeepSeek-V4 `hc_pre` kernel fused into **3** `pl.spmd`
scopes where the **second** scope (`hc_post`) writes three GM outputs in one
fanned-out spmd task — `pre_val_gm` (inout), `post` (inout), and `x_mixed`
(output, the function's return) — e.g. `hc_pre_fused_draft.py` with `mix_x`
fused into `hc_post`. The function ends with
`x_mixed = pl.reshape(x_mixed_view, [B, S, D]); return x_mixed`.

```
python models/deepseek/v4/repro_hc_pre_blocker2_selfraw_507018.py -p a2a3
```

(Real `FLASH` config: T=128, D=4096, HC_DIM=16384, MIX_HC=24. Run via
`task-submit` on an a2a3 device; the kernel compiles cleanly and deadlocks at
runtime with 507018.)

The 4-spmd variant (mix_x as its **own** scope, so `x_mixed` is that scope's
sole output) passes — confirming the trigger is the multi-output scope, not the
data flow.

### Expected Behavior

The scope's returned SSA value aliases to the output arg it is actually a new
SSA version of:

```cpp
const Tensor& x_mixed_view_inline52__rv_v2 = x_mixed_view_inline52;   // the x_mixed output
```

### Actual Behavior

Generated `orchestration/hc_pre_test.cpp` (multi-output `hc_post` Submit):

```cpp
// hc_post Submit outputs:
params_t1.add_inout(pre_val_gm_inline83);      // [2]  shape [128, 8]   numel = 1024
params_t1.add_inout(post_2d_inline73);         // [3]
params_t1.add_output(x_mixed_view_inline52);   // [4]  shape [128, 4096]  (== x_mixed)
rt_submit_aiv_task(2, params_t1);

const Tensor& x_mixed_view_inline52__rv_v2 = pre_val_gm_inline83;     // WRONG: aliased to output [2]

uint32_t x_mixed_v1_inline4_shapes[3] = {64, 2, 4096};               // numel = 524288
Tensor x_mixed_v1_inline4 = x_mixed_view_inline52__rv_v2.reshape(x_mixed_v1_inline4_shapes, 3);
```

`pre_val_gm` is `[128, 8]` (numel 1024); reshaping it to `[64, 2, 4096]`
(numel 524288) fails `valid_reshape` → AICPU subtask abort → scheduler
GLOBAL_STUCK → host `507018` (`sched_error_code=100 runtime_status=-100`).

Device log (a2a3, two independent task-submit-locked runs):

```
[ERROR] AICPU ... assert_impl "Assertion failed: valid_reshape(new_shapes, new_ndims)"
[ERROR] AICPU ... "Location: runtime/.../tensormap_and_ringbuffer/runtime/tensor.h:435"
        Stack: AicpuExecutor::run -> aicpu_execute -> simpler_aicpu_exec
```

### Git Commit ID

3f421313 (pypto, branch main)

### NPU Kind

Ascend 910B

### Host Platform

Linux (aarch64)

### Additional Context

Fix direction: in `GenerateSingleReturnAlias` (and the analogous tuple/Submit
paths), map the returned SSA result to the output arg sharing its SSA
base/buffer root, instead of the `out_indices[0]` fallback when
`FindReturnedParamIndex` is empty for a Group/Spmd wrapper. See
`.claude/rules/pass-submit-awareness.md` (Submit tuple-return aliasing).

Two secondary observations surfaced while diagnosing this:

1. **Diagnosability:** an AICPU-side `debug_assert(valid_reshape)` aborts the
   subtask silently and the failure only appears as a scheduler 507018/507046
   stream-sync timeout. Printing `numel()` / `new_shapes` / `new_ndims` /
   `kernel_id` at `tensor.h:435` (and latching a distinct error code instead of
   GLOBAL_STUCK when an executor subtask aborts) would point straight at the
   kernel instead of looking like a scheduler deadlock.

2. **Latent (separate):** `next_block_idx` is a non-atomic `int16_t` mutated by a
   concurrent read-modify-write across scheduler threads
   (`scheduler_dispatch.cpp:311-318`) — a real data race at `aicpu_thread_num>1`,
   though it is NOT this failure (the dispatch trace shows all blocks dispatched).

title: [Bug] Distributed codegen misses Submit callees in next-level program extraction
body:
### Component

Codegen

### Description

Distributed PTO backend codegen can drop child task functions that are referenced through orchestration `Submit` expressions instead of normal `Call` nodes. The generated next-level program then omits functions that the orchestration still references, so validation fails when compiling a JIT decode kernel that submits helper kernels such as `down_seed`.

This is reproducible on current PyPTO `origin/main` without a local `_CallCollector.visit_expr(Submit)` hook. Adding Submit callee collection makes the same serving generation compile and run.

### Steps to Reproduce

From `/data/liuxu/pypto-serving`, with PyPTO installed from `hw-native-sys/pypto` commit `0944c7b11e95029d079ca4a8c591744421ee4bb1` but without the local Submit collector hook in `python/pypto/backend/pto_backend.py`:

```bash
task-submit --device auto --max-time 900 --run "cd /data/liuxu/pypto-serving && PTO2_RING_HEAP=4294967296 PTO2_RING_TASK_WINDOW=1048576 PTO2_RING_DEP_POOL=1048576 SA_PROFILE_OUTPUT=offline_5_without_submit_collector_trace.json SA_PROFILE_LEVEL=kernel python examples/model/qwen3_14b/npu_generate.py --model-dir /data/linyifan/models/Qwen3-14B --prompt 'Huawei is' --platform a2a3 --max-seq-len 512 --max-new-tokens 5 --profile --device-id {}"
```

The generated error report is at:

```text
/data/liuxu/pypto-serving/build_output/_jit_qwen3_decode_host_20260609_140851/next_levels/decode_fwd/report/codegen_errors.txt
```

### Expected Behavior

The distributed backend should include all GlobalVar callees reachable through `Submit` expressions in the generated child/next-level program. `decode_fwd` should compile successfully, including helper functions such as `down_seed`, `gate_seed`, `up_seed`, and `out_seed` when they are submitted by orchestration.

### Actual Behavior

Compilation fails during distributed backend generation for `decode_fwd`:

```text
Failed to generate orchestration 'decode_fwd': Internal error: function 'down_seed' not found after validation. [/data/liuxu/pypto-serving/pypto-lib/models/qwen3/14b/decode_layer.py:608:4]
Check failed: callee_func != nullptr at /data/liuxu/pypto/src/codegen/orchestration/orchestration_codegen.cpp:2174
```

The summarized report says:

```text
1 function(s) failed to compile:

  Function    | Error
  ------------+--------------------------------------------------------------
  decode_fwd  | Internal error: function 'down_seed' not found after
              | validation. [/data/liuxu/pypto-serving/pypto-
              | lib/models/qwen3/14b/decode_layer.py:608:4]
```

### Git Commit ID

`0944c7b11e95029d079ca4a8c591744421ee4bb1`

### NPU Kind

Other (please specify in description)

Ascend910 shown by `npu-smi`; this appears to be a distributed codegen issue rather than hardware-specific.

### Host Platform

Linux (aarch64)

### Additional Context

The likely root cause is that `_CallCollector` in `python/pypto/backend/pto_backend.py` only records `GlobalVar` callees from normal `Call` nodes. In this generated IR, helper kernels are referenced through `Submit` expressions, so they are not included in the next-level chip program even though orchestration still submits them.

A local one-method fix was enough to make the same generation compile and pass 128-token decode:

```python
def visit_expr(self, expr: _ir_core.Expr) -> None:
    if isinstance(expr, _ir_core.Submit) and isinstance(expr.op, _ir_core.GlobalVar):
        self.callee_names.append(expr.op.name)
    super().visit_expr(expr)
```

With that hook restored, `/data/liuxu/pypto-serving` PR #29 completed a 128-token generation run with 127 decode steps.

title: [Bug] Distributed host codegen drops rank-slice materialization for device child without distributed args
body:
### Component

Codegen

### Description

A distributed host orchestrator can submit a per-rank child with rank-sliced tensor arguments and `device=r`:

```python
for r in pl.range(pld.world_size()):
    self.child(x[r], y[r], device=r)
```

If the child has no `pld.DistributedTensor` / `pld.window` argument, the generated `host_orch.py` references temporary rank-slice tensors such as `t__tmp_v1` and `t__tmp_v2`, but never materializes them. Runtime then fails with `KeyError: 't__tmp_v1'`.

Adding an unused dummy distributed window argument to the child makes the generated host code materialize the same rank slices before building `TaskArgs`, and the program passes. This looks like a distributed host codegen/materialization bug rather than a model issue.

Related but not duplicate:

- #1349 tracks broader rank-reducing slice codegen work. This repro shows the rank slice is generated correctly on the distributed-child-argument path but omitted on the no-distributed-argument path.
- #1579 was another missing materialization bug, but for `pl.spmd` composite dynamic `core_num`, not distributed host child tensor slices.
- #1707 and #1691 are different distributed codegen/runtime failures.

### Steps to Reproduce

Save the following script as `repro_rank_slice_dummy.py` in a checkout that can import `pypto` and the local golden runner, then run the commands below.

<details>
<summary>Minimal repro script</summary>

```python
import argparse

import pypto.language as pl
import pypto.language.distributed as pld
from pypto.ir.distributed_compiled_program import DistributedConfig


N_RANKS = 2
ROWS = 16
COLS = 32


def build_program(*, with_dummy: bool):
    if with_dummy:
        return build_program_with_dummy()
    return build_program_no_dummy()


def build_program_no_dummy():
    @pl.program
    class RankSliceNoDummyRepro:
        @pl.function(type=pl.FunctionType.InCore)
        def add_one(
            self,
            x: pl.Tensor[[ROWS, COLS], pl.FP32],
            y: pl.Out[pl.Tensor[[ROWS, COLS], pl.FP32]],
        ) -> pl.Tensor[[ROWS, COLS], pl.FP32]:
            for row in pl.parallel(ROWS):
                x_row = pl.slice(x, [1, COLS], [row, 0])
                y_row = pl.add(x_row, 1.0)
                y = pl.assemble(y, y_row, [row, 0])
            return y

        @pl.function(type=pl.FunctionType.Orchestration)
        def child(
            self,
            x: pl.Tensor[[ROWS, COLS], pl.FP32],
            y: pl.Out[pl.Tensor[[ROWS, COLS], pl.FP32]],
        ) -> pl.Tensor[[ROWS, COLS], pl.FP32]:
            y = self.add_one(x, y)
            return y

        @pl.function(level=pl.Level.HOST, role=pl.Role.Orchestrator)
        def host_orch(
            self,
            x: pl.Tensor[[N_RANKS, ROWS, COLS], pl.FP32],
            y: pl.Out[pl.Tensor[[N_RANKS, ROWS, COLS], pl.FP32]],
        ):
            for r in pl.range(pld.world_size()):
                self.child(x[r], y[r], device=r)

    return RankSliceNoDummyRepro


def build_program_with_dummy():
    @pl.program
    class RankSliceWithDummyRepro:
        @pl.function(type=pl.FunctionType.InCore)
        def add_one(
            self,
            x: pl.Tensor[[ROWS, COLS], pl.FP32],
            y: pl.Out[pl.Tensor[[ROWS, COLS], pl.FP32]],
        ) -> pl.Tensor[[ROWS, COLS], pl.FP32]:
            for row in pl.parallel(ROWS):
                x_row = pl.slice(x, [1, COLS], [row, 0])
                y_row = pl.add(x_row, 1.0)
                y = pl.assemble(y, y_row, [row, 0])
            return y

        @pl.function(type=pl.FunctionType.Orchestration)
        def child(
            self,
            x: pl.Tensor[[ROWS, COLS], pl.FP32],
            y: pl.Out[pl.Tensor[[ROWS, COLS], pl.FP32]],
            _dummy: pld.DistributedTensor[[N_RANKS, 1], pl.INT32],
        ) -> pl.Tensor[[ROWS, COLS], pl.FP32]:
            y = self.add_one(x, y)
            return y

        @pl.function(level=pl.Level.HOST, role=pl.Role.Orchestrator)
        def host_orch(
            self,
            x: pl.Tensor[[N_RANKS, ROWS, COLS], pl.FP32],
            y: pl.Out[pl.Tensor[[N_RANKS, ROWS, COLS], pl.FP32]],
        ):
            dummy_buf = pld.alloc_window_buffer(N_RANKS * 4)
            for r in pl.range(pld.world_size()):
                dummy = pld.window(dummy_buf, [N_RANKS, 1], dtype=pl.INT32)
                self.child(x[r], y[r], dummy, device=r)

    return RankSliceWithDummyRepro


def build_specs():
    import torch
    from golden import TensorSpec

    return [
        TensorSpec("x", [N_RANKS, ROWS, COLS], torch.float32, init_value=torch.randn),
        TensorSpec("y", [N_RANKS, ROWS, COLS], torch.float32, is_output=True),
    ]


def golden(values):
    values["y"][:] = values["x"] + 1.0


def main():
    from golden import run

    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    parser.add_argument("-p", "--platform", default="a2a3", choices=["a2a3", "a2a3sim", "a5", "a5sim"])
    parser.add_argument("-d", "--device", default="0,1", help="comma-separated device ids; need at least 2")
    parser.add_argument("--with-dummy", action="store_true")
    parser.add_argument("--compile-only", action="store_true")
    args = parser.parse_args()

    device_ids = [int(device) for device in args.device.split(",")]
    assert len(device_ids) >= N_RANKS, f"need at least {N_RANKS} devices, got {device_ids}"

    result = run(
        program=build_program(with_dummy=args.with_dummy),
        specs=build_specs(),
        golden_fn=golden,
        compile_only=args.compile_only,
        compile_cfg=dict(
            distributed_config=DistributedConfig(
                device_ids=device_ids[:N_RANKS],
                num_sub_workers=0,
            ),
        ),
        runtime_cfg=dict(platform=args.platform),
        rtol=1e-5,
        atol=1e-5,
    )
    if not result.passed:
        if result.error:
            print(result.error)
        raise SystemExit(1)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
```

</details>

Compile-only passes for both variants:

```bash
python repro_rank_slice_dummy.py -p a2a3 --compile-only -d 0,1
python repro_rank_slice_dummy.py -p a2a3 --compile-only --with-dummy -d 0,1
```

Run the failing no-dummy case on two devices:

```bash
task-submit --device auto --device-num 2 --run "python repro_rank_slice_dummy.py -p a2a3 -d {}"
```

Run the passing dummy control:

```bash
task-submit --device auto --device-num 2 --run "python repro_rank_slice_dummy.py -p a2a3 --with-dummy -d {}"
```

### Expected Behavior

The no-dummy and with-dummy variants should both materialize `x[r]` and `y[r]` rank slices before submitting the child task. A child that does not otherwise use distributed windows should still be callable with `device=r` from a distributed host orchestrator.

### Actual Behavior

The no-dummy variant compiles but fails at runtime before the child task can run:

```text
[RUN] compile done
[RUN] runtime ...
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "build_output/RankSliceNoDummyRepro_*/orchestration/host_orch.py", line 12, in host_orch
    _ta_0.add_tensor(make_tensor_arg(tensors["t__tmp_v1"]), TensorArgType.INPUT)
KeyError: 't__tmp_v1'
```

The generated no-dummy `host_orch.py` references temporary tensors without creating them:

```python
def host_orch(orch, _args, config, *, tensors, callables, sub_ids, _keep, world_size):
    t__tmp_v0 = world_size
    for r__idx_v0 in range(0, t__tmp_v0, 1):
        _ta_0 = TaskArgs()
        _ta_0.add_tensor(make_tensor_arg(tensors["t__tmp_v1"]), TensorArgType.INPUT)
        _ta_0.add_tensor(make_tensor_arg(tensors["t__tmp_v2"]), TensorArgType.OUTPUT_EXISTING)
        _keep.append(_ta_0)
        orch.submit_next_level(callables["child"], _ta_0, config, worker=r__idx_v0)
```

The with-dummy control passes:

```text
[RUN]   'y' PASS  shape=(2, 16, 32) dtype=torch.float32
[RUN] PASS
```

Its generated `host_orch.py` first materializes the rank slices, then builds `TaskArgs`:

```python
tensors["t__tmp_v1"] = tensors["x__ssa_v0"][r__idx_v0, 0:16, 0:32]
tensors["t__tmp_v2"] = tensors["y__ssa_v0"][r__idx_v0, 0:16, 0:32]
_ta_0.add_tensor(make_tensor_arg(tensors["t__tmp_v1"]), TensorArgType.INPUT)
_ta_0.add_tensor(make_tensor_arg(tensors["t__tmp_v2"]), TensorArgType.OUTPUT_EXISTING)
```

### Git Commit ID

`778dae483dcb3640d69bd271a39a5c8bc17a8b81`

### NPU Kind

N/A (not hardware-specific)

This is reproduced through the distributed `a2a3` runner, but the failure is a generated Python host-orchestration `KeyError` before device kernels do meaningful work.

### Host Platform

Linux (aarch64)

### Additional Context

Diagnosis: **pypto codegen / distributed host orchestration**. The failing program compiles, and the only difference between failing and passing variants is whether the child has an unused distributed window argument.

Observed local evidence:

- no-dummy task: `task_20260609_151815_734577963`, devices `5,7`, failed with `KeyError: 't__tmp_v1'`.
- with-dummy task: `task_20260609_151832_73935324595`, devices `7,9`, passed in `6.25s`.

Environment used for reproduction:

| Component | Version |
|---|---|

title: [Bug] Host-composed child kernels with duplicate name_hint fail instead of auto-disambiguating outlined function names
body:
### Component

Codegen

### Description

When two child kernels reuse the same `@pl.jit.inline` helper, each child can compile independently. However, composing those child kernels in one `@pl.jit.host` program can fail during `OutlineIncoreScopes` if the shared inline helper contains an incore scope with a fixed `name_hint`.

The outlined functions are inserted into one program/global function namespace without suffix-disambiguating duplicate names. In practice, the duplicate `name_hint` often comes from legitimate helper reuse, not from two unrelated code blocks accidentally choosing the same string.

This shows up when building a larger host orchestration from independently runnable pieces. For example, a decode-layer host that composes SWA attention and MoE EP has both subgraphs reusing HC helper code such as `hc_pre` / `hc_post`; those helpers contain common scopes such as `name_hint="linear"`. Each subgraph compiles independently, but the composed host fails with `Duplicate function name "linear"`.

The minimal repro below removes the model logic. It has two child kernels, `single_a` and `single_b`, both calling the same `@pl.jit.inline` helper `shared_helper`. That inline helper contains `name_hint="dup_scope"`. Each child compiles by itself. The host-composed version fails with `Duplicate function name "dup_scope"`.

Diagnosis: **pypto codegen / IR pass**. The failure occurs during pass execution before PTOAS/device execution:

```text
ValueError: Duplicate function name "dup_scope"
Check failed: function_names.find(name) == function_names.end() at src/ir/program.cpp:40
...
src/ir/transforms/outline_incore_scopes_pass.cpp:108
```

Related but not duplicate:

- #1244 is about printer disambiguation for distinct IR variables that share `name_hint`.
- #1708 is about distributed host codegen dropping rank-slice materialization for a device child without distributed args.

### Steps to Reproduce

Save this script as `repro_duplicate_name_hint_host.py` in a checkout that can import `pypto` and the local golden runner:

```python
import argparse

import pypto.language as pl
from golden import TensorSpec, run_jit
from pypto.ir.distributed_compiled_program import DistributedConfig


N_RANKS = 2
N = 16
TILE_N = 8


@pl.jit.inline
def shared_helper(
    x: pl.Tensor[[N, 1], pl.FP32],
    y: pl.Out[pl.Tensor[[N, 1], pl.FP32]],
    scale: pl.Scalar[pl.FP32],
):
    for b in pl.spmd(N // TILE_N, name_hint="dup_scope"):
        i = b * TILE_N
        xi = pl.load(x, [i, 0], [TILE_N, 1])
        yi = pl.mul(xi, scale)
        pl.store(yi, [i, 0], y)
    return y


@pl.jit
def single_a(
    x: pl.Tensor[[N, 1], pl.FP32],
    y: pl.Out[pl.Tensor[[N, 1], pl.FP32]],
):
    return shared_helper(x, y, 1.0)


@pl.jit
def single_b(
    x: pl.Tensor[[N, 1], pl.FP32],
    y: pl.Out[pl.Tensor[[N, 1], pl.FP32]],
):
    return shared_helper(x, y, 2.0)


@pl.jit.host
def host_orch(
    x: pl.Tensor[[N_RANKS, N, 1], pl.FP32],
    y_a: pl.Out[pl.Tensor[[N_RANKS, N, 1], pl.FP32]],
    y_b: pl.Out[pl.Tensor[[N_RANKS, N, 1], pl.FP32]],
):
    single_a(x[0], y_a[0], device=0)
    single_b(x[1], y_b[1], device=1)


def single_specs():
    import torch

    return [
        TensorSpec(
            "x",
            [N, 1],
            torch.float32,
            init_value=lambda: torch.arange(N, dtype=torch.float32).reshape(N, 1),
        ),
        TensorSpec("y", [N, 1], torch.float32, is_output=True),
    ]


def host_specs():
    import torch

    return [
        TensorSpec(
            "x",
            [N_RANKS, N, 1],
            torch.float32,
            init_value=lambda: torch.arange(N_RANKS * N, dtype=torch.float32).reshape(N_RANKS, N, 1),
        ),
        TensorSpec("y_a", [N_RANKS, N, 1], torch.float32, is_output=True),
        TensorSpec("y_b", [N_RANKS, N, 1], torch.float32, is_output=True),
    ]


def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    parser.add_argument("case", choices=["single-a", "single-b", "host"])
    parser.add_argument("-d", "--device", default="0,1")
    args = parser.parse_args()

    if args.case == "single-a":
        fn = single_a
        specs = single_specs()
        compile_cfg = None
    elif args.case == "single-b":
        fn = single_b
        specs = single_specs()
        compile_cfg = None
    else:
        fn = host_orch
        specs = host_specs()
        device_ids = [int(d) for d in args.device.split(",")]
        compile_cfg = {
            "distributed_config": DistributedConfig(
                device_ids=device_ids[:N_RANKS],
                num_sub_workers=0,
            ),
        }

    result = run_jit(
        fn=fn,
        specs=specs,
        compile_only=True,
        compile_cfg=compile_cfg,
    )
    if not result.passed:
        if result.error:
            print(result.error)
        raise SystemExit(1)
    print(f"{args.case}: compile passed")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
```

Run the standalone controls:

```bash
python repro_duplicate_name_hint_host.py single-a
python repro_duplicate_name_hint_host.py single-b
```

Observed:

```text
single-a: compile passed
single-b: compile passed
```

Run the host-composed case:

```bash
python repro_duplicate_name_hint_host.py host -d 0,1
```

### Expected Behavior

The host-composed program should compile. PyPTO should automatically disambiguate duplicate outlined function names produced from identical `name_hint` values, especially when they come from the same reused `@pl.jit.inline` helper. A stable suffix such as `_0`, `_1`, or parent/call-site context would be enough.

User code should not need to copy/re-wrap reusable inline helpers and manually rename every internal `name_hint` just because independently valid kernels are composed into a larger host orchestration.

### Actual Behavior

The host-composed case fails during pass execution:

```text
[RUN] compile ...
[RUN] compile done
Traceback (most recent call last):
  ...
  File "pypto/ir/pass_manager.py", line 356, in run_passes
    return self._pipeline.run(input_ir)
ValueError: Duplicate function name "dup_scope"
Check failed: function_names.find(name) == function_names.end() at src/ir/program.cpp:40

C++ Traceback (most recent call last):
 ...
 File "src/ir/transforms/outline_incore_scopes_pass.cpp", line 108
 File "src/ir/program.cpp", line 40
```

### Git Commit ID

`778dae483dcb3640d69bd271a39a5c8bc17a8b81`

### NPU Kind

N/A (not hardware-specific)

This reproduces in compile-only mode before device execution.

### Host Platform

Linux (aarch64)

### Additional Context

Environment used for reproduction:

| Component | Version |
|---|---|
| pypto-lib | `006673b6745a80ab4adc6055b84838609010948e` |
| pypto | `778dae483dcb3640d69bd271a39a5c8bc17a8b81` (branch: `main`) |
| pypto runtime (submodule) | `48980572b3537df4ed5e6d9720cb6162939eb58a` |
| pto-isa | `8e436661958d934be9fb1706c9ecc4a5c827d675` (branch: `main`) |
| ptoas | `0.44` |
| CANN | `not detected` |
| Python | `3.10.20` |

This blocks composing independently runnable model subgraphs in one host program. The current workaround is to copy/re-wrap helpers and manually give one side unique `name_hint` values, but that is brittle and defeats helper reuse.

title: [Bug] manual_scope cross-scope aliasing (#1705) incomplete: windowed (.view) write value-root not remapped, after-scope reader still fails C++ compile
body:
### Component

Codegen

### Description

Follow-up to #1697 (fixed by #1705). #1705 ("resolve manual_scope cross-scope tensors; unify output aliasing on remap") resolved the plain-`pl.assemble` and atomic/inout cases, but **one path remains broken**: a tensor created before a `pl.manual_scope`, written **inside** it via the **OptimizeOrchTensors Pattern-5 windowed-write** path (`.view()` window externalization), and read by a task **after** the scope, still fails the orchestration C++ compile:

```
error: '<name>__rv_v<N>' was not declared in this scope
```

The remaining trigger is specifically the **windowed write**: it roots the tensor's SSA-version chain at a **block-local `Tensor` value** (`<name>__rv_v2 = <base>;`, a `Tensor` by value, not a `const Tensor&` alias), declared *inside* the `PTO2_SCOPE(MANUAL)` block. #1705's remap follows `const Tensor&` alias chains to an enclosing-scope source, but **stops at that block-local value** — it does not chase the final hop (`value = base`) to the outer base — so the after-scope reader names the deep `__rv_v<N>` alias, which is out of scope.

Contrast (same generated `.cpp`): an atomic/inout tensor with **no** windowing is remapped to its outer base name and compiles fine.

Related: #1697 (closed), #1705 (partial fix), #1693 (inlined-scope `__ssa_v` cross-assignment, different trigger).

### Steps to Reproduce

```bash
# in a checkout at/after the #1705 fix:
python decode2l_embed_lmhead.py --model-dir <ckpt> --kv-dir <kv> --device <n> --validate --fused
```

`decode2l_embed_lmhead.py --fused` uses `decode_layer_fused.py`, which moves the MLP-tail residual-add (`down_cast_residual`) out of `manual_scope` into a single after-scope auto-dep writer that reads `post_norm_partial` (the residual `h1`, written inside the scope by `residual_rms_cast`).

NOTE: a standalone `@pl.jit` repro using a plain `pl.assemble` (no windowing) now **passes** after #1705 — so a faithful standalone repro must trigger the Pattern-5 windowed-write path. The concrete artifact is the generated `decode_fwd.cpp` from the command above.

### Expected Behavior

The orchestration `.cpp` should C++-compile. A manual_scope-internal tensor that becomes live-out should have its final version resolvable at the after-scope reader — regardless of whether it was written via a plain assemble (already handled by #1705) or via a Pattern-5 windowed `.view()` write.

### Actual Behavior

Generated `decode_fwd.cpp` (from `decode2l_embed_lmhead.py --fused`):

```
decode_fwd.cpp:977:46: error: 'post_norm_partial_inline265__rv_v14' was not declared in this scope
         params_t30.add_input(post_norm_partial_inline265__rv_v14);
RuntimeError: Orchestration compilation failed with exit code 1
```

Version-chain evidence in that file:

```
line 143 (outer):  const Tensor& down_acc_all_inline74 = alloc_2.get_ref(1);          // atomic, NO windowing -> works (Task 30 add_input(down_acc_all_inline74))
line 148 (outer):  const Tensor& post_norm_partial_inline265 = alloc_2.get_ref(6);    // base
line 319:          PTO2_SCOPE(PTO2ScopeMode::MANUAL) {                                 // manual scope opens
lines 375-381:       ... post_norm_partial_inline265__ssa_v0__window = post_norm_partial_inline265.view(...)   // Pattern-5 windowed write
line 405:            Tensor post_norm_partial_inline265__rv_v2 = post_norm_partial_inline265;   // BLOCK-LOCAL VALUE (chain root)
line 456/507/558/609: const Tensor& __rv_v5/v8/v11/v14 = <prev>;                       // chain, all inside the manual scope
line ~798:         }                                                                   // manual scope closes
line 977:          params_t30.add_input(post_norm_partial_inline265__rv_v14);          // after-scope reader -> __rv_v14 out of scope
```

`post_norm_partial` has 5 `.view()`/window references; `down_acc_all` has 0 — confirming the windowed-write path is the differentiator.

### Git Commit ID

61d289da00c5d931d0fe25f5bedffdda11cf9f77

### NPU Kind

N/A (not hardware-specific)

### Host Platform

Linux (aarch64)

### Additional Context

**Fix direction:** in the same `EmitTensorAlias` / output-remap logic touched by #1705 (`src/codegen/orchestration/orchestration_codegen.cpp`), the remap that resolves a manual_scope-internal alias to its enclosing-scope source must **chase through the block-local `Tensor` value root** (`<name>__rv_v2 = <base>;`) to the outer `<base>` — OR the windowed-write codegen should root its SSA chain at the enclosing base rather than emitting a block-local `Tensor` value. Either way the after-scope reader should resolve to the outer base name (as the atomic path already does).

**Impact:** blocks fusing a `manual_scope` MLP-tail output (e.g. `down_cast_residual` reading `post_norm_partial`) into an after-scope auto-dep writer — i.e. removing the redundant `out_consolidate` copy in the qwen3 decode kernel.

title: [Bug] Fused multi-output spmd scope miscompiles: per-head tile buffers coalesce → wrong results
body:
### Component

Codegen

### Description

When a per-token reduction like `mix_x` (`x_mixed[t] = Σ_h pre[t,h]·x[t,h,:]`) is computed in the **same** multi-output `pl.spmd` scope as other outputs (here `pre`/`post`), the generated AIV kernel computes that output **wrong** (~97.9% of elements off, small systematic error), while the other outputs (`post`, `comb`) in the same scope are correct. The **identical** source placed in its **own** `pl.spmd` scope produces correct results.

At least two distinct codegen defects surface only in the fused context:

1. **Per-head scale buffer coalescing.** The four per-head scales `pre_h = pl.reshape(pre_eps_t[h:h+1, :], [TILE, 1])` (rows of a transposed `[TILE, HC_PAD]` tile) are all allocated at the **same** UB address in the fused scope, so all four `row_expand_mul`s read head 0's coefficient. In a separate scope the same code gets distinct addresses.

   ```
   pre_h alloc addr (ptoas/*.pto):
     fused hc_post   : 74304, 74304, 74304, 74304   ← all coalesced
     separate hc_mix_x: 32768, 32832, 32896, 32960   ← distinct (base +0/+64/+128/+192), correct
   ```

2. **Residual wrongness after forcing distinct buffers.** Materializing each scale into its own buffer (`pre_h = pl.mul(pl.reshape(...), 1.0)`) makes the four addresses distinct (verified `512/576/640/704`) and the generated mix_x then looks **structurally correct** (subviews read rows 0/1/2/3, four distinct x head-slabs, four distinct `trowexpandmul`s), yet the output is **still ~97.9% wrong** on board. This residual defect is not visible at the UB-address level and is **not yet root-caused** — likely the transposed-tile data itself, or a numerical/dependency path specific to the single fused task.

Most-likely area: AIV tile memory-reuse / `pto.subview`+`reshape` of a transposed tile under UB pressure in a fused scope (the InitMemref / MemoryReuse / LegalizePtoBufferReuse / AllocateMemoryAddr pass chain).

### Steps to Reproduce

Using pypto-lib `models/deepseek/v4/verify_1702_fused_tileform.py` (fuses `mix_x` into the `hc_post` spmd scope):

1. On-board: `task-submit --device auto --run "python models/deepseek/v4/verify_1702_fused_tileform.py -p a2a3"` → `'x_mixed' FAIL ratio=97.94%`, `'post' PASS`, `'comb' PASS`.
2. Static (no device): run the same script locally — it dumps kernels before failing at `rtSetDevice`. Then compare per-head scale buffer addresses:
   ```
   grep -E 'pre[0-3]_inline[0-9]+__ssa_v0 = pto.alloc_tile' build_output/_jit_*/ptoas/hc_post.pto      # fused: identical base addr
   # vs the separate-scope draft (hc_pre_fused_draft.py):
   grep -E 'pre[0-3]_inline[0-9]+__tile = pto.alloc_tile'   build_output/_jit_*/ptoas/hc_mix_x.pto       # distinct addrs
   ```

### Expected Behavior

A multi-output spmd scope that computes a per-head reduction (transpose → per-row `reshape` to `[TILE,1]` → `row_expand_mul`) produces the same correct result whether that reduction is fused into a shared scope or placed in its own scope. Per-head scale buffers must get distinct addresses and the per-head coefficients must be applied correctly.

### Actual Behavior

In the fused scope the per-head scale buffers coalesce to one UB address (all heads read head 0), and even after forcing distinct buffers the fused output remains ~97.9% wrong. The same code in a separate scope is correct.

### Git Commit ID

7fe857a895078333dd95fdc8ab915f733664c063

### NPU Kind

Other (please specify in description) — observed on pypto-lib `--platform a2a3`. Root cause is codegen address allocation (deterministic in the dumped `.pto`), not silicon-specific.

### Host Platform

Linux (aarch64)

### Additional Context

- Related: #1702, #1693, #1573 (same family — orchestration/codegen mis-aliasing of multi-output scopes; distinct triggers).
- Workaround / fallback: keeping `mix_x` in its **own** spmd scope works correctly (3-spmd "Path A" and the 4-spmd draft both pass). This blocks only the further 2-spmd fusion.
- Severity: medium (correct fallback exists).

title: [Pass Bug] Orchestration marks pld.tensor.put dst window as add_input, dropping its write deps
body:
### Pass Name

Orchestration codegen (task Arg direction derivation for distributed ops)

### Description

When an InCore scope pushes to a peer's window via `pld.tensor.put`, orchestration codegen declares the **dst** `DistributedTensor` window as `add_input`. The dst of a put is a cross-rank **write** target, so the task graph records no write on the window: a downstream task that reads the same window gets a read-read pair (no RAW edge) and can run before the push completes, reading stale window data.

`pld.tile.remote_store` to the same window correctly emits `add_output`, so the identical kernel with the push expressed as `pl.load` + `remote_store` is race-free.

Found in DeepSeek-V4 2-rank EP MoE (pypto-lib `models/deepseek/v4/combine.py`): `combine_push` pushes `recv_y` rows to the peer's `routed_y_buf` window, then `combine_reduce` (separate spmd task) reads `routed_y_buf`. With the put form, `combine_reduce` races ahead of `combine_push` → wrong values with shifting locations (~10-30% of points off, validation fails). With `remote_store`, repeated PASS.

### Git Commit ID

454ecc9ab0e0843ffd89e03124e75b82a9d71cd2

### Before IR

InCore scope (jit.inline pl.at, simplified):

```python
with pl.at(level=pl.Level.CORE_GROUP, name_hint="combine_push"):
    ...
    pld.tensor.put(dst=routed_y_buf, peer=dst, src=recv_y_flat,
                   dst_offsets=[r_route, 0], src_offsets=[idx_lin, 0], shape=[1, D])
    # notify/wait barrier on combine_done ...

for tb in pl.spmd(T // 4, name_hint="combine_reduce"):
    ...  # reads routed_y_buf
```

### Expected IR

Generated orchestration declares the put dst window as a write (same as remote_store form):

```cpp
// Task 16: combine_push
params_t16.add_input(recv_y_flat...);
params_t16.add_output(ext_routed_y_buf);   // write recorded -> RAW edge to combine_reduce
```

### Actual IR / Error

```cpp
// Task 16: combine_push
params_t16.add_input(ext_routed_y_buf);    // dst window declared as input
params_t16.add_input(recv_y_flat...);
```

`combine_reduce` (`add_input(ext_routed_y_buf)`) then has no dependency on `combine_push` and reads the window before the push lands. On 2x a2a3 devices the model output fails ratio_reldiff with errors scattered across rows; flipping only the push back to `pld.tile.remote_store` (dst emitted as `add_output`) passes consistently.

### NPU Kind

Ascend 910B (a2a3, 2 devices)

### Host Platform

Linux (aarch64)

title: inline sub-functions cannot contain hand-placed scopes (auto_scope=False not inheritable) — blocks manual 4-ring tuning
body:
## Summary

Hand-placed runtime scopes (`with pl.scope()`) cannot be used inside `@pl.jit.inline` sub-functions: the inline decorator rejects `auto_scope=`, and the JIT specializer always re-emits inline functions as `@pl.function(type=pl.FunctionType.Inline)` without an auto_scope suffix. As a result, any model whose kernels are structured with inline sub-functions (the standard layout for layered LLMs) cannot do manual ring-level tuning at all — the only workaround is hand-inlining the whole sub-function into the entry.

## Context / motivation

The PTO2 runtime supports max 4 scope levels (4 HeapRings). With default `auto_scope=True`, compiler-placed AUTO scopes for deep loop nests (7 levels in Qwen3-14B `prefill_fwd`) collapse all inner levels into ring 3 — measured via scope_stats: ring3 carries 1.39 GB / 27.7k task-window slots while r0–r2 sit at ~0%. Hand-placing 4 balanced scopes (entry implicit + layer / token-block / token) reduces ring3 task-window pressure ~38% and moves ~10.5k slots to r0/r2. We could only realize this after manually inlining `prefill_layer` (~460 lines) into the entry.

## Reproduction

```python
@pl.jit.inline
def layer(...):
    for p0_idx in pl.range(tok_blocks):
        with pl.scope():     # Error: a hand-placed AUTO 'with pl.scope()' requires @pl.function(auto_scope=False)
            ...

@pl.jit(auto_scope=False)
def entry(...):
    for layer_idx in pl.range(n):
        with pl.scope():
            layer(...)
```

`@pl.jit.inline(auto_scope=False)` raises:
`TypeError: @pl.jit.inline does not accept an auto_scope= argument`

Patching the runtime flag does not help because the specializer re-parses from source:
- `pypto/jit/decorator.py:1794` — sub-decorators reject `auto_scope=`
- `pypto/jit/specializer.py:1641` — `if ctx.func_type == "inline": return "@pl.function(type=pl.FunctionType.Inline)"` (drops `auto_scope_suffix`)
- `pypto/language/parser/ast_parser.py:3412` — parse-time check rejects hand AUTO scope when flag is true

## Proposed fix

Let inline sub-functions inherit (or accept) the caller's `auto_scope` flag:
1. allow `auto_scope=` on `@pl.jit.inline` (or propagate caller's flag at specialize time — `build_specialize_context(auto_scope=dep._auto_scope)` already plumbs it),
2. emit the suffix in the specializer inline branch: `@pl.function(type=pl.FunctionType.Inline{auto_scope_suffix})`.

Scope semantics are unchanged — after inlining the body, scopes land inside the entry, exactly like the hand-inlined workaround.

## Environment

pypto main 2693682e, simpler 48980572, Qwen3-14B prefill_fwd (pypto-lib 65871d8), a2a3.

title: No way to create/retype tensors with symbolic dynamic dims — loop-carried hidden state forces per-layer copy-back
body:
## Summary

There is no way to create (or retype) a tensor whose dynamic dim carries the same *symbolic* dynamic var as a parameter, so a loop-carried hidden-state variable cannot be reassigned across layers once a sub-function boundary is removed. This blocks the natural ping-pong pattern and forces a full copy-back per layer.

## Reproduction

```python
PREFILL_TOKENS_DYN = pl.dynamic("PREFILL_TOKENS_DYN")

@pl.jit(auto_scope=False)
def entry(hidden_states: pl.Tensor[[PREFILL_TOKENS_DYN, HIDDEN], pl.BF16], ...):
    prefill_tokens = pl.tensor.dim(hidden_states, 0)
    for layer_idx in pl.range(num_layers):
        nxt = pl.create_tensor([prefill_tokens, HIDDEN], dtype=pl.BF16)
        ...  # compute layer into nxt
        hidden_states = nxt
        # Error: Cannot reassign 'hidden_states' with a different type:
        #   was pl.Tensor[[PREFILL_TOKENS_DYN, 5120], BF16],
        #   got pl.Tensor[[pl.tensor.dim(hidden_states, 0), 5120], BF16]
```

Attempted workarounds, all rejected:
- `pl.create_tensor([PREFILL_TOKENS_DYN, HIDDEN])` — dim is recorded as the runtime expression, not the symbolic var, so the types still differ.
- `nxt.bind_dynamic(0, PREFILL_TOKENS_DYN)` on a created tensor — `bind_dynamic` is parameter-only / unsupported there.
- A tiny `@pl.jit.inline` retype shim with the symbolic return annotation — the specializer substitutes the actual dim expression at the inline boundary, so the result type is again the expression.

The only working pattern is per-layer copy-back (`pl.assemble` of every tile into the parameter buffer), costing tokens x hidden x 2B of extra write traffic per layer. Inline sub-functions used to launder the type at the call boundary (callee param re-anchors to the symbolic dyn), which is why the original `prefill_layer` structure compiled — remove the boundary and the limitation surfaces.

## Proposed capability

Either:
1. let `pl.create_tensor` accept symbolic dyn vars and record them as the dim type, or
2. unify the type checker so `pl.tensor.dim(param, 0)` is recognized as equal to the param's symbolic dyn dim, or
3. provide an explicit `pl.retype(t, [PREFILL_TOKENS_DYN, HIDDEN])`.

## Environment

pypto main 2693682e, simpler 48980572, Qwen3-14B prefill_fwd (pypto-lib 65871d8), a2a3.

title: [Bug] #1702 follow-up: 507018 still triggers in a separate decoder model after PR #1718 — multi-output spmd return aliasing in additional code paths
body:
**Repository**: `hw-native-sys/pypto` > Filed as a follow-up after locally verifying PR #1718 against an internal > 45-layer decoder model on Ascend a2a3 (real device, single rank, dummy > weights). The orchestration codegen + chip_orch compile chain are **green** > end-to-end, chip workers come up cleanly, and 19 InCore kernels link, but > the very first AICPU stream synchronize still produces > `aclrtSynchronizeStreamWithTimeout (AICPU) failed: 507018`. The PR's author > explicitly noted on commit `0f4881cb` that "tuple / `__ssa_v1` / `__phi` > paths are untouched" — we believe one of those paths is what this model > hits. ## Summary PR #1718 (commits `80845cdf` + `0f4881cb`) fixed `GenerateSingleReturnAlias` and `VarLineageCollector::VisitStmt_(AssignStmt)` to disambiguate a multi-Out spmd-scope return via the result Var's SSA base, replacing the blind `out_indices[0]` fallback. That fix is correct and validated on the DeepSeek-V4 `hc_pre + mix_x` kernel cited in the PR commit message. **It does not fix the 507018 we hit on a separate decoder model**, which uses sibling InCore patterns that the SSA-base disambiguation cannot uniquely resolve (or that go through one of the explicitly-untouched lineage paths). The downstream symptom is identical to the dsv4 trigger that PR #1718 fixes: all kernels and orchestration compile, the chip becomes `ready`, then the very first stream sync poisons the device with 507018 and `aclrtResetDeviceForce` is needed to unstick the card. Per the original #1702 root-cause write-up, this strongly suggests another instance of the same family (orchestration mis-aliasing a multi-output scope to the wrong output, kernel emits a shape that fails `valid_reshape` on AICPU, scope never FINs, scheduler latches GLOBAL_STUCK). ## What PR #1718 fixes (recap, for context) From the PR's own commit messages: - `80845cdf` — In `GenerateSingleReturnAlias`, when the result Var's SSA base uniquely matches one Out/InOut arg, use that mapping instead of the unreliable `FindReturnedParamIndex().value_or(out_indices[0])`. Validated on board against the DeepSeek-V4 `hc_pre` kernel fused with `mix_x` in the same multi-output spmd scope. - `0f4881cb` — Apply the same SSA-base disambiguation in `VarLineageCollector::VisitStmt_(AssignStmt)` (the lineage-tracer sibling path), and add two regression tests in `tests/ut/codegen/test_spmd_scope_tid_codegen.py`. The commit message of `80845cdf` explicitly notes: > Same family as #1573 / #1693 (orchestration mis-aliasing multi-output > scopes), distinct trigger and code path; **those paths > (tuple / `__ssa_v1` / `__phi`) are untouched**. ## What still fails (post-merge, on board) After ff-merging PR #1718 into `main` and rebuilding the Python package, a single-rank single-layer decode through our internal model (TP=8/EP=8 layer on `device_ids=[0]`, `--dummy-weights`) reaches kernel exec but immediately poisons the AICPU on first sync. ### Environment | Component | Pin | |---|---| | pypto | `main` at `0f4881cb` (PR #1718 ff-merged) | | simpler runtime (submodule) | `afb5c5a9` (origin/main, with a local `runtime_compiler.py` host-strip patch — unrelated to this issue) | | pto-isa | `109c9f72` | | PTOAS binary | `v0.44` | | Python | 3.11.14 (`--system-site-packages` over CANN's torch_npu 2.9.0) | | CANN | 9.0.0-beta.1 | | Driver | 25.5.1 | | Hardware | Ascend 910B (a2a3) — 8-card pod, this run uses logical `device_ids=[0]` | ### Reproducer (model command, no isolated minimal repro) > The PR's own commit message acknowledges that this family does **not** > reproduce in a standalone `@pl.program` UT — "it only triggers through the > jit.inline + tail-appended `create_tensor`-scratch path that this kernel > exercises" — and that a faithful regression test was tracked as a follow-up. > The same isolation difficulty applies to our trigger: any standalone scope > we extract drops the surrounding orchestration that drives > `FindReturnedParamIndex` to nullopt + ambiguous SSA base. The reproducer > below uses the full model command; we are happy to bisect further if > instrumentation guidance helps. The model in question (an internal 45-layer MoE/dense-mix decoder with TP=8, EP=8 wave fan-out) is in our private fork; if you can suggest specific orchestration-pass dump flags that would let us pinpoint the offending scope without sharing the model code, we will run them and attach the output. Compile chain that succeeds (sanitized log): ``` V5 [Incore] Compiling (AIC): .../kernels/aic/full_k_proj.cpp V5 [Incore] Compiling (AIC): .../kernels/aic/full_q_proj.cpp V5 [Incore] Compiling (AIC): .../kernels/aic/full_gate_proj.cpp V5 [Incore] Compiling (AIV): .../kernels/aiv/full_out_proj_aiv.cpp V5 [Incore] Compiling (AIV): .../kernels/aiv/full_head_gate.cpp V5 [Incore] Compiling (AIV): .../kernels/aiv/dense_down_proj_tp_aiv.cpp V5 [Incore] Compiling (AIV): .../kernels/aiv/full_out_resid_add.cpp V5 [Incore] Compiling (AIV): .../kernels/aiv/dense_residual_add_tp.cpp V5 [Incore] Compiling (AIV): .../kernels/aiv/dense_gate_up_silu_tp_aiv.cpp V5 [Incore] Compiling (AIC): .../kernels/aic/dense_gate_up_silu_tp_aic.cpp V5 [Incore] Compiling (AIC): .../kernels/aic/full_v_proj.cpp V5 [Incore] Compiling (AIV): .../kernels/aiv/tp_all_reduce.cpp V5 [Incore] Compiling (AIV): .../kernels/aiv/full_qk_norm_zc.cpp V5 [Incore] Compiling (AIC): .../kernels/aic/dense_down_proj_tp_aic.cpp V5 [Incore] Compiling (AIV): .../kernels/aiv/full_rope_kv_cache.cpp V5 [Incore] Compiling (AIC): .../kernels/aic/full_fa_fused_aic.cpp V5 [Incore] Compiling (AIV): .../kernels/aiv/dense_post_rmsnorm_zc.cpp V5 [Incore] Compiling (AIV): .../kernels/aiv/full_rmsnorm_zc.cpp V5 [Incore] Compiling (AIV): .../kernels/aiv/full_fa_fused_aiv.cpp V5 [Incore] Compiling (AIC): .../kernels/aic/full_out_proj_aic.cpp V5 [Orchestration] Compiling: .../orchestration/chip_orch.cpp ... 19 InCore objects emitted, all successful (sizes 115k..463k bytes) V5 [Orchestration] Compilation .../chip_orch.cpp.orch_*.so successful: 738120 bytes [chip_process pid=

dev=0] ready ``` Failure (immediate, on first AICPU sync): ``` [ERROR] sync_run_streams: [device_runner_base.cpp:877] aclrtSynchronizeStreamWithTimeout (AICPU) failed: 507018 [ERROR] recover_device_or_mark_unusable: [device_runner.cpp:456] Device unrecoverable after AICore error 507018: aclrtSynchronizeDeviceWithTimeout failed: 507046. Marking DeviceRunner unusable; run() will fail fast and finalize() will force-reset the card (a soft in-process reset does not clear the poison). [WARN] force_reset_device: [device_runner.cpp:553] force_reset_device: aclrtResetDeviceForce(0) cleared the poisoned card RuntimeError: WorkerThread::dispatch_process: child failed (code=1): chip_process dev=0: RuntimeError: run_prepared failed with code 507018 ``` The 2-second gap between the AICPU 507018 and the `recover_device_or_mark_unusable` line is the same scheduler-stuck signature documented in PR #1718's commit message (scope never FINs → GLOBAL_STUCK latches → host-side timeout). The kernel side and the orchestration side both compiled cleanly through the same passes the dsv4 case goes through; this is not a new error class, just a new trigger of the existing family. ## Suspected scope class The 19 InCore kernels above include several with multi-output, same-shape returns that are good candidates for the untouched `tuple` / `__ssa_v1` / `__phi` paths called out on commit `0f4881cb`. From a static read: - `dense_gate_up_silu_tp_aic` / `..._aiv` — TP-sliced fused (gate, up, silu) tile emits two same-shape (or near-same-shape) GM outputs from a single InCore scope; if the outliner appends scratch/`create_tensor` tails the way the dsv4 kernel did, the same `out_indices[0]` blind fallback could fire. - `tp_all_reduce` — ring all-reduce body has multi-window writes (signal + data) that are different shapes but share an SSA-renamed parent through the per-step phi. - `full_qk_norm_zc` — fused (q-norm, k-norm) with two same-shape outputs. - `full_rope_kv_cache` — co-emits q-rotated, k-rotated, KV-cache slot writes. - MoE dispatch / combine / routed-expert paths — multi-rank fan-out scopes that each return multiple per-expert buffers (this run does not exercise the MoE path because layer 0 is `full_dense`, but the same family applies). We have not yet bisected which of these is the actual offender. The simplest in-house path is to port the dsv4 PR #474 workaround pattern (scalar `pl.write` → `add_output`) into each candidate, but that's a model-side band-aid for a codegen-side root cause and is exactly what PR #1718 was supposed to make unnecessary. ## Suggested fix direction The PR explicitly carves out three sibling lineage paths as untouched — **tuple**, **`__ssa_v1`**, and **`__phi`**. Extending the SSA-base disambiguation introduced in PR #1718 to those paths (or, conversely, hardening every consumer of the lineage tracer / `GenerateSingleReturnAlias` result so it cannot silently fall back to `out_indices[0]` when the SSA base fails to uniquely resolve) would close the family completely. Two concrete asks: 1. Could the team look at whether the PR #1718 SSA-base check can be propagated into `VarLineageCollector` for the tuple/phi/`__ssa_v1` cases — the same pattern (uniquely-matching Out/InOut arg by SSA root) should apply. 2. If a kernel that hits this latches the device with `force_reset_device` needed (vs. a clean Python exception), it would help us a lot if the AICPU diagnostic could surface the **scope name** that failed `valid_reshape` — currently we only see `507018` host-side, with no pointer to which `chip_orch.cpp` line emitted the bad reshape. ## What we tried locally - Verified PR #1718 ff-merges cleanly onto current `main` (`a1b066df`, origin/main as of 2026-06-09), no submodule pin shift. - Rebuilt pypto under Python 3.11 (`pip install --no-build-isolation .`). - Confirmed our smoke probe and an a2a3sim compile of the full layer chain are still green after the merge. - Single-rank, dummy-weights dispatch on a real Ascend a2a3 still produces the 507018 above. ## References - PR #1718 — `fix(codegen): also resolve multi-output spmd return in the lineage tracer; add regression tests (#1702)` - Issue #1702 — original SSA aliasing report (the same downstream symptom we still observe). - Issue #1693 — the predecessor in the same family. - Issue #1573 — earlier in the same family. - DeepSeek-V4 PR #474 — the model-side scalar `pl.write` → `add_output` workaround that some downstream models use to avoid the family entirely. We can attach a sanitized full plog or run a one-off instrumentation patch on our pod if it would help triage. Thanks for getting #1702 across the line at the dsv4 site — happy to chase the residual cases together.

title: [Pass Bug] AutoDeriveTaskDependencies demotes user-written pl.manual_scope() to AUTO when deps go through a pl.array of TaskIds → full serialization
body:
### Pass Name

AutoDeriveTaskDependencies

### Description

Since PR #1701 (commit `f9a9e5b1`), `AutoDeriveTaskDependencies` analyzes **user-written `pl.manual_scope()`** bodies in the default pipeline. Hand-tuned MPMD kernels commonly express dependencies by collecting per-iteration TaskIds from a `pl.parallel` / `pl.at` fan-out into a `pl.array.create(..., pl.TASK_ID)`, then referencing them downstream as `deps=[arr[i], ...]`.

The pass cannot resolve a TaskId **array-element** dep (`arr[i]`) back to the loop producer's TaskId var, so for every real RAW/WAW hazard against a loop-fanned producer it computes `covered_by_user_edge=false`. Because that producer is `dynamic_producer=true` (inside a loop), it triggers the `dynamic_prior_producer_requires_scope_lift` fallback, which **strips the scope and demotes it to `manual=false` (AUTO)**.

Once the scope is AUTO, runtime TensorMap/OverlapMap tracking re-engages. The model's tasks atomic-add / `assemble` into shared buffers with overlapping regions, so the runtime conservatively serializes every writer — i.e. the entire scope runs **fully serial**, which is exactly what the user wrote `pl.manual_scope()` to avoid.

Net effect: a valid, idiomatic manual scope (explicit `deps=` only, no runtime tracking) silently loses all its parallelism. The user's `deps=[arr[i]]` edges are correct and complete; the pass just can't statically match them.

### Git Commit ID

f9a9e5b1434b580904dece31e933f2e17a2c5bec

### Before IR (Input)

Condensed structure that triggers the demotion (a real Qwen3-14B decode layer hits this in 4 separate manual scopes). The key shape is: TaskId array + `pl.parallel` producer fan-out writing a shared buffer + a downstream consumer that depends on the producers via `deps=[arr[i]]`.

```python
import pypto.language as pl

@pl.program
class Before:
    @pl.function
    def main(self, x: pl.Tensor[[128, 512], pl.BF16],
             w: pl.Tensor[[512, 512], pl.BF16],
             acc: pl.Tensor[[128, 512], pl.FP32]) -> None:
        with pl.manual_scope():
            prod_tids = pl.array.create(4, pl.TASK_ID)
            # producer fan-out: 4 tasks each atomic-add a column block of `acc`
            for n in pl.parallel(4):
                n0 = n * 128
                with pl.at(level=pl.Level.CORE_GROUP, name_hint="producer") as p_tid:
                    c = pl.matmul(x, w[:, n0:n0 + 128], out_dtype=pl.FP32)
                    acc = pl.assemble(acc, c, [0, n0], atomic=pl.AtomicType.Add)
                prod_tids[n] = p_tid               # collect per-iteration TaskId

            # consumer reads ALL of `acc` (true RAW) and depends on the producers
            # ONLY through the TaskId array elements — this is what the pass can't match
            with pl.at(level=pl.Level.CORE_GROUP, name_hint="consumer",
                       deps=[prod_tids[0], prod_tids[1], prod_tids[2], prod_tids[3]]):
                s = pl.row_sum(pl.mul(acc, acc))
                # ... uses s ...
```

### Expected IR (After Transformation)

The `pl.manual_scope()` stays **MANUAL**. The pass adds no compiler edges (the user already covered the hazard via the array deps) and does **not** demote the scope:

```text
RuntimeScopeStmt(manual=True, name_hint="...")
  # producer / consumer tasks keep their user deps=[prod_tids[...]]
  # no compiler_manual_dep_edges added; scope is NOT lifted to AUTO
```

Codegen then emits `PTO2_SCOPE(PTO2ScopeMode::MANUAL)`, runtime TensorMap/OverlapMap tracking stays suppressed, and the fan-out runs in parallel as authored. (Equivalent to pre-#1701 behavior for this scope.)

### Actual IR or Error

Every manual scope is demoted to AUTO; `compiler_manual_dep_edges` is empty everywhere:

```text
=== SCOPE AUTO:.../AUTO:...  (tasks..., user_edges=N, compiler_edges=0) ===   # was MANUAL
RuntimeScopeStmt(manual=False, ...)   # demoted; PTO2_SCOPE() instead of PTO2_SCOPE(MANUAL)
```

With `PYPTO_AUTO_DEPS_LOOP_CARRY_DEBUG=1`, the pass logs the cause for each downstream consumer:

```text
hazard call=consumer prior_task_id=p_tid_..._ssa_v0 covered_by_user_edge=false dynamic_producer=true
fallback_reason=dynamic_prior_producer_requires_scope_lift call=consumer
```

Real-model evidence (Qwen3-14B decode `qwen3_decode_mpmd`, compiled via `compile_for_test`): all 4 manual scopes fall back; consumers `residual_rms_cast{,_0..3}__windowed`, `post_rms_reduce`, `silu`, `down_cast_residual` each report `dynamic_prior_producer_requires_scope_lift` with `covered_by_user_edge=false` against loop producers `out_tid` / `gate_tid` / `down_tid`.

Fallback decision site: `src/ir/transforms/auto_derive_task_dependencies_pass.cpp:973` (the `covered_by_user_edge` check + `dynamic_producer` lift). The matcher `CanonicalizeTaskIds` / `LookupTaskIdForVar` has no lineage for `pl.array` TaskId store/load, so `deps=[arr[i]]` never canonicalizes to the producer var.

### NPU Kind (if relevant)

N/A (not hardware-specific) — the demotion happens in the IR pass; the serialization manifests at runtime but is independent of NPU arch.

### Host Platform (if relevant)

N/A (not hardware-specific)

### Additional Context

**Why model-side can't work around it:** the producers are fundamentally a `pl.parallel` fan-out (tens of tasks), so their TaskIds can only be collected via a `pl.array`; the consumer genuinely reads the whole shared buffer (true RAW, not separable). There is also no switch to skip manual-scope analysis — `analyze_auto_scopes_for_deps` only gates AUTO scopes, and the pass reads only the `PYPTO_AUTO_DEPS_LOOP_CARRY_DEBUG` debug env var.

**Suggested fixes (for discussion):**
1. Teach the pass to resolve TaskId-array element deps: track `pl.array` TASK_ID store/load lineage so `deps=[arr[i]]` (filled by `arr[i] = producer_tid`) canonicalizes to the producer TaskId. Then `covered_by_user_edge=true`, no fallback, scope stays MANUAL — model unchanged.
2. Add an opt-out (e.g. `derive_manual_scope_deps=False` via `RunConfig` / `ir.compile`) so a user-written `pl.manual_scope()` is honored verbatim and never demoted to AUTO (restores pre-#1701 semantics).
3. Design question: should a user's explicit `pl.manual_scope()` be treated as fully user-managed, with AUTO-derivation limited to AUTO / compiler-generated scopes?

Related: RFC #1368 (Automatic manual-scope task dependency derivation) flagged "disjointness can't be proven statically" as an open question; this is a concrete manifestation. Introduced by #1701.

**Reproduction** (no device needed): compile the orchestration via `compile_for_test`, walk each `RuntimeScopeStmt`, and observe `manual=False` with `compiler_edges=0`; re-run with `PYPTO_AUTO_DEPS_LOOP_CARRY_DEBUG=1` to capture the `fallback_reason=dynamic_prior_producer_requires_scope_lift` lines.

title: [Bug] _extract_local_tensor_metas does not track pl.reshape — inline dep resolution fails with reshaped tensors
body:
### Component

Other (please specify in description)

### Description

`_extract_local_tensor_metas` in `python/pypto/jit/decorator.py` tracks metadata for local tensor variables produced inside a JIT function body (`pl.create_tensor`, `pl.slice`, `pl.window`, dep call returns), but **does not track `pl.reshape`**. When a caller reshapes tensors before passing them to an `@pl.jit.inline` dep, the specializer passes stale (pre-reshape) metadata to the inline function's parameter resolution, causing compilation failures.

### Steps to Reproduce

```markdown
@jit.inline
def copy_inline(
    x: pl.Tensor[[128, 128], pl.BF16],
    y: pl.Out[pl.Tensor[[128, 128], pl.BF16]],
):
    with pl.at(level=pl.Level.CORE_GROUP):
        tile = pl.load(x, [0, 0], [128, 128])
        pl.store(tile, [0, 0], y)
    return y

@jit
def reshape_caller(
    x: pl.Tensor[[2, 64, 128], pl.BF16],
    y: pl.Out[pl.Tensor[[2, 64, 128], pl.BF16]],
) -> pl.Tensor[[2, 64, 128], pl.BF16]:
    x_flat = pl.reshape(x, [128, 128])
    y = pl.reshape(y, [128, 128])
    y = copy_inline(x_flat, y)
    y = pl.reshape(y, [2, 64, 128])
    return y
```

### Expected Behavior

`_extract_local_tensor_metas` should track `pl.reshape` results so that the specializer can resolve inline dep parameters correctly. The `_walk` function should have a `"reshape"` dispatch branch alongside `create_tensor`, `slice`, and `window`.

### Actual Behavior

```
ValueError: missing inferred tensor metadata for parameter 'x'
```

The metadata for `x_flat` is never created (no meta at all), and `y` keeps its original parameter shape `(2, 64, 128)` instead of `(128, 128)`.

### Git Commit ID

bda839de6be01e75852f57ef4118c42bd9ef408f

### NPU Kind

N/A (not hardware-specific)

### Host Platform

Linux (aarch64)

### Additional Context

Root cause: the `_walk` function dispatches on `fn.attr` for `pl.*` method calls. It handles `"create_tensor"`, `"slice"`, and `"window"` but has no branch for `"reshape"`. Fix adds a `_reshape_meta` helper that resolves the new shape via `_resolve_shape` and inherits dtype from the source tensor.

title: [Feature] Define DeepSeek V4 KV cache contract for serving integration
body:
## 背景

DeepSeek V4 服务化接入前，需要先把 PyPTO 侧要承载的 KV cache / state metadata contract 定清楚。下面整理 DeepSeek V4 KV cache / state 的目标输入 contract，尽量保留字段边界和讨论结论的完整语义，而不是压缩成简版 tracker。

## 按 Cache 类型整理的目标输入

本节按 KV cache / state 类型整理服务化目标 contract。shape 默认使用
token-major 的调度 batch：

```text
R = num_reqs
T = num_tokens = sum(q_lens)
W = sliding_window
ori_block_size = ordinary sliding-window KV rows per page
cmp_base_block_size = main compressed KV base page size before compression
cmp_page_size = cmp_base_block_size // compress_ratio
idx_base_block_size = CSA indexer KV base page size before compression
idx_page_size = idx_base_block_size // 4
state_block_size = compressor state rows per page
H = num_attention_heads
D = hidden_size
head_dim = DeepSeek V4 MLA row semantic dim, currently 512
idx_head_dim = CSA indexer row semantic dim
C4 = 4
C128 = 128
```

block/page size 定稿：

| 类型 | 目标 contract 口径 | vLLM 对齐口径 | 当前 PyPTO 适配值 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 普通 SWA KV | `ori_block_size = 64` | DeepSeek V4 SWA cache 当前为 64 rows/page | `PY_PTO_BLOCK_SIZE = 128` |
| HCA 主 compressed KV | `cmp_base_block_size = 256`，`cmp_page_size = 2` | `MLAAttentionSpec.storage_block_size = 256 // 128` | 当前 PyPTO tensor 仍用 128 rows/page |
| CSA 主 compressed KV | `cmp_base_block_size = 256`，`cmp_page_size = 64` | `MLAAttentionSpec.storage_block_size = 256 // 4` | 当前 PyPTO tensor 仍用 128 rows/page |
| CSA Indexer KV | `idx_base_block_size = 256`，`idx_page_size = 64` | vLLM V4 indexer backend 支持 base block 256 | 当前 PyPTO tensor 仍用 128 rows/page |
| HCA Compressor State | `state_block_size = 8` | vLLM `DeepseekCompressorStateCache` ratio-128 state block size | `C128_COMPRESSOR_BLOCK_SIZE = 8` |
| CSA Compressor State | `state_block_size = 4` | vLLM `DeepseekCompressorStateCache` ratio-4 state block size | `C4A_COMPRESSOR_BLOCK_SIZE = 4` |

因此服务化接口里不要只暴露一个全局 `block_size`。cache manager 可以内部有统一
allocation policy，但传给 kernel/builder 的 contract 应按 cache 类型使用对应的
`*_page_size` 或 `*_block_size`。

所有 cache 类型共用的基础 metadata：

| 输入 | Shape | Type | 含义 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `q_lens` | `[R]` | `int32` | 每个 request 本轮调度的 query token 数。普通 decode 通常为 1，MTP/verifier 可能大于 1，prefill/chunked prefill 可以变长。 |
| `cu_q_lens` | `[R + 1]` | `int32` | `q_lens` 的前缀和。第 `r` 个 request 的 token 行范围是 `[cu_q_lens[r], cu_q_lens[r + 1])`。等价于 vLLM 的 `query_start_loc`。 |
| `context_lens` | `[R]` | `int32` | 本轮调度 token 可见/写入前，已经 committed 的历史长度。MTP 接受/提交边界需要这个字段。 |
| `kv_seq_lens` | `[R]` | `int32` | 本轮调度后的序列长度。等价于 vLLM 的 `seq_lens`；普通 decode/prefill 下通常是 `context_lens + q_lens`。 |
| `token_to_request` | `[T]` | `int32` | 每个 token-major 行所属的 request id。可以由 `cu_q_lens` 推导，但显式传入可以避免 kernel/builder 里反复展开。 |
| `position_ids` | `[T]` | `int32` or `int64` | 每个 token 的绝对位置，用于 RoPE、compressor boundary 判断和 block-table 查表。 |

### 普通 Sliding-Window KV

持久化 cache 目标形态：

```text
逻辑服务化形态:
ori_kv: [ori_num_blocks, ori_block_size, row_dim]

当前 PyPTO kernel 适配形态:
ori_kv: [ori_num_blocks, PY_PTO_BLOCK_SIZE, 1, head_dim]
```

这里第三维 `1` 是当前 PyPTO kernel 沿用通用 paged-KV 布局时的
`num_kv_heads = 1` 维度，不是服务侧必须暴露的语义。DeepSeek V4 MLA 的普通 KV
本质是每 token 一条 latent KV row。当前 BF16 kernel 的 `row_dim = head_dim`；
后续如果接入 FP8 MLA storage backend，可以把每行 pack 成 vLLM DeepSeek V4 的
584-byte row，但这不应改变逻辑 metadata contract。

| 输入 | Shape | Type | 含义 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `ori_kv` | 逻辑 `[ori_num_blocks, ori_block_size, row_dim]`；当前 PyPTO 适配 `[ori_num_blocks, PY_PTO_BLOCK_SIZE, 1, head_dim]` | 当前为 `bf16`；未来可由 storage backend 决定 | 普通 sliding-window KV 存储。SWA、HCA、CSA attention 都会读写它。 |
