title: Feature: indexed GM-row gather with loop-local / per-iteration indices (paged_gather #1644 is single-shot only)

type.name: Feature
type.description: A request, idea, or new functionality

body:
## Summary

We need an indexed GM-row gather (gather scattered rows of a paged KV pool into UB/L1) that can be driven by **loop-local / per-iteration indices** — usable inside an `spmd` or `pl.range` / `CORE_GROUP` loop where each iteration gathers a different set of rows. The recently merged `pl.paged_gather` (#1644) is exactly the right primitive conceptually, but it is **single-shot only**: its `indices` must be a kernel-input (or otherwise tile-lowering-surviving) tensor used in one call with no enclosing runtime loop. That does not fit per-token sparse attention.

## Motivation

In the DeepSeek-V4 unified decode sparse-attention kernel (`models/deepseek/v4/decode_sparse_attn.py`), the compressed-KV gather is ~half the decode wall. Per token it does a paged lookup `phys = block_table[idx // block_size] * block_size + idx % block_size` and gathers the selected rows — byte-for-byte what `paged_gather` does internally. Fusing it (gather straight into L1, feed the QK/PV matmul, drop the ~84 MB `sparse_kv` GM round-trip) is the single biggest remaining decode optimization.

## What we tried (all rejected)

Calling `pl.paged_gather` with a per-(token, block) index, three index forms:

1. a runtime slice `cmp_logical_idx[g_t:g_t+1, off:off+128]` inside an AIV `pl.spmd`
2. the same slice inside `pl.at(level=pl.Level.CORE_GROUP)` + `pl.range`
3. a freshly **materialized** index — `pl.create_tensor([1, 128], INT32)` written from the slice — inside the CORE_GROUP loop

All three fail at lowering with:

```
pypto.InternalError: tensor.paged_gather: indices must be TensorType
Check failed: idx_type at src/ir/transforms/op_conversion_registry.cpp:1482
```

## Root cause

`paged_gather`'s lowering (op_conversion) runs **after** the tile-lowering passes, so any tensor created or sliced inside a runtime loop has already become a tile / `partition_view` by then and is no longer a `TensorType`. Only tensors that survive tile-lowering (kernel inputs, or top-level tensors used whole with no per-iteration indexing) stay `TensorType`. The ST test (`tests/st/runtime/ops/test_paged_gather.py`) passes precisely because it calls `paged_gather` once, outside any loop, on a kernel-input `idx`.

## Request

Either of:

- **(A)** Extend `paged_gather` so `indices` (and `block_table`) may be **loop-local / per-iteration** tensors — e.g. lower the per-row scalar load loop to read the index from a tile / `partition_view`, or run the conversion before tile-lowering / re-materialize the index at the call site.
- **(B)** Add a tile-level `mgather` (GM-row indexed gather into UB/L1) intended for use **inside** `spmd` / `pl.range`, taking a UB index tile.

Either unblocks fusing the gather into per-token attention. (A) preserves the paged semantics; (B) is the lower-level building block.

## Environment

- pypto `main` (e.g. `3c92d01c`), target a2a3 (Ascend 910B/C).

title: [Bug] codegen: manual_scope TaskId can't be loop-carried into Array[TASK_ID]
body:
### Component

Codegen

### Description

A `TaskId` captured inside `pl.manual_scope()` cannot be loop-carried into a `pl.array(pl.TASK_ID)` across a `pl.range` loop. Orchestration codegen fails with an `INTERNAL_CHECK`:

```
Internal error: scalar yield to array carry must resolve to a TaskId variable registered in manual_task_id_map_
Check failed: tid_binding != nullptr at src/codegen/orchestration/orchestration_codegen.cpp:1389
```

**Root cause.** When a `pl.range` loop carries an `Array[TASK_ID]` whose slots are filled per-iteration by a `pl.parallel` block (the "scalar yield to array carry" path), codegen resolves each yielded tid through `manual_task_id_map_`. A tid produced **inside `pl.manual_scope()`** is not registered there, so the lookup fails. The identical kernel compiles cleanly when the producer runs in the ordinary auto-dep region (no `manual_scope`) — see the contrast below, where the *only* difference is the `with pl.manual_scope():` wrapper.

This looks like the same family as the (closed) #1577 "TaskId array element scalar deps are not registered in auto-scope codegen", but the complementary direction: #1577 was the **read** path (`array.get_element(Array[TASK_ID]) -> Scalar[TASK_ID]` used in `deps=`); this is the **write / loop-carry** path (a `manual_scope` tid yielded into a carried `Array[TASK_ID]`), and it still fails on latest `main` (`3ec5e838`).

**Secondary issue:** `compile_for_test()` *prints* the error but does not raise — the failure only becomes fatal (`PartialCodegenError`) in the device/codegen path. Ideally the frontend would reject this earlier with a clear user-facing diagnostic instead of an `INTERNAL_CHECK`.

**Real-world impact:** in the qwen3-14b decode (`models/qwen3/14b/decode_layer.py`), `dcr_xgamma`'s `DOWN_ON` sliced writers of `out` / `normed_out` WAW-serialize on one core when emitted in the auto-dep region (the `OutWindowExternalizer` Pattern-5 that should keep them parallel bails because the task writes two outputs). Moving the writer **into** `manual_scope` removes the WAW (parallel writers), but is blocked by this codegen limitation because the per-layer dcr tids are loop-carried (`prev_out_tids` / `prev_normed_tids`). We had to fall back to a single `pl.spmd` dispatch instead.

### Steps to Reproduce

Compile-only, no device needed:

```python
import sys
import pypto.language as pl
import torch
from pypto.backend import BackendType, set_backend_type

N, LOOP, ROWS, COLS = 4, 2, 16, 256
TILE = COLS // N

@pl.jit.inline
def layer(
    x: pl.Tensor[[ROWS, COLS], pl.FP32],
    y: pl.Tensor[[ROWS, COLS], pl.FP32],
    prev_tids: pl.Array[N, pl.TASK_ID],
    out_tids: pl.Array[N, pl.TASK_ID],
) -> pl.Tensor[[ROWS, COLS], pl.FP32]:
    # consumer of the PREVIOUS iteration's carry -> makes `carry` truly loop-carried
    with pl.at(level=pl.Level.CORE_GROUP, name_hint="consumer",
               deps=[prev_tids[i] for i in range(N)]):
        y[0:ROWS, 0:COLS] = pl.add(y[0:ROWS, 0:COLS], 1.0)
    # produce N tids INSIDE manual_scope and yield them into the carried array
    with pl.manual_scope():                       # <-- remove this wrapper -> compiles fine
        for n in pl.parallel(N):
            with pl.at(level=pl.Level.CORE_GROUP, name_hint="prod",
                       deps=[prev_tids[n]]) as prod_tid:
                c0 = n * TILE
                y[0:ROWS, c0:c0 + TILE] = pl.add(y[0:ROWS, c0:c0 + TILE], 1.0)
            out_tids[n] = prod_tid                # <-- scalar yield to array carry
    return y

@pl.jit
def repro(x: pl.Tensor[[ROWS, COLS], pl.FP32], y: pl.Out[pl.Tensor[[ROWS, COLS], pl.FP32]]):
    carry = pl.array.create(N, pl.TASK_ID)
    with pl.at(level=pl.Level.CORE_GROUP, name_hint="seed") as seed_tid:
        y[0:ROWS, 0:COLS] = pl.add(x[0:ROWS, 0:COLS], 0.0)
    for s in pl.unroll(N):
        carry[s] = seed_tid
    for _i in pl.range(LOOP):                     # LOOP > 1 forces cross-iteration carry
        y = layer(x, y, carry, carry)
    return y

if __name__ == "__main__":
    set_backend_type(BackendType.Ascend910B)
    repro.compile_for_test(torch.randn([ROWS, COLS]), torch.empty([ROWS, COLS]))
```

**Contrast (compiles clean):** delete the `with pl.manual_scope():` line and de-indent the `for n in pl.parallel(N):` block by one level (producer in the auto-dep region). The kernel is otherwise identical and compiles without error — isolating `pl.manual_scope()` as the trigger.

### Expected Behavior

Either:
1. codegen supports loop-carrying a `manual_scope`-produced `TaskId` into an `Array[TASK_ID]` (register such tids in `manual_task_id_map_` / honor C++ lexical scope lifetime, in line with the #1577 fix discussion), or
2. the frontend rejects this pattern with a clear, user-facing error — not an `INTERNAL_CHECK` (`Internal error: ...`).

### Actual Behavior

Orchestration codegen aborts:

```
Failed to generate orchestration 'repro': Internal error: scalar yield to array carry
must resolve to a TaskId variable registered in manual_task_id_map_
Check failed: tid_binding != nullptr at src/codegen/orchestration/orchestration_codegen.cpp:1389
```

(Via `compile_for_test` the error is printed but not raised; via the normal device/codegen path it surfaces as a fatal `PartialCodegenError`.)

### Git Commit ID

3ec5e838 (pypto, main)

### NPU Kind

N/A (not hardware-specific)

### Host Platform

Linux (aarch64)

### Additional Context

Related: #1577 (closed — complementary "read" direction of the same `manual_task_id_map_` registration gap).

| Component | Version |
|---|---|
| pypto | `3ec5e838` (branch: `main`) |
| pypto runtime (submodule) | `2668be5a` |
| pypto-lib | `556f615` |
| pto-isa | `b9122ec` |
| ptoas | `v0.45` |
| CANN | not detected |

title: [RFC] Explicit AIV split: pl.split_aiv + aiv_shard/aic_gather replacing SplitVectorKernel auto-analysis
body:
### Summary

Introduce an **explicit, user-driven AIV-split DSL** for mixed cube+vector (AIC/AIV) kernels, replacing the compiler-inferred splitting in the `SplitVectorKernel` pass. The surface is three constructs: a `for aiv_id in pl.split_aiv(2):` SPMD loop that binds the sub-core index, and two boundary ops that mark every full↔half transition across the cube↔vector boundary — `pl.aiv_shard(tile, mode)` (full→half, AIC→AIV) and `pl.aic_gather(tile, mode)` (half→full, AIV→AIC). The split **mode** (`UP_DOWN`/`LEFT_RIGHT`) is declared on the transfer ops in 2D-tile vocabulary and **validated**, not inferred. This deletes the brittle index-space analysis that currently miscompiles split-axis sub-slice stores, and lands on existing, already-correct codegen (`tpop_from_aic` halves, `tpop_from_aiv` keeps full) so codegen/PTOAS need no changes.

Related: #1034 (split-axis reduction / GM-mediated semantics), #1447 (SplitVectorKernel odd-`N` validation), #1789 (cross-core split dual-AIV deadlock).

### Motivation

**The concrete blocker.** A distilled flash-attention inner step (`qk_pv`: QK^T → online-softmax → PV) at `M_TILE=64, HEAD_DIM=512, K_TILE=128` hits a progression of compiler blockers:

1. **L0C (Acc) overflow** — two co-resident FP32 matmul accumulators, QK `[64,128]` (32 KB) + PV `[64,512]` (128 KB) = 160 KB > 128 KB. *Fixed* by #1805 (global largest-first packing now reuses the dead QK slot).
2. **Vec overflow** — the `[64,128]` softmax intermediates hit 197632 B > 188416 B. *Worked around* by adding `optimizations=[pl.split(pl.SplitMode.UP_DOWN)]`, which halves the row axis across the two AIV sub-cores.
3. **[CURRENT] ptoas codegen failure** — with the `UP_DOWN` split active, the strided `H_TILE`-row stores (`mi[r0:r0+16] = qk_mi[r0:r0+16]`) produce:
   ```
   'pto.tstore' op expects dst static element count (8) to match src valid_shape static element count (16)
   ```

**Root cause.** `SplitVectorKernel` is a *syntactic, per-statement shape-halver with no model of the index space*. It halves a `tile.slice`'s **result type** (`[16,1]`→`[8,1]`) but leaves its **shape/offset args** (`[16,1]`), manufacturing the mismatched `tstore(subview<16>, partition<8>)`. The failing pattern (strided sub-slice stores along the split axis) is **structural to online-softmax**, so the failure is endemic under buffer pressure, not incidental. The pass is a per-op whitelist (`load/store/full/create/reshape` get arg rewrites; `tile.slice` and everything else fall through to result-type-only halving), which is fragile and unbounded as new ops appear.

**Why explicit beats fixing the auto-pass.** When the user authors the partition, the slice shapes and result types are self-consistent by construction, so the entire mismatch class disappears. The compiler stops doing index-space inference and instead just *validates declared intent* and *stamps the per-transfer `split`*. Kernel authors already write explicit tile offsets, `get_subblock_idx`, and cross-core handoffs — this is idiomatic, not new burden.

### Design

#### API (three constructs)

```python
def split_aiv(n: int = 2) -> SplitAivIterator: ...
    # for aiv_id in pl.split_aiv(2):  -> body runs once per AIV sub-core.
    #   aiv_id = pl.tile.get_subblock_idx(); n is HW-fixed at 2 (validated).

def aiv_shard(tile: T, mode: SplitMode) -> T: ...
    # AIC->AIV scatter: this lane's half of a full cube tile.
    # result type = input with the split axis HALVED.

def aic_gather(tile: T, mode: SplitMode) -> T: ...
    # AIV->AIC gather: reassemble per-lane halves into the full tile the cube consumes.
    # result type = input with the split axis DOUBLED.  (inverse of aiv_shard)
```

`mode` is `SplitMode.UP_DOWN` (split rows / axis 0) or `SplitMode.LEFT_RIGHT` (split cols / axis 1), expressed in **2D-tile vocabulary**.

#### Worked example (the `qk_pv` kernel)

```python
with pl.at(level=pl.Level.CORE_GROUP, name_hint="qk_pv"):
    qk_raw  = pl.matmul(q, k, b_trans=True, out_dtype=pl.FP32)         # AIC, full [M, K]
    for aiv_id in pl.split_aiv(2):
        qk_h    = pl.aiv_shard(qk_raw, pl.SplitMode.UP_DOWN)           # [M//2, K]  full->half
        qk_sc   = pl.mul(qk_h, SOFTMAX_SCALE)
        qk_mi   = pl.row_max(qk_sc)                                    # [M//2, 1]
        qk_exp  = pl.exp(pl.row_expand_sub(qk_sc, qk_mi))
        qk_li   = pl.row_sum(qk_exp)
        qk_bf16 = pl.cast(qk_exp, target_type=pl.BF16)                 # [M//2, K]
        qk_full = pl.aic_gather(qk_bf16, pl.SplitMode.UP_DOWN)         # [M, K]    half->full
        qk_oi_f = pl.matmul(qk_full, v, out_dtype=pl.FP32)            # [M, HEAD] cube sees FULL, deduce ok
        qk_oi   = pl.aiv_shard(qk_oi_f, pl.SplitMode.UP_DOWN)          # [M//2, HEAD] full->half
        base = aiv_id * (M_TILE // 2)
        for sub in pl.unroll((M_TILE // 2) // H_TILE):
            r0 = sub * H_TILE
            oi[base + r0 : base + r0 + H_TILE, :]  = qk_oi[r0:r0+H_TILE, :]   # GM store: lane's owned rows
            mi[base + r0 : base + r0 + H_TILE, 0:1] = qk_mi[r0:r0+H_TILE, 0:1]
            li[base + r0 : base + r0 + H_TILE, 0:1] = qk_li[r0:r0+H_TILE, 0:1]
```

The user makes **one annotation per full↔half transition**. Everything else flows by type.

#### Semantic model — closed under two boundary ops

A tile is either **full** (AIC vocabulary, `[M,…]`) or **half** (AIV-lane vocabulary, `[M//2,…]`). `aiv_shard` is the only full→half edge; `aic_gather` is the only half→full edge. The type itself (`[M]` vs `[M//2]`) encodes which — **no split-state analysis or propagation is needed**, and cube ops always see full operands so their shape deduction is unchanged. This is what makes `qk_oi_f = matmul(qk_full, v)` type-check: `qk_full` is full `[M,K]` (post-gather), so the matmul deduces `[M,HEAD]` normally. Feeding a half into a cube op is rejected by the verifier (see below).

#### Mode is declared, not inferred

The split direction is a property of the **2D tile at the transfer** — `tile.tpush_to_aiv`/`tpop_from_aic` carry a `split` int attr (`None=0/UpDown=1/LeftRight=2`), and tiles are already 2D by `ExpandMixedKernel` time (`FlattenTileNdTo2D` is pass 15, `ExpandMixedKernel` 21, `SplitVectorKernel` 23). A *generic high-dim slice* cannot reliably name "row" vs "col" because the high-dim→2D-tile axis mapping (flatten/layout/transpose) is decided by passes that run after the user's source. So the user declares the mode in 2D-tile vocab on the shard/gather op, and the compiler **validates** it at the 2D-tile boundary rather than guessing.

#### Lowering — onto existing, already-correct paths

```
aiv_shard(x, mode)  ->  cube  tile.tpush_to_aiv(x, split=N)  +  AIV  tile.tpop_from_aic(split=N)   # HALVES (existing)
aic_gather(x, mode) ->  AIV   tile.tpush_to_aic(x, split=N)  +  cube tile.tpop_from_aiv(split=N)    # KEEPS FULL (existing)
```

From `split_vector_kernel_pass.cpp:400-406`: *"`tpop_from_aic`: AIV consumes from cube — halve the popped tile … `tpop_from_aiv`: AIC consumes from vector — keep full tile shape."* The two new ops are exactly the two existing pop behaviors surfaced to the user; orchestration codegen (`RequiresDualAivDispatch` is already boolean) and the `.pto`/PTOAS layer (per-transfer `split`) are unchanged.

#### Compiler-side changes, by pass

- **Frontend** (`language/dsl_api.py`, `parser/ast_parser.py`): add `split_aiv` to `_VALID_ITERATORS`; `_parse_split_aiv_for_loop` (mirror `_parse_spmd_for_loop`) opens an `InCore` scope with attr `{"split_aiv": True}` and binds `aiv_id = tile.get_subblock_idx()`. Reject `n != 2`, loop kwargs (`init_values/chunk/stage/deps`), and a scope that also carries `optimizations=[pl.split(...)]`.
- **New IR ops** `tile.aiv_shard` / `tile.aic_gather` (`src/ir/op/tile_ops/`): one `tile` arg + `split` int attr; type inference halves / doubles the mode axis (`CHECK_SPAN` even extent).
- **`ExpandMixedKernel`** (pass 21): lower `aiv_shard`/`aic_gather` to their `tpush`/`tpop` pairs with `split = int(mode)` from the op (today `MakeSplitKwargs()` stamps the `split=0` placeholder; now it carries the declared mode).
- **`SplitVectorKernel`** (pass 23): for `split_aiv` functions, **skip the per-op halving entirely** (tiles already half via the shard type). Retain only `dual_aiv_dispatch` stamping.
- **New `AivSplitVerifier`** (registered in `PropertyVerifierRegistry`): the validation below.

#### Validation (pass-time, span'd)

| Check | Rule |
| --- | --- |
| even extent | `aiv_shard`: split-axis even; `aic_gather`: result extent even |
| **full-operand pairing** | a cube op may only consume *full* tiles; a half must pass through `aic_gather` first (this is the check that catches the `matmul(half, …)` mistake) |
| mode consistency | a half from `aiv_shard(_, a)` later `aic_gather`'d must use axis `a` (def-use link) |
| `get_subblock_idx` scope | only valid inside a `split_aiv` function (else it silently returns 0 and both lanes write the same rows) |
| GM offset ↔ mode axis | a `Split(a)` tile's GM store must address axis `a` by `aiv_id` |
| slot-size | `GetCommonSlotSizeBytes` succeeds across all transfers |
| mode policy | conservative single-mode gate (see Open Questions) — one deletable `CHECK` |

#### Multi-mode finding (ISA fact, corrects an earlier assumption)

We verified that **per-transfer split modes are mechanically supported** by the runtime/PTOAS, *not* limited to one mode per kernel: the pipe `pipe_key` (`FlagID|DirType|SlotNum|LocalSlotNum|SlotSize`) does **not** encode the split mode; `CreateInitializePipe` fixes only slot *size*/direction/depth (`GetCommonSlotSizeBytes` = max); the split is realized per-`tpop` ("AIC pushes one full tile, both AIV0/AIV1 consume their halves from the same slot", `runtime/.../tpush-tpop-sim.md`); and `RequiresDualAivDispatch` is a boolean. The existing "conflicting cross-core split modes" error in `SplitVectorKernel` is therefore a **software simplification** tied to its one-`split_dim`-per-function rewrite, not a hardware law. The explicit model removes that coupling, so mixed modes become structurally possible (subject to a PTOAS confirmation probe — see Open Questions).

### Affected Files

- `python/pypto/language/dsl_api.py` — **Modify** — `split_aiv`, `aiv_shard`, `aic_gather`
- `python/pypto/language/parser/ast_parser.py` — **Modify** — `_VALID_ITERATORS` + `_parse_split_aiv_for_loop` + double-decl reject
- `python/pypto/language/__init__.py`, `op/__init__.py`, `pypto_core/*.pyi` — **Modify** — exports + stubs
- `src/ir/op/tile_ops/aiv_shard.cpp` (+ `aic_gather`) — **New** — `tile.aiv_shard` / `tile.aic_gather` ops + type inference
- `python/bindings/modules/*.cpp` — **Modify** — bindings for the new ops
- `src/ir/transforms/expand_mixed_kernel_pass.cpp` — **Modify** — lower shard/gather to `tpush`/`tpop` with `split=N`
- `src/ir/transforms/split_vector_kernel_pass.cpp` — **Modify** — bypass per-op halving for `split_aiv` functions
- `src/ir/transforms/aiv_split_verifier.cpp` — **New** — validation + registry entry
- `docs/{en,zh-cn}/dev/passes/` + DSL docs — **New/Modify** — pass doc + `pl.split_aiv`/`aiv_shard`/`aic_gather`

### Testing Plan

`tests/ut/ir/transforms/test_aiv_shard.py` (before/after, `ir.assert_structural_equal`):

1. The `qk_pv` case: `aiv_shard(UP_DOWN)` + `H_TILE` sub-slice store **compiles through ptoas** (the original regression).
2. `LEFT_RIGHT` column shard → `split=2`, even-`N` validated.
3. Type check: `aiv_shard([M,K], UP_DOWN)` → `[M//2,K]`; `aic_gather([M//2,K], UP_DOWN)` → `[M,K]`.
4. Full-operand pairing: `matmul(half, …)` without `aic_gather` raises a span'd error.
5. Error cases: odd extent; reduce-on-split-axis; `get_subblock_idx` outside `split_aiv`; GM offset on the wrong axis; double-declaration with `pl.split`.
6. Single-mode gate fires on two differing modes (until lifted).
7. Codegen parity: post-lowering IR matches the legacy `pl.split` path for an equivalent whole-tile kernel.

### Alternatives Considered

- **Fix the auto-pass (`SplitVectorKernel`) systematically** — add a `SplitState` (FullAxis/SubRegion) model + coordinate-transform rewrite + keep split-axis loops rolled. Rejected as the primary path: it re-implements the index-space reasoning the pass keeps getting wrong; the unrolled strided store leaves the iteration structure unrecoverable (offsets `32,48` index a 32-row tile). Worth retaining as the *legacy* path for simple whole-tile kernels.
- **Generic slice as the transfer marker** (`qk_raw[aiv_id*half:…]`) — rejected: a high-dim source slice can't be mapped to the 2D-tile row/col mode (flatten/layout/transpose intervene), so the compiler can't reliably check `UP_DOWN` vs `LEFT_RIGHT`.
- **`mode=` on the `split_aiv` loop** — rejected: the mode is a property of each AIC↔AIV transfer, not of the SPMD loop; multiple transfers may differ.
- **Remove the loop entirely** (infer dual-AIV from shard ops, use `get_subblock_idx()` directly) — rejected: the GM output store needs the lane index, so a bound `aiv_id` + a scoped per-lane region is cleaner than scattered `get_subblock_idx()` calls.

### Rollout / Migration

- `pl.split_aiv` (explicit) and `pl.split(mode)` (auto) **coexist in parallel**, converging on byte-identical post-detection IR (`split` Function attr + `dual_aiv_dispatch`, `tpush`/`tpop` carrying `split=N`), so codegen and PTOAS need zero changes.
- Explicit is the recommended path for index-space-aware kernels; auto is retained as the simple on-ramp. **Do not** make auto lower to explicit (synthesizing correct `aiv_id`-indexed slices for arbitrary kernels is exactly the inference the auto path lacks).
- No backward-incompatible change: existing `pl.split` users are untouched; new ops are additive.

### Security Considerations

None. This is a compiler-internal DSL/IR change with no new external input surface, network, or secret handling. The added verifier strictly *tightens* validation (turns silent miscompiles into pass-time errors).

### Open Questions

1. **Region boundary / cube roundtrip.** How the cube assembles two lanes' halves for an intermediate `matmul` (via `aic_gather` → `tpop_from_aiv` full path) needs a prototype to confirm against PTOAS on a small two-lane example before the pass is written.
2. **PTOAS mixed-mode probe.** Hand-author a `.pto` with two `tpop`s (`split=1`, `split=2`) and run `ptoas` to definitively decide whether the conservative single-mode gate can be deleted.
3. **Naming.** `aic_gather` (scatter/gather symmetry) vs `aic_merge` / `aic_assemble`. Feedback welcome.
4. **Pure-AIV split (no cube transfer).** Has no shard op to trigger dual-dispatch; out of scope here, or add a thin `with pl.dual_aiv()` marker only if a real case appears.

title: [Pass Bug] MemoryReuse global largest-first packing (#1805) drops PIPE_MTE3<->PIPE_V sync -> stale read, ~17.5% wrong output
body:
### Pass Name

MemoryReuse (`src/ir/transforms/memory_reuse_pass.cpp`)

### Description

PR #1805 (commit `035359b9`, "global largest-first packing for MemoryReuse
buffer reuse") introduces a numerical-correctness regression. After this
commit the MemoryReuse pass repacks tile buffers into tighter/overlapping
offsets, but a required `PIPE_MTE3 <-> PIPE_V` synchronization at the new
reuse boundary is **not** inserted (the flags present before the commit are
dropped). A vector op then reads a tile before the MTE3 store that fills it
completes -> stale read -> corrupted output.

Reproduces with the dsv4 `prefill_sparse_attn` kernel (pypto-lib):
`python models/deepseek/v4/prefill_sparse_attn.py -p a2a3 -d <dev>`
=> `attn_out` fails `ratio_allclose(atol=1e-4, rtol=1/128)` with
error_count ~= 92000/524288 (~17.5%), deterministic every run.

Bisect (each step rebuilt with `cmake --build build --parallel`):

| pypto commit | result |
|---|---|
| #1759 `1217e0c1` (cross-scope deps) | PASS |
| #1810 `2cd14c2c` (parent of #1805) | PASS |
| **#1805 `035359b9` (MemoryReuse global largest-first packing)** | **FAIL ~17.5%** |
| HEAD `d2471cbb` (main) | FAIL ~17.5% |

The only file recompiled at the culprit commit is `memory_reuse_pass.cpp`.

A minimal `@pl.program` reproducer has not yet been isolated; the Before/Actual
below are the codegen-level manifestation (kernel
`prefill_hca_attn_qk_softmax_tile`) captured by comparing the PASS-era vs
FAIL-era `build_output`.

### Git Commit ID

d2471cbb (culprit: 035359b9 / PR #1805)

### Before IR (Input)

```python
# No minimal @pl.program reproducer isolated yet.
# Repro: models/deepseek/v4/prefill_sparse_attn.py (pypto-lib @ e36b94d1)
#
# Codegen evidence (PASS-era, pypto @ 2cd14c2c, parent of #1805):
#   kernel prefill_hca_attn_qk_softmax_tile holds 8 PIPE_MTE3<->PIPE_V flags,
#   e.g. an MTE3 store guarded by:
#       set_flag(PIPE_MTE3, PIPE_V, EVENT_ID0)
#       ... (vector consumer) ...
#       wait_flag(PIPE_MTE3, PIPE_V, EVENT_ID0)
#   buffer offsets: v25..v29 = 81920 / 73728 / 65536 / 81984 / 90176
```

### Expected IR (After Transformation)

```python
# After MemoryReuse, the cross-pipe sync guarding the reused buffer must be
# preserved: every MTE3 store into a reused tile that a vector op later reads
# keeps its matching set_flag(PIPE_MTE3, PIPE_V)/wait_flag(PIPE_MTE3, PIPE_V).
# Tighter packing is fine ONLY if the reuse boundary still emits the sync.
```

### Actual IR or Error

```shell
# FAIL-era (pypto @ 035359b9 / d2471cbb): kernel prefill_hca_attn_qk_softmax_tile
# keeps only 4 of the 8 PIPE_MTE3<->PIPE_V flags (net loss of 4 across ALL
# kernels: 404 -> 400). Both a set_flag(PIPE_MTE3, PIPE_V, EVENT_ID0) and its
# matching wait_flag(PIPE_MTE3, PIPE_V, EVENT_ID0) are removed.
#
# buffer offsets repacked into overlapping ranges:
#   v25..v29 = 69696 / 65536 / 69760 / 65600 / 77952
#
# runtime validation:
#   'attn_out' FAIL (ratio_allclose(atol=0.0001, rtol=0.0078125, max_error_ratio=0.005))
#   ratio_allclose fail: error_count=92186/524288 (ratio=17.5831%, allowed<=0.5000%)
```

### NPU Kind (if relevant)

Ascend 910C (observed on-device; root cause is in the pass and likely not hardware-specific)

### Host Platform (if relevant)

Linux (aarch64)

### Additional Context

Related: #1475 (a different MemoryReuse hazard — WAR serialization of
independent matmuls — not the same root cause). Repro kernel lives in
pypto-lib (`models/deepseek/v4/prefill_sparse_attn.py`, commit `e36b94d1`).

title: [Bug] Intermittent CI failure: test_l3_ring_allreduce P=2 — corrupted output on NPU/HCCL
body:
### Component

Backend

### Description

`tests/st/distributed/test_l3_ring_allreduce.py::TestL3RingAllReduce::test_ring_allreduce[2]` fails intermittently in NPU CI with HCCL backend. The same test passes consistently:
- In sim Docker (`--platform=a2a3sim`), shared memory has no write visibility restrictions
- With P=4 (multi-step ring, different buffer layout)
- With P=2 in sim (passes every run)

The P=2 failure produces corrupted output: max diff = 227.0 (suspiciously close to 100 + 128 - 1 — rank 1's start offset plus ~half the chunk). The actual output shows rank 1's data in the first portion and mixed/combined data later, suggesting rank 0's `pld.tile.remote_load` during the first reduce-scatter step reads partially stale data from rank 1's HCCL window.

Root cause hypothesis: the stage-in writes (Phase 1: `pl.store` to `scratch` DistributedTensor) are not guaranteed visible across the HCCL interconnect before the first RS round's `TNOTIFY`/`TWAIT` barrier completes. While PTOAS inserts MTE pipe drains before `TNOTIFY` (issue #711 fix), those only drain local MTE pipes — they do not establish a global happens-before for the HCCL fabric. The first `remote_load` can therefore read stale/partial scratch data.

A proposed fix adds an explicit pre-RS synchronization round (dedicated signal row 0, notify-all/wait-all barrier before Phase 2) to guarantee cross-rank window visibility. This fix passes sim Docker (P=2, P=4, full distributed suite: 43/43 pass) but requires NPU verification.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Run the ring allreduce P=2 test on NPU hardware with 2+ devices:

```
pytest tests/st/distributed/test_l3_ring_allreduce.py -v \
  --forked --platform=a2a3 --device=0,1 \
  -k "test_ring_allreduce[2]"
```

2. The failure is intermittent — may need multiple CI runs to reproduce. Observed in CI on `hw-native-sys/pypto` main branch.

3. Expected vs actual failure:

Expected: `outputs` matches element-wise sum of all rank inputs (closed-form golden)
Actual: `max diff = 227.0`, output shows rank 1's data mixed with partial sums

### Expected Behavior

Ring allreduce P=2 produces correct allreduced output on NPU hardware, consistent with P=4 and sim behavior.

### Actual Behavior

```
AssertionError: ring allreduce P=2 mismatch: max diff = 227.0

Actual output pattern: values [100, 102, 104, ...] — rank 1's data (starts at 100).
After position ~127, values jump to [356, 358, ...] — rank 0 + rank 1 data combined
but skewed. This is rank 1's entire chunk followed by a partially accumulated chunk.

The corruption is deterministic in the data pattern but intermittent in CI — only
hits with P=2 on HCCL, never on sim or P=4.

[chip_process pid=1015915 dev=12] ready
[chip_process pid=1015905 dev=3] ready
[SDMA] Created 48 STARS streams OK
[SDMA] STARS query AICPU kernel completed OK
[SDMA] Created 48 STARS streams OK
[SDMA] STARS query AICPU kernel completed OK
```

### Git Commit ID

03db2b9f3accee795f81e3e89632fa547ddee983

### NPU Kind

Ascend 910B (CI runner)

### Host Platform

Linux (x86_64)

### Additional Context

- Test file: `tests/st/distributed/test_l3_ring_allreduce.py`
- The ring algorithm follows the NCCL-style chunked reduce-scatter + allgather schedule with `2(P-1)` per-round notify/wait barriers
- Data layout: each rank owns P=2 chunk slots of SIZE=256 / 2 = 128 floats each in the `scratch` HCCL window
- P=2 is a degenerate case of the ring (single-step RS + single-step AG = 2 rounds)
- Signal layout: `2(P-1) × P` INT32 cells, zero-initialized by `alloc_window_buffer`
- A proposed fix branch exists: `fix-ring-allreduce-p2-hccl-sync` on `fork-gbisbas` — adds a pre-RS global notify/wait barrier round, verified in sim Docker (2/2 ring tests pass, 43/43 full distributed suite)
- The fix uses one extra signal row: `total_rounds = 2*(n_ranks−1) + 1`, with row 0 dedicated to stage-in synchronization

title: [Bug] Precision regression: tile.transpose_view L1-load-sharing pass corrupts opposite-b_trans matmul output (qwen3-14b prefill)
body:
### Component

Other — IR transform pass (`ConvertTensorToTileOps` + new `tile.transpose_view` op)

### Description

Commit `ad203ba5` (PR #1776 / #1801, "feat(pass): share one L1 load across opposite-b_trans matmuls via tile.transpose_view") introduces a precision regression. When a single Mat tensor is consumed by both a `b_trans=True` and a `b_trans=False` `pl.matmul`, the pass now loads it to L1 once and realizes the transposed use as a zero-copy `tile.transpose_view` (NZ↔ZN) aliasing the same buffer, instead of two separate GM→L1 loads. The transposed-view path produces wrong results: the qwen3-14b prefill end-to-end output mismatches the torch golden on ~99% of elements.

Root cause is almost certainly an incorrect block/scatter layout mapping in the NZ↔ZN `transpose_view`, or unsound buffer aliasing/memory-reuse for the shared L1 buffer — the consuming matmul reads the wrong data layout.

Located by `git bisect` (22-commit range): first bad commit = `ad203ba5`, parent `0242a356` is good. Crucially, `ad203ba5` reproduces the failure with the **old** runtime submodule (`19b2c0be`), which isolates the cause to the pypto compiler pass (not the runtime). Reverting `ad203ba5` on top of latest `main` restores PASS.

Note: PR #1825 ("forbid in-place transpose (output must not reuse input buffer)"), the current `main` tip, does **not** fix it — the regression is still present on latest `main`.

Related: hw-native-sys/pypto#1821 (different pass bug — MemoryReuse, PR #1805 — also causing wrong prefill output; separate root cause).

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Build pypto at `2acba585` (latest `main`) with runtime submodule `b7d04b45`.
2. Run the qwen3-14b prefill kernel on a real Ascend 910B device:
   ```bash
   PTO2_RING_HEAP=2147483648 PTO2_RING_TASK_WINDOW=131072 PTO2_RING_DEP_POOL=131072 \
     python models/qwen3/14b/prefill_fwd.py -p a2a3 -d <device>
   ```
   (pypto-lib commit `65871d8`)
3. Observe the validation result for output tensor `out`.

### Expected Behavior

`'out' PASS` — device output matches the torch golden within `rtol=5e-3, atol=5e-3`.

### Actual Behavior

```
[RUN]   'out' FAIL  shape=(16, 152064) dtype=torch.float32
Output(s) does not match golden: ['out']
  'out' FAIL  shape=(16, 152064) dtype=torch.float32
    Mismatched elements: 2399695/2433024  rtol=0.005 atol=0.005
    [0] actual=0.03084510937333107, expected=0.32421907782554626
    [1] actual=-0.13147500157356262, expected=-0.3582838773727417
    ...
```

Bisect summary:

| pypto commit | result |
|---|---|
| `0242a356` (parent of culprit) | PASS |
| `ad203ba5` (PR #1776/#1801, culprit) — even with old runtime `19b2c0be` | FAIL |
| `2acba585` (latest main, incl. PR #1825) | FAIL |
| latest main with `ad203ba5` reverted | PASS |

### Git Commit ID

`2acba585` (bug reproduces on latest `main`; first bad commit `ad203ba5`)

### NPU Kind

Ascend 910B

### Host Platform

Linux (aarch64)

### Environment

| Component | Version |
|---|---|
| pypto-lib | `65871d8` |
| pypto | `2acba585` (branch: `main`); first bad commit `ad203ba5` |
| pypto runtime (submodule) | `b7d04b45` |
| pto-isa | `b2d297e1` (branch: `main`) |
| ptoas | `0.45` |
| CANN | not detected |

### Additional Context

- Reproduction is on real NPU; the functional simulator (`a2a3sim`) instead hits a hard runtime assertion (`index < output_count_` in `aicpu_executor.cpp`) on the same build, consistent with the same root cause manifesting differently.
- Touched files in the culprit commit: `python/pypto/ir/op/tile_ops.py`, `src/ir/op/tile_ops/transform.cpp`, `src/ir/transforms/convert_tensor_to_tile_ops_pass.cpp`, `src/ir/transforms/memory_reuse_pass.cpp`, `src/backend/common/pto_ops_common.cpp`.

title: [Bug] _extract_local_tensor_metas does not track subscript-slice sugar t[a:b] — inline dep resolution fails (sibling of #1755)
body:
### Component

Other (please specify in description) — JIT front-end metadata inference (`_extract_local_tensor_metas` in `python/pypto/jit/decorator.py`).

### Description

`docs/pypto-coding-style.md` states the subscript-slice sugar and `pl.slice` are equivalent:

```python
tile = pl.slice(hidden_states, [BATCH_TILE, K_STEP], [b0, k0])
tile = hidden_states[b0 : b0 + BATCH_TILE, k0 : k0 + K_STEP]   # "equivalent"
```

They are **not** equivalent for a tensor that is sliced inside a `@pl.jit` **dep** function and then forwarded into a nested `@pl.jit.inline` callee. `_extract_local_tensor_metas` (decorator.py:585) is the walker that infers `TensorMeta` for local tensors so inline-dep params can be resolved. Its own docstring enumerates the **only** forms it tracks:

1. `var = pl.create_tensor([shape], dtype=...)`
2. `var = pl.slice(src, [shape], [...])`
3. `v1, ... = jit_dep(args)`   (Out-param inheritance)

(plus `pl.reshape`, added in #1755).

The subscript-sugar form `var = src[a : b, ...]` (an `ast.Subscript`, not an `ast.Call` to `pl.slice`) is **not** one of the tracked forms, so it produces **no** local `TensorMeta`. When such a `var` is passed to an inline callee that needs a static shape (e.g. `pl.reshape`), the callee param gets `tensor_meta = None` and `Specializer._build_params` raises:

```
ValueError: @pl.jit: missing inferred tensor metadata for parameter 'ori_kv'.
This usually means the tensor's shape/dtype could not be statically determined. ...
```

This is the direct sibling of #1755 (same walker, same `_build_params` failure) — #1755 added `pl.reshape`; the subscript-slice-sugar case is still missing.

### Steps to Reproduce

Deterministic reproduction via the sibling `pypto-lib` repo (DeepSeek-V4 decode forward), whose `decode_fwd` is a `@pl.jit` dep of a `@pl.jit.host` entry and forwards GM-cache slices into `@pl.jit.inline` attention kernels that `pl.reshape` them:

1. In `pypto-lib`, edit `models/deepseek/v4/decode_fwd.py` and convert the GM-cache `pl.slice(...)` calls to the subscript-sugar form, e.g.

   ```python
   # before (works):
   kv_cache_l0 = pl.slice(kv_cache, [B * ORI_MAX_BLOCKS, BLOCK_SIZE, 1, HEAD_DIM], [0, 0, 0, 0])
   # after (fails):
   kv_cache_l0 = kv_cache[0 : B * ORI_MAX_BLOCKS, 0 : BLOCK_SIZE, 0 : 1, 0 : HEAD_DIM]
   ```

   (The callees reshape these: `decode_attention_swa.py:179` `pl.reshape(kv_cache, ...)`, `decode_sparse_attn.py:146-147` `ori_kv`/`cmp_kv`, etc.)

2. Run:

   ```bash
   python models/deepseek/v4/decode_fwd.py --compile-only -p a2a3
   ```

3. Observe the `missing inferred tensor metadata` error at specialization time (~1.2s, before codegen). Converting more slices back to `pl.slice` just moves the error to the next reshaped param (`ori_kv` -> `cmp_kv` -> `attn_sink` -> ...), confirming the failure is general, not tensor-specific.

### Expected Behavior

Per the documented equivalence, `src[a : b, ...]` should produce the same local `TensorMeta` as `pl.slice(src, [b - a, ...], [a, ...])`, so the forwarded inline-dep param resolves and the kernel compiles. `_extract_local_tensor_metas` should handle the `ast.Subscript` slice form the same way it handles `pl.slice` (dtype inherited from `src`; each sliced dim resolved as `stop - start`, falling back to the parent dim when not statically resolvable; `DynDim`s flowing through transparently).

### Actual Behavior

```
File ".../pypto/jit/specializer.py", line 1695, in _build_params
    raise ValueError(
ValueError: @pl.jit: missing inferred tensor metadata for parameter 'ori_kv'.
This usually means the tensor's shape/dtype could not be statically determined.
Pass the tensor directly as a function argument, or ensure any intermediate
pl.create_tensor() used for this parameter has a statically inferable shape and dtype.
```

### Git Commit ID

459027c0e3df36a161d2728fe7cf05ebacb8fdcb

### NPU Kind

N/A (not hardware-specific)

### Host Platform

Linux (aarch64)

### Additional Context

- Related: #1755 (same walker / same `_build_params` failure, fixed for `pl.reshape`).
- The walker only runs on **dep** functions discovered by a host/entry. A standalone `@pl.jit` **entry** that slices with sugar and calls an inline callee compiles fine (the entry is specialized directly with concrete arg metas), so the bug only surfaces in the host -> `@pl.jit` dep -> nested-inline chain — exactly the dsv4 decode/prefill forward structure.
- Suggested fix site: add an `ast.Subscript` branch to `_extract_local_tensor_metas` mirroring the existing `pl.slice` (`_slice_meta`) handling.

title: [Bug] Flaky ST: test_dynamic_paged_attention[256-64-128-64-8192-32768] intermittently fails on a2a3 with AICore error 507018
body:
### Component

Other (please specify in description) — system test (`tests/st/runtime/framework_and_models/`) failing at on-device execution of the generated paged-attention kernel on the a2a3 backend/runtime.

### Description

The system test `tests/st/runtime/framework_and_models/test_dynamic_paged_attention.py::TestDynamicPagedAttentionKernels::test_dynamic_paged_attention[256-64-128-64-8192-32768]` (test name `dynamic_paged_attention_256bat_64h_128d_64bs`; params `batch=256, num_heads=64, head_dim=128, block_size=64, context_len=8192, max_model_len=32768`) **intermittently fails** on a2a3 with AICore error code **507018**.

When it fails, the device is marked unrecoverable and is force-reset. The failure is non-deterministic (~1/3 hit rate in local reproduction), so it occasionally turns the whole `system-tests` CI job red without any related code change.

This is **not** caused by a specific diff — it was hit while triaging PR #1834 (a Python-only runtime-default rename, zero `.cpp/.h` changes), and reproduces independently of that PR. The generated kernel is identical to `main`.

### Steps to Reproduce

Run the single parametrization on an a2a3 device. A single run often passes; repeat it to surface the flakiness:

```bash
export PYTHONPATH=/path/to/pypto/python:$PYTHONPATH
python -m pytest \
  "tests/st/runtime/framework_and_models/test_dynamic_paged_attention.py::TestDynamicPagedAttentionKernels" \
  -k "256-64-128-64-8192-32768" \
  -v --device=<dev> --platform=a2a3 \
  --pto-isa-commit=016396b57e2c17093f1194e6acd89bb112b0ab24 \
  --count=3
```

Observed locally (2026-06-23):
- Single isolated run: PASSED (~72s).
- `--count=3`: **1 failed / 2 passed** (failed on the 3rd repetition with the same 507018 signature).

### Expected Behavior

The test passes deterministically on every run; the device is not poisoned.

### Actual Behavior

One repetition out of three fails:

```
RuntimeError: run_prepared failed with code 507018
  File ".../runtime/device_runner.py", line 638, in execute_on_device
    return worker.run(cid, orch_args, cfg)
  File ".../simpler/worker.py", line 2587, in run
  File ".../simpler/task_interface.py", line 544, in _run_slot
    return self._impl.run(int(callable_id), args, config)

[ERROR] sync_run_streams: [device_runner_base.cpp:881]
        aclrtSynchronizeStreamWithTimeout (AICPU) failed: 507018
[ERROR] recover_device_or_mark_unusable: [device_runner.cpp:481]
        Device unrecoverable after AICore error 507018:
        aclrtSynchronizeDeviceWithTimeout failed. Marking DeviceRunner unusable;
        a soft in-process reset does not clear the poison.
[WARN]  force_reset_device: [device_runner.cpp:578]
        aclrtResetDeviceForce cleared the poisoned card
```

### Git Commit ID

Reproduced on `1e18b0de` (PR #1834 head, based on `origin/main`); not branch-specific — the kernel matches `main`.

### NPU Kind

Other (please specify in description) — a2a3 (`--platform=a2a3`; `npu-smi info` reports the chip as `Ascend910`).

### Host Platform

Linux (aarch64)

### Additional Context

Related: #1388 (closed — flaky `test_paged_attention_spmd_ptoas` with the same 507018 device-unrecoverable signature), #1789 (open — same 507018 code but a different root cause). The shared 507018 + force-reset signature across multiple paged-attention ST variants suggests a common intermittent device/AICore fault rather than a per-test bug.

title: Track: a2a3 tile-op ST gaps deferred from PR #1823 (gemv family, bitwise int32, prelu, rem, sin/cos width-128, matmul_bias narrow-N)
body:
_Auto-audited tracking issue: each deferred op was re-verified against the freshly-cloned a2a3 pto-isa headers and PyPTO codegen; reported symptoms were corrected where the audit disagreed (see Verification notes)._


These tile operators were excluded from a2a3 on-board ST coverage in PR #1823 due to a2a3 ISA / codegen gaps. This issue tracks them so they are not forgotten. Each item below records the audited root cause (which can differ from the originally reported symptom — see Verification notes), the load-bearing evidence, and the fix direction.

## pto-isa limitations (a2a3 ISA / PTOAS, file against pto-isa)

- [ ] **gemv_acc** — a2a3 lacks the 3-tile shared-accumulator overload of `TGEMV_ACC` that `TMATMUL_ACC` has; in-place `cOut==cIn` accumulation can't be assembled. PyPTO codegen is correct (Acc aliasing via `make_acc_codegen`, not a tmov). Evidence: `build_output/_deps/pto-isa/include/pto/npu/a2a3/TMatmul.hpp:120` (only 4-tile `TGEMV_ACC_IMPL`, no 3-tile overload like `:180`), `pto_instr.hpp:800`/`:808`, `README.md:81` (TGEMV_ACC = TODO vs `:94` TMATMUL_ACC = Yes). Fix: add the 3-tile shared-acc overload + PTOAS support in pto-isa, flip README TODO→Yes; PyPTO just un-defers ST. No PyPTO code change.

- [ ] **rem / rems** — a2a3 `RemInt32Instr` emulates int32 modulo via int32→fp32→int32 round-trip, clobbering src0/src1 in place and losing precision past fp32's 24-bit mantissa; `rems` shares the same precision-loss class plus a tmp-row mismatch. PyPTO codegen is correct (kSimpleOps + tmp operand from PR #1823). Evidence: `build_output/_deps/pto-isa/include/pto/npu/a2a3/TRem.hpp:67-85` (round-trip, in-place input clobber at `:82-83`), `:147-148` (static_assert advertises int32), a5's true `vmod` at `TRem.hpp:72`; `TRemS.hpp:67-82`; tmp-row asymmetry `TRemS.hpp:135` (≥1) vs `TRem.hpp:161` (≥2). Fix: pto-isa stage the round-trip through scratch tmp (stop clobbering inputs), route int32 to a true integer-modulo path like a5. Keep out of a2a3 ST until landed.

- [ ] **xor / xors** — a2a3 `TXOR`/`TXORS` are TOR+TAND+TNOT composites whose static_assert restricts element type to 16-/8-bit ints; int32 (default `int`/`torch.int32`) trips the assert at PTOAS. PyPTO codegen is dtype-agnostic passthrough. Evidence: `build_output/_deps/pto-isa/include/pto/npu/a2a3/TXor.hpp:28-30` (int8/uint8/int16/uint16 only — int8/uint8 ARE allowed), `TXor.hpp:49-60`, `TBitwiseSOp.hpp:121-135`; `pto_ops_common.cpp:2254`/`:2282`; `tests/st/runtime/ops/test_bitwise.py:21`. Fix (immediate, no code): re-enable a2a3 ST restricted to int16/uint16 (mirror the shipped `not_` pattern). If int32 xor is actually required, file pto-isa to widen the composites. Optionally tighten PyPTO deducers so int32 xor fails at compile with a clear message.

- [ ] **and_ / or_ (+ scalar ands/ors)** — int32 specifically is a2a3-unsupported: `TAND`/`TOR` accept only 1-/2-byte integral types (32-bit is A5-only), so an int32 tile yields the cryptic PTOAS `pto.tand invalid kind of type`. The ops themselves ARE supported on a2a3. Evidence: `build_output/_deps/pto-isa/include/pto/npu/a2a3/TAnd.hpp:75`, `TOr.hpp:65-67`, `tand.md` Target-Profile Restrictions (A2A3 = 1-/2-byte; A5 adds 4-byte); `KNOWN_ISSUES.md:216-222`. Fix: re-test with INT16/UINT16 and un-defer; add a PyPTO DSL/IR-level dtype check rejecting 32-bit and_/or_ on a2a3 with an actionable message. (See Verification notes — `shl`/`shr` split out below.)

- [ ] **sin / cos at width-128 / cols ≥ 64** — on-device-reproduced: `[8,128]` FP32 sin/cos correct for cols 0–63, garbage for 64–127 (64/1024 wrong), while `sqrt` at the same shape passes. sin/cos are software-decomposed (`LowerSinCos`) into ~30 primitives including FP32↔INT32 `tcvt` round-trips and 2-source binary ops — the only ops exercising those at width 128. Readable pto-isa headers handle 128 cols correctly (`TCvt.hpp:1166-1176`/`:1207-1208` → 2 repeats; `TBinOp.hpp` contiguous flatten), so the residual defect is most plausibly an assembler/intrinsic-level miscompile of the tcvt round-trip or 2-source binary on the second 64-element segment, below the C++ template layer. Evidence: `src/ir/transforms/lower_composite_ops_pass.cpp:317-373`/`:647-648`; `pto_ops_common.cpp:2261-2270` (no sin/cos mapping, sqrt single `pto.tsqrt`); `KNOWN_ISSUES.md:278-284`; `tests/st/runtime/ops/test_unary_math.py:49-58`. Fix: do NOT change PyPTO. Localize on device with an isolation ST running only (a) FP32→INT32→FP32 cast and (b) a single 2-source binary at `[8,128]`, comparing cols 0–63 vs 64–127; file pto-isa against the offending intrinsic (mirrors issue #173 / #1790 second-segment-tail pattern). Keep the `[8,128]` case skipped meanwhile.

## PyPTO codegen bugs

- [ ] **prelu** — codegen mapping-table arity is wrong (2, should be 3); the DSL/IR 3-arg shape `(tile, slope, tmp)` is correct and matches the 4-operand `TPRELU_IMPL(dst,src0,src1,tmp)` ISA contract (tmp is mandatory scratch). `MakeNaryCodegenPTO`'s `CHECK(args.size()==arity)` rejects the 3-arg call at compile time. Evidence: root cause at `src/backend/common/pto_ops_common.cpp:2260` `{tile.prelu, pto.tprelu, 2}`; arity check `:437`; `build_output/_deps/pto-isa/include/pto/npu/a2a3/TPrelu.hpp:42-62`/`:38-39`; DSL `python/pypto/language/op/tile_ops.py:1894`/`:1907`; IR `src/ir/op/tile_ops/elementwise.cpp:682-695`. Fix: change `:2260` to arity 3, then re-enable and verify a2a3 prelu ST. One-line change.

- [ ] **subc / subsc — wrong-doc (NOT a miscompute)** — hardware and PyPTO codegen are both correct (`a - b + c`); the defect is PyPTO docs/op-descriptions advertising `lhs - rhs - rhs2`, so a user gets `a-b+c` silently. Evidence: `build_output/_deps/pto-isa/include/pto/cpu/ElementOp.h:399-403`/`:605-608` (`a-b+c`); `tsubc.md:15`/`:61`, `tsubsc.md:15`; faithful codegen `pto_ops_common.cpp:2273`/`:2290`; wrong docs at `python/pypto/language/op/tile_ops.py:1946`/`:1981` and `src/ir/op/tile_ops/elementwise.cpp:714`/`:743`. Fix: correct the four docstrings/descriptions to `lhs - rhs + rhs2` / `lhs - scalar + rhs2`. No codegen change. If `a-b-c` is genuinely intended, that's a separate feature (no a-b-c primitive in pto-isa) and must be raised with the user.

- [ ] **expands (tile.expands)** — orphan duplicate op: IR op + DSL alias exist and `tensor.expands→tile.expands` routes to it, but it has NO f_codegen, so it crashes codegen. `TEXPANDS` is only reachable via the separate `tile.full` (`pl.full`) path. Evidence: `src/ir/op/tile_ops/broadcast.cpp:412`; reachable via `tile_ops.py:1402-1414` and `op_conversion_registry.cpp:177`; working path `pto_ops_common.cpp:3429-3435`; no reg in `pto_ops_common.cpp`. Fix: register an f_codegen emitting `pto.texpands` (mirror `MakeFullCodegenPTO`), or preferably retire `tile.expands` and route `pl.expands`/`tensor.expands` to the existing `tile.full` path.

- [ ] **sum (tile.sum)** — has axis/keepdim but is never lowered to `tile.row_sum`/`tile.col_sum` and has NO f_codegen → crashes codegen (intentionally used as a guaranteed-failure case in a codegen UT). The working reduction path is `pl.row_sum`/`pl.col_sum` → `pto.trowsum`/`pto.tcolsum`. Evidence: `src/ir/op/tile_ops/reduction.cpp:209`; `flatten_tile_nd_to_2d_pass.cpp:2020-2050` (only remaps axis); `tests/ut/codegen/test_pto_codegen.py:1548-1574`. Fix: add a lowering rewriting `tile.sum(axis)` → row_sum (last axis) / col_sum (axis 0) with the required tmp, or retire `tile.sum` and steer users to `pl.row_sum`/`pl.col_sum`.

## Needs design (operand-shape / valid-shape decision)

- [ ] **gemv / gemv_bias — IN PROGRESS** (see below) — 1-row lhs must be loaded to the Left (L0A) cube tile as `Rows==1` + row_major (none_box L1) with K aligned to `512/sizeof` (K%128 fp32, K%256 bf16) so a2a3 `TExtractToLeft`/`TMovToLeft` dispatch to the `TExtractToAVector` 1-row path. No ISA feature missing. Evidence: `build_output/_deps/pto-isa/include/pto/npu/a2a3/textract_common.hpp:470-479` (Rows==1 && isRowMajor → vector path), constraint on COLS at `:99-118` (`srcCol/dstCol % (512/sizeof)`), `tmov_common.hpp:17-20`, `tmatmul_kernel.cpp:347-353` (`RunTGEMV` reference), `constants.hpp:33-34`; PyPTO `pto_type_utils.cpp:129-137`, `pto_ops_common.cpp:2323-2325`, `matmul.cpp:308-350`. Fix: drive K alignment and row_major/none_box lhs load layout from the DSL/load (user controls K alignment via shapes/valid_shapes per the perf-sizes rule). **Being actively addressed in this worktree** (`test_gemv.py` loads `[1,k]` lhs to Mat with K aligned to 128/256) — track as in-progress, not just deferred.

- [ ] **sels (tile.sels)** — IR op reachable from `pl.sels` but NO f_codegen, and its 3-arg signature `(lhs,rhs,select_mode)` does not match the real a2a3 `TSELS` (vsel-style: `dst,mask,src,tmp,scalar`). Evidence: `src/ir/op/tile_ops/elementwise.cpp:872`; `build_output/_deps/pto-isa/include/pto/npu/a2a3/TSels.hpp:20-26`/`:52-56`; no reg in `pto_ops_common.cpp`. Fix: correct REGISTER_OP to the real TSELS shape (mirror `tile.sel`/`TSEL`) then add an f_codegen emitting `pto.tsels`; or retire the orphan op + DSL alias if redundant.

- [ ] **matmul_bias narrow-N** — the matmul_bias output (L0C Acc) valid_shape is always the full physical `[M,N]` (operand narrowing never propagated), so `tile.store` copies the full `[M,N]`; but `mad` writes only `[validRow x validCol]` and never clears L0C tail columns, so `[:, VALID_N:]` ships stale data. narrow-M/K pass (whole-row zero / no tail); narrow-N fails (stale within partially-written Nz blocks). Evidence: `src/ir/op/tile_ops/matmul.cpp:232`/`:255-257`; `build_output/_deps/pto-isa/include/pto/npu/a2a3/TMatmul.hpp:192-199`; CPU ref `pto/cpu/TMatmul.hpp:23-41`/`:196-214`; `tstore_common.hpp:163-204`; `pto_ops_common.cpp:1410`; `tests/st/runtime/ops/test_gemv.py:179-186`. Fix (primary, pypto-codegen): propagate operand valid_shapes into `DeduceTileMatMul*Type` (output valid_row from lhs, valid_col from rhs) so `tile.store` copies only `[M, VALID_N]` and GM `[:, VALID_N:]` keeps its pre-initialized zero. Alternative: clear the Acc tail columns in cube codegen. (Spans both layers; the pto-isa no-tail-zero behavior is a hardware reality to work around, not a fix target.)

## Verification notes

Several originally reported symptoms were refuted or corrected by the audit:

- **gemv_acc** — reported as a "missing acc→acc `pto.tmov`" in PyPTO. Refuted: PyPTO handles acc accumulation correctly via Acc-address aliasing (`make_acc_codegen`, same lambda as the working `matmul_acc`); the real gap is the pto-isa TGEMV_ACC TODO / missing 3-tile shared-acc overload.
- **subc / subsc** — reported as `pto.tsubc` miscomputing (`a-b-c`). Refuted: hardware computes `a-b+c` and PyPTO codegen is faithful; the defect is a PyPTO wrong-doc that advertises `a-b-c`. A naive `a-b-c` numpy reference is why ST mismatched, not a device miscompute.
- **gemv 1-row** — reported as hitting the `TExtractToA` `srcRow/dstRow % 16 == 0` static_assert. Corrected: the 1-row + row_major case explicitly *skips* `TExtractToA` (`textract_common.hpp:470-479`) and goes to `TExtractToAVector`, whose real constraint is on K (cols) `% (512/sizeof)`, not rows. Symptom cited the wrong static_assert.
- **xor / xors** — reported as "only int16/uint16". Imprecise: the static_assert also permits int8/uint8; only int32/int64 are unsupported.
- **and_ / or_ / shl / shr** — reported as "PTOAS rejects `pto.tand/tor/tshl/tshr` as unsupported on a2a3". Overbroad: the ops ARE supported; the real trigger is the **int32 element type** on tand/tor (a2a3 is 8/16-bit only, 32-bit is A5-only). Furthermore **shl / shr are likely over-attributed** — `TShl.hpp:42-45` / `TShr.hpp:42-45` allow 8/16/32-bit signed+unsigned, so i32 shifts should assemble at the ISA-impl level. The i32 error was observed for `tand` and assumed family-wide. Action: re-test shl/shr with int32 on device; if PTOAS still rejects, that is a *separate* real pto-isa/PTOAS verifier-vs-impl gap to file with an i32-shift repro — confirm on device before attributing. Correct the KNOWN_ISSUES/PR wording from "op unsupported" to "i32 element type unsupported for tand/tor on a2a3 (8/16-bit only)".
- **prelu** — reported as a DSL/`pto.tprelu` signature mismatch. Corrected: the DSL/IR 3-arg shape is correct and matches the ISA; the actual bug is the codegen mapping-table arity (2 instead of 3).
- **matmul_bias narrow-N** — reported simply as "the cube does not zero `[:, VALID_N:]`". Refined: the precise cause is a PyPTO valid_shape/value mismatch (output valid_shape hardcoded to full physical `[M,N]`), with the cube's no-tail-zero being the underlying hardware reality.

A temp-operand codegen fix for `trem/trems/txor/txors` was already landed in PR #1823; only `not_` and `matmul_bias` ST were retained on a2a3 in that PR.

title: [RFC] Move LowerCompositeOps before ConvertTensorToTileOps
body:
## Summary

Propose moving `LowerCompositeOps` (slot 14) to run **before** `ConvertTensorToTileOps` (slot 12), so composite collectives can emit clean tensor-level primitives like `pld.tensor.get`/`pld.tensor.put` and let the existing conversion registry handle flattening + VEC staging tile allocation uniformly.

## Problem

`LowerCompositeOps` currently runs **after** `ConvertTensorToTileOps`. Because tensor-to-tile conversion has already run, composite lowerings cannot emit tensor-level ops — they must duplicate the conversion logic: compute `[rows, cols]` from N-D shapes, allocate a `tile.create`, and emit `pld.tile.get`/`pld.tile.put` directly.

This duplication bit us in [feat/relax-get-dst](https://github.com/georgebisbas/pypto/tree/feat/relax-get-dst): relaxing `pld.tile.get`'s dst to accept plain `Tensor` required fixing the verifier, codegen, and DSL wrappers — but the reviewer pointed out the same fix was missing in `op_conversion_registry.cpp`. The duplicated flattening logic in `LowerCompositeOps`'s `LowerTensorBroadcastRule` must now also be kept in sync with any future type-constraint changes.

## Current pass ordering

| Slot | Pass |
|------|------|
| 12 | `ConvertTensorToTileOps` |
| 13 | `OptimizeOrchTensors` |
| 14 | `LowerCompositeOps` |

`LowerCompositeOps` has **empty PassProperties** — requires nothing, produces nothing — suggesting no hard dependency on the output of passes 12-13.

## Proposed

| Slot | Pass |
|------|------|
| ~12 | `LowerCompositeOps` ← moved earlier |
| 12 | `ConvertTensorToTileOps` ← runs after, picks up tensor-level get/put |

With this, composites could emit `pld.tensor.get(dst, peer, src)` and let `ConvertTensorToTileOps` handle the `tile.create` + `pld.tile.get` uniformly.

## Open questions

1. Does `LowerCompositeOps` depend on any `IRProperty` or IR shape from `ConvertTensorToTileOps`? The allreduce lowering emits `tile.load`/`tile.store` — those would need rewriting to tensor-level ops.

2. What does `OptimizeOrchTensors` do to orchestration-level variables? Does `LowerCompositeOps` need its output?

3. Composite ops currently use `tile.remote_load` directly. Full benefit requires rewriting all composite lowerings to emit tensor-level primitives.

## References

- `src/ir/transforms/lower_composite_ops_pass.cpp` — all lowering rules
- `src/ir/transforms/op_conversion_registry.cpp` — `pld.tensor.get`/`put` → `tile.create` + `pld.tile.get`/`put`
- `docs/en/dev/passes/12-convert_tensor_to_tile_ops.md`
- `docs/en/dev/passes/14-lower_composite_ops.md`
- Notes: [`pypto-3.0-notes/pr_plans/36-move-lower-composite-ops-before-convert-tensor-to-tile.md`](https://github.com/georgebisbas/pypto-3.0-notes/blob/main/pr_plans/36-move-lower-composite-ops-before-convert-tensor-to-tile.md)

title: [Bug] pl.split(UP_DOWN) scope producing a GM tensor for a following unsplit scope 507018-deadlocks
body:
### Diagnosis

**pypto** (codegen/runtime) — a kernel that compiles cleanly emits code that 507018-deadlocks at runtime on a2a3. The trigger is a purely structural property of the UP_DOWN split + a cross-scope GM dependency; there is no compile-time error.

### Description

A heavy `pl.spmd(optimizations=[pl.split(pl.SplitMode.UP_DOWN)])` scope that writes a GM scratch tensor which is then consumed by a **following UNSPLIT** `pl.spmd` scope **507018-deadlocks at runtime**:

```
ERROR sync_run_streams: aclrtSynchronizeStreamWithTimeout (AICPU) failed: 507018
ERROR recover_device_or_mark_unusable: Device unrecoverable after AICore error 507018 ...
RuntimeError: run_prepared failed with code 507018
```

It **compiles cleanly** (no error/warning). UB high-water in the generated IR is only ~44KB, so this is **not** a UB-budget overflow.

#### Isolating controls (every one of these PASSes — only the combination deadlocks)

| Variant | Result |
|---|---|
| Heavy UP_DOWN scope writes comb result to a scratch consumed by a following **unsplit** scope | **507018 deadlock** |
| Same scope writing **final outputs** (no following consumer scope) | PASS |
| Bare `UP_DOWN producer → scratch → unsplit consumer` with **trivial** ops (`load/mul/store`) | PASS |
| **Opposite direction**: unsplit producer → GM → `UP_DOWN` consumer | PASS |
| The heavy vector work alone under UP_DOWN (mix_x-style FP32 D-loop, OR comb softmax/sinkhorn) | PASS |
| Whole kernel **unsplit** | PASS |

So the deadlock requires BOTH: (a) a heavy UP_DOWN scope, AND (b) it produces a GM tensor consumed by a following unsplit scope. The bare directional dependency alone (trivial work) does not trigger it, and the reverse direction (unsplit→UP_DOWN) is fine.

#### Reproduction

`python models/deepseek/v4/_tmp_updown_combo.py -p a2a3` (in pypto-lib). Self-contained kernel:

```python
import pypto.language as pl

T = 128; HC_MULT = 4; HC_PAD = 8; W = HC_MULT * HC_PAD
D = 4096; T_TILE = 16; D_TILE = 256; ITERS = 4; EPS = 1e-6

@pl.jit
def combo_split(
    xb: pl.Tensor[[T, HC_MULT * D], pl.BF16],
    xp: pl.Tensor[[T, W], pl.FP32],
    xc: pl.Tensor[[T, W], pl.FP32],
    out_x: pl.Out[pl.Tensor[[T, D], pl.BF16]],
    out_c: pl.Out[pl.Tensor[[T, W], pl.FP32]],
):
    comb_scratch = pl.create_tensor([T, W], dtype=pl.FP32)
    # ---- SPLIT (UP_DOWN) producer scope: mix_x D-loop + comb softmax/sinkhorn ----
    for ob in pl.spmd(T // T_TILE, name_hint="combo", optimizations=[pl.split(pl.SplitMode.UP_DOWN)]):
        t0 = ob * T_TILE
        rs = pl.create_tile([T_TILE, 1], dtype=pl.FP32, target_memory=pl.MemorySpace.Vec)
        mx = pl.create_tile([T_TILE, 1], dtype=pl.FP32, target_memory=pl.MemorySpace.Vec)
        ph0 = pl.load(xp, [t0, 0], [T_TILE, HC_PAD], valid_shapes=[T_TILE, 1], target_memory=pl.MemorySpace.Vec)
        ph1 = pl.load(xp, [t0, 1], [T_TILE, HC_PAD], valid_shapes=[T_TILE, 1], target_memory=pl.MemorySpace.Vec)
        ph2 = pl.load(xp, [t0, 2], [T_TILE, HC_PAD], valid_shapes=[T_TILE, 1], target_memory=pl.MemorySpace.Vec)
        ph3 = pl.load(xp, [t0, 3], [T_TILE, HC_PAD], valid_shapes=[T_TILE, 1], target_memory=pl.MemorySpace.Vec)
        pre0 = pl.row_sum(pl.recip(pl.add(pl.exp(pl.neg(ph0)), 1.0)), rs)
        pre1 = pl.row_sum(pl.recip(pl.add(pl.exp(pl.neg(ph1)), 1.0)), rs)
        pre2 = pl.row_sum(pl.recip(pl.add(pl.exp(pl.neg(ph2)), 1.0)), rs)
        pre3 = pl.row_sum(pl.recip(pl.add(pl.exp(pl.neg(ph3)), 1.0)), rs)
        for db in pl.range(D // D_TILE):
            d0 = db * D_TILE
            y = pl.row_expand_mul(pl.cast(pl.load(xb, [t0, 0 * D + d0], [T_TILE, D_TILE], target_memory=pl.MemorySpace.Vec), target_type=pl.FP32), pre0)
            y = pl.add(y, pl.row_expand_mul(pl.cast(pl.load(xb, [t0, 1 * D + d0], [T_TILE, D_TILE], target_memory=pl.MemorySpace.Vec), target_type=pl.FP32), pre1))
            y = pl.add(y, pl.row_expand_mul(pl.cast(pl.load(xb, [t0, 2 * D + d0], [T_TILE, D_TILE], target_memory=pl.MemorySpace.Vec), target_type=pl.FP32), pre2))
            y = pl.add(y, pl.row_expand_mul(pl.cast(pl.load(xb, [t0, 3 * D + d0], [T_TILE, D_TILE], target_memory=pl.MemorySpace.Vec), target_type=pl.FP32), pre3))
            pl.store(pl.cast(y, target_type=pl.BF16, mode="rint"), [t0, d0], out_x)
        p0 = pl.fillpad(pl.load(xc, [t0, 0 * HC_PAD], [T_TILE, HC_PAD], valid_shapes=[T_TILE, HC_MULT], target_memory=pl.MemorySpace.Vec), pad_value=pl.PadValue.min)
        p1 = pl.fillpad(pl.load(xc, [t0, 1 * HC_PAD], [T_TILE, HC_PAD], valid_shapes=[T_TILE, HC_MULT], target_memory=pl.MemorySpace.Vec), pad_value=pl.PadValue.min)
        p2 = pl.fillpad(pl.load(xc, [t0, 2 * HC_PAD], [T_TILE, HC_PAD], valid_shapes=[T_TILE, HC_MULT], target_memory=pl.MemorySpace.Vec), pad_value=pl.PadValue.min)
        p3 = pl.fillpad(pl.load(xc, [t0, 3 * HC_PAD], [T_TILE, HC_PAD], valid_shapes=[T_TILE, HC_MULT], target_memory=pl.MemorySpace.Vec), pad_value=pl.PadValue.min)
        g0 = pl.fillpad(pl.add(pl.row_expand_div(pl.exp(pl.row_expand_sub(p0, pl.row_max(p0, mx))), pl.row_sum(pl.exp(pl.row_expand_sub(p0, pl.row_max(p0, mx))), rs)), EPS), pad_value=pl.PadValue.zero)
        g1 = pl.fillpad(pl.add(pl.row_expand_div(pl.exp(pl.row_expand_sub(p1, pl.row_max(p1, mx))), pl.row_sum(pl.exp(pl.row_expand_sub(p1, pl.row_max(p1, mx))), rs)), EPS), pad_value=pl.PadValue.zero)
        g2 = pl.fillpad(pl.add(pl.row_expand_div(pl.exp(pl.row_expand_sub(p2, pl.row_max(p2, mx))), pl.row_sum(pl.exp(pl.row_expand_sub(p2, pl.row_max(p2, mx))), rs)), EPS), pad_value=pl.PadValue.zero)
        g3 = pl.fillpad(pl.add(pl.row_expand_div(pl.exp(pl.row_expand_sub(p3, pl.row_max(p3, mx))), pl.row_sum(pl.exp(pl.row_expand_sub(p3, pl.row_max(p3, mx))), rs)), EPS), pad_value=pl.PadValue.zero)
        for it in pl.range(ITERS):
            g0 = pl.row_expand_div(g0, pl.add(pl.row_sum(g0, rs), EPS))
            g1 = pl.row_expand_div(g1, pl.add(pl.row_sum(g1, rs), EPS))
            g2 = pl.row_expand_div(g2, pl.add(pl.row_sum(g2, rs), EPS))
            g3 = pl.row_expand_div(g3, pl.add(pl.row_sum(g3, rs), EPS))
            cs = pl.add(pl.add(pl.add(g0, g1), pl.add(g2, g3)), EPS)
            g0 = pl.div(g0, cs); g1 = pl.div(g1, cs); g2 = pl.div(g2, cs); g3 = pl.div(g3, cs)
        # comb -> GM SCRATCH (consumed by the following UNSPLIT scope) == TRIGGER
        pl.store(g0, [t0, 0 * HC_PAD], comb_scratch)
        pl.store(g1, [t0, 1 * HC_PAD], comb_scratch)
        pl.store(g2, [t0, 2 * HC_PAD], comb_scratch)
        pl.store(g3, [t0, 3 * HC_PAD], comb_scratch)
    # ---- UNSPLIT consumer scope: reads the scratch the split scope wrote ----
    for ob in pl.spmd(T // T_TILE, name_hint="combo_consume"):
        t0 = ob * T_TILE
        for g in pl.range(HC_MULT):
            grp = pl.load(comb_scratch, [t0, g * HC_PAD], [T_TILE, HC_PAD], valid_shapes=[T_TILE, HC_MULT], target_memory=pl.MemorySpace.Vec)
            pl.store(pl.set_validshape(grp, T_TILE, HC_MULT), [t0, g * HC_MULT], out_c)
    return out_x
```

Redirecting the four `comb_scratch` stores to a final output (`out_c`) and deleting the consumer scope makes it PASS — that one change is the difference between hang and pass.

Note: the device run also occasionally fails earlier with `halMemCtl rc=13 (EACCES)` on some cards (an unrelated PMU/register-permission issue) — retry until a good card runs the kernel; the 507018 is deterministic on a good card.

Related (distinct root causes): #1789 (within-scope event-allocation 507018, not cross-scope), #1840 (flaky paged-attention 507018), #1820 (AIV split DSL RFC), hw-native-sys/pypto-lib#362 (UP_DOWN precision drift).

### Environment

| Component | Version |
|---|---|
| pypto-lib | `f658207` |
| pypto | `94db6529` (branch: `main`) |
| pypto runtime (submodule) | `fcc33bcb` |
| pto-isa | `a1d60eb0` |
| ptoas | `0.46` |
| CANN | not detected |

### Host Platform

Linux (aarch64)

title: [Feature] Surface simpler's RunTiming through pypto's ChipWorker/RegistrationHandle so callers can reuse simpler's --rounds benchmark mode
body:
### Summary

simpler **already has** a rounds-based benchmark mode (`runtime/simpler_setup/scene_test.py`): `--rounds N` registers the callable once (`worker.register(...)`, scene_test.py:1201), loops `for round_idx in range(rounds)` (:1222), and each round does `timing = worker.run(handle, chip_args, config=config)` (:1243) — where `simpler.Worker.run` **returns a `RunTiming`** — collecting `(host_wall_us, device_wall_us)` (:1245) and reporting per-round averages via `_log_round_timings` (:328). `runtime/tools/benchmark_rounds.sh` drives this across ST examples.

The problem: pypto's wrapper around the same simpler worker **discards** that `RunTiming`. `pypto.runtime.worker.ChipWorker.run` (`python/pypto/runtime/worker.py:402`, `:409-412`) receives the `RunTiming` from `_run_chip` (`:443-458`, which returns `self._impl.run(cid, ...)` = simpler's `RunTiming`) but returns tensor outputs only; `RegistrationHandle.__call__` (`:556-566`) delegates to it and likewise drops timing. So any caller going through pypto's public Worker path — rather than `simpler.Worker` directly — cannot reuse simpler's benchmark mode.

Please surface the `RunTiming` that simpler already returns through pypto's register-once path, so pypto callers can run the same `--rounds` benchmark (register once, run N cheap launches, read per-round `device_wall_us`).

### Motivation / Use Case

We want a benchmark mode in pypto-lib's daily CI that measures each kernel's **on-device** time (~1 ms range). pypto-lib's golden harness dispatches through pypto (`execute_compiled` / `ChipWorker`), not `simpler.Worker`, so it cannot tap simpler's existing `scene_test` `--rounds` benchmark. The only public timed pypto entry is `execute_compiled` (#1679), which is **one-shot** (`register` → `run` → `close` per call), so looping it re-pays host register/load every iteration (hundreds of ms/round), swamping device time.

The infrastructure to do this correctly already exists end-to-end in simpler (`prepare_callable` + `run_prepared(..., out_timing)` cheap repeated launches with per-invocation `PtoRunTiming`; `simpler.Worker.run` returns it; `scene_test` consumes it). The one missing link is that pypto's wrapper hides it. Closing that gap lets pypto-lib reuse simpler's benchmark mode instead of reinventing it.

- One-shot timing (#1679, CLOSED) covers `execute_compiled` / `execute_on_device` only.
- Worker init/run/close lifecycle (#1155, CLOSED) exposes register-once reuse but never returns `RunTiming` from the repeated calls.
- simpler's `scene_test` `--rounds` mode is the prior art to mirror — it just needs the pypto Worker layer to stop swallowing `RunTiming`.

### Proposed API / Behavior

Mirror what `scene_test` does with `simpler.Worker`, but through pypto's public Worker. In rough order of preference:

1. A timing-returning variant on the handle / worker so the register-once + rounds loop can read it:

```python
h = worker.register(compiled)
for _ in range(rounds):
    outputs, timing = h.run_timed(a, b)        # or worker.run_timed(compiled, ...)
    samples.append(timing.device_wall_us)
```

2. A high-level benchmark helper that owns the loop + aggregation (the pypto equivalent of `scene_test --rounds` + `_log_round_timings`):

```python
stats = pypto.runtime.benchmark(compiled, args, rounds=100, warmup=3,
                                platform="a2a3", device_id=0)
# stats.device_wall_us_min / _median / samples ...
```

3. At minimum, stop discarding the `RunTiming` already produced by `_run_chip` so it is reachable from the public register-once path.

Keep `RegistrationHandle.__call__` / `ChipWorker.run`'s existing tensor-return contract intact (timing is opt-in via the new entry point) for backward compatibility.

### Additional Context

- simpler benchmark mode (prior art): `runtime/simpler_setup/scene_test.py` — `--rounds`, register-once (`:1201`), rounds loop (`:1222`), `worker.run` returns `RunTiming` (`:1243`), collect `(host_wall_us, device_wall_us)` (`:1245`), `_log_round_timings` (`:328`); driver `runtime/tools/benchmark_rounds.sh`.
- simpler C API already supports per-invocation timing on cheap launches: `run_prepared(..., PtoRunTiming *out_timing)` (`runtime/src/common/worker/pto_runtime_c_api.h:202-208`).
- pypto gap: `ChipWorker.run` discards timing (`python/pypto/runtime/worker.py:402`, `:409-412`); `_run_chip` already returns it (`:443-458`); `RegistrationHandle.__call__` (`:556-566`).
- `execute_compiled` is one-shot (`python/pypto/runtime/runner.py:1183`).
- For L3+ DAG runs `device_wall_us` is currently 0 (only L2 single-task runs carry a real device wall) — a benchmark helper should document / handle this.
- Related: #1679, #1155
- Repo HEAD at filing: `05b1b852`

title: [Bug] pl.split(UP_DOWN) silently miscompiles a scope containing a row reduction (row_sum) — wrong numerics, no error
body:
### Diagnosis

**pypto** — `pl.split(SplitMode.UP_DOWN)` codegen. A scope whose body contains a row reduction (`pl.row_sum`) compiles cleanly and runs without error but produces WRONG output under UP_DOWN. The same scope with `SplitMode.NONE` is correct. Most likely the split pass fans the reduction's free-axis across the two AIV subblocks, yielding partial sums with no cross-subblock combine. Critically it is NOT rejected at compile time — it silently miscompiles. (Related #1034 / #1820 note split-axis reductions are meant to be *rejected*; this case slips through and corrupts results instead.)

### Description

Repro: per-token row-normalize `y[i,:] = x[i,:] / sum_j x[i,j]`. A tiny dummy matmul is present only to *engage* UP_DOWN (a pure-vector scope does not trigger the split otherwise). `T_TILE=16` so the `[T_TILE,1]` FP32 reduction tile splits to `[8,1]`=32B and does NOT hit the separate col-major 32B-align wall — isolating the reduction bug alone.

On-device (a2a3), comparing each output `y` against torch golden:

| scope | split | `y` result |
|---|---|---|
| direct: `row_sum -> [T,1] -> recip -> row_expand_mul` | NONE | PASS |
| direct (same body) | UP_DOWN | **FAIL (wrong numerics)** |
| reshape: `row_sum -> [1,T] -> recip -> [T,1]` (rms_norm pattern) | NONE | PASS |
| reshape (same body) | UP_DOWN | **FAIL (wrong numerics)** |

Both reduce forms fail under UP_DOWN and pass under NONE → it is the `row_sum` reduction itself, not the reshape.

Minimal self-contained repro (also at `models/deepseek/v4/_tmp_updown_reduce_repro.py` in pypto-lib):

\`\`\`python
import pypto.language as pl

T_TILE, C, NTASK = 16, 512, 8
T = NTASK * T_TILE
MM_M = MM_K = 128 ; MM_N = 32   # dummy-mm dims only

# split mode is the ONLY difference between PASS and FAIL:
#   NONE -> PASS,  UP_DOWN -> FAIL
@pl.jit
def repro(x: pl.Tensor[[T, C], pl.BF16],
          y: pl.Out[pl.Tensor[[T, C], pl.BF16]],
          dummy_out: pl.Out[pl.Tensor[[NTASK * MM_M, MM_N], pl.BF16]]):
    for t in pl.spmd(NTASK, optimizations=[pl.split(pl.SplitMode.UP_DOWN)]):  # vs NONE
        t0 = t * T_TILE
        acc = pl.matmul(x[0:MM_M, 0:MM_K], x[0:MM_N, 0:MM_K], b_trans=True, out_dtype=pl.FP32)
        dummy_out[t*MM_M:t*MM_M+MM_M, 0:MM_N] = pl.cast(acc, target_type=pl.BF16, mode="rint")
        xc = pl.cast(x[t0:t0+T_TILE, 0:C], target_type=pl.FP32)
        inv = pl.recip(pl.row_sum(xc))            # [T_TILE,1]  <-- reduction
        yc = pl.row_expand_mul(xc, inv)
        y[t0:t0+T_TILE, 0:C] = pl.cast(yc, target_type=pl.BF16, mode="rint")
    return y
\`\`\`

Expected: UP_DOWN either produces correct `y` (combine partial sums across subblocks) or is rejected at compile time. Actual: silent wrong output.

### Environment

| Component | Version |
|---|---|
| pypto-lib | \`9f31b7e\` |
| pypto | \`c3e362ba\` (branch: \`main\`) |
| pypto runtime (submodule) | \`95197fd7\` |
| pto-isa | \`1ba8f54b\` (branch: \`main\`) |
| ptoas | \`0.46\` |
| CANN | \`9.0.0\` |

### Host Platform

\`Linux (aarch64)\`

### Additional Context

Related: hw-native-sys/pypto#1034, hw-native-sys/pypto#1820 (split-axis reduction should be rejected), hw-native-sys/pypto-lib#362 (reduction-order drift under split in a matmul scope). Surfaced while testing the dummy-mm→UP_DOWN trick on DeepSeek-V4 decode `rms_norm`; the production hc_pre work already avoids this by keeping `row_sum`/RMS out of split scopes.
