title: [Bug] dep_gen (DFX) instrumentation breaks full-occupancy pl.system.syncall -> AICore timeout 507018
body:
### Component

Backend (runtime `dep_gen` / DFX dependency-capture instrumentation)

### Description

`dep_gen` (the DFX dependency-capture runtime instrumentation, `enable_dep_gen=True`, on by default) perturbs AICore/AIV core occupancy and breaks the **full-occupancy contract** of `pl.system.syncall(core_type="mix")`.

An in-kernel `syncall(core_type="mix")` is a hard FFTS cross-core barrier: **every** dispatched block must reach it (on 910B that is all 24 AIC + 48 AIV lanes). With `dep_gen` enabled, the extra instrumentation work changes which cores are occupied / when they arrive, so some cores never reach the barrier and the AICore side times out.

The kernel is functionally correct: with `dep_gen` disabled the exact same program passes golden validation on device. Only the DFX instrumentation flips it from PASS to a hang/timeout, so `dep_gen` is altering scheduling/occupancy behavior it should be transparent to.

### Steps to Reproduce

```markdown
1. Take a mixed cube+vector `@pl.jit` kernel that dispatches all NUM_CORES
   blocks so every AIC (24) + AIV (48) lane participates, and uses an in-kernel
   `pl.system.syncall(core_type="mix")` barrier (full-occupancy contract: every
   dispatched block must arrive at the barrier).
2. Run it on a 910B device with dep_gen ENABLED (the default, enable_dep_gen=True).
   Concrete downstream repro — pypto-lib qwen3-14b fused decode kernel:
     python models/qwen3/14b/decode_layer.py -p a2a3 -d 0     # dep_gen on
3. Observe the run hang, then abort with AICore timeout 507018.
4. Re-run the SAME kernel with dep_gen disabled:
     python models/qwen3/14b/decode_layer.py -p a2a3 -d 0 --no-dep-gen
   -> golden PASS.
```

### Expected Behavior

`dep_gen` (DFX dependency capture) instrumentation must be transparent to scheduling/occupancy: enabling it must not change the set of cores that reach a full-occupancy `syncall(core_type="mix")` barrier. The kernel should PASS regardless of the `dep_gen` setting.

### Actual Behavior

With `dep_gen` enabled the run hangs, then fails:

```
[ERROR] validate_runtime_impl: [runtime_maker.cpp:623] PTO2 runtime failed: orch_error_code=0 sched_error_code=100 runtime_status=-100
RuntimeError: run_prepared failed with code 507018
```

Disabling `dep_gen` (`--no-dep-gen` / `enable_dep_gen=False`) makes the identical kernel PASS. The instrumentation appears to occupy cores / add work such that not all AIC+AIV blocks arrive at the `syncall` barrier, producing the AICore timeout (507018).

### Git Commit ID

80bac774e64f55c5e7b336d4184f9222ff43073d

### NPU Kind

Ascend 910B

### Host Platform

Linux (aarch64)

### Additional Context

- Downstream kernel / PR exercising this: hw-native-sys/pypto-lib#656 (fused rope+attn+softmax qwen3-14b decode; in-kernel `syncall` barriers between rope / attn / online-softmax phases).
- Worked around downstream in pypto-lib CI with a per-file `# ci: no-dep-gen` directive that appends `--no-dep-gen` for kernels using a full-occupancy `syncall`. That workaround should be removable once this is fixed.
- Related (same AICore error code 507018, but different root cause): #1840 (intermittent paged-attention device fault), #1789 (fence EVENT_ID reallocation hazard).

title: [Bug] hard-form pl.system.syncall deadlocks (AICore 507018) at partial core occupancy — no compile-time check
body:
### Component

Codegen

### Description

A kernel using the **hard (FFTS) form** of `pl.system.syncall` deadlocks on device with `RuntimeError: run_prepared failed with code 507018` (AICore timeout) when the enclosing `pl.spmd(N)` launch does **not fill all physical cores** of the barrier's `core_type`. The hard barrier (`SYNC_AIV_ONLY_ALL` / mix) waits for *every* physical core of that type to arrive; the unlaunched cores never reach the barrier, so the FFTS wait never completes.

There is **no compile-time diagnostic** — the mistake only surfaces at runtime as a timeout, and it leaves the device draining/reset (subsequent runs on that device fail with `code 13` until reset). The compiler already knows both the launch block count (`pl.spmd(N)`) and the target SoC's physical core count per core type, so this is statically checkable.

### Steps to Reproduce

Minimal on-device repro (Ascend 910B = 48 physical AIV cores): a SPMD elementwise add with a hard `pl.system.syncall(core_type="aiv_only")` between the loads and the add, launched at partial occupancy. Mirrors `tests/st/runtime/cross_core/test_syncall.py` (whose docstring already documents that hard SYNCALL needs full AIV occupancy).

```python
TR = TC = 128
N = 24  # < 48 physical AIV  -> PARTIAL occupancy (set N = 48 for the passing control)

@pl.program
class PartialSyncAll:
    @pl.function(type=pl.FunctionType.InCore)
    def add(self, a: pl.Tensor[[N*TR, TC], pl.FP32], b: pl.Tensor[[N*TR, TC], pl.FP32],
            out: pl.Out[pl.Tensor[[N*TR, TC], pl.FP32]]) -> pl.Tensor[[N*TR, TC], pl.FP32]:
        i = pl.tile.get_block_idx(); o = i * TR
        ta = pl.load(a, [o, 0], [TR, TC]); tb = pl.load(b, [o, 0], [TR, TC])
        pl.system.syncall(core_type="aiv_only")          # HARD barrier
        out = pl.store(pl.add(ta, tb), [o, 0], out); return out

    @pl.function(type=pl.FunctionType.Orchestration)
    def orchestrator(self, a, b, out):
        with pl.spmd(N):                                  # N=24 < 48 -> partial
            out = self.add(a, b, out)
        return out
```

Run on `a2a3`. `pl.spmd(24)` (partial) → 507018. Changing **only** `pl.spmd(24)` → `pl.spmd(48)` (full occupancy) → **PASS**. Occupancy is the sole variable.

### Expected Behavior

The compiler rejects a hard-mode `syncall` whose enclosing `pl.spmd` launch does not fill all physical cores of the barrier's `core_type`, with a clear compile-time error, e.g.:

> `hard pl.system.syncall(core_type="aiv_only") requires the spmd launch to fill all 48 AIV cores, but pl.spmd(24) launches 24 blocks. Use mode="soft" (GM-polling) for partial occupancy.`

At minimum, a documented static diagnostic instead of a silent runtime 507018 + device reset.

### Actual Behavior

Compiles silently; on device the run hangs until the FFTS wait times out and the device is force-reset:

```
[ERROR] sync_run_streams: aclrtSynchronizeStreamWithTimeout (AICPU) failed: 507018
[ERROR] recover_device_or_mark_unusable: AICore error 507018: bounded device drain failed (force reset will follow in finalize)
RuntimeError: run_prepared failed with code 507018
```

The device is left unusable afterwards (later runs fail with `code 13` until it recovers).

### Environment

| Component | Version |
|---|---|
| pypto | `d598b41b` (branch: `main`) |
| pypto runtime (submodule) | `02bd0c4f` |
| pto-isa | `e722679` |
| ptoas | `0.48` |
| CANN | not detected |

### Host Platform

Linux (aarch64)

### NPU Kind

Ascend 910B

### Additional Context

- The **soft** form already works at partial occupancy: `pl.system.syncall(mode="soft", core_type="aiv_only", gm_workspace=ws, used_cores=N)` (see the `*Soft*` case in `tests/st/runtime/cross_core/test_syncall.py`). A compile-time check for the hard form would make the hard-vs-soft occupancy contract explicit and catch the footgun early.
- Related: hw-native-sys/pypto#1931 (dep_gen instrumentation perturbing a *full*-occupancy syncall → 507018) — a distinct root cause; this issue is specifically the **missing compile-time occupancy guard** for the hard form.

title: manual_scope writes need a first-class dependency bridge for downstream auto dependency analysis
body:
## Problem

When a kernel uses `pl.manual_scope()` to avoid conservative auto-dependency serialization, writes performed inside the manual scope are not visible enough to downstream auto dependency analysis.

In `pypto-lib` DeepSeek V4 routed expert, we currently need an extra marker task (`exp_routed_tile_done`) after each non-empty expert tile. The marker performs a tiny self-assignment on `recv_y` only to make the downstream combine stage wait for the manual compute chain.

Conceptually the desired dependency is:

```text
manual compute chain -> recv_y tile is ready -> downstream combine
```

But today we have to encode it as:

```text
manual compute chain -> exp_routed_tile_done marker task -> downstream combine
```

The marker task has no real computation value. It is only a dependency bridge.

## Why this matters

This exposes an incompleteness in manual dependency modeling:

1. Keeping `exp_w2_act` inside `manual_scope()` removes the routed expert internal serialization, but downstream auto dependency analysis does not reliably know that the `recv_y` tile write is ready.
2. Moving `exp_w2_act` outside `manual_scope()` makes the `recv_y` write visible to auto dependency analysis, but dynamic `recv_y` slice writes become conservative again and can serialize across tiles.
3. The current workaround adds one marker task per non-empty tile, which preserves correctness and avoids the large serialization outliers, but adds scheduler/task overhead and is semantically awkward.

## Observed evidence

In `pypto-lib` experiments:

- With `exp_w2_act` outside `manual_scope()` and `deps=[w2_tids[tile_idx]]`, standalone `expert_routed.py` can pass correctness.
- In the full 7-layer `decode_fwd.py` graph, rank0 swimlane showed `exp_w2_act_2` serialization even though each tile is logically independent:
  - `build_output/_jit_l3_decode_fwd_20260703_091204/dfx_outputs/rank0/d0/merged_swimlane_20260703_091320.json`
  - `exp_w2_act_2` count: 44
  - span: ~3491.42 us
  - duration sum: ~305.34 us
  - dependency fanin showed a chain where later `exp_w2_act_2` tasks depended on previous `exp_w2_act_2` tasks, e.g. `r1t359` depending on `r1t357`.

With the marker workaround, the model can express the intended downstream wait, but at the cost of extra `exp_routed_tile_done` tasks.

## Minimal pattern

Pseudo-pattern of the current workaround:

```python
with pl.manual_scope():
    with pl.spmd(..., name_hint="exp_w2_mm", deps=[...]) as w2_tid:
        ...
    with pl.spmd(..., name_hint="exp_w2_act", deps=[w2_tid]) as w2_act_tid:
        recv_y_flat[...] = ...

# Outside manual_scope, just to register recv_y readiness for auto deps.
with pl.spmd(..., name_hint="exp_routed_tile_done", deps=[w2_act_tid]):
    recv_y_flat[tile_slice, 0:16] = recv_y_flat[tile_slice, 0:16]
```

What we want is a first-class way to tell PyPTO that a manual-scope task has produced a specific tensor slice/range, so downstream auto dependency analysis can wait on that producer without requiring a fake read/write marker task.

## Requested capability

Please consider adding an API or compiler/runtime support for one of these:

- declare that a manual-scope task writes a tensor slice/range visible to downstream auto dependency analysis;
- export a manual dependency token as the producer of a tensor region;
- create a zero-overhead dependency fence/annotation that connects manual-scope task completion to downstream tensor readiness;
- or otherwise let `manual_scope` participate in auto dependency analysis at explicit output boundaries.

The important property is: the downstream auto-dependent consumer should depend on the real manual producer task, not on an extra no-op marker task.

## Expected behavior

For independent routed expert tiles writing disjoint `recv_y` regions:

- no conservative serialization among independent tile writers;
- downstream combine waits for each tile's actual producer;
- no extra marker task per tile is needed.

title: bug: explicit deps=[task_id] silently dropped inside manual_scope for tasks that read tensors
body:
## Summary

Inside `pl.manual_scope()`, explicit `deps=[task_id]` on a task that reads a tensor written outside the scope is **silently dropped** by the compiler. The tensor dep (from the tensor's producer) overrides/supersedes the explicit TaskId dep, even though `manual_scope` documentation states "only explicit `deps=[tid]` edges apply".

## Repro

```python
with pl.manual_scope():
    gate = pl.system.task_dummy(deps=None)  # unflagged gate, no deps

    # This task READS hidden_states (written outside manual_scope by dcr_xgamma)
    with pl.at(level=pl.Level.CORE_GROUP, name_hint="rms_recip", deps=[gate]) as rms_tid:
        x = hidden_states[:, ...]  # tensor read
        ...

    # This task only WRITES (no tensor read from outside scope)
    with pl.at(level=pl.Level.CORE_GROUP, name_hint="kv_seed", deps=[gate]) as kv_seed_tid:
        k_proj = pl.assemble(k_proj, pl.full(..., value=0.0), ...)
```

## Expected behavior

Both `rms_recip` and `kv_seed` should have `gate` as their (only) producer in the dep graph, since:
1. `deps=[gate]` is explicitly set
2. We're inside `manual_scope` which suppresses auto-dep tracking

## Actual behavior

- **kv_seed** (write-only): `gate` IS the producer ✓
- **rms_recip** (reads `hidden_states`): `gate` is **silently dropped** — the producer becomes whoever last wrote `hidden_states` (e.g. `dcr_xgamma` from the previous layer), NOT `gate` ✗

## Evidence from compiled orchestration C++

**kv_seed** — explicit deps preserved:
```cpp
PTO2TaskId params_t6_deps[1];
if (gate_dummy.is_valid()) params_t6_deps[...] = gate_dummy;
params_t6.set_dependencies(params_t6_deps, params_t6_deps_count);
```

**rms_recip** — no `set_dependencies` with gate, only tensor dep from `add_input(cur)`:
```cpp
L0TaskArgs params_t3;
params_t3.add_input(cur);  // tensor dep → connected to dcr_xgamma, NOT gate
// NO set_dependencies with gate
```

## Impact

This breaks the early-dispatch gate pattern: a user creates an unflagged `task_dummy` to prevent a consumer from being early-dispatched (by ensuring it has an unflagged producer). The gate works for write-only tasks but silently fails for tasks that read tensors — the compiler replaces the gate with the tensor producer, which may be flagged, causing unintended early dispatch.

## Environment

- pypto: `39a13a90` (origin/main)
- simpler: `2593759e` (origin/main, post-#1245)
- workload: qwen3-14B `decode_fwd.py` 2-layer decode

title: [Bug] L3 swimlane dispatch: _make_call_config assigns int enable_l2_swimlane to bool enable_dep_gen setter → TypeError
body:
### Component

Other — Runtime (L3 distributed dispatch, `python/pypto/runtime/distributed_runner.py`)

### Description

In `_make_call_config` (`python/pypto/runtime/distributed_runner.py`, line 431), `enable_dep_gen` is computed as:

```python
call_config.enable_dep_gen = dfx.enable_dep_gen or (
    co_enable_swimlane_dep_gen and dfx.enable_l2_swimlane
)
```

`dfx.enable_l2_swimlane` is an **int** (0/1/2, from a `type=int, choices=(0,1,2)` CLI flag). With `enable_dep_gen` falsy and `co_enable_swimlane_dep_gen` True, the `and`/`or` chain returns the int `1` (not a bool), which is then assigned to the `CallConfig.enable_dep_gen` pybind setter — and that setter only accepts `bool`. So **any L3 distributed run with `--enable-l2-swimlane 1` crashes** in `_make_call_config` before dispatch.

Introduced by PR #1872 (commit `6ba49ef9`), which added this DFX block wholesale — earlier revisions of `_make_call_config` had no such assignment. Reached on the resident/prepared-worker path (`_run_compiled` → `_make_call_config`).

A one-line `bool(...)` wrap fixes it (verified locally — the swimlane run then passes end-to-end and writes `merged_swimlane_*.json`):

```python
call_config.enable_dep_gen = bool(
    dfx.enable_dep_gen or (co_enable_swimlane_dep_gen and dfx.enable_l2_swimlane)
)
```

### Steps to Reproduce

Any L3 distributed kernel run with swimlane enabled, e.g. (in pypto-lib):

```bash
python models/deepseek/v4/decode_layer.py -p a2a3 --ep 2 --enable-l2-swimlane 1 -d <dev>
```

### Expected Behavior

Swimlane-enabled L3 dispatch runs; `enable_dep_gen` is assigned a `bool`.

### Actual Behavior

```
File ".../pypto/runtime/distributed_runner.py", line 431, in _make_call_config
    call_config.enable_dep_gen = dfx.enable_dep_gen or (
TypeError: (): incompatible function arguments. The following argument types are supported:
    1. (self, arg: bool, /) -> None

Invoked with types: _task_interface.CallConfig, int
```

### Git Commit ID

`7a3a381e6461c3077135e317b168a3073cf347f2`

### NPU Kind

N/A (not hardware-specific)

### Host Platform

Linux (aarch64)

### Additional Context

Related: #1931 (dep_gen co-enabled with swimlane trips the full-occupancy `pl.system.syncall` → AICore timeout 507018 — the same PR #1872 co-enable path). Note the suggested `bool()` fix only addresses the type crash and leaves the co-enable behavior intact; kernels carrying a `no-dep-gen` marker may still need #1931 addressed separately.

title: [Feature] Explicit `alloc_tile` IR op so codegen is 1:1 (root-fix for PTOAS if/else-yield miscompile)
body:
### Summary

Promote the PTO **tile handle** (`pto.alloc_tile`) from a codegen-synthesized artifact to a **first-class IR op** (`alloc_tile`), so PTO codegen becomes a strict 1:1 emitter and tile-buffer *placement / aliasing* decisions move out of codegen into the IR/passes. This is the root fix for a confirmed `memory_planner=PTOAS` miscompile and removes a whole class of codegen-scope hacks.

### Motivation / Use Case

**Confirmed correctness bug** (found while extending `memory_planner=PTOAS`, added in #1934): `compile(memory_planner=MemoryPlanner.PTOAS)` **silently miscompiles any `if/else`-yield (phi) kernel**.

Minimal repro — `if c: r1 = mul(ta, ta); yield r1  else: r2 = add(ta, ta); yield r2`, then store the phi result:

- **PYPTO / level3 (correct):** `r1` and `res` share addr `16384`; the else branch inserts a `TMOV` copying `r2` into `res`'s addr → the store reads the right data.
- **PTOAS / level2 (WRONG):** `res` gets its own addr `32768`; the then-branch writes `r1 @16384`, the else writes `r2 @32768`, **no `TMOV`** → taking the `then` branch stores `res @32768`, which was **never written** → garbage. Confirmed by compiling the `.pto` with `ptoas` and reading the CCE (`TASSIGN` addresses + missing `TMOV`); at the MLIR level ptoas rejects it as `use of undeclared SSA value name` once handles are shared in-branch.

Loop-carried accumulators are already correct; the hole is must-alias that needs a codegen-emitted `tile.move` or a return_var handle-merge: **if/else-yield**, and **for-loops whose yield buffer diverges from init**.

**Root cause — two levels, but only one is on the IR:**

- `tile.alloc` (existing IR op): allocates a base memory *region* → base `Ptr` (`mem_vec_N`); `InitMemRef` hoists it to the function head. **Codegen emits nothing for it** (`MakeTileAllocCodegenPTO` returns `""`, `src/backend/common/pto_ops_common.cpp:1871`); it only supplies the base-`Ptr` identity that `MemRef`s share for aliasing.
- `pto.alloc_tile` (the tile *handle*): **not an IR op** — it is *synthesized by codegen* (`PTOCodegen::EmitAllocTileForVar`) per tile var, emitted **at the var's definition site** (in-branch for `r1`). So the "which scope / which handle aliases which" decision leaks into codegen. In level3 the shared physical `addr` masks it; in level2 (no addr) a handle defined inside a `then`-branch but used in the `else`-branch and after the `if` is an undeclared-SSA scoping violation.

This also violates the repo's own codegen principle (`docs/en/dev/codegen/00-pto_codegen.md`: *"codegen must be a strict 1-to-1 translation — no analysis / placement decisions"*).

### Proposed API / Behavior

**Design (A): explicit `alloc_tile` op, keep the two levels.**

- Keep `tile.alloc` = region alloc (base `Ptr`), unchanged; codegen still emits nothing.
- New **`alloc_tile` IR op** = the handle: references `(base Ptr, byte_offset, shape)` with an **optional physical `addr` attribute** (present under PYPTO/level3, absent under PTOAS/level2). Produces a tile-handle SSA value.
- A **pass owns placement + must-alias dedup**: for each must-alias group (if-phi = both branch yields + return_var; loop-carry; in-place DPS) emit **exactly one** `alloc_tile` op at the scope that **dominates all uses** (function head / loop pre-header), and make all members **use that handle SSA**. Aliasing becomes **structural (shared SSA)**, not addr-based.
- **Codegen degrades to strict 1:1**: emit `pto.alloc_tile` where the IR `alloc_tile` op sits; `addr` is just an optional attribute. Delete `EmitAllocTileForVar`'s synthesis and the per-var / return_var handle-dedup hacks; `emit_tile_addr` collapses to "does the op carry an `addr` attr".
- **Verifier**: add "every `alloc_tile` result dominates all its uses" (SSA dominance) — currently unenforceable because the handle isn't on the IR.

This fixes the class at the root: PTOAS if/else-yield and divergent for-yields become correct with **no `tile.move`** and **no codegen scope decisions**; level2/level3 differ only by the presence of the `addr` attribute.

**Relationship to existing `tile.alloc`:** two complementary levels — `tile.alloc` = memory region (base `Ptr`), new `alloc_tile` = handle/view onto a region.

**Migration / affected components:**
1. Define the `alloc_tile` IR op (C++ IR + bindings + stubs + printer/parser).
2. `InitMemRef` (or a dedicated pass): emit explicit `alloc_tile` ops at correct scope instead of leaving handle synthesis to codegen.
3. New/extended pass to place + must-alias-dedup `alloc_tile` ops (this is where `MaterializeSemanticAliases`'s if-phi unification belongs).
4. Codegen: `EmitAllocTileForVar` → 1:1 emit from the IR op; remove handle-dedup / return_var special-casing (`pto_codegen.cpp`, `pto_control_flow_codegen.cpp`).
5. Adapt `MemoryReuse` / `AllocateMemoryAddr` (they set `byte_offset_`/addr on MemRefs → now set the `addr` attr on `alloc_tile` ops).
6. Verifier: alloc_tile-dominates-uses.
7. Docs (en + zh-cn) + tests.

### Alternatives Considered

- **Design (B): collapse to one op** — a single `alloc_tile` that allocates and returns a handle, with aliasing via shared SSA and views via a `subview` op, retiring the base-`Ptr`/`MemRef` aliasing model. Cleaner end-state but a much larger redesign; out of scope here, noted as a possible future direction.
- **Interim guard (not a fix):** make PTOAS **error out** for if/else-yield (and divergent for-yield) so it can't silently miscompile until (A) lands. Recommended as a stopgap.

### Additional Context

- Introduced by / relates to **#1934** (merged; added `memory_planner=PTOAS`). The PTOAS **loop-carry** path is correct; only the must-alias-with-move cases are affected.
- **WIP prototype** exists on local worktree branch `feat/memory-planner-stage2`: (1) `MaterializeSemanticAliases` unifies if-phi branch yields + return_var onto one MemRef in PTOAS mode with **no `tile.move`** — verified correct at IR level; (2) codegen dedups the branch producers (`r1`/`r2` → one handle). It stalls exactly at the in-branch scoping wall this issue fixes — which is why the proper fix is the explicit-op design.
- Effort: **large** (RFC-level IR refactor). Priority: **high-ish** (latent silent miscompile in a merged, opt-in feature).

title: [Performance] Support valid-shape-preserving packed tile layouts for small Sinkhorn reductions
body:
## Summary

PyPTO needs a way to express a valid-shape-preserving packed tile layout for small batched reductions, so kernels like DeepSeek V4 `hc_pre` can rewrite Sinkhorn normalization without falling back to GM scratch or losing correctness.

The motivating pypto-lib performance issue is: https://github.com/hw-native-sys/pypto-lib/issues/700

## Git Commit ID

`a39100f296b15ef2d4086bff3389a2055aef1f9d`

## NPU Kind

Other / target used by the reproducer is `a2a3`.

## Host Platform

Linux (aarch64)

## Reproduction Script

The current repro is the pypto-lib DeepSeek V4 HC pre-processing kernel:

```bash
# In pypto-lib
python models/deepseek/v4/hc_pre.py -p a2a3 -d <device>
```

The problematic pattern is a small Sinkhorn over 4x4 matrices. Today the implementation naturally becomes four narrow row tiles, each shaped like `[T, 8]` with valid columns = 4. Conceptually, the optimization wants to write something equivalent to:

```text
# Current logical layout
row0, row1, row2, row3: [T, 8(valid 4)]

# Desired row-normalization layout
stack(row0, row1, row2, row3): [T * 4, 8(valid 4)]
row_sum / row_normalize on the packed tile

# Desired regrouping for column normalization
reshape/regroup back to [T, 4, 4] semantics without GM scratch
```

During an experimental layout rewrite, the following limitations blocked a correct and efficient implementation:

```text
pl.assemble(...) could not assemble a TileType source into tensor scratch.
set_validshape(...) on a sliced/static tile failed because the source tile_buf did not carry dynamic validShape.
A store/load scratch fallback compiled, but produced incorrect comb output and added overhead.
```

## Expected Performance

PyPTO should allow this packed small-reduction layout to be represented as tile/view transformations while preserving valid shape and dependencies. For the pypto-lib workload, the desired outcome is better vector lane utilization in the Sinkhorn section without increasing GM traffic or changing numerical behavior.

The in-core target is to avoid the current nearly idle late vector lanes for the `COMB_T_TILE=8` layout:

| Current layout | Active time / events |
| --- | ---: |
| `VECTOR#7` | `0.022us / 2 events` |
| `VECTOR#8` | `0.018us / 2 events` |
| `VECTOR#9` | `0.009us / 1 event` |

An experimental constant-only change to `COMB_T_TILE=16` improved some sublane utilization, but did not provide a robust L2 win, so the request here is for a real layout/view capability rather than simple tile-size tuning.

## Actual Performance

Current PyPTO patterns force the pypto-lib kernel to keep four independent narrow Sinkhorn row tiles. The resulting vector work is imbalanced, and layout rewrite attempts either fail to compile cleanly or require GM scratch with correctness/performance problems.

Measured pypto-lib baseline on the investigated setup:

- `core0.veccore0`: VECTOR about `526615` cycles
- `core0.veccore1`: VECTOR about `523449` cycles
- `core0.cubecore0`: CUBE about `4271` cycles

This indicates the bottleneck is vector/Sinkhorn rather than cube.

## Profiling Data (Optional)

pypto-lib local trace artifact from the investigation:

```text
build_output/incore_hc_pre_fused_hc_pre_decode_real_20260706_1555/hc_pre_fused.clean.json
```

Some local experiments:

- `COMB_T_TILE=16`: improved `VECTOR#7/#8` in-core utilization, but L2 timings were noisy and not a stable win.
- `COMB_T_TILE=32`: passed decode but was slower in the checked run.
- Stack-to-scratch rewrite: compiled/runs, but `comb` failed validation (`122/128` mismatches, max abs diff about `0.151278`) and was slower.

## Additional Context

Related existing PyPTO issues that may overlap with the needed compiler behavior:

- https://github.com/hw-native-sys/pypto/issues/594 (`valid_shape` inference)
- https://github.com/hw-native-sys/pypto/issues/1034 (split-axis reduction semantics)

Requested capability could be one or more of:

- tile stack/concat for same-shaped tiles while preserving valid shape,
- valid-shape-preserving tile reshape/regroup views,
- valid-shape-preserving slices from packed tiles,
- or a safe compiler-recognized same-core scratch pattern with correct dependencies and no unnecessary GM round-trip.

title: [RFC] In-core Tensor reinterpret by shape+stride: extend tensor.reshape vs new tensor.view
body:
### Summary

We need a way to reinterpret a **GM Tensor over the same physical buffer** with a chosen shape + stride **in-core** (zero-copy). Today codegen only emits a **fixed, canonically-derived** `pto.make_tensor_view` per kernel parameter (`EmitMakeTensorViews`, `src/codegen/pto/pto_codegen.cpp:840`); there is no way to re-interpret a Tensor with a chosen shape/stride inside a kernel. `tensor.as_layout` is the only in-core Tensor reinterpret today, but it only does an ND↔DN flip with internally-derived shape/stride.

This RFC compares **two candidate approaches** and asks which to take:

- **Approach A** — extend the existing `tensor.reshape` to work in-core.
- **Approach B** — add a new `tensor.view` op modeled on `tensor.as_layout`.

For the two motivating scenarios the resulting IR type and emitted `.pto` are **byte-identical** between A and B; the decision is about semantics, surface area, and user-facing expressiveness (see Alternatives).

### Motivation

Two concrete needs:

1. **High-dim NZ `tile.load` 2D-collapse.** `MakeTileLoadCodegenPTO` (`src/backend/common/pto_ops_common.cpp:1534-1602`, ~70 lines) hand-folds a rank>2 NZ Mat load's leading dims into a synthetic 2D `make_tensor_view` (`[prod(leading), last]`, strides `[last, 1]`) plus mixed-radix offset decomposition, in the codegen hot path — the hardware ND2NZ path only accepts a 2D GlobalTensor. An in-core reinterpret lets `FlattenTileNdTo2D` (pass 15) produce the 2D tensor **in IR** and delete this special-casing.

2. **allreduce lowering flatten-to-1D for auto-chunk.** An upcoming lowering refactor wants to flatten a high-dim window-bound tensor to **1D** `[TOTAL]` (`TOTAL = prod(all dims)`) so it can **auto-chunk** for the collective. This needs a reinterpret that preserves the `DistributedTensorType` window binding.

Both scenarios only need a **canonical row-major** reinterpret (NZ → 2D strides `[C,1]`; allreduce → 1D strides `[1]`); neither needs a non-canonical/arbitrary stride today.

### Background: how in-core dispatch and tensor→tile conversion work

- **orch vs in-core codegen** is dispatched by the op's **scope**, not the op itself: the same op name registers both a `REGISTER_ORCHESTRATION_OP` handler (`src/codegen/tensor_op_codegen.cpp`) and an in-core `backend.RegisterOp(...).f_codegen` handler (`src/backend/common/pto_ops_common.cpp`). `tensor.as_layout` already has **both**.
- **`ConvertTensorToTileOps` (pass 12)** decides tensor→tile purely by identity (`src/ir/transforms/convert_tensor_to_tile_ops_pass.cpp:531-546`): if the op is in `OpConversionRegistry` it is converted to a tile op; if it is a `TensorOp`-category op that is neither registered nor in `kPassthroughTensorOps` it hard-fails; otherwise it passes through unchanged (stays a Tensor, later emits `make_tensor_view`). `tensor.as_layout` passes through because it does not set a `TensorOp` category.
- **Crucial existing fact:** `src/ir/transforms/op_conversion_registry.cpp:174` already has `RegisterSimple("tensor.reshape", "tile.reshape")`. So an in-core `tensor.reshape` **already means "become a tile"** — pass 12 converts it and inserts a Phase-1 Vec `tile.load`.

Note both motivating consumers insert the reinterpret **after** pass 12 (`FlattenTileNdTo2D` = pass 15, allreduce lowering = pass 14), so pass 12 never sees the inserted node in either approach.

### Approach A — extend `tensor.reshape` to in-core

Changes:
- Add an **in-core PTO codegen handler** for `tensor.reshape` (emit `pto.make_tensor_view` + `RegisterTensorView`, sharing the `as_layout` path at `pto_ops_common.cpp:3470`; strides derived canonically by `EmitMakeTensorViews`).
- Add `set_output_memory_inherit_input()` to the `tensor.reshape` registration (zero-copy view must alias the input MemRef).
- Switch `DeduceTensorReshapeType` from strict `As<TensorType>` to `AsTensorTypeLike` + `DistributedTensorType` passthrough (preserve `window_buffer_`, strategy β, cf `tensor.slice` `src/ir/op/tensor_ops/memory.cpp:268-272`).
- **No change to `op_conversion_registry.cpp`.** The existing `tensor.reshape → tile.reshape` entry still governs *pre-pass-12* user reshapes; the *post-pass-12* inserted `tensor.reshape` never reaches the registry, stays a Tensor, and hits the new in-core handler.

Emitted code (scenario 1, NZ flatten to 2D):
```
x2d = tensor.reshape(x, (B*M, K))        # inserted by FlattenTileNdTo2D (post pass 12)
  ->  %x2d = pto.make_tensor_view %x, shape = [B*M, K], strides = [K, 1] {layout = #pto.layout<nd>}
```
Emitted code (scenario 2, allreduce flatten to 1D):
```
t1d = tensor.reshape(target, (TOTAL,))   # DistributedTensor, window_buffer_ preserved
  ->  %t1d = pto.make_tensor_view %target, shape = [TOTAL], strides = [1] {layout = #pto.layout<nd>}
```

Pros:
- No new op — smallest surface (no new DSL symbol / stub / docs).
- `reshape ≡ canonical flatten` reads naturally.

Cons / limitations:
- **Same name, two meanings by pipeline position:** `tensor.reshape` before pass 12 → `tile.reshape`; after pass 12 → GM view. Distinguished only by *where in the pipeline* it appears.
- **Users cannot express a GM reinterpret via `reshape`** in InCore DSL — a user-written `pl.reshape` is pre-pass-12 and always becomes a tile.
- **Canonical strides only** (reshape has no stride param) — no arbitrary/non-canonical reinterpret. (Not a blocker for the two current scenarios.)

### Approach B — new `tensor.view` op

```python
pl.tensor.view(input: Tensor, shape: Sequence[int], stride: Sequence[int] | None = None,
               *, layout: TensorLayout = ND) -> Tensor
```
- Single meaning: reinterpret a GM Tensor over the same buffer; inherits input MemRef; **never** converts to a tile. Modeled on `tensor.as_layout` — **not** in `OpConversionRegistry`, no `TensorOp` category → passes through pass 12.
- `stride=None` → canonical row-major; explicit `stride` supported for arbitrary reinterprets.
- `AsTensorTypeLike` input; `DistributedTensorType` passthrough (strategy β).
- Dual codegen (orch metadata reinterpret + in-core `make_tensor_view` + `RegisterTensorView`), same as `as_layout`.

Emitted code is identical to Approach A for both scenarios (`tensor.view(x,(B*M,K),(K,1))` / `tensor.view(target,(TOTAL,),(1,))` → the same `make_tensor_view`).

Pros:
- No semantic collision with `reshape → tile.reshape`; single, unambiguous meaning.
- **Users can explicitly express** a GM reinterpret (`pl.tensor.view(...)`) inside InCore.
- Supports arbitrary (non-canonical) stride — future-proof (overlapping/strided views, non-contiguous flatten).

Cons:
- A new op across all layers: C++ registration + deduce, orch + in-core codegen, Python IR + DSL wrappers, type stubs, docs, tests.

### Alternatives Considered

- **Add an optional `stride` param to `tensor.reshape`** (a hybrid of A): gains arbitrary stride without a new op, but keeps Approach A's same-name-two-meanings overload and still cannot be user-expressed as a GM reinterpret. Listed for completeness.

Summary of the tradeoff: for the two scenarios A and B are byte-identical in output. Pick A for minimal surface if a **compiler-internal, canonical-only** reinterpret is acceptable; pick B if a **user-expressible, unambiguous, stride-general** reinterpret is wanted, at the cost of a new op.

### Open Questions

1. **Which approach — A (extend `tensor.reshape`) or B (new `tensor.view`)?** This is the primary decision this RFC seeks feedback on. Is a user-facing / unambiguous GM reinterpret worth a new op, or is a compiler-internal, canonical-only reinterpret via `reshape` sufficient?
2. **Op category / pass-12 gate (B):** keep `tensor.view` out of `set_op_category("TensorOp")` so it passes through like `as_layout`, or set the category and add it to `kPassthroughTensorOps`? (Only matters if users write it before pass 12.)
3. **Offset recompute ownership (both):** moving the NZ 2D-collapse out of codegen means the `tile.load` mixed-radix offset recompute must live in `FlattenTileNdTo2D`. Same change or a follow-up?
4. **Semantics/validation:** canonical flatten (reshape-style element-count check) vs `as_strided`-style (allow non-canonical, no strict check)?
5. **Tensor-only vs Tile-polymorphic:** Tiles already have `tile.reshape` / `tile.transpose_view` — keep this Tensor-only?
6. **Distributed physical constraints:** after 1D flatten, do the per-rank slot assumptions in allgather/reduce_scatter (currently 2D `[NR, SIZE]`) still hold, or must they be relaxed in the lowering refactor?

### Affected Files (indicative)

- Approach A: `src/ir/op/tensor_ops/transform.cpp` (deduce → `AsTensorTypeLike` + distributed; add `set_output_memory_inherit_input()`), `src/backend/common/pto_ops_common.cpp` (in-core handler for `tensor.reshape`), Python DSL/stub only if signature changes.
- Approach B: same set **plus** new op registration, new DSL symbol (`python/pypto/{ir,language}/op/tensor_ops.py`), type stubs, docs.
- Both: `tests/ut/ir/...` — deduce-type + codegen tests.

### Testing Plan

- Deduce-type UT: shape/stride/layout on the result `TensorView`; `DistributedTensorType` input preserves `window_buffer_`; validation errors.
- Codegen snapshot: in-core emits `pto.make_tensor_view … shape=[…] strides=[…]` and a downstream `tile.load` resolves to it.
- `/compare-codegen`: no diff on existing cases (consumers unchanged in this RFC's scope).

title: [Code Health] Orchestration codegen emits unconditional TaskId is_valid() guard on every dependency

labels.name: code health
labels.description: Technical debt, robustness concerns, code quality improvements

body:
### Category

Technical Debt (cleanup, refactor)

### Component

Codegen

### Description

When orchestration codegen builds the `PTO2TaskId <task>_deps[K]` array that is handed to `set_dependencies(...)`, it wraps **every** dependency TaskId in an `is_valid()` guard before inserting it:

```cpp
// generated orch C
PTO2TaskId task_7_deps[3];
uint32_t task_7_deps_count = 0;
if (tid_a.is_valid()) task_7_deps[task_7_deps_count++] = tid_a;
if (tid_b.is_valid()) task_7_deps[task_7_deps_count++] = tid_b;
if (tid_c.is_valid()) task_7_deps[task_7_deps_count++] = tid_c;
task_7.set_dependencies(task_7_deps, task_7_deps_count);
```

`is_valid()` is a single compare against the invalid sentinel (`runtime/src/common/task_interface/pto_task_id.h:44` — `return raw != UINT64_MAX;`), so each guard is one predictable branch. The guard exists because a TaskId **can** legitimately hold the `PTO2TaskId::invalid()` sentinel and such an id must never reach `set_dependencies`. The sentinel arises only in a few cases:

- a `None` loop-carry seed (`system.task_invalid` → `PTO2TaskId::invalid()`),
- a loop-carried `iter_arg` TaskId on the first iteration (before its producer has run),
- an unwritten array-carry slot.

**The problem:** the guard is emitted *unconditionally* for every dependency, including TaskIds that are **statically known-valid** — e.g. an id produced by a `pl.submit(...)` earlier in the same straight-line scope and never assigned the invalid sentinel. For those ids `is_valid()` is provably always true, so the branch is dead weight. The codegen already acknowledges this in its own comments:

> "The guard is a cheap always-true branch for ids known valid." (`orchestration_codegen.cpp:2511-2512`)
> "Guard every entry with `is_valid()`; the branch is a harmless always-true test for ids already known valid." (`orchestration_codegen.cpp:2560-2561`)

In dependency-heavy orchestration (many `deps` per task, over a trip-counted loop), this emits one redundant branch per dependency per task on the AICPU orchestration hot path. There is currently **no analysis** that distinguishes guaranteed-valid TaskIds from possibly-invalid ones, so the guard is applied uniformly.

### Location

Three unconditional emission sites, all in `src/codegen/orchestration/orchestration_codegen.cpp`:

- `orchestration_codegen.cpp:2529` — `EmitManualDeps()` (manual / explicit `deps=[...]` wiring)
- `orchestration_codegen.cpp:528` — `EmitCompilerDepArrayBarrier()` (compiler-derived compressed loop fan-in barrier)
- `orchestration_codegen.cpp:1343` — dynamic dependency-yield collection (`if (<tid>.is_valid()) { ... }`)

Runtime definition of the guarded predicate:

- `runtime/src/common/task_interface/pto_task_id.h:44` — `constexpr bool is_valid() const { return raw != UINT64_MAX; }`

### Proposed Fix

Derive, at the dependency-emission point, whether each TaskId can ever hold the invalid sentinel, and only guard the ones that can:

1. Classify a TaskId binding as **guaranteed-valid** when it is the direct output of a `pl.submit(...)` in the current straight-line scope and is never sourced from `system.task_invalid`, a loop-carried `iter_arg` seed, or an array-carry slot.
2. For guaranteed-valid ids, emit the unconditional insert: `deps[cnt++] = tid;` (drop the `if (tid.is_valid())`).
3. Keep the existing guard for possibly-invalid ids (loop-carried `iter_arg`, `None`/`system.task_invalid` seeds, array-carry slots).

This is a codegen-only change (the three sites above share the `emit_one_dep`-style helper), preserves correctness for the sentinel cases, and removes the always-true branches from the common straight-line submit path.

### Priority

Medium (minor risk / perf; no correctness impact — should fix in next few releases)

title: [RFC] Window-Buffer Allocation API Is Byte-Centric and Error-Prone
body:
> **This is a request for comment (RFC), not a committed work plan.** The goal is
> to discuss whether the window-buffer allocation API should change and, if so,
> which direction to take. Feedback on the options below — especially the
> trade-offs and the open questions — is very welcome.

### Summary

`pld.alloc_window_buffer(size)` takes a **raw byte count**, so every caller manually
computes `product(shape) × bytes_per_element` and then restates the *same* shape and
dtype one line later in `pld.window(buf, shape, dtype=...)`. This leaks a hardware
detail (byte size) into the frontend, duplicates information across two calls, and is
a silent foot-gun when the multiplier is wrong. This RFC lays out the problem and
several possible API directions, from a tiny accessor to a shape+dtype allocation
API, and asks which (if any) we should pursue.

### Motivation

The current pattern:

```python
data_buf   = pld.alloc_window_buffer(nr * SIZE * 4)   # magic 4 = FP32 bytes
signal_buf = pld.alloc_window_buffer(nr * 4)          # magic 4 = INT32 bytes
...
data = pld.window(data_buf,   [nr, SIZE], dtype=pl.FP32)   # shape+dtype AGAIN
sig  = pld.window(signal_buf, [nr, 1],    dtype=pl.INT32)  # shape+dtype AGAIN
```

Why the current state is insufficient:

1. **Byte arithmetic leaks to the frontend.** The user must know FP32 = 4 bytes,
   BF16 = 2, and remember `nelements × bytes`. That is a runtime/HW concern, not a
   modeling concern.
2. **Duplication / two sources of truth.** Shape and dtype are stated at the alloc
   (implicitly, via the byte math) *and* again at `window()`. The two can silently
   drift out of sync.
3. **Silent corruption on a wrong multiplier.** A wrong constant (or forgetting a
   dimension in the product) under/over-allocates the buffer — no error, just memory
   corruption at runtime.
4. **Not self-documenting.** `alloc_window_buffer(nr * SIZE * 4)` needs a comment to
   explain what it is; the intent (`an nr×SIZE FP32 buffer`) is lost.
5. **Sub-byte bug surface.** Ad-hoc `bits / 8` truncates 4-bit types (INT4/UINT4/
   FP4/HF4) to 0 bytes; only `(bits + 7) / 8` is correct. Scattering this math across
   call sites invites the wrong variant.

### Design

Candidate directions, ordered smallest → largest change. These are alternatives to
discuss, not a sequence to implement.

**Option 1 — a dtype byte-size accessor (tiny)**
```python
buf = pld.alloc_window_buffer(nr * SIZE * pl.FP32.byte_size())
```
Give `DataType` a `byte_size()` accessor (`(bits + 7) / 8`, so sub-byte types round
up correctly) and replace the magic constants with it. Removes the magic *numbers*
and centralizes the rounding, but the caller still writes byte arithmetic and still
restates shape+dtype at `window()`.

**Option 2 — a `dtype.nbytes(shape)` accessor (tiny)**
```python
buf = pld.alloc_window_buffer(pl.FP32.nbytes([1, SIZE]))
```
Moves the `product(shape) × byte_size` multiply onto the dtype. Still says "bytes" at
the call site, but drops the hand-written multiply.

**Option 3 — a pure sizing helper `pld.window_bytes(shape, dtype)` (small–medium)**
```python
buf = pld.alloc_window_buffer(pld.window_bytes([nr, SIZE], pl.FP32))
```
Keeps the byte-only alloc but offers one composable helper taking shape+dtype. Must
support **both** static (Python-int) and dynamic (IR-expression) shapes — see Open
Questions — so it cannot be a plain Python function.

**Option 4 — fused alloc + view for single-use buffers (medium)**
```python
data = pld.window([1, SIZE], dtype=pl.FP32)   # allocate + view in one call
```
Removes the byte/alloc concept entirely for the common single-view case. Would need
to stay an *overload*: the two-phase `alloc → window` is intentional for buffers
reused across loop iterations with multiple views, so both forms must coexist.

**Option 5 — `alloc_window_buffer(shape, dtype)` (author's leaning)**
```python
data_buf   = pld.alloc_window_buffer([nr, SIZE], dtype=pl.FP32)
signal_buf = pld.alloc_window_buffer([nr, 1],    dtype=pl.INT32)
```
The alloc computes `product(shape) × byte_size(dtype)` internally. The user never
sees bytes; shape+dtype are stated once at the natural place. Eliminates *both* the
byte arithmetic and the shape-product foot-gun. Largest change — the alloc op's IR
signature, parser, and builder must accept shape+dtype and lower to a byte count.

### Alternatives Considered

- **Option 5** looks like the ergonomic end state: it matches what the user means
  ("give me an nr×SIZE FP32 window buffer") and removes both the duplication and the
  foot-guns — at the cost of an IR-signature change to the alloc op.
- **Option 1** (byte-size accessor) is a correct, minimal, independently useful first
  step regardless of the larger direction: it kills the magic numbers and centralizes
  the `(bits + 7) / 8` rounding.
- **Options 2 / 3** are low-risk intermediates that build on the accessor while a
  larger alloc-op change is scoped.
- **Status quo** (raw byte count): rejected — it is the source of the foot-guns above.

### Open Questions

1. Is this worth changing at all, or is the byte-only alloc acceptable with just a
   byte-size accessor (Option 1) to remove the magic numbers?
2. Which direction should we target — the minimal accessor, or the full
   shape+dtype allocation API (Option 5)?
3. **Static-vs-dynamic sizing (the governing constraint):** window-buffer dimensions
   can be static (a Python `int` such as `SIZE`) or dynamic (an IR expression such as
   `pld.world_size()`). Any "compute bytes from shape+dtype" logic must lower to an IR
   *expression* when a dimension is dynamic, not merely evaluate to a Python int. Does
   this argue for putting the sizing logic in the alloc op itself (Option 5) rather
   than in a helper?
4. For a fused alloc+view (Option 4), is keeping the two-phase `alloc → window` form
   as an overload sufficient for the reuse-across-iterations case, or does that split
   the mental model?

title: [New Op] pl.dequant_fp4 — MXFP4 (e2m1 + E8M0) weight dequant for bandwidth-bound expert matmuls
body:
## Operation Level

Tensor-level / block-level (operates on a weight tile inside the matmul K-loop).

## Proposed Name & Signature

```python
pl.dequant_fp4(
    w_fp4: Tile,                  # packed e2m1 (2 elements / byte)
    scale_e8m0: Tile,             # per-group E8M0 scale (1 scale per 32 elements)
    target_type: DataType = pl.INT8,   # or pl.FP8
) -> Tile                          # dequantized weight tile in target_type
```

## Semantics Description

Dequantize a packed MXFP4 weight tile to a wider dtype the cube matmul accepts, applying the per-group E8M0 scale:

1. Unpack e2m1 nibbles → FP values (maps to pto-isa `TExtract` for `float4_e2m1x2_t`).
2. Multiply by the E8M0 group scale (`float8_e8m0_t`, one per 32 elements).
3. Cast to `target_type` (INT8 or FP8) for the cube.

**Why dequant-and-cube instead of native FP4 MMA:** pypto's cube matmul path explicitly does **not** support FP4 operands — `src/ir/transforms/auto_tile_matmul_l0_pass.cpp:205`: _"FP4 et al. which the cube path does not support"_. So MXFP4 weights must be dequantized before the cube. The win is **halved GM weight bytes** (read FP4, dequant on-the-fly in UB), not cube compute throughput.

## Example Usage

```python
# expert_routed.py / expert_shared.py gate_mm K-loop:
for k0 in pl.pipeline(0, D, K_TILE, stage=2):
    x_k      = recv_x[..., k0:k0+K_TILE]                       # INT8 activation
    w_fp4_k  = routed_w1[..., n0:n0+N_TILE, k0:k0+K_TILE]      # FP4 packed
    w_sc_k   = routed_w1_scale[..., n0:n0+N_TILE, k0:k0+K_TILE]  # E8M0 group scale
    w_k      = pl.dequant_fp4(w_fp4_k, w_sc_k, target_type=pl.INT8)
    acc      = pl.matmul_acc(acc, x_k, w_k, b_trans=True)       # INT8 cube
```

## Hardware Support Considerations

The building blocks **already exist** at the tile-ISA layer (a5/950 has native FP4); this is a DSL + codegen exposure gap, not new hardware:

- `pto-isa/include/pto/npu/a5/TInsert.hpp` — FP4 load / ND2NZ (`byteValidCol = validCol/2` for `float4_e2m1x2_t`, `float4_e1m2x2_t`).
- `pto-isa/include/pto/npu/a5/TExtract.hpp` — FP4 unpack (`M_STEP_MIN_VAL_B4 = 4` for fp4).
- `pto-isa/include/pto/npu/a5/TStore.hpp` — supports `float4_e2m1x2_t` / `float4_e1m2x2_t` / `float8_e8m0_t`.

## Motivation

DSv4 routed/shared expert FFN is weight-bandwidth-bound in deployment (each active expert reads ~24 MB of INT8 weights; 256 routed experts contend for HBM). The model config already declares `expert_dtype="fp4"` / `scale_fmt="ue8m0"`, but pypto-lib kernels run INT8 because pypto can't consume FP4 yet. Halving weight bytes is the only remaining lever with meaningful headroom (code-level tile tuning is exhausted — see pypto-lib#723 and PR #719).

## Asks

1. The `pl.dequant_fp4` op above → codegen to pto-isa `TExtract` + E8M0 scale apply.
2. Matmul K-loop codegen: allow fusing **load-FP4 → `dequant_fp4` → cube** (or stage dequant in UB, then cube).
3. FP4 packed-tensor load / ND2NZ path (pto-isa `TInsert` already handles FP4 col-align).
4. ptoas encoding for the new op (likely free if reusing existing FP4 instructions).

## Related

- Consumer-side adoption: **pypto-lib#723** (`[Feature] DSv4 routed/shared experts: adopt MXFP4 weights`) — blocked on this op.
- pypto#1902 (`[RFC] A8W8 quant/dequant/matmul fusion`) — same theme (quant/dequant/matmul fusion), different bit-width (8-bit).

title: [Feature] Add MX (MXFP8/MXFP4) DSL ops — matmul_mx, tget_scale_addr, tquant/tdequant — the only gap blocking MX kernels
body:
## Summary

The full A5 (Ascend 950 / arch35) MX matmul stack is ready **except the pypto DSL frontend**. There is currently no way to author an MX (MXFP8 / MXFP4) matmul from the pypto language layer, which blocks any MX-precision kernel work in `pypto-lib`. This is a request to add the missing MX DSL ops (`matmul_mx`, `mx_quant`/`tquant`, `tdequant`, `tget_scale_addr`, MX load) and register them via `REGISTER_OP`.

## Context

We are implementing a DeepSeek V4 decode kernel on A5 with a **Hybrid MXFP8–MXFP4** precision strategy (weights MXFP8 = FP8 E4M3 + per-32 E8M0 scale; MoE routed experts MXFP4 = FP4 E2M1; activations MXFP8 block-32 dynamic quant; KV/compressed-KV/index-KV cache C16→FP8). The current kernel is W8A8C16 (symmetric INT8 weights, per-token dynamic INT8 activations, INT8×INT8→INT32 matmul with manual dequant, BF16 caches). Moving to MX requires MX matmul support all the way down to the DSL.

## What already works (verified layer-by-layer)

| Layer | MX matmul support | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| Hardware A5/arch35 (`mad_mx`) | ✅ | — |
| **pto-isa** tile lib (NPU + CPU) | ✅ | `include/pto/npu/a5/TMatmul.hpp` (`TMatmulMx` / `TMATMUL_MX_IMPL(a, aScale, b, bScale)`), `include/pto/cpu/TMatmul.hpp:44`, `cpu/MXTypes.hpp` (e4m3/e5m2/e8m0/e2m1x2), ST test `tests/npu/a5/.../tmatmul_mx` |
| **ptoas** (PTO-IR op + EmitC emit + bytecode; tilelang `mad_mx`) | ✅ | `include/PTO/IR/PTOOps.td:684-783` (`pto.tmatmul.mx/.acc/.bias`), `lib/PTO/Transforms/PTOToEmitC.cpp:8911-8961` (emits `TMATMUL_MX`), opcode `0x1033`; `ptoas/0.45 tilelang_dsl/semantic.py:284` (`mad_mx`) + `lowering.py:2070` |
| **a5sim** (Ascend 950 backend on pto-isa CPU impl) | ✅ (ISA/runtime) | `pypto-lib/golden/runner.py:108` maps `a5sim → BackendType.Ascend950`; CPU `TMatmulMX` implemented |
| **pypto DSL** (`pl.matmul_mx` / `REGISTER_OP` / builder) | ❌ **gap (hard blocker)** | see below |

## The gap (pypto DSL)

- `pl.matmul` has no scale parameter (`.../pypto/language/op/unified_ops.py:688`). There is no `matmul_mx` / `mx_quant` / `tget_scale_addr` / `mx_load` DSL op or `REGISTER_OP` anywhere in the repo.
- Only **dead scaffolding** exists: the name mapping `{"tile.matmul_mx", "pto.tmatmul.mx", 4}` (`src/backend/common/pto_ops_common.cpp:2601`) and a memspace special-case comment *"not yet registered via REGISTER_OP"* (`infer_tile_memory_space_pass.cpp:54`) — but nothing upstream can actually create the op.
- The official status doc `docs/zh-cn/dev/ptoas-op-status.md:117` confirms: `pto.tmatmul.mx | tile | ✅(ISA) | ❌ frontend | MISSING`. `tget_scale_addr`, `tquant`, `tdequant` are likewise **MISSING**.

## Request

Add and register (via `REGISTER_OP`) the MX DSL op set so MX kernels can be authored from pypto:

- `matmul_mx` (matmul with A/B scale operands → `pto.tmatmul.mx` / `.acc` / `.bias`)
- `tquant` / `mx_quant` (block-32 MX dynamic quant, MXFP8 E4M3 + E8M0 scale; MXFP4 E2M1)
- `tdequant`
- `tget_scale_addr` (scale-tile address resolution)
- MX load path

## Impact

Once the DSL is connected, **a5sim can validate immediately without real hardware** (it runs the same codegen, compiled against the pto-isa CPU headers). This one frontend gap is the sole prerequisite blocking all downstream MX kernel work.

title: [Bug] Empty-deps task_dummy(deps=[]) is silently elided by orchestration codegen (never submitted, no dependency edge)
Reshape view drops cross-task RAW dependency (orchestration omits dep edge)
body:
## Summary

A RAW dependency edge is **dropped** when the producer writes a tensor `T` through a **reshape view** and the consumer (in a different task) reads `T` through a **direct view**. The two views cover the same bytes, but the generated orchestration emits no dependency between the two tasks, so the reader can execute before the writer → non-deterministic data corruption.

Reshape is a pure view / metadata operation and must not change dependency semantics, but the task-graph dependency analysis appears to key on the immediate view's base descriptor rather than resolving it to the underlying allocation.

## Environment

- pypto @ `23f8447b` (`chore(runtime): bump submodule to c94aa9f3 (#1977)`)
- platform `a2a3`, EP=2 (2 cards)
- Surfaced in pypto-lib `models/deepseek/v4/moe.py`; reproducer PR: **hw-native-sys/pypto-lib#727**

## Symptom

In the DeepSeek-V4 MoE dispatch, a producer task (`dispatch_gather`) writes the compact activation buffer `recv_x_out`, and consumer tasks (`exp_gate_mm` / `exp_up_mm`) read it. The producer writes through a reshape view; the consumers read a direct view. The consumers do **not** order after the producer → validation fails non-deterministically (error ratio varies 13%–48% run to run, a clear race).

The exact same producer also writes three sibling buffers (`recv_scale_out` / `recv_w_out` / `recv_r_route_out`) through **direct** `[e:e+1]` slice views, and *those* consumers order correctly. Only the one buffer routed through a reshape view loses its edge.

## Root cause (from generated orchestration)

Producer — writes `recv_x_out` **via a reshape view**:

```cpp
// recv_x_out_inline: TensorCreateInfo [32, 16, 4096] INT8   (the allocation)
Tensor recv_x_out_flat = recv_x_out_inline.reshape({512, 4096}, 2);   // reshape view
Tensor x_out_row       = recv_x_out_flat.view({1, 4096}, {out_row, 0});
params_gather.add_output(x_out_row);                                  // write
```

Consumer (`exp_gate_mm`) — reads `recv_x_out` **via a direct view**:

```cpp
Tensor x_local = recv_x_out_inline.view({1, 16, 4096}, {local_i, 0, 0});   // direct view
params_gate.add_input(x_local);
rt_submit_aic_task(..., params_gate);        // NO set_dependencies() linking it to the gather
```

Both `x_out_row` and `x_local` alias the same `recv_x_out_inline` allocation and overlap in bytes when `out_row ∈ [local_i*16, local_i*16+16)`, but the consumer task carries no dependency on the producer. By contrast the direct-view siblings (`recv_scale_out` etc.) produce the expected edges.

## Minimal reproducer (conceptual)

Two tasks over one internal tensor `T` shaped `[A, B, C]`:

- Task 1 writes `reshape(T, [A*B, C])[row : row+1, :]`
- Task 2 reads `T[a : a+1, :, :]` (with `row` inside `[a*B, (a+1)*B)`)

Expected: Task 2 depends on Task 1 (RAW). Actual: no edge emitted; Task 2 may run first.

(Full end-to-end reproducer: pypto-lib#727 — `python models/deepseek/v4/moe.py -p a2a3 --ep 2`.)

## Why it was previously masked

In the original single-task dispatch, `recv_count_out` (a scalar count the host reads via `get_tensor_data`) and `recv_x_out` were produced by the **same** task. The host read on `recv_count_out` blocked on that task and incidentally made `recv_x_out` ready before the matmul was even submitted, so the missing device edge never mattered. Splitting the count out into an earlier task removes that accidental host-side gating and exposes the dropped edge.

## Expected behavior

A write through `reshape(T, …)` (or any chain of pure view ops) and a read of `T` (or another view of it) that overlap in the underlying allocation must produce a RAW dependency, exactly as two direct slice views of `T` already do. The dependency resolver should normalize view/reshape chains to the root allocation + byte range before computing overlap.

## Possibly related

May be the RAW analog of the previously observed reshape-aliased **WAR** miss (two reshape views of the same buffer not tracked). If there is an existing tracking issue for reshape-view aliasing, this is likely the same underlying resolver limitation.

title: [RFC] Pluggable DSA Memory-Planning Solver + PyPTO Adapter
body:
**Design RFC for review** — feedback especially welcome on the Open Questions (sync-cost fidelity vs ptoas `GraphSyncSolver`, per-pool decomposition, and coordination with ptoas #913).

cc @Hzfengsy @lyfne123

---

# RFC: Pluggable DSA Memory-Planning Solver + PyPTO Adapter

## Status

**Draft — request for comments.** Author: Toni Boehnlein. 2026-07-08. Scopes the
*design* and *interface*; module layout and pass-order wiring are a follow-up.

## Summary

PyPTO plans local memory in two passes — `MemoryReuse` (coloring → buffers share a
`base_` Ptr) and `AllocateMemoryAddr` (bump → one max-sized slot per base group, no
region reclaim). No principled Dynamic Storage Allocation (DSA) formulation splits
*which buffers share* from *where each goes* this way, and the split is why a freed
region cannot be subdivided (issue #1908).

**Proposal:** a standalone, reusable **DSA solver** behind a field-standard interface
(buffers with lifetimes + sizes → offsets) plus a thin **PyPTO adapter**. The adapter
carries an **optional, capability-negotiated cost overlay** for NPU structure the
standard formulation drops — chiefly that *reuse isn't free*: overlapping two
lifetime-disjoint buffers manufactures a cross-pipe synchronization a pure peak
objective doesn't cost (today handled only by one hard-coded rule, #1949).
Off-the-shelf solvers consume the core; PyPTO's own (local-search) solver consumes
the overlay.

The hook is the principled solver. **As a byproduct it dissolves #1908** —
buffer-granularity packing subdivides freed regions natively. The fix ships on the
**v1** path and does **not** depend on the overlay/local-search research (**v2**).

## Motivation

`MemoryReuse`'s capacity-gated packing (#1949, now in main) separates pipelined
double-buffers to avoid a serializing false-WAR (#1475) — one hard-coded sync-aware
reuse decision. Two gaps remain: **(1)** that
awareness is one special case, not a general cost the placer optimizes → E2
generalizes it; **(2)** coloring is split from offset assignment, so a producer's
freed 64 KB slot can't be subdivided into a consumer's two lifetime-disjoint 32 KB
buffers → L0A overflow (#1908) → buffer-granularity planning closes it.

The standard DSA problem (min peak, no concurrent overlap) is a *projection* that
drops this overlay — capturing it without contaminating the portable core is the
design's real content.

**Strategic context.** ptoas has its own planner, and PTOAS #913 rewrites it toward a
func-level first-fit-by-lifetime planner (same algorithm class). The org keeps both
(pypto L3 / ptoas L2, `memory_planner` switch #1934) and consolidates later —
**coordinate with the #913 owners**; a pypto-owned L3 planner's niche shifts if the org
picks ptoas. Pursue anyway: (a) the reusable/benchmarkable solver is independent of
which planner ships; (b) the overlay models L3 reuse→sync info ptoas can't see; (c)
the fragmentation needs fixing on L3 now.

## Background

Core DSA — buffers each `(size, lifetime, align)` → offsets, min peak (or fit a cap),
no overlap for lifetime-overlapping buffers — recurs across systems; they differ in the
solver *and* which extensions they model (so the core is common, not identical).

| System | Problem object | Solver |
| --- | --- | --- |
| MiniMalloc (ASPLOS'23) | CSV `id,lower,upper,size` → `offset` | exact DFS over canonical solutions + pruning |
| TelaMalloc (ASPLOS'22) | same | heuristic search + ILP/CP-SAT |
| XLA | `BufferInterval{size,start,end,colocations}` → `Chunk` | `GlobalDecreasingSizeBestFitHeap` (heuristic, not optimal) + `NoFragmentationStatsHeap` (loose lower bound) |
| TVM USMP | `BufferInfo{size,align,conflicts[],pool_candidates[]}` → `PoolAllocation` | `greedy_by_size` / `greedy_by_conflicts` / `hill_climb` (local search) |
| ptoas (incl. #913) | free-region outline / `bufferLifeVec` per (core,pipe) | first-fit + region split/coalesce |

MiniMalloc's public CSV is single-pool/single-interval (no colocations/pins/multi-pool);
XLA's best-fit *heap* is a heuristic. **Benchmark:** MiniMalloc `challenging/` — A–K (11 instances, 154–454
buffers, 1 MiB), curated so greedy/best-fit *fail* → it exercises only the core and is
adversarial to best-fit.

## Goals / Non-goals

**Goals:** an IR-free `DsaSolver` library (reads the MiniMalloc CSV subset); a thin
adapter (IR → `DsaProblem`, `DsaResult` → MemRef addresses); an optional overlay; fix
the fragmentation as a byproduct (v1); evaluate vs MiniMalloc-optimal + the XLA lower bound.
**Non-goals:** not replacing ptoas's planner (L2); not solving sync/event-id allocation
(only *estimating* its cost); no new IR node.

## Design

### Core vs. overlay; constraint vs. cost

```
core DSA (portable)                overlay (pypto-specific, optional)
buffers {intervals,size,align,     E1 multi-interval liveness  ← CONSTRAINT (changes feasibility)
pool}, colocations, separations,   E2 reuse → sync cost        ← COST (re-ranks feasible set)
pinned, pool_caps → offsets        E3 bank-conflict cost       ← COST
```

The overlay is **not homogeneous**: E2/E3 (costs) re-rank the feasible set, but E1
changes *what is feasible* — a hull-only solver can report infeasible on an instance
that *fits*, so "infeasible ⇒ genuine OOM" is only defined once E1 is supported.

### Interface

```cpp
struct Buffer { BufferId id; std::vector<Interval> intervals; uint64_t size, align; PoolId pool; };
                                     // intervals: E1 union; core solver uses the hull

struct ReusePenalty { BufferId a, b; uint64_t penalty; };   // reason: cross_pipe|cross_core|event_budget
struct BankGeometry  { PoolId pool; uint64_t bank_size; uint32_t num_banks; };
struct CostModel {                                          // sparse DATA, not opaque callbacks
  std::vector<ReusePenalty> reuse_penalties;                // only cross-pipe lifetime-disjoint pairs
  std::vector<BankGeometry> banks;
  struct { double sync, bank, peak_slack; } weights;
};

struct DsaProblem {
  std::vector<Buffer> buffers;
  std::vector<std::pair<BufferId,BufferId>> colocations;    // hard SAME offset (must-alias)
  std::vector<std::pair<BufferId,BufferId>> separations;    // hard KEEP-APART even if lifetime-disjoint
  std::vector<PinnedBuffer> pinned;                         // fixed offset + (interval | whole-program)
  std::map<PoolId,uint64_t> reserved_base, pool_caps;
  std::optional<CostModel> cost_model;                      // nullopt = core-only
};

enum class SolveStatus { kFeasible, kInfeasibleProven, kBestEffortNoFit, kTimeout, kUnsupported };
struct ObjectiveValue { uint64_t peak, sync, bank; std::map<PoolId,uint64_t> peak_by_pool;
                        std::optional<uint64_t> lower_bound; bool optimality_proven; };
struct DsaResult { SolveStatus status; std::optional<DsaSolution> solution;
                   ObjectiveValue objective; std::vector<std::string> diagnostics; };

struct SolverCapabilities { bool multi_interval, cost_model, colocations, separations, pinned, multi_pool; };
class DsaSolver { public:
  virtual SolverCapabilities capabilities() const = 0;
  virtual DsaResult solve(const DsaProblem&) = 0;           // never "just returns a solution"
};
```

### Objective — mode-split

- **Core / benchmark** (`cost_model == nullopt`): minimize peak subject to no-overlap.
- **Overlay** (`cost_model` set): peak is a **hard per-pool constraint** (`peak_by_pool ≤
  cap`); among fitting packings minimize `w_sync·Σsync + w_bank·Σbank`. Peak enters
  *only* as feasibility — below-cap peak on transient L0 scratch is dead space, so
  shaving it must never cost a barrier. `weights.peak_slack` is an optional weak
  regularizer for backends that value footprint (default 0).

### Overlay extensions

- **E1 (constraint) · multi-interval liveness.** Today `var_liveness` is a single
  `[def,last_use]` hull → v1 uses hulls (parity); multi-interval is a later refinement
  (ptoas has `bufferLifeVec`).
- **E2 (cost) · reuse → sync.** Same-pipe reuse ≈ free; cross-pipe costs an event-id
  (palette 8 intra / 16 cross-core) or a full barrier. `reuse_penalties` estimates what
  ptoas's `GraphSyncSolver` charges. **Caveat:** the hardware pipe isn't in PyPTO IR at
  pass 30/31 (only *core* AIC/AIV; the pipe is assigned in ptoas) → the adapter
  reconstructs it from op kind + memory space.
- **E3 (cost) · bank conflict** on `offset mod bank_size`, coupled to `align` (if
  commensurate, alignment fixes the residue — weights aren't independent).

Pipeline depth is **not** an overlay item — the adapter pre-expands a depth-N buffer
into N staggered clones + `separations`, reducing to the core.

### Reuse edges (formal)

Two buffers induce a reuse edge iff: same pool; address intervals intersect; live sets
disjoint; a hazard crosses the ordered boundary. Colocated pairs are excluded (a
must-alias overlaps deliberately). Sub-region packing: each later tenant induces its own
edge with the prior tenant. The solver maintains a **per-move adjacency delta**
(sweep/interval index) — `cost(placement)` is not recomputed from scratch.

### Pluggability & degradation (honest)

MiniMalloc / XLA-heap / TVM-USMP are **offline oracles** over CSV or **reimplementations**
behind our interface — not in-process plugins. Core solvers don't honor
`colocations`/`separations`/`pinned`/multi-pool natively → the adapter preprocesses
(merge colocated → super-buffer; carve pins/separations as keep-outs). `SolverCapabilities`
advertises each. A core-only path merges `intervals` to hulls, drops the overlay, and may
run a **bounded** iterative "solve → add separations → re-solve" (governed — adding
separations shrinks the feasible set and can loop back into the fragmentation). `solve()` returns a
`DsaResult`: `kInfeasibleProven` = real OOM; `kBestEffortNoFit` escalates, it does not
error.

### Adapter + pass order

| Field | Source |
| --- | --- |
| `Buffer{size,align,pool}` | each MemRef; `pool` = memory space |
| `intervals` (E1) | `MemoryReuse` `var_liveness` — single hull today |
| `colocations` | `MaterializeSemanticAliases` (pass 29) must-aliases |
| `separations` | 910B `load`+`tpop_from_aic` hazard, `forbid_output_alias`, pipeline clones |
| `pinned` / `reserved_base` | `reserve_buffer` / per-space `reserved_start` |
| `reuse_penalties`, `banks` | reconstructed pipe class + `PassContext::GetBackendHandler()` |

Write-back: offset → MemRef address; colocations → shared base. The WAR is realized by
**ptoas's address-interval sync** at L3 (confirmed: PyPTO's tile path emits no
`set_flag`/`wait_flag`) → disjoint sub-region tenants aren't serialized (a **v1
correctness gate**). The solver replaces `AllocateMemoryAddr`'s offset walk and subsumes
`MemoryReuse`'s opportunistic half; pass 29 must-aliases + the hazard guard stay inputs.

**v1 must include both** the buffer-granularity fragmentation fix **and** pipeline-clone
separation (the #1949 clones become `separations`, the capacity shed becomes separation
relaxation on overflow). Otherwise peak-only v1 collapses the clones and **serializes
pipelined kernels**, a regression invisible to a "peak ≤ bump" gate.

## Affected Files (coarse)

- `src/ir/transforms/dsa/` — **New** — IR-free library (types, best-fit-decreasing,
  exact DFS, local search, CSV subset I/O, independent validator).
- `src/ir/transforms/allocate_memory_addr_pass.cpp` — **Modify** — replace the bump with adapter + solver.
- `src/ir/transforms/memory_reuse_pass.cpp` — **Modify** — reduce to liveness + must-alias + separations + hazard guard.
- `include/pypto/ir/transforms/` (**New** adapter header); `tests/ut/ir/transforms/` (**New/Modify**).

## Testing Plan

- **Standalone:** A–K — exact DFS owns feasibility;
  report peak vs MiniMalloc-optimal (ground truth), and the loose `NoFragmentationStats`
  bound only where no optimum is known (don't report the NoFrag gap as achievable).
- **Independent validator** on every output (caps, align, pins, colocations, separations,
  no-overlap, objective recompute); **differential** small-instance tests vs the exact
  solver; **proven-infeasible** and **timeout** tests.
- **#1908 regression:** the A-stationary chained matmul now fits; retire the
  output-stationary workaround (`test_chained_matmul_uses_mat_scratch`).
- **No regression:** per-kernel peak ≤ bump **and** a pipeline-clones-stay-distinct assertion.
- **Overlay:** cheap (same-pipe) vs expensive (cross-pipe) collapse both fit → cost-aware
  solver picks cheap. **E1:** instance that fits only with multi-interval. Determinism +
  CSV round-trip.
- **Before v2 defaults:** a **model-vs-measured** study — `Σreuse_penalty` vs actual
  ptoas event-ids/barriers (a one-round ptoas feedback may beat a static heuristic).

## Security

Compile-time resource exhaustion only: exact solvers are offline/test-only; in-pass
solvers are time-boxed → `kTimeout` → deterministic fallback (best-fit / bump). No
secrets, no runtime I/O.

## Alternatives

- **A · group-granularity first-fit** (the issue's literal proposal): insufficient — the
  pre-grouped producer slot stays co-live with the double-buffer → 96 KB. The minimal fix
  is **buffer-granularity** first-fit-by-lifetime.
- **B · sub-region reuse in `MemoryReuse`:** a non-portable, shape-specific patch.
- **Extend the solver contract with sync:** breaks core-solver pluggability → optional
  overlay instead.
- **Two RFCs (fix vs. research):** rejected — the **v1-independent-of-v2** rollout gives
  the decoupling without splitting the document.

## Rollout

Level3-first; **v1 is independent of and can land ahead of v2.**
**v0** offline library + harness. **v1** the fragmentation fix + pipeline separation (flagged,
core only, gate = peak ≤ bump AND clones distinct; falls back to the bump). **v2** overlay
+ local search (gated on the model-vs-measured study and #913 coordination). Level2
untouched.

## Open Questions

- **Sync-cost fidelity (v2 crux):** is a pipe-pair + budget heuristic enough for
  `reuse_penalty`, or is a one-round ptoas feedback loop needed (re-couples the tools)?
- **Hard vs. soft** for scarce resources (event-ids, peak) — one general answer, not
  per-resource?
- **Pools genuinely fixed?** If a tile may live in L0A *or* Mat/L1, fixing `pool` at
  collection is the biggest modeling loss. If fixed (expected), the problem **decomposes
  into k independent per-pool solves** (E2/separations intra-pool) — state and exploit it.
- **Conditional non-conflict:** phi-family / branch-exclusive vars share despite
  overlapping hulls today; a pure interval-overlap solver drops this (raises peak on
  branch-heavy kernels). Encode as `colocations` + a `may_overlap` exemption list?

## References

Issues/PRs: #1908, #1949 (capacity-gated, merged), #1934 (planner switch); ptoas #913.
MiniMalloc (ASPLOS'23, `github.com/google/minimalloc`); TelaMalloc (ASPLOS'22); TVM USMP
RFC 0009; OpenXLA `heap_simulator`.

title: [Bug] split_aiv (aiv_shard/aic_gather) cross-half GM exchange races non-deterministically over a multi-dispatch loop (qwen3-14b fused decode; hard syncall alone is not the trigger)
body:
> **Update — root cause isolated to `split_aiv` (see the [minimal-repro comment](https://github.com/hw-native-sys/pypto/issues/1981#issuecomment-4921217612)).**
> A ~130-line standalone kernel that strips all attention math shows: a hard `pl.system.syncall` re-dispatched N times in one program does **not** by itself race (both an `aiv_only` and a `mix`+cube barrier-loop are deterministic over 40 layers). Adding fa_fused's **`split_aiv` cross-half GM exchange (`aiv_shard`/`aic_gather`, #1894/#1923)** is what makes it race (rare/non-deterministic: 7/10 identical-input runs fail, error ratio 3.66–10.16%). `sync_start=True` does **not** prevent it. So the "two effects" in the Details below are really **one**: `split_aiv`; `sync_start` + cross-layer serialization only *reduce* the fa_fused race (they cut barrier overlap) but cannot fix its `split_aiv` root.

## Background

In pypto-lib, `models/qwen3/14b/decode_layer.py` on `a2a3` has a correctness problem: the fused decode `decode_fwd` — a `for layer in pl.range(40)` loop that dispatches ONE `pl.spmd(NUM_CORES=24)` "fa_fused" per layer, each fa_fused containing **two hard `pl.system.syncall(core_type="mix")` barriers** — produces **non-deterministic output across identical-seed runs**. A single dispatch (`--fwd-layers 1`) is deterministic and golden-PASS vs torch (ratio_allclose atol/rtol 3e-3); at 40 layers the greedy argmax flips on some batch rows, differently each run.

Reproduce with:

    python models/qwen3/14b/decode_layer.py -p a2a3 -d <device> --validate-fwd --fwd-layers 40

Run 3× with the same seed and compare the printed `kernel_argmax`: it changes between runs (observed batch-row 2 = 69732 in one run, 90295 in another; other rows also flip). `sample match` follows the racy kernel argmax, so on-device generation is wrong on the affected rows.

Reproduction environment:

| Component | Version |
|---|---|
| pypto-lib | `try/sync-start @ 4aefde4` (reverted commit cfb9f0d re-applied on baseline) |
| pypto | `ace5f620` (branch `chore/bump-runtime-c94aa9f3`) |
| simpler | `c94aa9f3` (detached; matches pin) |
| pto-isa | `f72c24cd` (runtime-managed clone, actually used) |
| ptoas | `0.48` |
| CANN | not detected |

Version note: the pypto checkout is a bump-runtime WIP branch. `runtime/pto_isa.pin` records `83d01313`, but `ensure_pto_isa_root` re-checkouts the managed clone (`build_output/_deps/pto-isa`) to `f72c24cd` on every run (it overrode a manual checkout back to `f72c24cd`), so `f72c24cd` is what actually runs. The race reproduces on it and is **not** a pto-isa version artifact.

Diagnosis: **pypto / simpler (boundary unclear)** — hard `pl.system.syncall` (FFTS mix barrier) is unreliable when its enclosing `pl.spmd` is dispatched many times within one compiled program. The syncall op / `sync_start` / `split_aiv` are pypto primitives; FFTS barrier execution + task-graph scheduling is simpler. Please reassign if purely runtime.

## Details

What was tried (narrows the root cause):

1. `sync_start=True` on the fa_fused `pl.spmd` (atomic block launch) **substantially reduces** the race (from every-run-wrong/many-rows to rare/near-correct) — barrier participation/launch timing is a major factor. (fa_fused had no `sync_start` originally.)
2. Forcing consecutive fa_fused dispatches to **serialize** — thread the prev layer's fa_fused producer TaskId into the next layer's fa_fused `deps=`, so no two fa_fused / no two syncall barriers ever overlap in the task graph — reduces it **further**, to a rare single-row residual.
3. **Key**: since serializing the barriers (no barrier coexistence) still leaves a residual race, the residual is **not** syncall-barrier overlap. It is intra-fa_fused, suspected the `split_aiv` cross-half GM exchange (`aiv_shard`/`aic_gather`, cf. pypto#1894 / #1923) accumulating over 40 layers.

So there appear to be **two** effects: (a) a hard-syncall barrier issue tied to repeated/pipelined dispatch of the barriered spmd (mitigated by `sync_start` + serialization), and (b) a residual intra-fa_fused (split_aiv) non-determinism.

Precedent in-tree: DeepSeek-V4 `models/deepseek/v4/hc_pre.py` uses the *identical* hard-mix-syncall fused-`pl.spmd(24)` + `split_aiv` pattern and ships a switchable `syncall`/`separate` impl that **defaults to the dep-edge `separate` version** (#724) — the fused hard-syncall path is not the default in the one other place it exists.

The `sync_start=True` + serialization mitigation lives on branch `try/sync-start` (`4aefde4`).

Related: pypto#1935 (hard syncall deadlock at partial occupancy), pypto#1931 (dep_gen breaks full-occupancy syncall) — same primitive, different failure modes.

title: [Pass Bug] IRMutator drops kAttrDevice remap during loop unrolling (P=1 host-orch codegen)
body:
### Pass Name

IRMutator (`IRMutator::VisitExpr_(const CallPtr&)` in `src/ir/transforms/mutator.cpp`) — the generic attribute-remapping logic that `UnrollLoops` relies on when specializing a single-iteration `pl.range` host-orchestration loop.

### Description

Reported by @vloncar while working on a more advanced example of distributed linear attention.
Reproduced by @georgebisbas.

When a `host_orch` (`pl.Level.HOST`, `pl.Role.Orchestrator`) function contains a loop `for r in pl.range(P): ... self.chip_orch(..., device=r)` and `P == 1`, the loop gets unrolled (single iteration), substituting the loop variable `r` with the literal `0` via `DeepClone`.

`IRMutator::VisitExpr_(const CallPtr&)` re-mutates a whitelist of `Var`-typed dependency attributes during this substitution, but the whitelist omits `kAttrDevice` — an `ExprPtr`-valued attribute holding the device expression (`device=r`). As a result, every whitelisted attribute and all call arguments get correctly rewritten to reference the literal `0`, but `kAttrDevice` keeps pointing at the now-stale/unbound `r` variable.

This produces IR — and consequently generated `host_orch.py` orchestration code — that references an undefined Python variable, crashing at runtime with a `NameError`.

The same program compiled with `P == 2` (no unrolling, loop variable stays a real loop-carried var) works correctly, which is what makes this specifically a **loop-unrolling / single-iteration specialization** bug rather than a general `device=` attribute bug.

### Git Commit ID

10d6b12

### Before IR (Input)

```python
import pypto.language as pl

@pl.program
class Before:
    @pl.function(type=pl.FunctionType.Orchestration)
    def chip_orch_stage2(
        self,
        Q: pl.Tensor[[L, DK], pl.FP32],
        # ... other per-chip tensor args ...
        O: pl.Out[pl.Tensor[[L, DV], pl.FP32]],
    ) -> pl.Tensor[[L, DV], pl.FP32]:
        return self.gla_stage2(Q, ..., O)

    @pl.function(level=pl.Level.HOST, role=pl.Role.Orchestrator)
    def host_orch(
        self,
        Q: pl.Tensor[[P, L, dk], pl.FP32],
```
