5. **Codegen** — emit `L0TaskPredicate` + `Arg::set_predicate(...)` in orchestration codegen (operand/op/target only; the runtime derives `elem_size` from the tensor dtype).
6. **Verifier** — a `SubmitVerifier` enforcing the contract that the predicate tensor's producer is one of the task's deps (else the dispatch-point read races an unwritten value).

### Alternatives Considered

- **Read the value in orchestration and branch on submit** — stalls on `wait_for_tensor_ready`, serializes the pipeline. Rejected.
- **Submit all experts, branch inside the kernel** — still pays launch/core/data-movement per empty expert. Rejected.
- **Dynamic task count (submit only non-empty experts)** — breaks the static task-graph / AOT-orchestration model. Rejected.

### Additional Context

- Runtime feature: [hw-native-sys/simpler PR #1314](https://github.com/hw-native-sys/simpler/pull/1314), commit `7d526e12`; runtime currently pinned at `cddf2b6c`.
- Reference test on the runtime side: `tests/st/{a2a3,a5}/tensormap_and_ringbuffer/predicated_dispatch/` (gate=0 skips, gate=1 dispatches; passes on a2a3sim and onboard a2a3).
- Frontend precedent to mirror end-to-end: `allow_early_resolve` (simpler #1065) — same `pl.spmd → Submit → SubmitToCallView → orchestration codegen` chain, emitting `Arg::set_allow_early_resolve(true)`.

title: [Tracking] Dispatch-predicate frontend — phased rollout
body:
Umbrella tracking issue for landing the runtime **dispatch predicate** in the pypto frontend, in phases. Origin feature request: [hw-native-sys/pypto#2059](https://github.com/hw-native-sys/pypto/issues/2059). Runtime mechanism: [hw-native-sys/simpler#1314](https://github.com/hw-native-sys/simpler/pull/1314) (`DispatchPredicate` / `Arg::set_predicate`), already on `upstream/main` via the runtime bump to `a756969c`.

> **Status (2026-07-26):** Phases 1–3 are merged to `main`; Phase 4 (`pl.at`) is up for review in [hw-native-sys/pypto#2151](https://github.com/hw-native-sys/pypto/pull/2151). The frontend is now feature-complete — the dispatch predicate is authorable on the call form (`pl.spmd_submit` / `pl.submit`), the `with pl.spmd(...)` scope form (all three spellings), and `with pl.at(level=pl.Level.CORE_GROUP, ...)`. Only the **optional** Phase 5 polish remains.

### Background

A dispatch predicate lets a statically-materialized SPMD task be conditionally retired (never dispatched to a core) based on a value only a prior task produces — evaluated by the scheduler at the dispatch point, not in orchestration. Motivating use case: MoE "skip empty experts" (`row_count[e] > 0`). See #2059 for the full rationale.

### Surface

```python
# Call form (Phase 1)
out, tid = pl.spmd_submit(self.expert, x, out, core_num=N,
                          deps=[gather_tid],              # operand's producer
                          predicate=(row_count[e] > 0))

# Scope form (Phase 3)
with pl.spmd(N, deps=[gather_tid], predicate=(row_count[e] > 0)) as tid:
    out = self.expert(x, out)

# pl.at scope form (Phase 4) — CORE_GROUP only
with pl.at(level=pl.Level.CORE_GROUP,
           deps=[gather_tid], predicate=(row_count[e] > 0)) as tid:
    out = self.expert(x, out)
```

The comparison is parsed as an **ordinary expression but never evaluated** — `rc[e]` is the DSL's usual sugar for `pl.read`, so it lowers to plain IR (`Gt(Cast(tensor.read(..)), 0)`) reusing the existing comparison nodes. It rides on `Submit.predicate` and is never in a statement position, so the read does not execute in orchestration. Expressiveness is fixed to `tensor[indices] OP int-literal`.

### Phases

- [x] **Phase 1 — Core frontend** — `pl.spmd_submit` / `pl.submit` `predicate=(t[i] > 0)`. **PR: [hw-native-sys/pypto#2067](https://github.com/hw-native-sys/pypto/pull/2067)** (merged).
  - IR: a single `Submit.predicate` field holding the comparison Expr — reuses the existing `Eq/Ne/Lt/Le/Gt/Ge` nodes over `tensor.read` instead of a bespoke encoding, so reflection needs no new leaf type and the shape stays open for a future multi-condition runtime. Decomposition into the runtime's `operand OP target` triple lives in orchestration codegen.
  - Pass safety: visitor/mutator walk + all Submit reconstruction sites preserve the predicate.
  - Cross-layer: nanobind ctor takes one optional `predicate` Expr + `ir.pyi` (no enum needed).
  - Codegen: `EmitPredicateHint` → `L0TaskPredicate` + `Arg::set_predicate(...)`.
  - Printer / deserializer round-trip; `NoNestedCall` verifier exempts the predicate (a declarative spec, not an evaluated expression — flattening it would turn the read into a real orchestration load).
  - Parser validation: operand is a tensor subscripted to one element, integer-scalar indices, index count == rank, integer-literal target, single (unchained) comparison; mirrored `0 < t[i]` normalized to `t[i] > 0`.
  - **Producer∈deps contract enforced at the parser boundary** (see Phase 2).
  - Tests: parser/IR + codegen UTs, onboard **a2a3** end-to-end ST; DSL docs (en + zh-cn).
- [x] **Phase 2 — Producer∈deps contract** — ~~a `SubmitVerifier` with use-def analysis~~ → **landed in Phase 1 at the parser boundary** (PR #2067): each submit's result Vars are tracked against its producer TaskId, and a predicate whose operand producer is absent from `deps=` is rejected. Without it the scheduler could evaluate the predicate before the producer wrote the tensor and dispatch on stale data. **Extended in Phase 3** to cover scope-produced operands (see below).
  - Residual (accepted, author's responsibility — not statically provable): an operand with no tracked producer (e.g. a function parameter), and `Array[N, TASK_ID]` dep entries which do not name their producers individually.
  - Optional follow-up: an IR-level verifier would additionally cover hand-built / deserialized IR, which the parser check does not see. Low priority — the DSL is the only way to author a predicate today.
- [x] **Phase 3 — `with pl.spmd(predicate=...)` scope form** — **PR: [hw-native-sys/pypto#2092](https://github.com/hw-native-sys/pypto/pull/2092)** (merged). Accepted on **all three** spmd spellings: plain `with`, `with ... as tid`, and `for i in pl.spmd(...)`. Same expression, validation, lowering, and runtime ABI as the call form. `pl.at(..., predicate=...)` was deliberately **out of scope** here — the C++ side is shared, so a later cut is parser + `dsl_api` only. **Done in Phase 4 below**, and that prediction held.
  - The scope outlines only at `OutlineSpmdScopes`, so between parse and outline the predicate rides on `SpmdScopeStmt.attrs_` as the **first Expr-valued scope attr**, carrying live SSA Vars (operand tensor + indices).
  - **Correction to the original plan:** this needed **four** attr walkers, not the two anticipated (`VisitScopeAttrs` / `MutateScopeAttrs`) — also `ConvertToSSA::SubstScopeAttrs` (versions the operand; mirrors the `kAttrDevice` ExprPtr handling on `Call`) and **DCE `FindLiveRoots`** (else the operand's feeding assignment looks dead, and its removal leaves a dangling attr ref — the same failure class as #1456). Missing any one produces a silently-wrong dangling reference, so a `kAttrPredicate` constant was introduced to make the set greppable.
  - **Serialization needed no change** — the `ExprPtr` attr branch already existed; only a new printer method (`PrintScopePredicateAttr`) was added, narrower than the "scope serializer/printer handling" originally anticipated.
  - `ScopeOutliner` moves the attr onto `Submit.predicate` and forces the Submit shape (synthesising a TaskId Var when the scope has no `as tid`), exactly like `allow_early_resolve`. `NoNestedCall` exempts the scope predicate via a new `ShouldVisitScopeAttr(key)` hook (same rationale as the Submit-field exemption in Phase 1; the hook keeps the base walker the single source of truth).
  - **Scope-producer tracking** so the Phase-2 contract genuinely applies to the scope form — a tensor produced by `with pl.spmd(...) as tid:` was previously untracked, so a missing `deps=` was silently certified. The deps-remediation hint is tailored per form (the plain / `for` forms cannot take `deps=`, so they are pointed at the `as tid` capture form instead of at a kwarg that would itself be rejected).
  - Cluster nesting rejects `predicate=` at parse time, and `UnwrapNestedSpmd` asserts it for hand-built / deserialized IR (such a scope is unwrapped into the Group function and never produces a `Submit`, so the predicate would be silently dropped).
  - **Drive-by fix:** `structural_hash` now **skips** Var-/Expr-valued scope attrs instead of throwing — a latent bug that already made every `with pl.spmd(...) as tid:` (`task_id_var`) un-hashable, which this change would otherwise have extended to any scope predicate.
  - Tests: parser (all three forms, canonical attr order, print round-trip, cluster + deps rejection, per-form hint), transforms (SSA versions the operand to the producing scope's result, DCE liveness, `structural_hash` regression), codegen (full `Default` pipeline → `set_predicate`), and an on-board **a2a3** ST proving the scope and submit forms skip/dispatch identically on hardware.
- [x] **Phase 4 — `pl.at(..., predicate=...)` scope form** — **PR: [hw-native-sys/pypto#2151](https://github.com/hw-native-sys/pypto/pull/2151)**. The cut Phase 3 deferred ("the C++ side is shared, so a later cut is parser + `dsl_api` only"). Confirmed accurate: every scope-attr walker (`VisitScopeAttrs` / `MutateScopeAttrs` / `ConvertToSSA::SubstScopeAttrs` / DCE `FindLiveRoots` / `structural_hash` / `NoNestedCall`) and `ScopeOutliner` were already scope-kind agnostic, so no new plumbing was needed.
  - **Placement restricted to where the scope becomes an independently submitted L0 task**, since anywhere else the predicate has no runtime carrier: `level=pl.Level.CORE_GROUP` only (a Hierarchy `pl.at` inside an Orchestration function survives the whole `Default` pipeline un-outlined — `OutlineHierarchyScopes` is `Opaque`-only — and never produces a `Submit`), and not nested inside `pl.cluster()` / `pl.spmd()` / another `pl.at` (the inner dispatch is folded into the enclosing Group / Spmd wrapper; codegen emits `set_predicate` from the *outer* call only). Both rejected at parse time; `ScopeOutliner` and a new `AssertNoInnerDispatchPredicate` in `OutlineClusterScopes` re-assert them for hand-built / deserialized IR.
  - **Scope-producer tracking extended to `with pl.at(...) as tid:`**, so the Phase-2 contract genuinely applies. Unlike `pl.spmd`, `pl.at` accepts `deps=` on *every* form, so the remediation hint always offers it rather than redirecting to the `as tid` capture form.
  - **Outliner bug found and fixed (also affected the Phase-3 `pl.spmd` form):** `ScopeOutliner` read `kAttrPredicate` raw, bypassing its own `store_target_renames_` substitution. A `pl.at` body typically writes its tensor with `pl.store`, so the attr names a scope-local post-store alias that outlining drops — the emitted `Submit` then referenced a dangling Var (caught by `UseAfterDefCheck`). The operand is now resolved exactly as the synthesised call's args are. Latent for `pl.spmd` too, whenever a predicate operand was written by an earlier sibling `pl.at` scope.
  - Tests: parser (attr landing, canonical order, print round-trip, no-`as tid` form, level + three nesting rejections, shared shape validation, scope-producer contract, hint wording), transforms (SSA versioning, outliner rebinding, DCE liveness), codegen (`set_predicate` block, operator/operand-order, emission order, plus a `windowize=True` case — `windowize` is `pl.at`-only and is the only DSL path reaching the predicate entry in `WindowExternalization`'s view-synthesised key filter). On-board **a2a3** ST gains a `pl.at` variant: **6/6 pass** across all three authoring forms. Full UT suite 7791 passed, 2 skipped. Docs updated (en + zh-cn).
- [ ] **Phase 5 (optional) — polish** — remaining:
  - Orchestration-codegen doc note for `set_predicate`.
  - A runnable MoE "skip empty experts" example under `examples/`.
  - ~~Broader ST parity vs the runtime `predicated_dispatch` case~~ → **done in Phase 3**, extended in Phase 4: `tests/st/runtime/scheduling/test_predicated_dispatch.py` is the frontend counterpart of the runtime's hand-written scene test and now covers the submit, `pl.spmd` scope and `pl.at` scope forms on a2a3.

> **Dropped: comparison-expression sugar.** Originally planned as a separate phase on top of a `pl.dispatch_pred(tensor, indices, op, target)` constructor. Per review feedback the expression is strictly constrainable *and* extends better (a future runtime multi-condition predicate maps naturally onto `a[0] > 0 and b[0] > 0`, whereas the constructor would need a combinator API). The constructor was therefore removed entirely rather than shipped and later deprecated — `predicate=(t[i] > 0)` is the only surface, and `pl.dispatch_pred` never ships.

### Carried constraints

- **Expressiveness** is fixed to `tensor[indices] OP const` (one comparison), matching the runtime's single-comparison `DispatchPredicate`. Chained comparisons, arithmetic, boolean combination, and non-literal right-hand sides are rejected at parse time; reduce anything richer to a single gate value in a prior kernel. Native multi-condition would require a runtime-side change.
- **Contract**: predicate operand producer ∈ `deps=` — enforced at the parser where statically provable (Phase 2), extended to scope-produced operands in Phase 3.

title: [Performance] Recreating CommDomain per L3 dispatch adds ~124 ms lifecycle overhead
body:
## Background

In pypto-lib, `models/deepseek/v4/decode_fwd.py` on Ascend 910B (`a2a3`, EP=2) has a severe performance problem outside the existing runtime STRACE window: every prepared L3 dispatch recreates and releases its communication domain/window buffers.

Across 100 measured rounds after 5 warmup rounds, CommDomain allocation plus backend release costs 123.80 ms on average, while the kernel's STRACE effective time is only 47.78 ms.

Reproduce with:

    PYPTO_BENCH=1 python tools/comm_domain_timing.py \
        models/deepseek/v4/decode_fwd.py \
        -p a2a3 --ep 2 -d 0,1

Reproduction environment:

| Component | Version |
|---|---|
| pypto-lib | `2e6cc68a2b43fb7748769b10fb6976619ec43971` (branch: `temp`) |
| pypto | `7759b264a0327735cb2ff6dccb2e0c1c9f937c31` (branch: `main`) |
| simpler | `a756969cfb4b25756792e6fbcb198d08beb6eea0` (detached) |
| ptoas | `0.48` |
| pto-isa | `83d01313d9bfc247c4b7c8bcf969d1019f0d106f` (detached) |
| CANN | `9.0.0` |
| Driver | `26.0.rc1` |

All simpler, ptoas, and pto-isa versions match the pins from the current pypto checkout.

Diagnosis: **pypto/simpler L3 communication lifecycle** — PyPTO lowers the window-buffer declarations into `with orch.allocate_domain(...)` inside the generated orchestration entry. Therefore every call through a prepared `DistributedWorker` performs a fresh collective allocation and release. The bundled simpler runtime implements the dynamic-domain handshake using file-based IPC announcement and barriers with 100 ms and 50 ms polling intervals, respectively.

### Summary

Prepared L3 programs should be able to reuse their communication domain and window buffers across dispatches. Currently, `decode_fwd` allocates and releases a 2,523,416-byte window per rank on every benchmark round.

The communication lifecycle overhead is approximately 2.59x the measured kernel execution time and accounts for about 72% of the combined lifecycle-plus-kernel time.

### Git Commit ID

`7759b264a0327735cb2ff6dccb2e0c1c9f937c31`

### NPU Kind

Ascend 910B

### Host Platform

Linux (aarch64)

### Reproduction Script

Save the following as `tools/comm_domain_timing.py` in a pypto-lib checkout:

```python
import atexit
import runpy
import statistics
import sys
import time
from collections import defaultdict
from pathlib import Path

from simpler.worker import Worker

WARMUP = 5
samples = defaultdict(list)


def wrap(method_name, phase):
    original = getattr(Worker, method_name)

    def timed(self, *args, **kwargs):
        start = time.perf_counter_ns()
        result = original(self, *args, **kwargs)
        elapsed_us = (time.perf_counter_ns() - start) / 1_000
        samples[phase].append(elapsed_us)
        print(
            f"[COMM_TIMING] phase={phase} "
            f"seq={len(samples[phase]) - 1} us={elapsed_us:.3f}",
            flush=True,
        )
        return result

    setattr(Worker, method_name, timed)


wrap("_allocate_domain", "alloc")
wrap("_release_domain_now", "free")


def report():
    for phase in ("alloc", "free"):
        values = samples[phase][WARMUP:]
        print(
            f"[COMM_TIMING_SUMMARY] phase={phase} samples={len(values)} "
            f"min_us={min(values):.3f} "
            f"median_us={statistics.median(values):.3f} "
            f"mean_us={statistics.fmean(values):.3f} "
            f"max_us={max(values):.3f}",
            flush=True,
        )

    paired = [
        alloc_us + free_us
        for alloc_us, free_us in zip(
            samples["alloc"][WARMUP:],
            samples["free"][WARMUP:],
        )
    ]
    print(
        f"[COMM_TIMING_SUMMARY] phase=alloc_plus_free samples={len(paired)} "
        f"min_us={min(paired):.3f} "
        f"median_us={statistics.median(paired):.3f} "
        f"mean_us={statistics.fmean(paired):.3f} "
        f"max_us={max(paired):.3f}",
        flush=True,
    )


atexit.register(report)

target = Path(sys.argv[1]).resolve()
sys.argv = [str(target), *sys.argv[2:]]
sys.path[:0] = [str(target.parent), str(Path.cwd())]
runpy.run_path(str(target), run_name="__main__")
```

Run:

    PYPTO_BENCH=1 python tools/comm_domain_timing.py \
        models/deepseek/v4/decode_fwd.py \
        -p a2a3 --ep 2 -d 0,1

### Expected Performance

The communication domain/window should be allocated once per prepared worker or compiled-program lifetime and reused across benchmark and serving dispatches.

Steady-state dispatches should not pay collective VMM allocation, IPC handle exchange/import, file barriers, and collective teardown on every invocation.

### Actual Performance

EP=2, 2,523,416-byte window per rank, 100 measured rounds:

| Phase | Median | Mean | P95 | Min | Max |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| CommDomain allocate | 103.26 ms | 85.36 ms | 107.52 ms | 2.13 ms | 153.84 ms |
| Backend release | 51.66 ms | 38.44 ms | 53.65 ms | 1.42 ms | 57.35 ms |
| Allocate + release | 154.64 ms | 123.80 ms | 158.86 ms | 3.57 ms | 205.91 ms |
| Kernel effective | 48.43 ms | 47.78 ms | — | 45.60 ms | 49.91 ms |

The latency is strongly quantized:

- Allocation: 80/100 rounds took at least 75 ms; 19/100 took less than 10 ms.
- Release: 73/100 rounds took at least 10 ms; 27/100 took less than 10 ms.
- One-time base communicator initialization took 1.428 seconds and was excluded by warmup.

The quantization matches the current implementation:

- `domain_read_announce` retries every 100 ms.
- `file_barrier` retries every 50 ms.

This means the observed number is the complete end-to-end dynamic CommDomain lifecycle, not isolated `aclrtMalloc` latency.

### Profiling Data

STRACE reports:

    effective_us (100 rounds) min=45604.6 median=48431.4 mean=47780.2 max=49913.1

Parent-side instrumentation reports:

    phase=alloc median_us=103264.900 mean_us=85358.586
    phase=free median_us=51664.668 mean_us=38442.592
    phase=alloc_plus_free median_us=154636.000 mean_us=123801.193

### Additional Context

Potential directions:

1. Hoist CommDomain/window allocation into `DistributedCompiledProgram.prepare()` and release it when the prepared worker closes.
2. Cache domains by program/domain identity, worker set, window size, and buffer layout.
3. If per-dispatch allocation must remain supported, replace file polling with event-driven synchronization or substantially shorter waits.
4. Preserve fresh logical state between dispatches by explicitly resetting counters/buffers rather than physically reallocating the window.

Related: #1189, #1968

title: [Feature] Front-end DSL primitive for cross-core (cube↔vector) sync — expose pto.sync.set / pto.sync.wait
body:
## Summary

Expose a user-facing pypto Python DSL primitive that emits the existing PTO IR cross-core synchronization ops `pto.sync.set` (`SyncSetOp`) / `pto.sync.wait` (`SyncWaitOp`), so kernel authors can hand-write cube↔vector (AIC↔AIV) producer/consumer pipelines. The IR ops and their lowering already exist in PTOAS — only the front-end entry point is missing.

## Motivation / Use Case

Reimplementing hand-written CANN Ascend-C attention kernels natively in pypto (e.g. `models/qwen3/14b/kernels/paged_attention_cce`) requires expressing the cube–vector rendezvous. The CCE version drives it with `AscendC::CrossCoreSetFlag<MODE, PIPE>(id)` / `CrossCoreWaitFlag(id)` and three flags (`qkReady` / `softmaxReady` / `pvReady`) to pipeline **QK (cube) → online-softmax (vector) → PV (cube) → rescale (vector)** with a 2-stack lookahead (`PRE_LAUNCH=2`) and a 3-slot GM workspace.

There is currently no pypto DSL way to place such a rendezvous by hand. Automatic sync insertion (GraphSyncSolver) covers dependency-driven fencing, but a hand-authored software pipeline needs **explicit, pipe-precise control**:
- trigger the flag on a specific pipe's completion (`PIPE_FIX` / `PIPE_MTE3`) — i.e. exactly when the producer's store lands in GM;
- a chosen static or dynamic event id;
- the flag decoupled from data movement, so the author controls buffer depth / lookahead.

The plumbing is already wired downstream:
- PTO IR: `SyncSetOp` (`pto.sync.set`) / `SyncWaitOp` (`pto.sync.wait`) — `include/PTO/IR/PTOOps.td:2769`; args: `pipe`, `event_id` (static) / `event_id_dyn`, `ffts_mode` (0..2).
- Lowering: `lib/PTO/Transforms/PTOToEmitC.cpp:1313` → `ffts_cross_core_sync` (A3) / `set_intra_block` (A5), building the FFTS message via `getFFTSMsg`; `sync.wait` → `wait_flag_dev`.
- Event-id allocation: `GraphSyncSolver` has a `CROSS_CORE_SYNC` mode with 16 cross-core event ids (2 reserved) — `include/PTO/Transforms/GraphSyncSolver/Utility.h:31`.

So this request is only for the **DSL front-end** that reaches these ops.

## Proposed API / Behavior

Illustrative (names TBD):

```python
# producer (cube) side, after the result store to GM
pl.sync.set(pipe=pl.PIPE_FIX, event_id=1)     # or pl.PIPE_MTE3
# consumer (vector) side, before the read
pl.sync.wait(pipe=pl.PIPE_MTE2, event_id=1)
```

- `pipe`: which pipe's completion triggers / is awaited (maps to `SyncSetOp.pipe`).
- `event_id`: static int **or** a dynamic index value (`SyncSetOp` already supports both via `event_id` / `event_id_dyn`).
- optional `ffts_mode` (0..2, A3) → `SyncSetOp.ffts_mode`.
- Lowers 1:1 to `pto.sync.set` / `pto.sync.wait`. Should interoperate with (or cleanly opt out of) GraphSyncSolver's automatic event-id allocation so manual and auto sync do not collide on ids.

## Alternatives Considered

- **tpush / tpop** (queue primitives that package GM buffer + FFTS flag): fine for simple producer/consumer, but a queue abstraction may not expose the pipe-precise trigger point, the chosen buffer depth (3 slots), or the decoupled lookahead needed to match a hand-tuned pipeline. An explicit `sync.set/wait` is the low-level escape hatch.
- **Keep authoring these kernels as CCE externs** (status quo): defeats the goal of a native pypto implementation + apples-to-apples perf comparison.

## Additional Context

- Concrete driver: pypto-lib todo "用 pypto 接口重新实现 5 个子 kernel" (`models/qwen3/14b/kernels/paged_attention_cce/todo.md`). `BlockMmadQK` is already reimplemented in pypto; the cube–vector epilogue pipeline is blocked on these primitives.
- Related: hw-native-sys/pypto#1911 (auto-fencing V2C GM deps), hw-native-sys/pypto#1906 (put-fence cross-rank), hw-native-sys/pypto#1820 (explicit AIV-split DSL).

title: [New Op] Add PyPTO frontend for pto.tprefetch_async (async GM→L2 prefetch)
body:
### Operation Level

**Other** — a comm/system-level **asynchronous memory-prefetch primitive**, not a tensor/block compute op. It starts an SDMA-backed async prefetch from GM into **L2 cache** and returns an async event/session pair for completion tracking.

### Proposed Name & Signature

PTOAS now implements the full op family (see **Additional Context**), but PyPTO has **no frontend at all** for it. The op family needs four coordinated pieces exposed at the DSL, plus three new IR value types (`PrefetchAsyncContext`, `AsyncEvent`, `AsyncSession`).

Proposed DSL surface (final namespace is a design decision for the implementer — a dedicated `pl.prefetch.*` module is suggested since this is neither a plain `pl.tile.*` compute op nor a `pld.*` distributed op):

```python
# 1. Build an async-prefetch context from a GM workspace buffer (i8 scratch)
ctx: pl.PrefetchAsyncContext = pl.prefetch.make_context(workspace)

# 2. Kick off an async GM -> L2 prefetch of a flat contiguous 1D GM region;
#    returns an async completion event
event: pl.AsyncEvent = pl.prefetch.async_prefetch(src, ctx)

# 3. Project the session bound to the context
session: pl.AsyncSession = pl.prefetch.session(ctx)

# 4. Wait for the prefetch to complete
done: bool = pl.prefetch.wait(event, session)
```

Mapping to the PTOAS ops:

| PyPTO frontend (proposed) | PTOAS op |
| --- | --- |
| `pl.prefetch.make_context(workspace)` | `pto.make_prefetch_async_context` |
| `pl.prefetch.async_prefetch(src, ctx)` | `pto.tprefetch_async` → `TPREFETCH_ASYNC(src, ctx)` |
| `pl.prefetch.session(ctx)` | `pto.get_prefetch_async_session` |
| `pl.prefetch.wait(event, session)` | `pto.comm.wait_async_event` |

### Semantics Description

- **`make_context(workspace)`**: materializes a first-class `PrefetchAsyncContext` from a GM workspace pointer (i8 scratch region used by the SDMA path).
- **`async_prefetch(src, ctx)`**: starts one asynchronous prefetch from GM into **L2 cache** via SDMA CMO. Returns an `AsyncEvent`. Does **not** block.
  - **Constraint (mirrors PTOAS `verify()`):** `src` must be a **flat contiguous logical-1D GM** region (view-like / GM memref). Non-1D or non-GM sources must be rejected at PyPTO IR verification time, matching the PTOAS op's input checks.
- **`session(ctx)`**: pure projection of the async session tied to `ctx` (used to wait on the returned event).
- **`wait(event, session)`**: waits for the async prefetch to complete; yields a boolean/`i1` done flag.

The op is a **cache hint / latency-hiding primitive**: it does not change any tensor values, only warms L2. Unlike most PTO intrinsics, `TPREFETCH_ASYNC` does not carry implicit wait-event synchronization — completion is explicit via the event/session.

### Example Usage

```python
@pl.program
class PrefetchExample:
    @pl.function
    def main(self, x: pl.Tensor[[4096], pl.FP32], ws: pl.Tensor[[1024], pl.INT8]) -> pl.Tensor[[4096], pl.FP32]:
        # Warm L2 with x while other work proceeds
        ctx = pl.prefetch.make_context(ws)
        evt = pl.prefetch.async_prefetch(x, ctx)
        session = pl.prefetch.session(ctx)

        # ... unrelated compute overlaps the prefetch ...

        pl.prefetch.wait(evt, session)   # ensure x is resident in L2 before the hot loop
        # ... consume x from the now-warm cache ...
        return x
```

### Hardware Support Considerations

- Maps directly to the Ascend PTO-ISA intrinsic `TPREFETCH_ASYNC(src, ctx)`, implemented over **SDMA CMO** (cache-management ops).
- Effective only on **A3 / A5**. On platforms where `SdmaWorkspaceManager::Init` is unavailable, PTOAS falls back to a **no-op prefetch** (with a runtime warning); PTOAS also exposes `PTO_DISABLE_SDMA_WORKSPACE_INIT=1` as an A3/A5 runtime fallback. The PyPTO frontend should degrade gracefully (functional no-op) on unsupported targets rather than error.
- Since it only warms cache, correctness is target-independent; only performance benefits are hardware-specific.

### Motivation / Use Case

`pto.tprefetch_async` is the only PTOAS primitive that lets a kernel **proactively pull GM data into L2 cache asynchronously**, overlapping the fill latency with unrelated compute. This is a key latency-hiding lever for memory-bound kernels (large GEMM operands, attention KV, MoE expert weights) where the working set exceeds on-chip capacity but fits in L2.

Today PyPTO cannot express this at all:
- The status matrix (`docs/zh-cn/dev/ptoas-op-status.md`, updated 2026-06-23) still marks `pto.tprefetch_async` as *"ptoas未实现 (ISA_ONLY)"* — but **PTOAS has since implemented the full op family** (op defs + verifiers + EmitC lowering to `TPREFETCH_ASYNC(...)` + runnable samples). The status doc row should also be corrected to reflect this.
- The related `pto.tprefetch` (prefetch into a local **tile** buffer, not L2) is likewise unimplemented in PyPTO (marked *MISSING (infra, skip)*), but is out of scope for this request — this issue is specifically about the **L2 async** path.

Exposing this unblocks manual latency-hiding in hand-written kernels and gives passes a target for future auto-prefetch insertion.

### Additional Context

Reference implementation in the PTOAS repo (sibling checkout `../PTOAS`):

- Op definitions: `include/PTO/IR/PTOOps.td`
  - `TPrefetchAsyncOp` — *"Asynchronously prefetch global data into L2 cache via SDMA CMO"*
  - `MakePrefetchAsyncContextOp`, `GetPrefetchAsyncSessionOp`
- Verifiers: `lib/PTO/IR/PTO.cpp` (`TPrefetchAsyncOp::verify()` — enforces flat-contiguous-1D GM `src`)
- EmitC lowering: `lib/PTO/Transforms/PTOToEmitC.cpp` → emits `TPREFETCH_ASYNC(...)` / `pto::PrefetchAsyncContext`
- Manual: `docs/PTO_IR_manual.md` § *`pto.tprefetch_async` - Asynchronous GM Prefetch into L2*
- Runnable samples: `test/samples/TPrefetchAsync/` (`tprefetch_async_binding.py` / `.pto` / compare script) and lit tests `test/lit/pto/tprefetch_async_*.pto`

Implementation will be a cross-layer effort: register the three IR value types + four ops in C++ (`include/pypto/ir/`, `src/ir/`), add nanobind bindings + `.pyi` stubs, build the `pl.prefetch.*` DSL surface, wire codegen to the PTOAS ops, and add unit + (A3/A5) system tests.

Related PyPTO op-status tracking: `docs/zh-cn/dev/ptoas-op-status.md` (row `pto.tprefetch_async`).

title: [Feature] Tensor API: keep matmul operands resident in L1 (Mat) across a loop (load-once / stationary operand)
body:
### Summary

At the **tensor API** level (`pl.matmul`), there is no way to keep a matmul operand **resident in L1 (`Mem.Mat`)** across a user-written loop. When the same operand (typically a small, stationary left matrix) is reused inside a `pl.range` loop, the compiler emits that operand's `tile.load(..., target_memory=Mem.Mat)` **inside the loop body**, so it is re-loaded from GM on every iteration instead of being loaded once and kept resident.

We would like a tensor-level mechanism to express "this operand stays resident in L1/Mat across the loop" (load-once / stationary operand), so users don't have to drop to the tile API to get it.

### Motivation / Use Case

A very common GEMM shape is a **small stationary left matrix multiplied against a large / streamed right matrix**: e.g. a resident weight or query tile swept across many KV / activation tiles. The intended hardware behavior is:

- load the small left operand into L1 (and on to L0A) **once**, keep it resident;
- **loop** over the large right operand, bringing on-chip only the right sub-matrix each iteration.

This is exactly the pattern users reach for when the right matrix is too large to fit L1 all at once and must be streamed. Today it cannot be expressed on the tensor API:

- The tensor API is otherwise the recommended, compiler-managed path (no manual `load`/`move`), but it silently reloads the stationary operand every iteration — redundant GM→L1 DMA traffic proportional to the loop trip count.
- `AutoTileMatmulL0` does **not** help: it only tiles the K-dimension of a *single* `tile.matmul`; it has no notion of cross-iteration operand residency for a user-written loop.
- A single wide `pl.matmul(lhs, rhs_wide)` only works when the *entire* right operand fits L1 (Mat ≤ 512KB on Ascend910B). A genuinely large right matrix overflows L1, because there is no L1-level streaming/tiling for one tensor-level matmul.

Net effect: for this whole class of kernels, users must abandon the tensor API and hand-manage memory spaces at the tile level.

### Proposed API / Behavior

Two possible directions (either would solve the use case):

**Option A — explicit residency hint** on the operand or the matmul:

```python
# left operand pinned to L1/Mat for the lifetime of the loop
lhs_resident = pl.resident(lhs, space=pl.Mem.Mat)
for n in pl.range(0, N, N_TILE):
    b_n = rhs[:, n : n + N_TILE]
    c_n = pl.matmul(lhs_resident, b_n, out_dtype=pl.FP32)  # loaded once, reused
    out = pl.assemble(out, c_n, [0, n])
```

**Option B — compiler LICM (loop-invariant code motion)**: when an operand and all of its `tile.load` arguments are loop-invariant, hoist the generated `tile.load(..., Mem.Mat)` out of the loop automatically. No API change; `pl.matmul(lhs, b_n)` inside a loop would "just work" (left loaded once).

### Alternatives Considered

- **Tile-level manual hoist (works today, verified):** load `lhs` to `Mem.Mat` + move to `Mem.Left` once *outside* the loop, reuse inside. This produces exactly the desired IR (see below). Downside: forces users off the tensor API and onto manual memory-space management for an otherwise-simple kernel.
- **Single wide `pl.matmul` + AutoTileMatmulL0 A-stationary:** only viable when the whole right operand fits L1; does not scale to a large/streamed right matrix.

### Additional Context

Verified on commit `aff862ba` by running the Default pass pipeline with `dump_ir` and inspecting the final IR.

**Naive tensor-level loop — left operand reloaded every iteration** (`ConvertTensorToTileOps` places the `lhs` load inside the loop, and no later pass hoists it out through all 44 passes):

```python
for n in pl.range(0, 2048, 128, init_values=(out,)):
    b_n     = pl.tile.load(rhs, [0, n], [128, 128], target_memory=pl.Mem.Mat)
    lhs_mat = pl.tile.load(lhs, [0, 0], [16, 128],  target_memory=pl.Mem.Mat)  # reloaded every iteration
    c_n     = pl.tile.matmul(lhs_mat, b_n)
    out     = pl.tile.store(c_n, [0, n], out)
```

**Tile-level manual hoist — left operand resident** (dedicated L0A allocation, loaded once outside the loop — the behavior we want the tensor API to be able to express):

```python
mem_left = pl.tile.alloc(pl.Mem.Left, 4096)
lhs_l1   = pl.tile.load(lhs, [0, 0], [16, 128], target_memory=pl.Mem.Mat)  # once, outside loop
lhs_left = pl.tile.move(lhs_l1, target_memory=pl.Mem.Left)                  # once, resident
for n in pl.range(0, 2048, 128, init_values=(out,)):
    b_l1    = pl.tile.load(rhs, [0, n], [128, 128], target_memory=pl.Mem.Mat)
    b_right = pl.tile.move(b_l1, target_memory=pl.Mem.Right)
    c       = pl.tile.matmul(lhs_left, b_right)  # reuses resident lhs_left
    out     = pl.tile.store(c, [0, n], out)
```

Related: #1595 (AutoTileMatmulL0 limitations).

title: [Pass Bug] AutoTileMatmulL0 / ChooseL0Tile shrinks K to fit a large N, degrading a full-K matmul into a K=32 tmatmul.acc chain
body:
## Background

In pypto-lib, an isolated decode-attention QK matmul (`models/qwen3/14b/bench_qk_compare.py`, `--impl pypto`, platform `a2a3`) has a **performance** problem traced to L0 tiling: when the score matmul is done stack-batched (`[16,128] @ Kᵀ` with N=512), pypto's L0 tile chooser shrinks the K dimension to 32 and turns one K=128 `tmatmul` into a chain of K=32 `tmatmul.acc`, making the stack-batched form ~1.05–1.16× slower than the per-page form that keeps K=128.

Reproduce (minimal, self-contained — same A operand and K=128 contraction, only N differs):

```python
import pypto.language as pl
from golden import TensorSpec, run_jit
import torch

M, K = 16, 128

def _mm(N):
    @pl.jit
    def mm(a: pl.Tensor[[M, K], pl.BF16],
           b: pl.Tensor[[N, K], pl.BF16],
           out: pl.Out[pl.Tensor[[M, N], pl.FP32]]) -> pl.Tensor[[M, N], pl.FP32]:
        for _ in pl.spmd(1, name_hint="mm"):
            ta = pl.load(a, [0, 0], [M, K], target_memory=pl.MemorySpace.Mat)
            tb = pl.load(b, [0, 0], [N, K], target_memory=pl.MemorySpace.Mat)
            tbt = pl.tile.transpose_view(tb)           # [K, N]
            s = pl.matmul(ta, tbt, out_dtype=pl.FP32)  # [M, N], contraction K=128
            out = pl.store(s, [0, 0], out)
        return out
    return mm

for N in (128, 512):
    run_jit(fn=_mm(N),
            specs=[TensorSpec("a", [M, K], torch.bfloat16, init_value=lambda: torch.randn(M, K)),
                   TensorSpec("b", [N, K], torch.bfloat16, init_value=lambda: torch.randn(N, K)),
                   TensorSpec("out", [M, N], torch.float32, is_output=True)],
            golden_fn=lambda v: None, compile_only=True,
            runtime_cfg={"platform": "a2a3"})
    # inspect build_output/_jit_mm_*/ptoas/mm_mm.pto
```

Reproduction environment:

| Component | Version |
|---|---|
| pypto-lib | `fae6826` (branch: `main`) |
| pypto | `9598f665` (branch: `codex/pto-buffer-ir`) |
| simpler | `438d5cb1` (branch: detached) |
| ptoas | `0.48` |
| pto-isa | `83d01313` |
| CANN | `9.0.0` |

Diagnosis: **pypto** — `AutoTileMatmulL0` pass / `ChooseL0Tile` (`include/pypto/ir/transforms/utils/l0_tile_chooser.h`, `src/ir/transforms/auto_tile_matmul_l0_pass.cpp`). This is a compile-time codegen choice; runtime/pto-isa/CANN versions are not implicated.

### Description

For a `tile.matmul` with small M (16) and K=128, the L0 tile chooser prefers a **large N** L0C and is then forced to **shrink K to 32** (L0B capacity: `[K,512]` bf16 must stay ≤ 64 KB). This degrades one efficient K=128 `pto.tmatmul` into a K-loop of K=32 `pto.tmatmul.acc` (a serial dependency chain on the [16,512] accumulator, with poorer cube-array fill and 4× the Q/K L0 extracts). Keeping K=128 and splitting **N** into L0-sized 128-wide blocks (as the N=128 case already does) would preserve full-K matmuls. There appears to be no "prefer splitting N over shrinking K" preference in the chooser.

The result is numerically correct (golden passes) — this is a **tiling-quality / performance** defect, not a miscompile.

### Before IR (Input)

Two `tile.matmul` kernels, identical except for N (see the minimal repro above): `[16,128] @ [K=128, N]`, contraction K=128.
- Case A: `N=128`
- Case B: `N=512`

### Expected IR (After Transformation)

Both cases keep the full **K=128** contraction. For N=512, N is split into 128-wide L0 blocks (4× independent `[16,128] @ [128,128]`), i.e. the same efficient L0 shapes the N=128 case already emits:

```
// N=128 (observed, and the shape N=512 should follow per 128-N-block):
%a_l0 : loc=left,  bf16, rows=16,  cols=128   // K = 128
%b_l0 : loc=right, bf16, rows=128, cols=128   // K = 128
pto.tmatmul(%a_l0, %b_l0) -> loc=acc [16,128]  // single, full-K, no acc-chain
// counts: tmatmul=1, tmatmul.acc=0, K-loop=0
```

### Actual IR or Error

For **N=512** the chooser shrinks K to 32 and emits a K-accumulation chain:

```
// N=512 (observed):
scf.for %ko = 0 to 128 step 64 {              // K split into 32-wide chunks
  %a_l0 : loc=left,  bf16, rows=16, cols=32    // K = 32  (was 128)
  %b_l0 : loc=right, bf16, rows=32, cols=512   // K = 32, N = 512
  tmatmul / tmatmul.acc(%acc[16,512], %a_l0, %b_l0)  // chained accumulate
}
// counts: tmatmul=1, tmatmul.acc=2 (per unroll), K-loop present
```

Same A operand and same K=128 contraction as N=128, yet K is compressed to 32 solely because N=512 was chosen for L0C. `ttrans=0` in both (the `transpose_view` is a zero-copy NZ↔ZN reinterpretation and is **not** the cause).

### Additional Context

- Real context: this is the decode QK (`Q·Kᵀ`) leaf of the Qwen3-14B paged-attention kernel, isolated in `pypto-lib/models/qwen3/14b/bench_qk_compare.py` and compared against the hand-written CANN `BlockMmadQK`. Device numbers (a2a3, `PYPTO_BENCH=1`, 100-round `effective_us`, median): per-page (auto N=128/K=128) **130 µs** ≈ hand-written CCE **126.6 µs** (1.03×); stack-batched N=512 (auto → K=32 acc-chain) **137 µs**.
- Attempting to force K=128 on the stack form via explicit N-split (`pl.tile.extract`/`slice` + `pl.matmul`) hits a second obstacle: 4 unrolled N-chunks × pipeline `stage=2` overflow L0B (128 KB > 64 KB), forcing a serial `pl.range` N-loop that loses ping-pong (151 µs). So the auto chooser's N-over-K preference, plus the buffer budget, both push away from the efficient full-K tiling that CCE gets by hand.
- Suggested fix direction: in `ChooseL0Tile`, when M is small and K fits at full width, prefer splitting N into L0-sized blocks (keep K maximal) rather than shrinking K to accommodate a large N in one L0C.

Related (L0-tiling, not duplicates): pypto#1595, pypto#1310, pypto#1776.

title: [Bug] pl.tile.row_max / row_sum silently compute zeros when tmp_tile is smaller than the input
body:
## Background

In pypto-lib, `models/qwen3/14b/bench_softmax_compare.py` on a2a3 has a **precision** problem: a native-DSL reimplementation of the CCE `EpilogueOnlineSoftmax` leaf produced all-zero row maxima, so every probability came out as `exp(0)=1` and the running softmax denominator landed at exactly 7*512=3584 instead of ~150-230.

Root-caused to the tile-level reduction API rather than the kernel: `pl.tile.row_max(tile, tmp_tile)` needs `tmp_tile` to have the SAME shape as the input (`[rows, cols]`). Passing an output-shaped `[rows, 1]` tmp compiles and runs cleanly but silently yields zeros.

Reproduce with:

    python models/qwen3/14b/bench_softmax_compare.py --impl pypto -p a2a3 -d 0

Reproduction environment:

| Component | Version |
|---|---|
| pypto-lib | `fae6826` (branch: `main`) |
| pypto | `8ebddcb` (branch: `main`) — also reproduces on `9598f66` (`codex/pto-buffer-ir`) |
| simpler | `a756969` (detached) |
| ptoas | `0.48` |
| pto-isa | `83d0131` |
| CANN | not detected (npu-smi 26.0.rc1) |

All components are on their pins (simpler == pypto `HEAD:runtime`, pto-isa == `runtime/pto_isa.pin`, ptoas == `PTOAS_VERSION`).

Diagnosis: **pypto** — the op is constructed and lowered without any check that `tmp_tile` is large enough, and the result is silently wrong.

### Component

Python Bindings

### Description

The tile-level reductions `pl.tile.row_max` / `pl.tile.row_sum` take an explicit `tmp_tile` scratch operand. Its required shape is undocumented and unvalidated. If it is smaller than the input tile, compilation succeeds, execution succeeds, and the result is **all zeros** — no error, no warning.

The tensor-level path is unaffected: `pl.row_max(tensor)` internally allocates a full-width scratch (confirmed in the generated `.pto`) and is correct.

Minimal A/B, identical apart from the tmp tile shape (input is `[8, 512]` fp32):

| tmp_tile shape | Result |
|---|---|
| `[8, 1]`   | **FAIL — all zeros** |
| `[8, 64]`  | **FAIL** |
| `[8, 256]` | **FAIL** |
| `[8, 512]` (== input) | PASS |

Generated IR confirms the contract difference — tensor-level emits `pto.trowmax ins(%s, %tmp : ...rows=8, cols=512..., ...rows=8, cols=512...)` whereas the tile-level call faithfully passes the user's `rows=8, cols=1` tmp straight through to `pto.trowmax` with no verifier complaint.

A follow-on symptom that makes this especially confusing to debug: feeding the (zeroed) result into `pl.row_expand_sub(s, m)` yields `s - m` that is *exactly* 0 everywhere, i.e. it looks like the op computed `x - x`.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Save as `probe.py`:

```python
import pypto.language as pl, torch, math
from golden import TensorSpec, run_jit

TASKS, RP, SL = 128, 16, 512
ROWS = TASKS * RP
SCALE = 1.0 / math.sqrt(128)

@pl.jit
def probe(scores: pl.Tensor[[ROWS, SL], pl.FP32],
          out_m: pl.Out[pl.Tensor[[ROWS, 1], pl.FP32]]) -> pl.Tensor[[ROWS, 1], pl.FP32]:
    for task in pl.spmd(TASKS, name_hint="probe"):
        r0 = task * RP
        # BUG: [8, 1] silently yields zeros; [8, SL] is correct.
        tmp = pl.create_tile([8, 1], dtype=pl.FP32, target_memory=pl.MemorySpace.Vec)
        s = pl.tile.muls(pl.load(scores, [r0, 0], [8, SL]), SCALE)
        m = pl.row_max(s, tmp)
        out_m = pl.store(m, [r0, 0], out_m)
    return out_m

def golden(v):
    s = v["scores"].reshape(TASKS, RP, SL).float() * SCALE
    v["out_m"].reshape(TASKS, RP, 1)[:, :8] = s[:, :8].max(dim=-1, keepdim=True).values

def init():
    s = torch.zeros(TASKS, RP, SL); s[:, :5, :] = torch.randn(TASKS, 5, SL) * 11.3
    return s.reshape(ROWS, SL)

torch.manual_seed(0)
r = run_jit(fn=probe,
            specs=[TensorSpec("scores", [ROWS, SL], torch.float32, init_value=init),
                   TensorSpec("out_m", [ROWS, 1], torch.float32, is_output=True)],
            golden_fn=golden,
            runtime_cfg={"platform": "a2a3", "device_id": 0, "enable_dep_gen": False},
            rtol=5e-3, atol=2e-2)
print("passed=", r.passed)
```

2. Run it from a pypto-lib checkout (so `golden` is importable): `python probe.py`
3. Observe `out_m` FAIL, every element `0.0`.
4. Change the tmp tile to `pl.create_tile([8, SL], ...)` and re-run — passes.

### Expected Behavior

Either:

- **(a)** `pl.tile.row_max` / `row_sum` reject an undersized `tmp_tile` at op construction (or in the IR verifier) with a clear message stating the required shape; **or**
- **(b)** if `[rows, 1]` is in fact the intended contract, codegen honors it and produces correct results.

Either way the required `tmp_tile` shape should be documented — the docstring currently says only "Temporary tile", and the unified wrapper's error message ("row_max on Tile requires tmp_tile argument") gives no shape guidance.

### Actual Behavior

Compiles and runs with no diagnostic; every reduced value is `0.0`.

Note this is easy to hit: the in-tree kernel `models/deepseek/v4/hc_pre.py:296-301` (pypto-lib) uses exactly the `pl.create_tile([COMB_T_TILE, 1], ...)` form as its `row_max` / `row_sum` scratch, with `COMB_T_TILE = 8` — i.e. the same output-shaped tmp that fails here. That usage may be silently affected and is worth auditing.

### Git Commit ID

`8ebddcb87a95c091c02f7f53b0a877c1e3f3d444`

### NPU Kind

Ascend 910B

### Host Platform

Linux (aarch64)

### Additional Context

Related: #1401 (`tile.row_sum` valid_shape propagation).

Found while reimplementing the 5 handwritten CCE attention leaf kernels in native pypto DSL to benchmark DSL-vs-handwritten (`models/qwen3/14b/bench_softmax_compare.py`). Workaround in that bench was to switch to the tensor-level slicing form.

title: [Bug] pto-isa resolution tracks main tip instead of runtime/pto_isa.pin, breaking all on-device STs
body:
### Component

Build System

### Description

`ensure_pto_isa_root()` in `python/pypto/runtime/device_runner.py` resolves pto-isa by **tracking the remote default branch tip**, not the pinned commit the runtime submodule uses. When no `commit` is passed it calls `_update_pto_isa_to_latest()` (`device_runner.py:261`):

```python
git fetch origin
git reset --hard origin/HEAD    # origin/HEAD -> origin/main
```

The runtime submodule does the opposite: `runtime/simpler_setup/pto_isa.py` force-checks-out `runtime/pto_isa.pin`, and its own comment notes the `--force` is load-bearing precisely because pto-isa's default branch is not a safe thing to follow.

The two policies have now diverged in a way that breaks the device test surface:

| checkout | commit | result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `runtime/build/pto-isa` (managed, follows `pto_isa.pin`) | `83d01313` | device STs pass |
| `build_output/_deps/pto-isa` (PyPTO, follows `origin/main`) | `ea90d400` | incore compile fails |

`83d01313` is an ancestor of `ea90d400` on the same `main` branch, 221 commits behind. Somewhere in that range, pto-isa commit `55bd170e` ("a2a3 ttrans ncdhw to fractal_nz_3d ub space optimization", 2026-06-01) introduced references to an undeclared `dstC0` in `include/pto/npu/a2a3/TTrans.hpp` (the surrounding scope only defines `validC0`) — an upstream compile regression that has been sitting on `main` for ~7 weeks.

Because `_update_pto_isa_to_latest()` runs on every device-test invocation, this is not a stale-cache problem and cannot be fixed by deleting `build_output/_deps/pto-isa`: a fresh clone re-runs `reset --hard origin/HEAD` and lands back on the broken tip. Manually checking out the pin does not survive either — the next test run resets it.

### Steps to Reproduce

```bash
# Any on-device system test, without PTO_ISA_ROOT or --pto-isa-commit:
env -u PTO_ISA_ROOT python -m pytest tests/st/runtime/ops/test_abs.py -v --platform=a2a3 --device=0
```

### Expected Behavior

PyPTO resolves pto-isa at the same commit the runtime submodule pins (`runtime/pto_isa.pin`), so on-device STs build against a known-good pto-isa without any per-invocation workaround.

### Actual Behavior

All on-device STs fail during incore compilation:

```
/data/.../build_output/_deps/pto-isa/include/pto/npu/a2a3/TTrans.hpp:464:25:
    error: use of undeclared identifier 'dstC0'
    unsigned validRow = dstC0;
                        ^
fatal error: too many errors emitted, stopping now [-ferror-limit=]
30 warnings and 20 errors generated.
```

Workarounds that do restore a green run (each has to be repeated per invocation):

- `PTO_ISA_ROOT=<path to a pto-isa at 83d01313>` — the env var short-circuits `ensure_pto_isa_root()` before the reset
- `--pto-isa-commit=83d01313d9bfc247c4b7c8bcf969d1019f0d106f`

### Git Commit ID

869d5b6518ea816f43769a8e3ab22831b0b214f4

### NPU Kind

Ascend 910B

### Host Platform

Linux (aarch64)

### Additional Context

**Proposed fix:** make `ensure_pto_isa_root()` default `commit` to the contents of `runtime/pto_isa.pin` when the caller does not pass one explicitly, falling back to the current follow-latest behaviour only when the pin file cannot be read. That aligns PyPTO with `runtime/simpler_setup/pto_isa.py` and makes the toolchain reproducible; bumping pto-isa then becomes a deliberate pin bump in one place rather than an implicit dependency on whatever landed on `main` that day.

Trade-off worth stating explicitly: PyPTO would stop automatically picking up new pto-isa features. Given that following `main` currently means silently inheriting a 7-week-old compile regression, reproducibility looks like the better default.

The upstream `TTrans.hpp` regression in `55bd170e` should be reported separately to `hw-native-sys/pto-isa`; pinning fixes PyPTO's exposure but not the underlying breakage.

Found while adding on-device system tests for the `pl.prefetch.*` op family (#2075) — every device run needed a manual `PTO_ISA_ROOT` override before it could compile.

title: [Bug] Column-slice of a dynamic-pitch tensor passed orch→incore silently reads wrong data (stride densified)
body:
### Component

Codegen (root cause spans op type-deduction + IR passes + PTO codegen — see Additional Context)

### Description

When an orchestration function column-slices a tensor whose **last dim (row pitch) is dynamic** (`pl.dynamic(...)`) and passes the slice into an incore kernel, the incore GM load **silently reads wrong data** — no error, no NaN, no diagnostic.

Root cause: the incore GM operand's stride is emitted as a **compile-time constant** baked into the generated `GlobalTensor<..., pto::Stride<...>>`. `kernel_entry` passes only `buffer.addr + start_offset` at runtime — never a stride. For a **static** pitch, the compiler stamps the true parent pitch (e.g. `Stride<...,128,1>`) and the result is correct. For a **dynamic** pitch there is no runtime channel to thread the pitch into the kernel, so codegen falls back to the **dense/contiguous** assumption `stride = inner load extent` (`Stride<...,64,1>`), i.e. it reads the `[32,64]` window as if it were contiguous. Only rows where the dense stride happens to equal the true pitch survive.

Note: the runtime `Tensor::view()` **does** compute the correct dynamic stride (`result.strides[i] = strides[i]`) and stores it on the Tensor struct — but the incore kernel never reads it.

The equivalent **static-shape** column slice is correct (verified: max diff 0.0). Only the dynamic-pitch case breaks.

### Steps to Reproduce

```python
import pypto.language as pl
import torch
from pypto.runtime import RunConfig

N = pl.dynamic("N")   # dynamic last dim (= row pitch) of the parent tensor

@pl.jit.incore
def copy_kernel(a: pl.Tensor, out: pl.Out[pl.Tensor]):
    t = pl.load(a, [0, 0], [32, 64])
    pl.store(t, [0, 0], out)
    return out

@pl.jit
def col_split_dyn(x: pl.Tensor[[32, N], pl.FP32],
                  out0: pl.Out[pl.Tensor], out1: pl.Out[pl.Tensor]):
    left  = pl.slice(x, [32, 64], [0, 0])
    right = pl.slice(x, [32, 64], [0, 64])   # column offset on dim 1
    out0 = copy_kernel(left, out0)
    out1 = copy_kernel(right, out1)
    return out0, out1

x = torch.randn(32, 128, dtype=torch.float32)
o0 = torch.zeros(32, 64); o1 = torch.zeros(32, 64)
# codegen-only inspection (no device/runtime needed):
col_split_dyn(x, o0, o1, config=RunConfig(save_kernels=True, codegen_only=True))
# Inspect kernels/aiv/copy_kernel.cpp -> the load GlobalTensor stride is
#   pto::Stride<2048, 2048, 2048, 64, 1>   (dense, WRONG)
# A static x: pl.Tensor[[32, 128], pl.FP32] instead bakes Stride<...,128,1> (correct).
```

Reproduces on `a2a3sim` (not hardware-specific). A full numeric run gives `left/right max diff ≈ 5.5 / 4.9` versus the expected `0.0`.

### Expected Behavior

The incore load reads the correct strided window (`left == x[:, 0:64]`, `right == x[:, 64:128]`), matching torch — `max diff ≈ 0`, identical to the static-pitch case. If dynamic strides cannot yet be supported, the compiler should **error loudly** rather than silently emit a dense stride.

### Actual Behavior

Silently wrong data, no error/warning:

```
left  max diff: 5.50   # expected 0.0
right max diff: 4.91
# generated kernels/aiv/copy_kernel.cpp:
pto::Stride<2048, 2048, 2048, 64, 1>   # dense row stride 64 — true parent pitch is 128
```

### Git Commit ID

f990c8d7c92484abde9ac0f674a044e7a9cc28c7

### NPU Kind

N/A (not hardware-specific)

### Host Platform

Linux (aarch64)

### Additional Context

Related: #2005 (silent GM data corruption), #631 (orchestration codegen for incore calls).

**Cross-layer trace (static works, dynamic breaks):**

- Slice type deduction drops the parent stride — `DeduceTensorSliceType` builds the result `TensorView` with empty stride (`src/ir/op/tensor_ops/memory.cpp:282-290`).
- `OptimizeOrchTensors` only stamps a `TensorView(stride=...)` for **statically provable** windows; for a symbolic pitch it bails (`ComputeRowMajorStrides` returns `{}` on any non-const dim, `src/ir/transforms/optimize_orch_tensors_pass.cpp:64-81`, In-param path `:1461-1557`; window gate `src/ir/transforms/utils/window_externalization.cpp:2674-2691`). The callee param stays a **bare** `pl.Tensor[[32,64]]`.
- `MaterializeTensorStrides` treats a bare/empty-stride TensorType as implicitly ND-packed and fills a **dense** stride from the type's own shape (`src/ir/transforms/materialize_tensor_strides_pass.cpp:87-107` via `BuildLogicalStridesFromLayout`, `include/pypto/ir/transforms/utils/tensor_view_semantics.h:72-125`).
- Codegen emits the dense stride: `EmitMakeTensorViews` canonical-ND fallback stamps `stride[rank-2] = shape[rank-1]` (`src/codegen/pto/pto_codegen.cpp:1016-1028`, gate `:973-974`; pre-emit `:806-826`). This is the single site that produces the dense `Stride<...,64,1>`.
- The `TensorViewCanonical` verifier does not catch it — symbolic stride relations pass under `relaxed_symbolic` (`tensor_view_semantics.h:206-281`).

**Fix direction (feasible; mirrors the existing dynamic-shape path):** thread the runtime stride the same way dynamic shapes / `valid_shape` scalars are threaded — the wrapper (`kernel_entry`) reads `tensor->strides[i]` and passes it as a separate scalar arg into the ptoas func, and codegen emits `GlobalTensor` with the ISA's dynamic stride slot. The ISA already supports this: `pto::DYNAMIC` (`= -1`), `Stride<...>` constructors that fill `DYNAMIC` slots from runtime `int64_t` values, and `GlobalTensor(data, shape, stride)` taking a runtime Stride (`runtime/build/pto-isa/include/pto/common/pto_tile.hpp`; existing use `Stride<1,1,1,DYNAMIC,1>` in `pto/npu/kernels/Pto_prefetch.hpp`). So the parent pitch must be promoted to a first-class dynamic dim that flows through the existing dynamic-dim → runtime-scalar materialization machinery, rather than being densified to a compile-time constant.

title: [Feature] Fully-resolved IR dump: pass dumps omit implicit tile layouts, making layout bugs hard to locate
body:
### Summary

`dump_passes=True` writes per-pass IR that is **not self-describing for tile layouts**. A tile's `blayout` / `slayout` / `fractal` are omitted from the printed `TileView` whenever they equal the memory-space *implicit* view, and canonical IR stores an implicit view as `nullopt`, so for those tiles nothing is printed at all.

Reading a dump therefore cannot tell you a tile's actual layout. Worst case, the printed form actively suggests the wrong answer: a `pl.Mem.Acc` tile that prints with **no** `TileView` is really `blayout=col_major, slayout=row_major, fractal=1024`, but reads as "defaults" (i.e. `none_box`).

Request: an option to dump **fully-resolved** layouts — print `GetEffectiveTileView()` for every tile rather than the sparse canonical form.

### Motivation / Use Case

Locating a layout bug is exactly when you reach for the pass dumps, and it is exactly when they mislead.

Concretely, while porting a fused flash-attention kernel I hit `'pto.trowmax' op expects src to use the row_major blayout`, and used the 45 pass dumps to find where the offending layout came from. I mis-attributed the source **three times in a row**, each time because I read "no `TileView`" as "default / `none_box`":

1. blamed the loop-carried seed — the seed prints without a `TileView`;
2. blamed `row_expand_mul` for "introducing" boxed output — its outputs *do* print `slayout=row_major` while its inputs print nothing, so it looks like the origin (it is not: `src/ir/op/tile_ops/broadcast.cpp:88` only inherits via `InheritTileViewLayout`);
3. blamed the `Mem.Acc` matmul results being `none_box` — they print without a `TileView`, but `Acc`'s implicit view is boxed, so they were the real source all along.

Every one of those was decidable from the IR — just not from the *printed* IR. With resolved layouts this would have been a single pass over one dump.

This also matters for anyone comparing two dumps: two tiles with identical printed types can have different real layouts (different `memory_space`), and two tiles with different printed types can have the same real layout.

### Proposed API / Behavior

An opt-in that makes the dump self-contained, e.g. either
- env var `PYPTO_PRINT_EXPLICIT_LAYOUT=1`, or
- a field next to `dump_passes` (e.g. `RunConfig.dump_passes_explicit_layout`).

When on, print every tile's resolved `blayout` / `slayout` / `fractal` from `GetEffectiveTileView(tile_type)`, including for tiles whose `tile_view_` is `nullopt`.

Note this needs BOTH sites — omission happens at two layers:
- storage: canonical IR keeps an implicit view as `nullopt`, so `python_printer.cpp:581` never enters the `PrintTileView` branch;
- printing: `python_printer.cpp:2763` / `:2780` drop `blayout` / `slayout` field-by-field when they match `GetImplicitTileView(shape, memory_space)`.

Changing the printer alone is not enough.

Default should stay as-is: the current concise form is right for diffing passes, and this is a debugging aid.

### Alternatives Considered

- **Reconstruct it by hand.** Cross-reference `memory_space` against the implicit table (`include/pypto/ir/tile_view_semantics.h:59-86`: `Mat`/`Left` → col_major/row_major; `Right` → slayout=col_major; `Acc` → col_major/row_major/fractal=1024; otherwise inferred from shape). Works, but it is exactly the step that is easy to get wrong, and it has to be redone for every tile in a 750-line dump.
- **Post-process the dumps with a script.** Possible, but it would have to re-derive the implicit view outside pypto and stay in sync with it — the logic already exists in-tree as `GetEffectiveTileView`.

### Additional Context

Related: #1498 — the printer dropping `blayout` on a packed-mask `TileView` breaks the print→parse round-trip. Same root cause (omitting implicit layout on print), narrower symptom; a resolved-layout dump mode would also make that class of bug visible.

Relevant code:
- `include/pypto/ir/tile_view_semantics.h:59-86` — `GetImplicitTileView`, the per-memory-space table
- `include/pypto/ir/tile_view_semantics.h:167` — `GetEffectiveTileView`, already resolves `nullopt` → implicit
- `src/ir/transforms/python_printer.cpp:581-590` — the `has_value()` guard
- `src/ir/transforms/python_printer.cpp:2763`, `:2780` — the per-field omission

Environment (not a repro, listed for context): pypto `869d5b6` (main), simpler `a756969c`, ptoas `v0.48`, pto-isa `83d01313`, pypto-lib `fae6826`, Linux aarch64.

title: [Bug] Codegen is blind to Submit nodes in two more sites, blocking hand-written AIC/AIV cross-core pipes
body:
## Background

In pypto-lib, hand-writing a cross-core AIC/AIV software pipeline
(`@pl.program` + `@pl.function(type=FunctionType.AIC/.AIV)` + manual
`tpush_to_aiv`/`tpop_from_aic`/`tpush_to_aic`/`tpop_from_aiv`) fails to compile
as soon as the AIC/AIV pair is dispatched with `pl.submit(...)` inside
`pl.cluster()` — which is the only way to get the two sides to run concurrently.

Reproduce with (compile-only, no device needed):

    python probe_manual_pipe.py -p a2a3sim

Reproduction environment:

| Component | Version |
|---|---|
| pypto-lib | `fae6826` (branch: `main`) |
| pypto | `869d5b65` (branch: `main`) |
| simpler | `a756969c` (branch: `detached`) |
| ptoas | `0.48` |
| pto-isa | `83d01313` |
| CANN | not detected |

All four components match their pins.

Diagnosis: **pypto** — two more sites of the known "exact-kind `As<Call>` dispatch
misses `Submit`" bug class (cf. #1615, #1707, both closed).

### Component

Codegen

### Description

Two codegen/util sites match only `Call` nodes and are blind to `Submit`, so any
`pl.submit`-dispatched AIC/AIV pair is invisible to them:

1. **`ComputeGMPipeWorkspaceElements`** (`src/codegen/orchestration/orchestration_analysis.cpp`)
   scans the callee tree for `initialize_pipe` to size the GM pipe workspace, using
   `transform_utils::GetCallFromStmt` — which is a plain
   `As<Call>(assign->value_)` and returns `nullptr` for a `Submit`. The scan
   therefore never descends into the submitted AIC/AIV kernels, finds no
   `initialize_pipe`, and computes a workspace of 0 elements.
   Note the *same file* already uses `AsCallOrSubmitView` at lines 179/254 with the
   comment "The consumer may be a Submit ... view it as a Call" — this scan just
   missed it.

2. **`CallVisitor`** (`src/ir/transforms/utils/wrapper_call_utils.cpp`) only
   overrides `VisitExpr_(const CallPtr&)`. A `Submit` is a different expr kind, so
   the walk never fires on it, and `FindGroupCallees` (which drives
   `GenerateGroupCallCode`) cannot find the AIC/AIV callees of a submitted pair.

### Steps to Reproduce

Minimal program — an AIC kernel and an AIV kernel exchanging one tile each way,
dispatched with `pl.submit` inside `pl.cluster()`:

```python
@pl.program
class ManualPipeProg:
    @pl.function(type=pl.FunctionType.AIC)
    def cube_side(self, q, kk, vv, sink: pl.InOut[...], task: pl.Scalar[pl.INDEX]):
        v2c = pl.system.reserve_buffer(name="probe_v2c", size=32768, base=0)
        c2v_imp = pl.system.import_peer_buffer(name="probe_c2v", peer_func="vec_side")
        pl.system.aic_initialize_pipe(c2v_imp, v2c, dir_mask=3, slot_size=8192)
        ...
        pl.tile.tpush_to_aiv(pl.matmul(q_l, k_r, out_dtype=pl.FP32), split=0)
        p = pl.tile.tpop_from_aiv(shape=[M, K], dtype=pl.BF16, split=0)
        ...
        return sink

    @pl.function(type=pl.FunctionType.AIV)
    def vec_side(self, out: pl.Out[...], task: pl.Scalar[pl.INDEX]):
        c2v = pl.system.reserve_buffer(name="probe_c2v", size=32768, base=0)
        v2c_imp = pl.system.import_peer_buffer(name="probe_v2c", peer_func="cube_side")
        pl.system.aiv_initialize_pipe(c2v, v2c_imp, dir_mask=3, slot_size=8192)
        s = pl.tile.tpop_from_aic(shape=[M, K], dtype=pl.FP32, split=0)
        ...
        pl.tile.tpush_to_aic(pl.cast(p, target_type=pl.BF16, mode="rint"), split=0)
        return ret

    @pl.function(type=pl.FunctionType.Orchestration)
    def main(self, q, kk, vv, sink, out):
        for t in pl.parallel(N):
            with pl.cluster():
                sink, _ = pl.submit(self.cube_side, q, kk, vv, sink, t)   # <-- Submit
                out, _  = pl.submit(self.vec_side, out, t)                # <-- Submit
        return out
```

Compile it (`ir.compile`, `-p a2a3sim`). A full runnable script is attached below.

### Expected Behavior

The program compiles: the GM pipe workspace is sized from the `initialize_pipe`
calls inside the submitted AIC/AIV kernels, and `FindGroupCallees` resolves both
callees of the cluster group.

### Actual Behavior

Two successive failures.

Before fix 1:

```
Failed to generate orchestration 'main':
  Internal error: injected gm_pipe_buffer tensor.create found without initialize_pipe ops
Check failed: workspace_elems > 0 at src/codegen/orchestration/orchestration_codegen.cpp:2817
```

After fix 1, before fix 2:

```
Failed to generate orchestration 'main':
  Internal error: no AIC callee found in Group 'main_cluster_0' body
```

Replacing `pl.submit` with direct calls makes it compile — confirming the fault is
purely the `Submit`-blindness, not the pipe code. (Direct calls are not a usable
workaround: they are sequential statements, so the two sides do not run
concurrently and the blocking `tpop`s deadlock — see the follow-up issue.)

### Proposed Fix

Both are one-liners in spirit; patch attached (verified: with both applied the
repro compiles, `passed=True`).

1. `ComputeGMPipeWorkspaceElements`: use `AsCallOrSubmitView(assign->value_ / eval->expr_)`
   instead of `transform_utils::GetCallFromStmt(stmt)`.
2. `CallVisitor`: add a `VisitExpr_(const SubmitPtr&)` override that routes through
   `SubmitToCallView` into the same match logic.

It is worth auditing for further instances of this class — #1615 already listed 8
passes with the same defect, and these two sites were not among them.

### Git Commit ID

869d5b6518ea816f43769a8e3ab22831b0b214f4

### NPU Kind

N/A (not hardware-specific)

### Host Platform

Linux (aarch64)

### Additional Context

Related: #1615, #1707 (same `As<Call>`-vs-`Submit` class, both closed).

Motivation: the auto-split (`@pl.jit`) form emits the vector→cube `tpush` and the
cube-side `tpop` at the *same* DSL site (the `matmul(cast(probs), V)`), so the
probs push cannot be hoisted away from its consumer. In a flash-attention decode
kernel this leaves the softmax→P@V→rescale leg with zero skew; an msprof in-core
trace shows CUBE(matmul) and VECTOR(compute) overlapping **0% of the span**
(makespan 61us vs ~38us if pipelined). `SkewCrossCorePipeline` cannot fix it
either — it demotes any cross-core loop with a genuine tile carry (the online-softmax
`m`/`l`/`o`) or multiple round-trips to plain `Sequential`. Hand-writing the pipe is
the only remaining option, hence this issue.

title: [Bug] Hand-written AIC/AIV cross-core pipe deadlocks on device (AICPU 507018) even at minimal size
body:
## Background

In pypto-lib, a hand-written cross-core AIC/AIV software pipeline
(`@pl.program` + `@pl.function(type=FunctionType.AIC/.AIV)` + manual
`tpush_to_aiv` / `tpop_from_aic` / `tpush_to_aic` / `tpop_from_aiv` +
`pl.system.*_initialize_pipe`, dispatched with `pl.submit` inside `pl.cluster()`)
compiles cleanly but **hangs on device**: AICPU 507018 / scheduler timeout. It
deadlocks even for the most trivial possible pipe — one tile each way, no loop.

Reproduce with:

    python probe_manual_pipe.py -p a2a3 -d 1

Reproduction environment:

| Component | Version |
|---|---|
| pypto-lib | `fae6826` (branch: `main`) |
| pypto | `869d5b65` (branch: `main`) + the 2-site `Submit` codegen fix from #2096 |
| simpler | `a756969c` (branch: `detached`) |
| ptoas | `0.48` |
| pto-isa | `83d01313` |
| CANN | not detected |

All four components match their pins. **The codegen fix from #2096 must be applied
for this repro to compile at all** — without it the `pl.submit` form fails in
orchestration codegen.

Diagnosis: **pypto** (possibly simpler) — the AIC and AIV halves of a cluster do
not appear to be co-scheduled as a pair; one whole side runs to completion while
the other never pairs with it.

### Component

Codegen

### Description

A minimal hand-written cross-core pipe deadlocks on device. The two halves
exchange exactly one tile in each direction:

- AIC: `matmul` → `tpush_to_aiv(score)` → `tpop_from_aiv(probs)` → `matmul` → `tpush_to_aiv(pv)`
- AIV: `tpop_from_aic(score)` → `exp` → `tpush_to_aic(probs)` → `tpop_from_aic(pv)` → `store`

Every `tpop` is matched by a `tfree`, each side does its own ring setup
(`reserve_buffer` for the direction it receives + `import_peer_buffer` for the peer
+ `aic/aiv_initialize_pipe(dir_mask=3, slot_size=8192)`), and `slot_num` is left at
the default (the GM workspace assumes 4 slots for `dir_mask=3`, so overriding it is
itself fatal). The FIFO order of pushes and pops matches on both sides.

The scheduler report is the informative part: **one entire side's tasks complete
while the other side has 1 running-stalled task and the rest never start.** With
8 tasks (16 total AIC+AIV):

```
completed=8/16  running=1  ready=0  waiting=7
```

and with 128 tasks (385 total) the same shape:

```
completed=257/385  running=1  ready=0  waiting=127
```

In both cases exactly one half of the pairs finishes and the other half is stuck,
which is what you would expect if the AIC and AIV kernels are dispatched as two
independent tasks rather than a co-scheduled cluster pair — the survivors run,
their partners never get a peer to rendezvous with, and the blocking `tpop`s hang.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Apply the `Submit` codegen fix from #2096 (otherwise this does not compile).
2. Build the minimal two-core program below and run it on a real device.

```python
@pl.program
class ManualPipeProg:
    @pl.function(type=pl.FunctionType.AIC)
    def cube_side(self, q, kk, vv, sink: pl.InOut[...], task: pl.Scalar[pl.INDEX]):
        v2c = pl.system.reserve_buffer(name="probe_v2c", size=32768, base=0)
        c2v_imp = pl.system.import_peer_buffer(name="probe_c2v", peer_func="vec_side")
        pl.system.aic_initialize_pipe(c2v_imp, v2c, dir_mask=3, slot_size=8192)

        q_l = pl.tile.move(pl.load(q, [task*M,0],[M,K], target_memory=pl.MemorySpace.Mat),
                           target_memory=pl.MemorySpace.Left)
        k_r = pl.tile.move(pl.tile.transpose_view(
                  pl.load(kk, [task*NB,0],[NB,K], target_memory=pl.MemorySpace.Mat)),
                  target_memory=pl.MemorySpace.Right)
        pl.tile.tpush_to_aiv(pl.matmul(q_l, k_r, out_dtype=pl.FP32), split=0)

        p = pl.tile.tpop_from_aiv(shape=[M, K], dtype=pl.BF16, split=0)
        p_l = pl.tile.move(p, target_memory=pl.MemorySpace.Left)
        v_r = pl.tile.move(pl.load(vv, [task*NB,0],[NB,K], target_memory=pl.MemorySpace.Mat),
                           target_memory=pl.MemorySpace.Right)
        o = pl.matmul(p_l, v_r, out_dtype=pl.FP32)
        pl.system.tfree_to_aiv(p, split=0)
        pl.tile.tpush_to_aiv(o, split=0)
        return sink

    @pl.function(type=pl.FunctionType.AIV)
    def vec_side(self, out: pl.Out[...], task: pl.Scalar[pl.INDEX]):
        c2v = pl.system.reserve_buffer(name="probe_c2v", size=32768, base=0)
        v2c_imp = pl.system.import_peer_buffer(name="probe_v2c", peer_func="cube_side")
        pl.system.aiv_initialize_pipe(c2v, v2c_imp, dir_mask=3, slot_size=8192)

        s = pl.tile.tpop_from_aic(shape=[M, K], dtype=pl.FP32, split=0)
        p = pl.exp(s)
        pl.system.tfree_to_aic(s, split=0)
        pl.tile.tpush_to_aic(pl.cast(p, target_type=pl.BF16, mode="rint"), split=0)

        o = pl.tile.tpop_from_aic(shape=[M, K], dtype=pl.FP32, split=0)
        ret = pl.store(o, [task*M, 0], out)
        pl.system.tfree_to_aic(o, split=0)
        return ret

    @pl.function(type=pl.FunctionType.Orchestration)
    def main(self, q, kk, vv, sink, out):
        for t in pl.parallel(N):          # N = 8
            with pl.cluster():
                sink, _ = pl.submit(self.cube_side, q, kk, vv, sink, t)
                out, _  = pl.submit(self.vec_side, out, t)
        return out
```

### Expected Behavior

The AIC and AIV halves of each cluster run concurrently on a paired cube/vector
core, rendezvous through the ring, and the program completes.

### Actual Behavior

Device hang, force reset required:

```
ERROR sync_run_streams: aclrtSynchronizeStreamWithTimeout (AICPU) failed: 507018
ERROR recover_device_or_mark_unusable: AICore error 507018: bounded device drain failed: 507014
ERROR validate_runtime_impl: PTO2 runtime failed: orch_error_code=0 sched_error_code=100 runtime_status=-100
ERROR validate_runtime_impl: PTO2 scheduler timeout sub_class=S1:running-stalled (detail=1)
      completed=8/16 running=1 ready=0 waiting=7 orch_done=1 stuck_task_id=8589934593 stuck_core=1
```

Notes narrowing it down:

- Not the pipeline logic: this is a single round-trip with no loop and no carried
  state; push/pop FIFO order matches on both sides.
- Not the dispatch form: replacing `pl.submit` with direct calls (which compiles
  without the companion fix) deadlocks with an identical signature.
- Not ring capacity: `slot_num` is left at the default 4 for `dir_mask=3`.
  (Overriding it to 8 also deadlocks, which is expected since the GM workspace is
  sized from `GetGMPipeSlotCount` — perhaps worth rejecting that override loudly.)
- Scales consistently: 8 tasks → `completed=8/16`, 128 tasks → `completed=257/385`;
  always exactly one side done, the other stuck.

### Git Commit ID

869d5b6518ea816f43769a8e3ab22831b0b214f4

### NPU Kind

Ascend 910B

### Host Platform

Linux (aarch64)

### Additional Context

Related: #2096 (blocks this repro from compiling at all), #1789 (also a 507018 deadlock in a cross-core kernel, but from
`EVENT_ID` reallocation in the auto-split fused form rather than manual
orchestration).

Motivation: the auto-split (`@pl.jit`) form ties the vector→cube `tpush` and the
cube-side `tpop` to a single DSL site, so the softmax→P@V→rescale leg of a
flash-attention decode kernel gets zero skew — an msprof in-core trace shows
CUBE(matmul) and VECTOR(compute) overlapping **0% of the span** (61us makespan vs
~38us if the two cores actually pipelined). `SkewCrossCorePipeline` demotes such a
loop (genuine tile carry `m`/`l`/`o`, multiple round-trips) to `Sequential`, so
hand-writing the pipe is the only way to skew both legs — which is what this issue
blocks.

title: [Code Health] Reject any pl.split(...) optimization on a scope carrying pl.split_aiv regions

labels.name: code health
labels.description: Technical debt, robustness concerns, code quality improvements

body:
### Category

Missing Validation

### Component

Passes / Transforms

### Description

A scope can currently carry **both** AIV-split annotations at once — a function-level
`optimizations=[pl.split(...)]` **and** a `pl.split_aiv(...)` region — provided the
function-level mode is `SplitMode.NONE`. These are two different mechanisms for
partitioning work across the two AIV sub-cores, and a scope should carry at most one.

The guard that exists already says as much in its own message ("these are mutually
exclusive AIV-split mechanisms"), but its predicate exempts `None`:

```cpp
// include/pypto/ir/transforms/utils/scope_outline_utils.h:918
CHECK_SPAN(!(incore_split.has_value() && incore_split.value() != SplitMode::None), op->span_)
    << "scope combines a function-level pl.split(...) (optimizations=[pl.split(...)]) with "
       "pl.split_aiv region(s); these are mutually exclusive AIV-split mechanisms. ...";
```

This is **weaker than the RFC it implements**. RFC #1820 specifies the frontend should
"Reject `n != 2`, loop kwargs (`init_values/chunk/stage/deps`), and a scope that also
carries `optimizations=[pl.split(...)]`" — with no mode qualifier.

Net effect: `pl.split(pl.SplitMode.NONE, slot_num=N)` + `pl.split_aiv(2, mode=UP_DOWN)`
compiles today. It reads to an author as "auto and manual split mixed on one scope" even
though the semantics are actually fine (`NONE` means *no* auto split, so there is nothing
to conflict with). The confusion is real and worth closing.

**Why the exemption is there.** `slot_num` — the cube→vector ring depth — has no home of
its own. `Split` is the only `Optimization` subclass (`optimizations.py` exports exactly
`["Optimization", "Split", "split"]`), so a kernel that wants a non-default ring depth
*must* name a split mode it does not want. Its docstring already concedes the two are
orthogonal: *"Valid with any `mode`, including `SplitMode.NONE`: ... `slot_num` sizes that
ring regardless of split mode."*

**Evidence that `mode=NONE` is vestigial in this position.** Three variants of the same
manual-split kernel (a fused mixed cube+vector scope whose epilogue is halved by an
explicit `pl.split_aiv(2, mode=UP_DOWN)` region):

| `optimizations=` | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `[pl.split(NONE, slot_num=4)]` | compiles |
| `[pl.split(NONE)]` | `Function 'score_aiv': Vec buffer usage (312576 bytes) exceeds platform limit (188416 bytes)` |
| *omitted entirely* | `Function 'score_aiv': Vec buffer usage (312576 bytes) exceeds platform limit (188416 bytes)` |
| `[pl.split(UP_DOWN, slot_num=4)]` | correctly rejected by the guard above |

Dropping the annotation entirely and keeping `pl.split(NONE)` fail at the same pass with
the **same byte count** — so `mode=NONE` contributes nothing. Only `slot_num` is
load-bearing (it shrinks the ring from the PTOAS default of 8 slots to 4).

### Location

```markdown
- `include/pypto/ir/transforms/utils/scope_outline_utils.h:918` — the `!= SplitMode::None` exemption
- `python/pypto/language/optimizations.py:36-86` — `Split` is the only `Optimization`, so `slot_num` has no other carrier
```

### Proposed Fix

Two steps, in order — the second cannot land alone without breaking every manual-split
kernel that needs a non-default ring depth.

**1. Give `slot_num` its own `Optimization` entry**, since it is orthogonal to splitting:

```python
# now — mode is vestigial, reads as auto+manual mixed
optimizations=[pl.split(pl.SplitMode.NONE, slot_num=4)]

# proposed — unambiguously manual
optimizations=[pl.c2v_ring(slot_num=4)]
```

`pl.split(mode, slot_num=...)` can keep accepting `slot_num` as a deprecated alias so
existing kernels keep working.

**2. Drop the `!= SplitMode::None` qualifier**, matching RFC #1820:

```cpp
CHECK_SPAN(!incore_split.has_value(), op->span_) << "...";
```

The three states then read distinctly: `pl.split(mode)` = auto, `pl.split_aiv(...)` =
manual, `pl.c2v_ring(...)` = neither, just pipe sizing.

### Priority

Medium (minor risk, should fix in next few releases)

### Additional Context

Found while converting the DeepSeek-V4 decode-indexer `score` scope to the explicit
manual `pl.split_aiv` form. Minimal shape of the accepted-today combination:

```python
for unit in pl.spmd(N, name_hint="score",
                    optimizations=[pl.split(pl.SplitMode.NONE, slot_num=4)]):   # annotation 1
    ...
    acc = pl.matmul(kv_i8_mat, qr_full, out_dtype=pl.INT32, b_trans=True)
    for aiv_id in pl.split_aiv(2, mode=pl.SplitMode.UP_DOWN):                   # annotation 2
        acc_h = pl.aiv_shard(acc)
        ...
```

Related: #1820 (the RFC specifying the rejection), #2006 (`SplitMode.NONE` behaviour).
