Narrowing `target`/`signal` to `DistributedTensor` was tried and reverted after it broke `pyright` on two legitimate call sites in `tests/ut/codegen/distributed/test_distributed_pto_codegen.py` (`test_tensor_view_preserves_loop_carried_distributed_metadata`, `test_tensor_view_preserves_while_carried_distributed_metadata`, lines ~960/980):

```python
for _i, (carried,) in pl.range(1, init_values=(data,)):
    result = pl.yield_(carried)
viewed = pl.tensor.view(result, [16, 16])
pld.system.wait(viewed, offsets=[0, 0], expected=1, cmp=pld.WaitCmp.Eq)
```

Here `data` is a `pld.DistributedTensor[[16, 16], pl.INT32]`. `pl.tensor.view` correctly preserves the input type via a `TypeVar`, so `viewed`'s static type is only as precise as `result`'s. But the loop-carry/yield machinery (`pl.range` / `pl.while_` / `pl.yield_`) does not currently propagate `DistributedTensor`-ness through the carried value — `result` is statically typed as plain `Tensor` even though the actual IR value is a distributed tensor (which is exactly why the C++ deducer accepts it at runtime today).

## Scope

Two related fixes, either or both:

1. Make `pl.range` / `pl.while_` / `pl.yield_`'s static typing DistributedTensor-aware for loop-carried values (likely a `TypeVar`-based overload on the loop-carry helpers, matching the pattern already used by `pl.tensor.view`).
2. Once (1) lands, narrow `notify`/`wait`'s `target`/`signal` parameters from `Tensor` to `DistributedTensor` in `system_ops.py`.

This is a cross-layer, behavior-visible typing change (affects what pyright accepts) — per `.claude/rules/cross-layer-sync.md`, better as its own PR than bundled into a docs-only change.

## Affected files

- `python/pypto/language/distributed/op/system_ops.py` (`notify`, `wait`)
- `python/pypto/language/op/tensor_ops.py` (`view`, for comparison — already TypeVar-correct)
- Loop-carry typing: wherever `pl.range` / `pl.while_` / `pl.yield_` are typed (likely `python/pypto/language/op/control_flow.py` or similar — needs investigation)

title: [Bug] Orchestration verification fails when passing a rebound DistributedTensor
body:
### Component

Codegen

### Description

After MaterializeDistTensorCtx, orchestration functions that thread DistributedTensor context can contain synthesized `pld.system.*` ops such as `pld.system.get_comm_ctx`. However, `IsBuiltinOp()` in [`pypto/src/ir/transforms/utils/op_predicates.cpp`](https://github.com/hw-native-sys/pypto/blob/bd4f3563c818dc995977d4631aab461a15f02426/src/ir/transforms/utils/op_predicates.cpp#L72) currently only recognizes these prefixes as builtins: `tile.`, `tensor.`,  `system.` `array.`
It does not treat `pld.system.*` as builtin, even though those ops are registered IR builtins and are introduced by passes.

As a result, transformed IR like this:
```python
@pl.function(type=pl.FunctionType.Orchestration, level=pl.Level.CHIP, role=pl.Role.Orchestrator)
def chip_orch(self, signal__ssa_v0: ..., signal_ctx: pld.CommCtxType) -> ...:
    signal__ssa_v1 = self.func_1(signal__ssa_v0, signal_ctx, attrs={...})
    signal_ctx_1: pld.CommCtxType = pld.system.get_comm_ctx(signal__ssa_v1)
    signal__ssa_v2 = self.func_2(signal__ssa_v1, signal_ctx_1, attrs={...})
    return signal__ssa_v2
```
contains a builtin `pld.system.get_comm_ctx(...)` call that `IsBuiltinOp()` misclassifies as non-builtin / user-level.
This can confuse downstream transforms/utilities that use `IsBuiltinOp()` to distinguish builtin ops from user calls.

### Proposed Fix

Extend `IsBuiltinOp()` (https://github.com/hw-native-sys/pypto/blob/bd4f3563c818dc995977d4631aab461a15f02426/src/ir/transforms/utils/op_predicates.cpp#L72) to include the distributed system prefix:
```cpp
return op_name.rfind("tile.", 0) == 0 || op_name.rfind("tensor.", 0) == 0 ||
       op_name.rfind("system.", 0) == 0 || op_name.rfind("array.", 0) == 0 ||
       op_name.rfind("pld.tile.", 0) == 0 || op_name.rfind("pld.tensor.", 0) == 0 ||
       op_name.rfind("pld.system.", 0) == 0;
```

### Steps to Reproduce

```markdown
python orch_verf_failed.py -p a2a3 -d 0,1


[orch_verf_failed.py](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/30587160/orch_verf_failed.py)
```

### Expected Behavior

Should run normally. And verification can pass for this case:
```
    @pl.function(type=pl.FunctionType.Orchestration, level=pl.Level.CHIP, role=pl.Role.Orchestrator)
    def chip_orch(
        self, signal__ssa_v0: pl.InOut[pld.DistributedTensor[[2, 1], pl.INT32, pl.MemRef("mem_ddr_0", pl.const(0, pl.INT64), 8)]], signal_ctx: pld.CommCtxType
    ) -> pld.DistributedTensor[[2, 1], pl.INT32]:
        signal__ssa_v1: pld.DistributedTensor[[2, 1], pl.INT32, pl.MemRef("mem_ddr_1", pl.const(0, pl.INT64), 8)] = self.func_1(
            signal__ssa_v0, signal_ctx, attrs={"arg_directions": [pl.adir.inout, pl.adir.scalar]}
        )
        signal_ctx_1: pld.CommCtxType = pld.system.get_comm_ctx(signal__ssa_v1)
        signal__ssa_v2: pld.DistributedTensor[[2, 1], pl.INT32, pl.MemRef("mem_ddr_2", pl.const(0, pl.INT64), 8)] = self.func_2(
            signal__ssa_v1, signal_ctx_1, attrs={"arg_directions": [pl.adir.inout, pl.adir.scalar]}
        )
        return signal__ssa_v2
```

### Actual Behavior

```
  Function   | Error
  -----------+--------------------------------------------------------------
  chip_orch  | Verification failed after 'GenerateOrchestration
             | preconditions' for properties {SplitIncoreOrch,
             | OrchestrationReferencesResolved, RuntimeScopesMaterialized,
             | ReturnParamsExplicit, IterArgCarryClassified}:
  -----------+--------------------------------------------------------------
```

### Git Commit ID

bd4f3563c818dc995977d4631aab461a15f02426

### NPU Kind

N/A (not hardware-specific)

### Host Platform

Linux (x86_64)

### Additional Context

_No response_

title: Ring allreduce: unaligned-data handling (dcci flush tail + 32B transfer alignment)
body:
Two alignment gaps in the ring allreduce kernel template that the mesh allreduce kernel already handles but the ring kernel currently does not.

### 1. dcci flush loop misses the chunk tail

**File:** `python/pypto/runtime/builtins/collectives/allreduce_ring/templates/kernel.cpp.in`

The dcci flush loop in both the Reduce-Scatter and AllGather phases steps by 16 elements (`i += 16`), which only covers the full chunk when `chunk_elems % 16 == 0`. Compile-time validation only guarantees `numel % NR == 0`, so a tail cache-line spanning the chunk end goes unflushed.

**Counter-example:** `numel = 18, NR = 2` → `chunk_elems = 9` (36 bytes). Chunk 1 starts at byte 36 and spans two cache lines; the 16-element stride misses the second one.

### 2. 32-byte transfer alignment is missing

The mesh allreduce kernel explicitly rounds ragged spans up to `kTransferAlignmentBytes` = 32 bytes (in `collectives/allreduce/templates/kernel.cpp.in`), aligning `tile_elems` to avoid partial-vector load/store. The ring kernel feeds `tile_elems` raw into `ShapeDyn` / `StrideDyn` with no such rounding.

### 3. `kRecvTileDebugValue` rename

The constant name at the top of the kernel reads like leftover debug scaffolding. The `TASSIGN` call is legitimate (it binds `recv_tile` to its buffer as a placeholder, overwritten by the subsequent `TLOAD`), but the constant should be renamed to something like `kRecvTileInitFill` with a one-line comment.

### Suggested approach

- Extract a shared alignment helper used by both mesh and ring kernel templates.
- For the dcci flush: step by 16 elements but emit one additional flush for the final partial cache-line.
- Add an ST case where `chunk_elems % 16 != 0` (e.g. `numel=18, NR=2`).
- Rename `kRecvTileDebugValue` → `kRecvTileInitFill`.

### Context

Raised in review of PR #2094 by @YunjiQin.

title: [Feature] Allow pl.aiv_shard on a vector-produced Vec tile so a per-lane scattered gather_row can be expressed inside pl.split_aiv
body:
## Background In pypto-lib, `models/deepseek/v4-flash/decode_sparse_attn.py` (`qk_pv`) on `a2a3` has a **compile** problem: there is no way to express, at tensor level, "the two AIV lanes each gather half of a scattered row set into UB, then hand the assembled tile to the cube as a matmul B-operand". `qk_pv` assembles each `[ATTN_K_TILE, HEAD_DIM]` sparse KV tile with 128 single-row `pl.gather_row` calls on the **cube**. Measured on 910B1, the cube's per-row `GM->L1` ND2NZ sustains only ~3.5 scattered 1 KB loads in flight (~21 us for the tile) while a vector lane reaches ~13 (~5 us), and `qk_pv` is 73% MTE2-occupied while its two AIV lanes idle at ~7%. Moving the gather to the AIV lanes is worth ~4% end-to-end on the layer. That works today only via a GM staging buffer plus hand-written `pl.system.set_ffts` + `sync_set`/`sync_wait` (the author-side barrier that #1911 describes). The tensor-level `split_aiv` + `aic_gather` formulation, which needs neither, is blocked. Reproduce with: python repro_aiv_shard_gather_row.py --fix 0 # the original rejection python repro_aiv_shard_gather_row.py --fix 1 # "derive from aiv_shard" python repro_aiv_shard_gather_row.py --fix 3 # "let the implicit path halve it" The repro case is **not committed** — save the file below at the pypto-lib repo root to run it. Files required: `repro_aiv_shard_gather_row.py` (self-contained; imports only `pypto.language` and pypto-lib's `golden` harness).
Reproduction case — repro_aiv_shard_gather_row.py (save at the pypto-lib repo root) ```python """Repro: no tensor-level way to split a scattered GM->UB gather across the two AIV lanes. Goal: the two AIV lanes each gather half of a scattered row set into UB, then the assembled [ROWS, HEAD_DIM] tile is handed to the cube as a matmul B-operand. The scattered row indices are runtime values (a paged KV top-k list), so the gather must accept arbitrary per-row source offsets. `pl.paged_gather(space=Vec)` is the only tensor-level op that produces a UB-backed Tensor, but it cannot be given a per-lane sub-range of the index list: * a sliced index tensor (static or dynamic) -> "indices must be TensorType" * a pl.aiv_shard(...) result -> "indices must be TensorType" * a [2, n/2] per-lane layout -> "requires 2D indices to have shape [1, n]" `pl.gather_row` does take arbitrary runtime offsets, and `pl.full` gives it a UB-backed Tensor accumulator. But putting that inside `pl.split_aiv` is rejected, and each of the three fixes LowerAutoVectorSplit suggests is itself blocked. Run each variant from the pypto-lib repo root: python repro_aiv_shard_gather_row.py --fix 0 # the original rejection python repro_aiv_shard_gather_row.py --fix 1 # "derive from aiv_shard" python repro_aiv_shard_gather_row.py --fix 3 # "let the implicit path halve it" """ import pypto.language as pl POOL_ROWS = 16384 HEAD_DIM = 512 ROWS = 128 HALF = ROWS // 2 Q_ROWS = 16 @pl.jit def fix0_half_extent( pool: pl.Tensor[[POOL_ROWS, HEAD_DIM], pl.BF16], idx: pl.Tensor[[ROWS], pl.INT32], q: pl.Tensor[[Q_ROWS, HEAD_DIM], pl.BF16], out: pl.Out[pl.Tensor[[Q_ROWS, ROWS], pl.FP32]], ): """Half-extent UB accumulator; the gather's SOURCE offset references aiv.""" with pl.at(level=pl.Level.CORE_GROUP, name_hint="fix0", allow_early_resolve=True): for aiv in pl.split_aiv(2, mode=pl.SplitMode.UP_DOWN): ub = pl.full([HALF, HEAD_DIM], dtype=pl.BF16, value=0.0) for k in pl.range(HALF): src = pl.cast(pl.read(idx, [aiv * HALF + k]), pl.INDEX) ub = pl.gather_row(ub, pool, [k, 0], [src, 0], [1, HEAD_DIM]) kv = pl.aic_gather(ub) out[0:Q_ROWS, 0:ROWS] = pl.matmul(q, kv, b_trans=True, out_dtype=pl.FP32) return out @pl.jit def fix1_aiv_shard( pool: pl.Tensor[[POOL_ROWS, HEAD_DIM], pl.BF16], idx: pl.Tensor[[ROWS], pl.INT32], q: pl.Tensor[[Q_ROWS, HEAD_DIM], pl.BF16], out: pl.Out[pl.Tensor[[Q_ROWS, ROWS], pl.FP32]], ): """Fix (1): derive the accumulator from a pl.aiv_shard result.""" with pl.at(level=pl.Level.CORE_GROUP, name_hint="fix1", allow_early_resolve=True): for aiv in pl.split_aiv(2, mode=pl.SplitMode.UP_DOWN): ub_full = pl.full([ROWS, HEAD_DIM], dtype=pl.BF16, value=0.0) ub = pl.aiv_shard(ub_full) for k in pl.range(HALF): src = pl.cast(pl.read(idx, [aiv * HALF + k]), pl.INDEX) ub = pl.gather_row(ub, pool, [k, 0], [src, 0], [1, HEAD_DIM]) kv = pl.aic_gather(ub) out[0:Q_ROWS, 0:ROWS] = pl.matmul(q, kv, b_trans=True, out_dtype=pl.FP32) return out @pl.jit def fix3_implicit( pool: pl.Tensor[[POOL_ROWS, HEAD_DIM], pl.BF16], idx: pl.Tensor[[ROWS], pl.INT32], q: pl.Tensor[[Q_ROWS, HEAD_DIM], pl.BF16], out: pl.Out[pl.Tensor[[Q_ROWS, ROWS], pl.FP32]], ): """Fix (3): no explicit boundary ops; both offsets reference the lane index.""" with pl.at(level=pl.Level.CORE_GROUP, name_hint="fix3", allow_early_resolve=True): for aiv in pl.split_aiv(2, mode=pl.SplitMode.UP_DOWN): ub = pl.full([ROWS, HEAD_DIM], dtype=pl.BF16, value=0.0) for k in pl.range(HALF): src = pl.cast(pl.read(idx, [aiv * HALF + k]), pl.INDEX) ub = pl.gather_row(ub, pool, [aiv * HALF + k, 0], [src, 0], [1, HEAD_DIM]) kv = ub out[0:Q_ROWS, 0:ROWS] = pl.matmul(q, kv, b_trans=True, out_dtype=pl.FP32) return out VARIANTS = {0: fix0_half_extent, 1: fix1_aiv_shard, 3: fix3_implicit} def golden(tensors): tensors["out"][:] = ( tensors["q"].float() @ tensors["pool"][tensors["idx"].long()].float().t() ).to(tensors["out"].dtype) def build_tensor_specs(): import torch from golden import TensorSpec return [ TensorSpec("pool", [POOL_ROWS, HEAD_DIM], torch.bfloat16, init_value=lambda: torch.randn(POOL_ROWS, HEAD_DIM)), TensorSpec("idx", [ROWS], torch.int32, init_value=lambda: ((torch.arange(ROWS, dtype=torch.int64) * 977) % (POOL_ROWS - ROWS)).to(torch.int32)), TensorSpec("q", [Q_ROWS, HEAD_DIM], torch.bfloat16, init_value=lambda: torch.randn(Q_ROWS, HEAD_DIM) / HEAD_DIM ** 0.5), TensorSpec("out", [Q_ROWS, ROWS], torch.float32, is_output=True), ] if __name__ == "__main__": import argparse from golden import run_jit parser = argparse.ArgumentParser() parser.add_argument("--fix", type=int, default=0, choices=sorted(VARIANTS)) parser.add_argument("-p", "--platform", type=str, default="a2a3") parser.add_argument("-d", "--device", type=int, default=0) args = parser.parse_args() result = run_jit( fn=VARIANTS[args.fix], specs=build_tensor_specs(), golden_fn=golden, runtime_cfg=dict(platform=args.platform, device_id=args.device), rtol=1e-2, atol=1e-2, ) print("PASS" if result.passed else f"FAIL {result.error}") ```
Reproduction environment: | Component | Version | |---|---| | pypto-lib | `14f3863` (branch: `perf/assemble-swa-decode-window-in-l1-drop-gm-gather`) | | pypto | `6234d0e9` (branch: `main`) | | simpler | `9922afdb` (detached) | | ptoas | `0.54` | | pto-isa | `83d01313` | | CANN | `8.5.1` (runs), `8.3.RC1.alpha003` at `ascend-toolkit/latest` | Version mismatch (off pinned): **simpler** expected `dccb8379080b43173744b9981de2542b3d025e19`, actual `9922afdb08cc6f203eaf39328661e2f2648d333d`. This is a **compile-time** failure in `LowerAutoVectorSplit` / `ConvertTensorToTileOps`; simpler is the runtime and takes no part in those passes, so the divergence is not believed to affect the result. ptoas and pto-isa are on their pins. Diagnosis: **pypto** — all three failures are raised by pypto compiler passes and verifiers. ### Summary `pl.gather_row` is the only op that gathers scattered GM rows at arbitrary **runtime** offsets, and `pl.full` is the only tensor-level way to give it a UB-backed `Tensor` accumulator. That pair cannot be placed inside a `pl.split_aiv` region: `LowerAutoVectorSplit` classifies `tile.gather_row` as full-width and names three fixes, and **each of the three is independently blocked**. | variant | what it does | result | |---|---|---| | `--fix 0` | half-extent `pl.full`, gather's **source** offset references `aiv_id`, `aic_gather` | `LowerAutoVectorSplit: a pl.split_aiv region mixes explicit tile.aiv_shard/tile.aic_gather boundary ops with plain full-width vector op(s) [tile.gather_row] ...` | | `--fix 1` | full-extent `pl.full` -> `pl.aiv_shard` -> gather -> `aic_gather` | `AivSplitValid`: *"'tile.aiv_shard' operand is in Vec, but it transfers a cube-produced value across the cross-core boundary and requires Acc. ... A Vec operand is vector-produced (pl.load / pl.full) and already lives on the AIV lane — drop the pl.aiv_shard and let the implicit affinity-gated split halve it."* | | `--fix 3` | full-extent `pl.full`, **both** offsets reference `aiv_id`, no boundary ops | `AllocatedMemoryAddr`: `Function 'fix3_aic': Mat buffer usage (1064960 bytes) exceeds platform limit (524288 bytes)` | Two observations: 1. In `--fix 0` the gather's **source** offset already references `aiv_id`, which is what fix (2) asks for ("an op whose arguments reference `aiv_id` is per-lane by construction and is accepted"). It is still rejected — the check appears to consider only the destination/accumulator, not the source. 2. Fix (1) is not applicable to this shape at all: `aiv_shard` is specified for a **cube-produced** (`Acc`) value crossing C2V, but the accumulator here is vector-produced (`Vec`). The diagnostic itself redirects to fix (3), which then overflows L1. The net effect is that a per-lane scattered gather has no tensor-level spelling, and the only working formulation is a GM staging buffer with hand-written `set_ffts` + `sync_set`/`sync_wait`. ### Motivation / Use Case DeepSeek-V4-Flash CSA decode. `qk_pv` is 29.7% of the layer's machine core-time and 73% MTE2-occupied on the cube, gathering 128 scattered 1 KB KV rows per tile; its AIV lanes are ~7% occupied. Micro-benchmarks on 910B1 (same binary, disjoint index sets, ordering-controlled): | path | us for one 128x512 BF16 tile | |---|---| | cube, 128 x `gather_row` (today) | 20.90 | | AIV pair, UB accumulate + coalesced store | 3.26 | The GM-staging workaround lands ~4% end-to-end on the layer, but it costs a 4 MB scratch buffer, triples the bytes moved (scattered read + write + read), and needs the manual barrier. `aic_gather` returning a `Tensor` in `Mat` — verified: with a `Tensor` input it returns `pl.Tensor[[256, 512], pl.BF16]` — would remove the staging buffer, the extra traffic, and the barrier in one step. ### Proposed API / Behavior Preferred (this is fix (1) made applicable): let **`pl.aiv_shard` accept a vector-produced `Vec` operand**, sharding a locally-built UB tile into per-lane halves. Today it is restricted to `Acc` (cube-produced, C2V). Accepting `Vec` would let a `pl.full` accumulator be sharded and then filled by per-lane `gather_row` calls, with `aic_gather` carrying the assembled tile to the cube: ```python for aiv in pl.split_aiv(2, mode=pl.SplitMode.UP_DOWN): ub = pl.aiv_shard(pl.full([ROWS, HEAD_DIM], dtype=pl.BF16, value=0.0)) # -> [ROWS/2, HEAD_DIM] for k in pl.range(ROWS // 2): src = pl.cast(pl.read(idx, [aiv * (ROWS // 2) + k]), pl.INDEX) ub = pl.gather_row(ub, pool, [k, 0], [src, 0], [1, HEAD_DIM]) kv = pl.aic_gather(ub) # -> [ROWS, HEAD_DIM] in Mat out = pl.matmul(q, kv, b_trans=True, out_dtype=pl.FP32) ``` Alternatives that would also unblock it: - **Honour fix (2) for DMA ops** — accept `tile.gather_row` as per-lane when *any* of its offsets (source included) references the region's lane index, not only the destination. - **Let `paged_gather` take a per-lane index range** — a sliced/sharded index tensor, or an explicit index-offset argument. Today `pl.paged_gather` is the only tensor-level op producing a UB `Tensor`, but it rejects a sliced index tensor (static *or* dynamic) with `indices must be TensorType`, rejects a `pl.aiv_shard` result with the same error, and rejects a `[2, n/2]` per-lane layout with `requires 2D indices to have shape [1, n], but got first dim 2`. Any one of these would make the `paged_gather` + `aic_gather` form work directly. ### Alternatives Considered - **GM staging + explicit barrier (what pypto-lib ships today).** The AIV lanes coalesce chunks into a GM scratch and the cube reloads them contiguously, ordered by `pl.system.set_ffts` + `sync_set(pipe=MTE3, core_type="aiv")` / `sync_wait(pipe=MTE2, core_type="aic")`. Correct and ~4% faster end-to-end, but needs a 4 MB scratch, triples bytes moved, and relies on the hand-written barrier that #1911 wants automated. Without the barrier the kernel passes 9/9 uninstrumented runs and fails 3/3 under `--enable-l2-swimlane 1` — a silent race, exactly the failure mode #1911 describes. - **Rewrite the qk_pv consumer chain at tile level.** `pl.tile.gather_row` accepts a `Vec` destination and arbitrary runtime offsets, so a `create_tile` + `tile.gather_row` + `aic_gather` chain works — but `aic_gather` then returns a `Tile`, and `pl.matmul` rejects mixed `Tensor`/`Tile` operands, so the whole QK/softmax/PV chain (~25 lines) has to move to tile level. Possible today; avoided because it makes the kernel materially harder to read for what should be an operand-plumbing detail. ### Additional Context Related: - #1911 — auto-fence AIV->AIC (V2C) GM read-after-write. The barrier this issue is trying to avoid needing is exactly the one #1911 proposes to automate; the shipped pypto-lib workaround is the "status quo" alternative listed there. - #2203 — `LowerAutoVectorSplit` halves a vector op's result without sharding its full-width operand. Same pass, adjacent defect family (that one is about elementwise ops with un-sharded operands; this one is about a DMA op being classified full-width). - #1820 — RFC for the explicit `pl.split_aiv` + `aiv_shard`/`aic_gather` DSL this issue exercises. - #2130 — `pl.pipeline` cannot generate skewed cross-core schedules without manual `sync_set`/`sync_wait`. Consistent with what was measured here: `pl.pipeline(stage=2)` over the staging chunks gave no overlap (349.8 vs 348.8 us) because the manual per-chunk handover already serialises the pair. - #2006 — `pl.split_aiv(2, SplitMode.NONE)` silently drops half the work. Measurements above are from 910B1, CANN 8.5.1, `--start-pos 8192`, `B=4 S=2 T=8`.

title: [Feature] Allow pl.MemRef on reshape-derived intermediate tiles (row-vector softmax terms)
body:
## Background In pypto-lib, tuning `models/qwen3/14b/bench_attention_swpipe_best_performance.py` (decode attention) on `a2a3`, we use `pl.MemRef("name")` declared allocations to break false WAR dependencies that MemoryReuse introduces by folding independent tiles onto one buffer (this is the intended use of #2171, and it wins ~2.3% on the cube-side K/V loads). We then tried to apply the same fix on the **vector** side — pinning the online-softmax intermediates (`d = exp(m - hm)`, a `[16,1]` decay column vector) so MTE2's next score load stops waiting on the vector reading the current one. This is rejected at trace time. Reproduce with: python repro_memref_intermediate.py -p a2a3sim The repro case is **not committed** — save the file below and run it.
Reproduction case — repro_memref_intermediate.py ```python """Minimal repro: pl.MemRef on a reshape-derived intermediate tile is rejected. The online-softmax decay d = exp(m - hm) is a [N,1] column vector; sub reshapes its operands, so exp(...) lands in its source tile's allocation and cannot be given its own buffer — even though pinning it is exactly how you'd break a false WAR that serialises the vector pipe.""" import pypto.language as pl import torch from golden import TensorSpec, run_jit N, K = 16, 128 @pl.jit def probe(x: pl.Tensor[[N, K], pl.FP32], out: pl.Out[pl.Tensor[[N, K], pl.FP32]]) -> pl.Tensor[[N, K], pl.FP32]: for _t in pl.spmd(1, name_hint="probe"): tmp = pl.create_tile([N, K], dtype=pl.FP32, target_memory=pl.MemorySpace.Vec) xt = pl.load(x, [0, 0], [N, K], target_memory=pl.MemorySpace.Vec) m = pl.row_max(xt, tmp) lm = pl.row_max(pl.tile.muls(xt, 0.5), tmp) hm = pl.maximum(lm, m) # We want d in its OWN Vec buffer to break the WAR against the next score # load. But exp(sub(...)) inherits its source (reshape) allocation: d: pl.Tile[[N, 1], pl.FP32, pl.MemRef("d_buf"), pl.Mem.Vec] = pl.exp(pl.sub(m, hm)) p = pl.exp(pl.row_expand_sub(xt, hm)) out = pl.store(pl.row_expand_mul(p, d), [0, 0], out) return out def main(): specs=[TensorSpec("x",[N,K],torch.float32,init_value=lambda:torch.randn([N,K])), TensorSpec("out",[N,K],torch.float32,is_output=True)] r=run_jit(fn=probe, specs=specs, golden_fn=None, runtime_cfg={"platform":"a2a3sim","device_id":0}, compile_only=True) print("passed=",r.passed) if __name__=="__main__": main() ```
Fails at trace time with: ``` ValueError: Tile 'd__ssa_v0' is produced by 'tile.reshape', which lands in its source tile's allocation, so it cannot be given one of its own. Bind the source tile instead. [repro_memref_intermediate.py:25:8] ``` Reproduction environment: | Component | Version | |---|---| | pypto-lib | `fd91568` (branch: main) | | pypto | `06fdbfc3` (branch: main) | | simpler | `9922afdb` | | ptoas | 0.54 | | pto-isa | `83d01313` | | CANN | not detected | Diagnosis: **pypto** — the `pl.MemRef` allocation binding (InitMemRef / MemoryReuse) refuses reshape-derived tiles. Related: pypto#2131, pypto#1475 (same family — false-dependency buffer folding), but distinct: this is a specific applicability gap in the #2171 `pl.MemRef` feature. ### Summary `pl.MemRef("name")` cannot be attached to a tile that is produced by a `tile.reshape` (i.e. any row/column-vector result of `sub` / `row_expand_*` / an `exp` fed by them). The error says "Bind the source tile instead", but the source is an anonymous reshape with no DSL-level name to annotate, so the guidance is not actionable. This blocks using `pl.MemRef` to break false WAR dependencies among the online-softmax column-vector intermediates (`lm`, `hm`, `d`, `m`, `l`) — exactly the terms whose buffer folding serialises the vector pipe. ### Motivation / Use Case `pl.MemRef` (#2171) is the sanctioned way to break MemoryReuse's false WAR folds. It works for full-width tiles produced by `load` / `exp(row_expand_sub(...))`, and gives real wins (cube-side K/V double-buffering, ~2.3% on qwen3-14b decode attn). But the online-softmax recurrence is dominated by `[N,1]` column-vector terms that are all reshape-derived, and those are precisely the ones MemoryReuse coalesces (one vec buffer held 22–26 tiles in our kernel). Being unable to pin them leaves a class of false vector-pipe dependencies with no user-level escape hatch, so the `pl.MemRef` win stops at the cube side. ### Proposed API / Behavior Allow `pl.MemRef` on a reshape-derived tile by giving the reshape *view* its own declared allocation (the reshape is a no-copy view; the request is to place the underlying storage in the named slot). If that is infeasible, at minimum make the diagnostic actionable: name the concrete source tile the user must bind, or accept the annotation on the reshape result and propagate it to the source alloc. ### Alternatives Considered - Binding the source: the "source" is an unnamed `pl.sub(...)` / `pl.reshape(...)` intermediate with no DSL variable to annotate. - Pinning only the full-width tiles we *can* pin (score, prob): verified — removes some V→MTE2 WAR flags (8→5) but not the column-vector folds, and does not move wall time in our case (those WARs happen to be masked by the cross-core QK_READY wait). The column-vector terms remain unaddressable.

title: [Feature] Allow pl.prefetch.async_prefetch to prefetch a sub-region (offset + size), not only a whole tensor
body:
### Summary

`pl.prefetch.async_prefetch(src, ctx)` can only prefetch a **whole** tensor: the IR
verifier requires `src` to be a `Var`/`IterArg` with a fully static shape that is
logically 1D (every dimension except the last must be 1), and codegen always emits a
`pto.partition_view` covering the entire tensor.

Please allow prefetching a **sub-region** — a base offset plus a length — so a caller
can warm only the slab it is about to consume.

### Motivation / Use Case

Trying `pl.prefetch` on the Qwen3-14B decode kernel (`models/qwen3/14b/decode_fwd.py`
in pypto-lib) showed the whole-tensor restriction makes the op inapplicable to the one
case it seems designed for — hiding weight-load latency behind unrelated compute.

**1. The region we want to warm is a slice, and slices are rejected.**
In the fused multi-layer decode, weights are stacked across layers: `wq` is
`[NUM_LAYERS * HIDDEN, HIDDEN]` = `[204800, 5120]` BF16 ≈ 2 GB, and layer `L` reads only
the row slab `wq[L*HIDDEN : (L+1)*HIDDEN, :]` (≈ 52 MB). There is no way to express that
slab: passing `wq[a:b, :]` fails with

```
prefetch.async_prefetch expects src to be a Var or IterArg
```

and passing `wq` itself fails with

```
prefetch.async_prefetch expects src to be a flat contiguous logical 1D GM region
(all dimensions except the last must be 1), but dimension 0 is 204800;
reshape the tensor to [N] or [1, ..., N] before prefetching
```

`pl.reshape(wq, [1, N])` is accepted, but it reshapes the *whole* tensor, so the only
thing that can be issued is a 2 GB prefetch — not what the layer needs.

**2. Whole-tensor is over L2 capacity even in the single-layer case.**
A2/A3 L2 is ~192 MB. One Qwen3-14B decode layer's weights total ≈ 660 MB
(wq 52 + wk 10.5 + wv 10.5 + wo 52 + w_gate 178 + w_up 178 + w_down 178 MB). Only the
smaller matrices fit, and the ones that dominate the memory traffic (`w_gate` / `w_up` /
`w_down`, 178 MB each) can never be prefetched whole. Sub-region prefetch would let a
kernel warm a tile-sized window that actually fits and actually stays resident.

**3. The underlying SDMA path already takes a base pointer and a length.**
This looks like a PyPTO-side restriction rather than a hardware or PTO-ISA one:

- pto-isa's `SdmaCmoPrefetch(__gm__ uint8_t *src, uint64_t messageLen, ...)`
  (`include/pto/comm/async/sdma/sdma_cmo_intrin.hpp`) is already expressed as
  base + length, and `TPrefetchAsyncIsFlatContiguous1D` only needs the region to be
  one packed contiguous run;
- PyPTO codegen already builds a `pto.partition_view`, but hardcodes it to the whole
  tensor — `EmitWholeTensorPartitionView` in `src/backend/common/pto_ops_prefetch.cpp`
  fills `offset_codes` with zeros and `size_codes` with the full shape.

A row slab `w[a:b, :]` of a packed row-major tensor **is** a single flat contiguous run
(base `= data + a * row_stride`, length `= (b - a) * row_stride`), so presenting it as a
`[1, len]` partition view should satisfy the existing pto-isa check without any change
below PyPTO.

### Proposed API / Behavior

Either an explicit offset/size pair:

```python
ctx = pl.prefetch.make_context()
# Warm just layer L's slab of the stacked weight.
evt = pl.prefetch.async_prefetch(wq, ctx, offset=layer_idx * HIDDEN * HIDDEN, size=HIDDEN * HIDDEN)
pl.prefetch.wait(evt, pl.prefetch.session(ctx))
```

or accepting a contiguous slice expression directly:

```python
evt = pl.prefetch.async_prefetch(wq[layer_idx * HIDDEN : (layer_idx + 1) * HIDDEN, :], ctx)
```

Notes on what would make it usable for the decode case:

- **A dynamic offset matters.** In a layer loop the slab base is `layer_idx * stride`
  with `layer_idx` a loop induction variable, so the offset should be allowed to be a
  scalar expression. Only the *size* needs to be a compile-time constant (it is what
  sets the byte extent).
- Keeping the "one flat contiguous run" requirement for the resulting region is fine —
  a full-width row slab of a packed tensor already satisfies it. Rejecting a
  non-contiguous region (e.g. a column slice) at IR-construction time with the current
  style of message would be the right behavior.

### Alternatives Considered

- **`pl.reshape(w, [1, N])` then prefetch** — accepted by the verifier, but it can only
  express the whole tensor, which is either the wrong region (stacked multi-layer
  weights) or larger than L2 (single-layer `w_gate`/`w_up`/`w_down`).
- **Passing each layer's weight slab as its own kernel parameter** — would make the
  region static, but needs `NUM_LAYERS × 7` extra parameters (280 for Qwen3-14B) and
  gives up the stacked-weight layout the rest of the kernel depends on.
- **Doing nothing and relying on the natural MTE2 stream** — this is the current state;
  it is what the request is trying to improve on.

### Additional Context

Measured on device (a2a3), Qwen3-14B single decode layer, batch 16, seq 4096, task
makespan from the L2 swimlane. The prefetch is numerically transparent as documented
(the golden check passed in every configuration) — this is purely about placement and
cost:

| Config | prefetch task exec | layer makespan | vs baseline |
|---|---|---|---|
| baseline (no prefetch), 6 runs | — | 989 / 1024 / 1029 / 1034 / 1035 / 1072 µs | — |
| whole `wk` (10.5 MB) | 414 / 423 / 494 µs | 1291 / 1326 / 1384 µs | +29% |
| whole `wk` + `wv` (21 MB) | ~415 µs each | 1317 / 1342 µs | +29% |
| whole `wq` (52 MB) | 423 / 501 µs | 1331 / 1395 µs | +32% |
| whole `wo` (52 MB) | 456 µs | 1347 µs | +31% |

The form that is expressible today, for reference — a standalone head task that issues
the pull and waits, which nothing else depends on:

```python
wo_flat = pl.reshape(wo, [1, HIDDEN * HIDDEN])
with pl.at(level=pl.Level.CORE_GROUP, name_hint="prefetch_wo"):
    pf_ctx = pl.prefetch.make_context()
    pf_evt = pl.prefetch.async_prefetch(wo_flat, pf_ctx)
    pl.prefetch.wait(pf_evt, pl.prefetch.session(pf_ctx))
```

**A second, separable problem:** the prefetch task carries a large fixed cost that is
nearly independent of the transferred size, so even with sub-region support a small warm
would not pay for itself. Isolated microbenchmark (one prefetch task plus one trivial
task, per-task `Avg Exec` from the swimlane):

| prefetched bytes | task exec |
|---|---|
| 0.52 MB | 533.7 µs |
| 8.39 MB | 400.3 µs |
| 67.1 MB | 733.9 µs |
| 4 × 0.52 MB, concurrent tasks | 489–577 µs each |

Dropping the `pl.prefetch.wait` does not help (8.39 MB, no wait: 386.6 µs), so the cost
is on the issue path (`make_context` / `tprefetch_async`), not in the wait; and four
concurrent tasks each pay it, so it is per-task rather than one-time SDMA setup. For
scale, a whole Qwen3-14B decode layer is ~1030 µs. Happy to split this into its own
performance issue if you'd prefer to track it separately.

In this particular kernel the regression above has a second cause worth flagging: the
fused attention is a full-occupancy `pl.spmd(..., sync_start=True)` dispatch, so a
~0.5 ms prefetch task holding one AIV pushed its head overhead from 24.4 µs to 352.3 µs
while its exec time was unchanged (309 → 313 µs). That is a scheduling interaction, not a
prefetch defect, but it means a long-running hint task is expensive next to a
full-occupancy dispatch.

Environment for the measurements above:

| Component | Version |
|---|---|
| pypto-lib | `fd91568` (branch: `main`) |
| pypto | `06fdbfc3` (branch: `main`) |
| simpler | `9922afdb` (detached) |
| ptoas | `0.54` |
| pto-isa | `83d01313` |
| Host | Linux (aarch64) |

Related: #2075 (added the `pl.prefetch` frontend and introduced the flat-1D constraint),
#2166 (ST coverage tracker, batch B19 lists the flat-contiguous-1D limit as a constraint
to cover).

title: [Bug] Orchestration-level pl.assemble(atomic=Add) is silently dropped — the output tensor is never written
body:
### Component

Codegen

### Description

`pl.assemble(target, source, offset, atomic=pl.AtomicType.Add)` only has a lowering path when it sits **inside** a `pl.at(level=pl.Level.CORE_GROUP, ...)` scope, where it becomes a `tile.store` with the atomic attr and finally `pto.tstore {atomicType = #pto<atomic_type atomic_add>}`.

When the same call is written **outside** the scope (at the orchestration level), nothing lowers it and nothing rejects it. The compile succeeds, and the emitted orchestration C++ never writes the target tensor at all — the partial results go into per-iteration scratch buffers that are then discarded.

This is not merely "the atomic combine degrades to a plain overwrite": the destination is left completely untouched, so the kernel returns whatever was in the output buffer. Silent wrong results, no error, no warning.

Three layers each have a reason not to catch it:

| Layer | Location | Why it misses |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Op type deduction | `src/ir/op/tensor_ops/memory.cpp:413-434` | Validates the atomic enum and the target dtype, but at construction time both target and source are `TensorType` whether or not the call is inside a scope — this layer cannot distinguish the two cases. |
| Conversion registry | `src/ir/transforms/op_conversion_registry.cpp:496-542` | The tile→tile and tensor→tile branches both assert `!atomic_add`, but the tensor→tensor case falls through to the fallback at :539-542, which forwards `kwargs` unchanged. The registry also only runs on InCore functions, so an orchestration-level assemble never reaches it. |
| Orchestration codegen | `src/codegen/orchestration/orchestration_codegen.cpp:3803-3809` | `HandleTensorAssembleAssign` checks only `args_.size() == 3` and ignores kwargs entirely; it emits no write, just aliases the LHS emit name to the target. |

Note the codebase already treats "atomic must survive lowering" as an invariant elsewhere: `src/ir/transforms/fuse_create_assemble_to_slice_pass.cpp:80-84` explicitly refuses to fold an atomic assemble, with a comment stating that doing so "would degrade split-K accumulation to a plain write". This path is simply unguarded.

### Steps to Reproduce

The only difference from the working split-K pattern in `tests/ut/jit/test_split_k.py` is that the `pl.assemble` is dedented out of the `with pl.at(...)` block.

```python
import pypto.language as pl
import torch
from pypto import backend, ir
from pypto.backend import BackendType
from pypto.jit.decorator import jit

_M, _N, _K, _SPLIT = 64, 64, 512, 4
_KS = _K // _SPLIT

backend.reset_for_testing()
backend.set_backend_type(BackendType.Ascend910B)


@jit
def orch_atomic(a: pl.Tensor, b: pl.Tensor, c: pl.Out[pl.Tensor]):
    for ks in pl.parallel(0, _SPLIT):
        with pl.at(level=pl.Level.CORE_GROUP, name_hint="split_k"):
            k0 = ks * _KS
            partial = pl.matmul(a[:, k0 : k0 + _KS], b[k0 : k0 + _KS, :], out_dtype=pl.FP32)
        # atomic assemble OUTSIDE the scope -> orchestration level
        c = pl.assemble(c, partial, [0, 0], atomic=pl.AtomicType.Add)
    return c


post = orch_atomic.compile_for_test(
    torch.randn(_M, _K), torch.randn(_K, _N), torch.empty(_M, _N)
)
print("compiled with no error")
```

### Expected Behavior

The compile should fail with an actionable error, e.g.:

```
pl.assemble(..., atomic=pl.AtomicType.Add) is only supported inside a
pl.at(level=pl.Level.CORE_GROUP, ...) scope, where it lowers to an atomic-add
tile.store into global memory. This assemble sits at the orchestration level,
where no atomic-combine instruction exists. Move it inside the scope that
produces the partial result.
```

### Actual Behavior

Compiles cleanly. The generated orchestration C++ never touches `ext_c`:

```cpp
const Tensor& ext_c = orch_args.tensor(2).ref();

PTO2_SCOPE() {
    for (int64_t ks = 0; ks < 4; ks += 1) {
        PTO2_SCOPE() {
            uint32_t ret0__out_ci_shapes[2] = {64, 64};
            TensorCreateInfo ret0__out_ci(ret0__out_ci_shapes, 2, DataType::FLOAT32);
            TaskOutputTensors alloc_0 = alloc_tensors(ret0__out_ci);   // fresh scratch each iteration
            const Tensor& ret0__out = alloc_0.get_ref(0);

            // Task 0: split_k
            L0TaskArgs params_t0;
            params_t0.add_input(ext_a);
            params_t0.add_input(ext_b);
            params_t0.add_output(ret0__out);                            // writes the scratch
            params_t0.add_scalar(ks);
            rt_submit_aic_task(0, params_t0);
        }
    }
}
```

The atomic attr survives in the orchestration IR all the way to codegen but has no consumer:

```python
c__ssa_v3: pl.Tensor[[64, 64], pl.FP32, ...] = pl.tensor.assemble(
    c__iter_v1, partial__ssa_v0, [0, 0], atomic=pl.AtomicType.Add)
```

and the outlined kernel's store carries no atomic:

```python
ret0__store: pl.Tensor[[64, 64], pl.FP32, ...] = pl.tile.store(partial__tile, [0, 0], ret0__out)
```

### Git Commit ID

52789b8d452d0bc4775112ea34092fb0fceb4804

### NPU Kind

N/A (not hardware-specific)

### Host Platform

Linux (aarch64)

### Additional Context

**Suggested fix.** The primary check belongs in `HandleTensorAssembleAssign` (`src/codegen/orchestration/orchestration_codegen.cpp:3803`) — in SSA form every orchestration-level `tensor.assemble` passes through it, so the guard is provably complete. Per `.claude/rules/error-checking.md` this is a documented user-facing limitation, so `CHECK_SPAN` rather than `INTERNAL_CHECK_SPAN`:

```cpp
void HandleTensorAssembleAssign(const AssignStmtPtr& assign, const CallPtr& call) {
  INTERNAL_CHECK_SPAN(call->args_.size() == 3, call->span_)
      << "Internal error: tensor.assemble expects 3 arguments";

  // An orchestration-level assemble emits no write of its own: it aliases the LHS
  // to the target and relies on the producing InCore kernel having stored into the
  // target's view. No orchestration instruction can perform an atomic combine, so
  // an atomic=Add here is silently dropped and split-K degrades to a racing write.
  CHECK_SPAN(call->GetKwarg<int>("atomic", 0) == static_cast<int>(ir::AtomicType::kNone),
             call->span_)
      << "pl.assemble(..., atomic=pl.AtomicType.Add) is only supported inside a "
         "pl.at(level=pl.Level.CORE_GROUP, ...) scope, where it lowers to an "
         "atomic-add tile.store into global memory. This assemble sits at the "
         "orchestration level, where no atomic-combine instruction exists. Move it "
         "inside the scope that produces the partial result.";

  std::string target_name = GenerateExprString(call->args_[0]);
  target_name = GetExternalTensorName(target_name);
  emit_name_map_[assign->var_.get()] = target_name;
}
```

A secondary guard on the `op_conversion_registry.cpp:539-542` fallback would catch the InCore tensor→tensor form earlier, with a more precise span.

**Compatibility.** Every existing `atomic=pl.AtomicType.Add` use in the repo is already inside a `pl.at` scope — `examples/kernels/10_split_k.py:62`, `tests/ut/jit/test_split_k.py`, and the four kernels in `tests/st/runtime/ops/test_atomic_add.py` — so the check breaks no existing case.

**Test.** A negative test belongs next to the positive one in `tests/ut/jit/test_split_k.py`, asserting `pytest.raises(ValueError)` on the repro above.

**Docs.** The `assemble` docstring (`python/pypto/language/op/tensor_ops.py:1784-1796`) currently only says the target "must lower to a global-memory store (a function output tensor)"; it should state explicitly that the call must be inside a `CORE_GROUP` scope. Same for the `docs/en/` and `docs/zh/` copies.

title: [Bug] Unified DSL ops silently drop Tensor-only kwargs on the Tile path — pl.matmul(..., b_trans=True) compiles silently wrong math
body:
### Component

Other — Python DSL frontend (`python/pypto/language/op/unified_ops.py`)

### Description

The unified DSL ops dispatch on input type (`Tensor` vs `Tile`) and accept a **superset** of kwargs covering both paths. When a kwarg applies only to the *other* path, it is **silently discarded** — no error, no warning.

For `pl.matmul` this is a correctness bug, not just a bad diagnostic:

```python
# python/pypto/language/op/unified_ops.py:785-808
def matmul(lhs, rhs, out_dtype=None, a_trans=False, b_trans=False, c_matrix_nz=False):
    """... Tensor path accepts extra kwargs (out_dtype, a_trans, b_trans, c_matrix_nz).
    Tile path ignores them."""                                    # <-- :796
    if isinstance(lhs, Tensor) and isinstance(rhs, Tensor):
        return _tensor.matmul(lhs, rhs, out_dtype, a_trans, b_trans, c_matrix_nz)
    if isinstance(lhs, Tile) and isinstance(rhs, Tile):
        return _tile.matmul(lhs, rhs)          # <-- :807  all four kwargs dropped
```

This is correct *IR design*, not an IR bug. At tensor level a value has no layout, so `a_trans`/`b_trans` is the only place the information can live. At tile level transposition is a **type property** — `tile.transpose_view` swaps the trailing dims and flips each layout field's major-ness (NZ↔ZN), zero-copy, aliasing the same buffer — and `tile.matmul` maps 1:1 onto `pto.tmatmul`, which has no transpose attribute (`src/backend/common/pto_ops_elementwise.cpp:444`). PRs #1776 → #1866 → #1883 deliberately *removed* transpose parameters from the tile layer in favour of the view. Tile ops should **not** gain transpose args.

The defect is that the frontend accepts a request it cannot honour and stays silent instead of rejecting it.

**The `@overload` declarations already encode the correct contract** — `matmul(lhs: Tile, rhs: Tile) -> Tile` takes no transpose kwargs, and pyright already rejects the call:

```
error: Argument of type "Tile" cannot be assigned to parameter "lhs" of type "Tensor" (reportArgumentType)
```

Only the runtime implementation fails to enforce what the overloads declare.

### Steps to Reproduce

**Repro 1 — silently wrong math (worst case).** A square B operand keeps the shapes consistent after the flag is dropped, so nothing errors:

```python
import pypto.language as pl

@pl.program
class SilentWrong:
    @pl.function(auto_scope=False)
    def main(self, a: pl.Tensor[[32, 128], pl.BF16], b: pl.Tensor[[128, 128], pl.BF16],
             out: pl.Out[pl.Tensor[[32, 128], pl.FP32]]) -> pl.Tensor[[32, 128], pl.FP32]:
        with pl.scope():
            at = pl.load(a, [0, 0], [32, 128], target_memory=pl.MemorySpace.Mat)
            bt = pl.load(b, [0, 0], [128, 128], target_memory=pl.MemorySpace.Mat)
            # User asks for A @ B^T. b_trans is dropped -> compiles A @ B.
            c = pl.matmul(at, bt, b_trans=True, out_dtype=pl.FP32)
            out = pl.store(c, [0, 0], out)
        return out

from pypto import ir
print(ir.python_print(SilentWrong))
```

Emitted IR — no `transpose_view`, no `b_trans`, no diagnostic at any stage:

```python
c: pl.Tile[[32, 128], pl.FP32, pl.Mem.Acc] = pl.tile.matmul(at, bt)
```

**Repro 2 — loud but misleading.** Same code with a non-square B (`[32,512]` / `[128,512]`) fails deep in C++ type deduction, naming the wrong thing:

```
Error: pl operation 'matmul': The operator tile.matmul requires matching inner dimensions,
       but got lhs K=512 and rhs K=128
Check failed: k_lhs_const->value_ == k_rhs_const->value_ at src/ir/op/tile_ops/matmul.cpp:78
```

This is how the bug was found in the wild — a `pypto-lib` DSv4 kernel (`decode_attention_csa.py`) whose matmul operands were changed from `Tensor` to `Tile` (`pl.create_l1` → `pl.create_tile`, tensor slice → `pl.load`). The `pl.matmul(..., b_trans=True)` line was untouched, but its dispatch target changed and the flag stopped being honoured. Nothing in the error mentions `b_trans`.

### Expected Behavior

`pl.matmul(tile_a, tile_b, b_trans=True)` should raise at the call site, naming the offending kwarg and pointing at the tile-level alternative — e.g.:

```
TypeError: pl.matmul: 'b_trans' is not supported for Tile operands. At tile level a
transposed operand is an explicit view: pl.tile.transpose_view(rhs).
```

The file already has this exact pattern implemented elsewhere and simply was not applied here: `row_expand_add` (`unified_ops.py:521-522`) raises, and `xor`/`xors` (`:1204`, `:1229`) call the dedicated `_reject_tmp_for_tensor` helper (`:1127`). `div`/`high_precision` (`:271`) and `slice`/`clamp` (`:724`) also guard correctly.

Only a non-default value needs to raise — passing `b_trans=False` explicitly is a no-op and should stay accepted.

### Actual Behavior

The kwarg is discarded with no error, warning, or IR trace. Depending on operand shapes this produces either a numerically wrong kernel that compiles and runs cleanly (Repro 1) or a C++ type-deduction error 40+ lines away from the cause that does not mention the dropped argument (Repro 2).

### Git Commit ID

07ab63e4773dabb09b13a563c94d1baa8dec421e

### NPU Kind

N/A (not hardware-specific)

### Host Platform

Linux (aarch64)

### Additional Context

A sweep of `unified_ops.py` and the Tensor/Tile op layers found this is a **class** of defect, not a one-off. Findings below are grouped by whether dropping the parameter changes results.

#### Semantically meaningful drops (fix first)

| # | Site | Dropped | Effect | Overloads correct? |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | `unified_ops.py:807` `matmul` | `a_trans`, `b_trans` | wrong math / bogus K error | ✅ yes — runtime guard only |
| 2 | `unified_ops.py:861` `matmul_acc` | `a_trans`, `b_trans` | same, plus M/N mismatch vs `acc` | ✅ yes — runtime guard only |
| 3 | `unified_ops.py:474` `rsqrt` | `high_precision` | **silent numerical regression** | ❌ **no overloads at all** |

**#3 deserves attention.** `tensor.rsqrt` carries `high_precision` as an op attr and the conversion pass allocates a scratch tile to emit the 2-operand high-precision `tile.rsqrt(src, tmp)`. `tile.rsqrt` has no such attr — precision is selected purely by *passing `tmp`* (`src/ir/op/tile_ops/unary.cpp:242-259`). The unified wrapper calls `_tile.rsqrt(input)` with no `tmp`, so `high_precision=True` silently yields the low-precision path. Unlike `matmul` there are **no `@overload` declarations**, so a type checker accepts `pl.rsqrt(tile, high_precision=True)` too — it needs an overload split *and* a runtime guard. The behaviour is documented in the docstring, but documenting a silent drop does not make it safe.

#### Strategy-meaningful drop

| # | Site | Dropped | Effect |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 4 | `unified_ops.py:949` `col_sum` | `tmp_tile` | Tensor path always lowers to the 1-arg **sequential** reduction; the requested binary-tree form (O(log M) depth, better FP accumulation) is discarded and the scratch tile is allocated but never used |

#### Benign drops (no result change, but same silent-swallow UX)

`tmp_tile` on the Tensor path of 8 reductions — `row_max` (`:873`), `row_sum` (`:892`), `row_min` (`:911`), `row_prod` (`:930`), `row_argmax` (`:998`), `row_argmin` (`:1015`), `col_argmax` (`:1032`), `col_argmin` (`:1047`). The conversion pass synthesizes its own scratch, so results match; the user's tile is silently dead while still consuming UB budget. None of the eight has `@overload`s.

#### Dead / unhonoured kwargs

- **`c_matrix_nz` is dead end-to-end.** Accepted at `unified_ops.py:791` → `language/op/tensor_ops.py:639` → `ir/op/tensor_ops.py:448`, registered at `src/ir/op/tensor_ops/matmul.cpp:200` — and **read by nothing**. Verified: a repo-wide grep returns only that one `set_attr` registration, the Python plumbing, and 4 test/example call sites that all pass `False`.
- **`out_dtype` default diverges between levels** (verified): `tensor.matmul` on FP16×FP16 with `out_dtype` omitted deduces **FP16** (`PromoteDataTypes`), while `tile.matmul` unconditionally deduces **FP32** for float inputs (`src/ir/op/tile_ops/matmul.cpp:88-89`). Identical source produces a different result dtype at the two levels with no kwarg involved.
- ⚠️ *Needs triage, not confirmed:* whether an explicit `out_dtype` on `tensor.matmul` survives lowering. The declared type is FP16 (verified), but I could not confirm in this session whether a compensating cast is inserted — the matmul survived `ConvertTensorToTileOps` unconverted in my minimal harness. Worth a separate check before acting on it.

#### Signature divergences that can misbind positionally

Separate from the silent-drop class, but the same porting hazard — these accept a positional argument that means something *different* at the other level, so nothing type-checks it:

- `random` — `valid_shape` inserted mid-signature: `tensor_ops.py:599` vs `tile_ops.py:717`. The 8th positional is `dtype` at tensor level and `valid_shape` at tile level.
- `ir.transpose` — 4th positional is `valid_shape` (`ir/op/tensor_ops.py:1797`) vs `tmp` (`ir/op/tile_ops.py:2629`).
- `ir.scatter_mask` — first two args swapped: `(input, dst, ...)` (`ir/op/tensor_ops.py:2491`) vs `(dst, src, ...)` (`ir/op/tile_ops.py:3025`).
- `scatter` / `gather` — unrelated ops sharing a name across the two levels (`language/op/tensor_ops.py:2321`, `:2069` vs `tile_ops.py:2591`, `:2475`).
- `mrgsort` — `exhausted` is keyword-only at tensor level, positional at tile level.

#### Suggested shape of the fix

A shared helper mirroring the existing `_reject_tmp_for_tensor` (`unified_ops.py:1127`), raising only when a cross-path kwarg holds a non-default value, applied to the sites above; plus `@overload` splits for the 9 functions that currently have none, so the static contract matches the runtime one. `matmul`/`matmul_acc` need the runtime guard only — their overloads are already right.

*Not fixed in this session by request — filing for tracking.*

title: [Bug] pl.create_tile resolves to two different functions — parser namespace rejects transpose=/flat_layout= that the signature advertises
body:
Related: #2264

### Component

Other — Python DSL frontend namespace exports (`python/pypto/language/op/__init__.py`)

### Description

`create_tile` is bound to **two different functions** in two namespaces, with different signatures:

```
pypto.language.create_tile      -> tile_ops.create
   (shape, dtype, target_memory=Vec, transpose=None, *, flat_layout=None)   # 5 params

pypto.language.op.create_tile   -> unified_ops.create_tile
   (shape, dtype, target_memory=Vec)                                        # 3 params
```

They are not the same object — `pypto.language.create_tile is pypto.language.op.create_tile` → `False`.

The DSL parser resolves unified `pl.<op>` calls against `pypto.language.op`, **not** `pypto.language` (`python/pypto/language/parser/ast_parser.py:8226-8228`):

```python
import pypto.language.op as _pl_op
op_func = getattr(_pl_op, op_name, None)
```

So inside a `@pl.function` body the parser gets the 3-parameter version and rejects `transpose=`, while everything a user consults outside the parser — `inspect.signature`, IDE autocomplete, the docstring at `tile_ops.py:285-300` — shows the 5-parameter version that does accept it. `flat_layout=` is rejected identically.

**The parser is not at fault.** The `pypto.language.op` restriction is intentional and documented at `ast_parser.py:8213-8224`: it exists so non-op DSL symbols (`pl.range`, `pl.const`, `pl.dynamic`) cannot be invoked as ops. That design is sound and should stay.

The defect is that the two package `__init__.py` files make **opposite choices for the same name**:

- `python/pypto/language/__init__.py:125` imports `create_tile` from `.op.tile_ops` → the 5-param alias (`tile_ops.py:323`, `create_tile = create`).
- `python/pypto/language/op/__init__.py:128` imports it from `.unified_ops`, deliberately overriding the `tile_ops` import above it. The comment at `:98-101` states the intent:

  > Unified dispatch (overlapping ops). Imported AFTER tile_ops so the unified versions override any same-named imports above (e.g. `abs`, `create_tile`) — direct `pl.abs(tensor)` users get the unified dispatch rather than the Tile-only path.

**That rationale does not apply to `create_tile`.** The override exists so unified Tensor/Tile dispatch wins, but `create_tile` is Tile-only — the Tensor counterpart is a separately named `create_tensor` — and `unified_ops.create_tile` performs no dispatch whatsoever:

```python
# python/pypto/language/op/unified_ops.py:1329-1340
def create_tile(shape, dtype, target_memory=MemorySpace.Vec) -> Tile:
    return _tile.create(shape, dtype, target_memory)     # no isinstance, no dispatch
```

It is a pure forwarder whose only effect is to narrow the signature. It was grouped with `abs` and the bitwise family, which genuinely need dispatch, but has no dispatch role of its own.

**How the drift happened:** `unified_ops.create_tile` dates from #138 (`b2b8d0b5`). `transpose` was added to `tile_ops.create` in #1809 (`3ec5e838`, `pl.create_l1` + `pl.gather_row` — kernel-driven paged gather into L1); `flat_layout` came later. Neither updated the older forwarder.

**Scope:** I compared every callable exported under both namespaces for a same-name/different-signature split. `create_tile` is the **only** one — this is isolated, not systemic.

### Steps to Reproduce

```python
import pypto.language as pl

@pl.program
class P:
    @pl.function(auto_scope=False)
    def main(self, a: pl.Tensor[[128, 512], pl.BF16],
             out: pl.Out[pl.Tensor[[128, 512], pl.BF16]]) -> pl.Tensor[[128, 512], pl.BF16]:
        with pl.scope():
            t = pl.create_tile([128, 512], pl.BF16,
                               target_memory=pl.MemorySpace.Mat, transpose=True)
            out = pl.store(t, [0, 0], out)
        return out
```

Confirm the namespace split independently:

```python
import inspect, pypto.language as pl, pypto.language.op as plop
print(inspect.signature(pl.create_tile))     # (..., transpose=None, *, flat_layout=None)
print(inspect.signature(plop.create_tile))   # (shape, dtype, target_memory=Vec)
print(pl.create_tile is plop.create_tile)    # False
```

### Expected Behavior

`pl.create_tile(..., transpose=True)` should parse, exactly as the signature the user sees advertises, and produce the transposed Mat (ZN) fractal layout — matching `pl.tile.create(..., transpose=True)`.

More generally, a given DSL op name should resolve to the same function whether it is reached through `pypto.language` or `pypto.language.op`.

### Actual Behavior

```
Error: pl operation 'create_tile': create_tile() got an unexpected keyword argument 'transpose'
  --> repro.py:9:16
   |
 9 |             t = pl.create_tile([128, 512], pl.BF16, target_memory=pl.MemorySpace.Mat, transpose=True)
   |                 ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
```

The error is doubly confusing: the parameter demonstrably exists on the `pl.create_tile` the user can inspect, and the message names `create_tile()` — a function the user never referenced by that path.

**Workaround (verified):** `pl.tile.create(...)` uses the category-op parser path, which resolves against `tile_ops` directly:

```python
t = pl.tile.create([128, 512], pl.BF16, target_memory=pl.MemorySpace.Mat, transpose=True)   # parses OK
```

### Git Commit ID

07ab63e4773dabb09b13a563c94d1baa8dec421e

### NPU Kind

N/A (not hardware-specific)

### Host Platform

Linux (aarch64)

### Additional Context

**Suggested fix.** Drop `create_tile` from the unified override list in `python/pypto/language/op/__init__.py` (remove it from the `from .unified_ops import (...)` block at `:128` and from `__all__` handling as needed) so the `from .tile_ops import (...)` import above wins in both namespaces, and delete the now-unused `unified_ops.create_tile`.

This is preferable to re-syncing the two signatures: adding `transpose`/`flat_layout` passthrough to the forwarder fixes today's symptom but leaves the duplicate definition in place, so the next parameter added to `tile_ops.create` reintroduces the identical bug. Removing the shadow eliminates the drift permanently. `tile_ops.py:323` already provides the `create_tile = create` alias, so the name stays available.

Worth adding a guard test that asserts every name exported from both `pypto.language` and `pypto.language.op` resolves to the same object, which would catch any future recurrence of this class.

**Relationship to #2264.** Both originate in `unified_ops.py` wrappers that are narrower than the underlying op, but they are distinct defects with distinct fixes:

| | #2264 | this issue |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Symptom | kwarg silently **dropped**, no error | kwarg **hard-rejected** at parse time |
| Cause | wrapper accepts the kwarg then discards it | two namespaces bind one name to two functions |
| Fix | runtime guards + `@overload` splits | remove the namespace shadow |

Note the audit in #2264 listed `create_tile` under "minor unified-API gaps" as simply not exposing `transpose`/`flat_layout`. That understated it — the parameters are not merely absent from a single wrapper, they are present on the function the name resolves to everywhere except the one namespace the parser reads.

title: [Bug] GM pipe workspace is sized for one ring, but a bidirectional pipe is two
body:
### Component

Codegen

### Description

`ComputeGMPipeWorkspaceElements` (`src/codegen/orchestration/orchestration_analysis.cpp`) sizes the injected `__gm_pipe_buffer` as:

```cpp
int GetGMPipeSlotCount(int dir_mask) {
  const int bidirectional = core_affinity::kDirMaskC2V | core_affinity::kDirMaskV2C;
  if (dir_mask == bidirectional) {
    return 4;                                  // slots per ring
  }
  ...                                          // 8 for unidirectional
}
...
total_bytes += static_cast<int64_t>(slot_count) * static_cast<int64_t>(slot_size);   // one ring's worth
```

Two problems:

**1. A bidirectional pipe is two rings, not one.** The A2A3 GM layout is C2V at offset 0 and V2C at `slot_num * slot_size`, total `2 * slot_num * slot_size`. This is specified in pto-isa's `docs/HL_ptoisa_newfeature20260306_TPUSH_TPOP.md`:

```text
:169   gm_slot_buf = gm_alloc(2 * SLOT_NUM * SLOT_SIZE)    // bidirectional
:222   buf_offset = (DIR_MASK & DIR_C2V) ? SLOT_NUM * SLOT_SIZE : 0
:223   v2c_ring_buf = GM_SLOT_BUFFER + buf_offset
```

and drawn explicitly at `:288` ("total size = 2 * SLOT_NUM * SLOT_SIZE for bidirectional"). We allocate half of that.

**2. An explicit `slot_num` is ignored.** `slot_count` is re-derived from `dir_mask`, so a pipe initialized with `pl.cross_core_slot(slot_num=N)` for any `N` other than the `dir_mask` default gets a workspace sized for the default. Deeper rings under-allocate proportionally.

Concretely, a `TPipe<0, DIR_BOTH, 1024, 4, 4>` is handed a 4096 B workspace where the documented layout needs 8192 B.

### Steps to Reproduce

Any bidirectional (`dir_mask=3`) cross-core pipe. The existing unit test `test_submit_dispatched_pipe_group_sizes_workspace_and_resolves_callees` (`tests/ut/codegen/test_orchestration_tensor_rw.py`) pins the current behaviour and shows it directly — a `dir_mask=3, slot_size=512` pipe asserts `shape_values == ["512"]` elements, i.e. `4 * 512 B`, one ring. The documented layout for that pipe is `2 * 4 * 512 B` = 1024 elements.

For `slot_num`: initialize a pipe with `slot_num=16` on a unidirectional `dir_mask`; the workspace is sized from the `dir_mask` default of 8 slots, half of what the pipe uses.

### Expected vs Actual

Expected: `ring_count(dir_mask) * slot_num * slot_size`, where `ring_count` is 2 for bidirectional and 1 otherwise, and `slot_num` comes from the pipe when it carries one.

Actual: `slot_count(dir_mask) * slot_size`.

### Impact

**Today: nothing observable**, plus silent under-allocation for any explicit `slot_num`. The under-allocation is currently consistent with a matching pto-isa defect: the device never applies the per-direction ring offset either (`include/pto/npu/a2a3/TPush.hpp` — both directions index `GM_SLOT_BUFFER + (tileIndex % SLOT_NUM) * SLOT_SIZE + entryOffset` with `entryOffset` always 0), so both rings really do live in the first half and the short allocation "fits". Fixing only this side changes nothing observable — measured, the resulting corruption is bit-identical.

**After the pto-isa fix: out-of-bounds GM writes** unless this lands first. That is the reason to fix it now and in this order — with the device-side offset applied and this sizing unchanged, the entire V2C ring falls past the end of the allocation.

The device-side half is filed against pto-isa (issue linked below), where it supersedes the withdrawn hw-native-sys/pto-isa#195. Together the two fix a silent cross-core corruption on A2A3 hardware: a GLA/ZeCO sequence-parallel forward that failed 5/12 configurations at C=16 and 6/12 at C=32 passes 24/24 with both applied.

### Environment

pypto `f621eca4` (verified unchanged on `main` `9f8e7532`), PTOAS 0.54, runtime `9922afdb`, Atlas A2/A3, fp32.

### Additional Context

A fix is ready and will be sent as a PR: multiply by a ring count derived from `dir_mask`, honour the `slot_num` kwarg when `initialize_pipe` carries one, update the one existing expectation that encodes the one-ring assumption, and add two tests pinning the rule. `tests/ut/codegen` + `tests/ut/ir/transforms`: 3195 passed.

title: [Feature] Support runtime (unspecialized) scalar parameters in annotation-driven compile()
body:
### Summary

`@pl.jit` kernels that carry a `pl.Scalar` parameter meant to be **runtime** (value supplied at dispatch, not baked into the IR) cannot be compiled via annotation-driven "signature mode" (`compile()` with no tensor args). Today the only escape hatch is positional sample-arg mode, which forces the caller to manufacture throwaway tensors for every tensor parameter just to reach the (trailing) scalar slot.

### Motivation / Use Case

`JITFunction.compile()` has two modes (`pypto/jit/decorator.py`):

- **Signature mode** — `compile()` with no positional args; tensor shape/dtype read from `pl.Tensor[[...], dtype]` annotations, dynamic dims stay extent-independent. No dummy tensors needed.
- **Sample-arg mode** — `compile(*args)`; tensor shape/dtype read from the passed torch tensors.

Mode selection (`_resolve_specialization`, `decorator.py:1948`):

```python
signature_mode = allow_signature_mode and not args and not any(_is_tensor(v) for v in kwargs.values())
```

A `pl.Scalar` annotation carries only a *type* (`pl.Scalar[pl.INT32]`), no value. In signature mode the scalar value is resolved by `_signature_scalar_value`, which **requires a literal `int`/`float`/`bool` and specializes that value into the compiled artifact** (`decorator.py:380`):

```python
if not isinstance(value, (int, float, bool)):
    raise TypeError(... "must be an int/float/bool" ...)
return value
```

So a scalar whose value varies at runtime (e.g. a per-step token count) **cannot use signature mode** — any value supplied gets baked in. The only workaround is sample-arg mode, which is positional: passing one positional arg disables signature mode, and `_bind_args` → `sig.bind` then requires a value for *every* parameter. Because such runtime scalars are typically trailing parameters, the caller must build throwaway (zero-storage meta) tensors for all preceding tensor params purely to land a placeholder in the scalar's positional slot.

Concretely, pypto-serving's DeepSeek executor has to build an entire meta-tensor tuple just to compile two kernels that each carry one runtime scalar:

```python
# pypto_serving/model/deepseek/npu_executor.py:199
def _runtime_scalar_compile_args(jit_fn, runtime_scalar_names):
    # tensors        -> torch.empty(shape, dtype, device="meta")  # zero storage
    # runtime scalars -> ctypes.c_int32()                         # deliberately NOT int/float/bool
```

The `ctypes.c_int32()` only works because `_bind_args` classifies scalars by `isinstance(value, (int, float, bool))` (`decorator.py:1794`), so a ctypes value is *not* captured into `scalar_values` and is left unspecialized. That is an implicit, undocumented contract: the supported path (signature mode) forces specialization, and the unspecialized path only works through this incidental type-filtering in positional mode.

### Proposed API / Behavior

A first-class way to mark a `pl.Scalar` parameter as **runtime / unspecialized** so it can be used in signature-mode `compile()`. Some options:

1. **Explicit runtime-scalar marker** — e.g. `pl.RuntimeScalar[pl.INT32]` (or `pl.Scalar[pl.INT32, runtime=True]`), which `_bind_args_from_signature` leaves out of `scalar_values` (treated like a dynamic dim: value independent, supplied at dispatch) instead of calling `_signature_scalar_value`.
2. **Accept a ctypes/sentinel value in signature mode** — relax `_signature_scalar_value` so a ctypes or sentinel value marks the scalar as unspecialized rather than erroring, mirroring what `_bind_args` already does implicitly.
3. **Keyword scalar binding that does not specialize** — allow `compile(my_scalar=<runtime int32>)` to keep signature mode (tensors from annotations) while leaving the scalar runtime-parametric.

Any of these would let kernels with runtime scalars compile from annotations alone and remove the meta-tensor workaround downstream.

### Alternatives Considered

- **Status quo** (sample-arg mode + meta tensors + ctypes placeholder): works today via the incidental `int/float/bool` filter in `_bind_args`, but is undocumented, couples "runtime-ness" to a type-filtering side effect, and forces every caller with a runtime scalar to build a full zero-storage tensor tuple. This is what pypto-serving currently does.

### Additional Context

- pypto commit: `a47d3004`
- Relevant code (`pypto/jit/decorator.py`): `_resolve_specialization` (`:1948`), `_bind_args_from_signature` (`:1799`), `_signature_scalar_value` (`:380`), `_bind_args` scalar classification (`:1794`).
- The `compile()` docstring already documents the no-arg signature path and notes "Scalar parameters have no value in the signature, so pass them as keyword args" (`decorator.py:2131`) — but that path specializes the value, which is exactly the gap for runtime scalars.
- Downstream workaround: `pypto_serving/model/deepseek/npu_executor.py:199` (`_runtime_scalar_compile_args`).

title: [Code Health] Persistent distributed mode depends on simpler private APIs

labels.name: code health
labels.description: Technical debt, robustness concerns, code quality improvements

body:
### Category

Technical Debt (cleanup, refactor)

### Component

Other — `python/pypto/runtime/` (distributed runtime integration with the `simpler` package)

### Description

PyPTO's **persistent distributed execution** mode is built on private members of
`simpler.worker.Worker`. It reaches them by name through `getattr`, and even documents the
dependency in its own error text ("persistent distributed execution requires Simpler's
private retention hooks"):

- `Worker._live_domains` — mutated directly (`del live_domains[handle.name]`) to hide a
  retained `CommDomain` from simpler's per-run release sweep.
- `Worker._execute_pending_domain_releases()` — called to force the deferred backend free.

Nothing in `simpler` promises either of these. They are implementation detail, so any
refactor inside `simpler` can silently invalidate the contract PyPTO relies on — and one
already has. Advancing the `runtime` submodule past the per-run resource isolation work
breaks the mode in two independent ways:

1. **Signature change.** `_execute_pending_domain_releases(self)` became
   `_execute_pending_domain_releases(self, resources: _RunResources)`. The no-argument
   call site raises:

   ```
   TypeError: Worker._execute_pending_domain_releases() missing 1 required
              positional argument: 'resources'
   ```

2. **Registry split — the deeper break.** CommDomain bookkeeping is no longer a single
   `Worker._live_domains`; each run also holds `resources.live_domains`, and the
   run-finalization cursor sweeps it:

   ```python
   ("live_domains", lambda: self._release_all_live_domains(resources)),
   ```

   `_detach_persistent_domain` only pops from `Worker._live_domains`, so the retained
   handle stays in the run's registry and is freed at the first fence. Retention is then
   silently gone, and the next request fails on the dead handle:

   ```
   RuntimeError: CommDomainHandle('p0:comm_d0') already released; do not pass it to
                 submit_* after release().
   ```

Two on-board system tests fail as a result:

- `tests/st/distributed/test_l3_notify_wait.py::TestL3NotifyWait::test_persistent_signal_exchange_resets_retained_window`
- `tests/st/distributed/test_l3_self_notify_credit_reset.py::TestL3SelfNotifyCreditReset::test_persistent_self_notify_credit_reset_without_window_reset`

The cost is recurring, not one-off: every future `runtime` bump has to re-derive whatever
private shape the retention hooks happen to have, and the failure surfaces only on
hardware, late, as an opaque `TypeError` or a stale-handle error rather than at import or
at a version check.

### Location

- `python/pypto/runtime/distributed_runner.py` — `_validate_persistent_runtime_hooks`
  (probes `_live_domains` / `_execute_pending_domain_releases`)
- `python/pypto/runtime/distributed_runner.py` — `_detach_persistent_domain`
  (`del live_domains[handle.name]`)
- `python/pypto/runtime/distributed_runner.py` — `_release_persistent_domains`
  (calls `_execute_pending_domain_releases()`)

### Proposed Fix

Move the contract into `simpler` as a supported CommDomain retention API, and have PyPTO
call only that. A prototype of this shape was verified on device — both system tests above
pass with it:

```python
# simpler.worker.Worker
def retain_comm_domain(self, handle: CommDomainHandle) -> None:
    """Keep handle alive past the fence of the run that allocated it."""

def release_comm_domain(self, handle: CommDomainHandle) -> None:
    """Free a domain previously detached by retain_comm_domain."""
```

Two details matter for correctness:

- The handle must carry a reference to its owning run's resources, bound at allocation, so
  `retain` can detach it from that run's registry under the same lock the release path
  uses. Today that reference exists only inside the `_release_fn` closure.
- A retained handle should stay in `Worker._live_domains` so `close()` still frees it as a
  residual rather than leaking it.

PyPTO's three call sites then collapse to `retain_comm_domain` / `release_comm_domain`,
with the hook probe checking for those two public names.

Filing here rather than only on the `simpler` side because the dependency is PyPTO's to
remove; the `simpler` API is the means. Worth adding a `simpler`-side test for the
retention semantics too, so the next refactor breaks a test instead of breaking PyPTO on
hardware.

### Priority

Medium (minor risk, should fix in next few releases)

title: [Feature] Support PTOAS global-entry V2C pipe so a cross-core payload can land in a sub-region of an L1 tile
body:
### Summary

PyPTO cannot express PTOAS's *global-entry* pipe form. As a result a V2C (AIV->AIC) payload can only ever be a whole freshly-popped value; it cannot be delivered into a sub-region of an L1 tile the kernel already owns. This forces "one gather per whole matmul operand", which in turn inflates the cross-core slot size and makes otherwise-valid kernels unschedulable.

#### Current behaviour

`tile.tpop_from_aic` / `tile.tpop_from_aiv` are registered `.no_argument()` with `f_deduce_type(DeduceUnknownType)` (`src/ir/op/tile_ops/cross_core.cpp:248-270`), so the result is always a Tile pinned to the ring slot. The DSL intrinsic mirrors this — `pl.tpop_from_aiv(*, shape, dtype, split, id) -> Tile` is keyword-only with no destination parameter (`python/pypto/language/op/system_ops.py:294-333`), while `pl.tpush_to_aic(tile, ...)` does take its operand.

Consequently a DSL write of the form `dst_l1_tile[a:b, :] = pl.aic_gather(ub_tile)` lowers to tpop + `pto.subview` + `pto.tmov` with `loc=mat` on BOTH sides. A2A3 has no such tmov pair — PTOAS lists the supported A2A3 pairs as `mat -> left/right/bias/scaling`, `vec -> vec`, `acc -> mat`, `acc -> vec` (`ptoas/docs/PTO_IR_manual.md:1565-1571`). ptoas fails with:

```
'pto.tmov' op expects a supported tmov address-space pair for this target
  loc("build_output/.../ptoas/qk_pv.pto":70:9)
```

Generated IR at that point:

```mlir
%chunk = pto.tpop_from_aiv {split = 1} -> !pto.tile_buf<loc=mat, dtype=bf16, rows=32, cols=512, ...>
%assemble_view = pto.subview %qk_kv[%micro_step, %c0] sizes [32, 512] valid [32, 512]
  : !pto.tile_buf<loc=mat, dtype=bf16, rows=128, cols=512, blayout=col_major, slayout=row_major, fractal=512>
  -> !pto.tile_buf<loc=mat, dtype=bf16, rows=32, cols=512, ...>
pto.tmov ins(%chunk : loc=mat ...) outs(%assemble_view : loc=mat ...)   // <-- no such instruction
```

### Motivation / Use Case

**Motivating kernel**

DeepSeek v4-flash sparse decode attention (pypto-lib `models/deepseek/v4-flash/decode_sparse_attn.py`, `qk_pv` SPMD region), reproduced with:

```
PTO_BENCH=1 python models/deepseek/v4-flash/decode_attention_csa.py -d 1 --enable-l2-swimlane 1 --start-pos 8192
```

The kernel stages 128 scattered 1 KB KV rows into a `[128, 512]` BF16 L1 tile in `[32, 512]` micro-chunks, using two AIV lanes to gather (an AIV sustains far more outstanding scattered loads than the cube's ND2NZ path), then runs `Q @ KV^T` and `P @ KV` off the one resident L1 tile via `transpose_view`. Every on-chip budget fits (L1 128 KB of 512 KB, UB 16 KB per lane of 184 KB, Acc 80 KB of 128 KB); the design is blocked purely by the missing lowering. Working around it by gathering the whole `[128, 512]` tile in one shot makes the cross-core slot 128 KB and overruns the UB budget.

### Proposed API / Behavior

#### What PTOAS already supports

`pto.tpop_from_aiv` has a second result form (`ptoas/docs/PTO_IR_manual.md:9721-9755`):

```mlir
%entry = pto.tpop_from_aiv {id = 0, split = 1} -> !pto.tensor_view<...>
```

> for global entries this waits for producer ready and assigns the current GM FIFO slot address into the returned GlobalTensor-like descriptor [...] A global-entry pop does **not** perform `TLOAD`; callers explicitly load from the returned GM entry or from views derived from it

And (`ptoas/docs/PTO_IR_manual.md:9236-9241`):

> When every transfer op bound to one pipe id uses a global entry, the pipe is a **global-only GM FIFO**. Its frontend initialize op carries `gm_slot_tensor` and may carry `slot_num`; `gm_slot_buffer`, `c2v_consumer_buf`, `v2c_consumer_buf`, `local_slot_num`, `pto.reserve_buffer`, and `pto.import_reserved_buffer` are **not used**.

i.e. a global-only pipe reserves NO on-chip memory at all.

The destination-side machinery also already exists: `tile.gather_row` is documented as "Load one GM row directly into a sub-region of an on-chip tile (DPS) ... `pto.subview` of `dst` + `pto.tload`, GM -> on-chip, **no `pto.tmov`**" (`python/pypto/language/op/tile_ops.py:485-495`; codegen `src/backend/common/pto_ops_datamove.cpp:297`). It is DPS, takes a dynamic `dst_offset`, and accepts a Mat/L1 destination. It only needs a GM `Tensor` source — which is exactly what a global-entry pop returns.

The subview itself is already legal and already emitted: per the `pto.subview` verifier (`ptoas/docs/PTO_IR_manual.md:960-1020`), for boxed row-major tiles the subview must keep the full source column extent with column offset 0, and sizes must be multiples of the inner boxed shape; `[micro_step, 0] sizes [32, 512]` on a `[128, 512]` BF16 NZ tile (16x16 inner box) satisfies all of it, and "lowering keeps parent physical stride/base semantics".

#### Proposed change (all at the PyPTO level; no ISA or PTOAS work needed)

1. IR: add global-entry variants of `tile.tpop_from_aiv` / `tile.tpop_from_aic` whose result is a GM Tensor descriptor rather than a Tile, plus a producer-side `tile.talloc_to_aic` / `talloc_to_aiv`.
2. Lowering: when an `aic_gather` result feeds a `tile.assemble` into a Mat tile (the exact pattern that produces mat->mat tmov today), emit pop-entry -> subview -> tload -> tfree instead. The compiler already computes the subview and the offset at that point.
3. Pipe setup: mark that pipe id global-only — carry `gm_slot_tensor` + `slot_num`, drop `reserve_buffer` / `import_peer_buffer` / the consumer-buf args.
4. Verifier: no change expected. `AivSplitValid` rejects `tile.assemble` inside a `pl.split_aiv` region; under this lowering the assemble is gone and the cube-side tload/subview sit outside the region regardless.

Target DSL shape:

```python
entry = pl.tpop_entry_from_aiv(shape=[ATTN_K_TILE_MICRO, HEAD_DIM], dtype=pl.BF16, split=1)  # -> Tensor (GM slot)
qk_kv = pl.tile.gather_row(qk_kv, entry, [micro_step, 0], [0, 0], [ATTN_K_TILE_MICRO, HEAD_DIM])
pl.tfree_from_aiv(...)
```

#### Acceptance criteria

1. A V2C payload can be delivered into a sub-region of a caller-owned L1 tile with no `pto.tmov`.
